questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The accounting equation is:
questions.e: Dual-aspect gives Assets = Capital + Liabilities; equivalently Capital = Assets - Liabilities. Every transaction affects two sides, keeping the equation balanced. Drawings reduce capital.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which concept assumes the business will continue indefinitely?
questions.e: Going concern justifies charging depreciation over useful life and classifying assets as fixed versus current. Without it, accounts would be drawn up on liquidation (break-up) values.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Outstanding salary is:
o: A personal account with a credit balance
questions.e: Outstanding expenses are personal accounts (representative persons) with credit balances, shown as current liabilities. Under accrual accounting they are recognised when incurred, not when paid.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The trial balance tests:
questions.e: Trial balance verifies debit-credit equality but misses errors of omission, principle, commission, compensating errors and original entry. A suspense account holds one-sided differences pending investigation.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Purchase of machinery for cash affects:
o: One real and one real account (machinery debit, cash credit)
questions.e: Machinery (real: debit what comes in) and cash (real: credit what goes out) — both real accounts. Every transaction touches at least two accounts under double entry.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The imprest system is used for:
questions.e: Petty cashiers receive a fixed float (imprest), reimbursed periodically for expenses incurred. It controls small payments while keeping the main cash book clean.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Depreciation under the written-down-value method:
o: Is charged only in the last year
Is higher in early years than straight-line
questions.e: WDV applies a fixed rate to the diminishing balance, front-loading the charge — useful when assets lose more value early. SLM spreads cost evenly over useful life.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Depreciation is added back in cash-flow statements because:
questions.e: Depreciation reduces profit without spending cash, so the indirect method adds it back to operating profit. It is an operating adjustment, not an investing or financing flow.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared by:
questions.e: The depositor prepares the BRS to reconcile the cash-book balance with the pass book, adjusting for unpresented cheques, uncredited deposits, bank charges and direct credits.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Cheques issued but not presented cause:
o: Pass-book balance is higher than the cash-book balance
Cash-book balance is higher than the pass-book balance
questions.e: Issuing a cheque credits the bank column of the cash book at once, reducing the cash-book balance immediately, while the bank debits the account only on presentation. So until presented, the pass book shows the higher balance. Uncredited deposits have the reverse effect.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Noting charges on a dishonoured bill are borne by:
o: The drawer (or the party causing dishonour)
questions.e: Noting charges paid to the notary public for recording dishonour are recoverable from the party liable — typically the drawer — and are debited to the relevant party's account.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Retiring a bill before maturity entitles the drawee to:
o: A rebate for the unexpired period
questions.e: Early retirement earns rebate (discount) for the unexpired term, credited to the drawee. Renewal, by contrast, cancels the old bill and draws a fresh one with interest.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Gross profit is shown in:
questions.e: Trading account computes gross profit (sales minus cost of goods sold); P&L derives net profit after indirect expenses. Manufacturing accounts add a manufacturing stage before trading.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Interest on capital is:
o: An appropriation shown in P&L Appropriation, not a charge
questions.e: Interest on partners' capital is appropriated only if profits suffice (per the deed); unlike interest on loans, it is not a charge. Interest on drawings is the reverse appropriation.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: In the absence of a partnership deed, profits are shared:
questions.e: The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 provides equal profit sharing, no interest on capital, no partner remuneration, and 6 per cent interest on partner loans when the deed is silent.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Goodwill on a partner's admission is credited to:
o: Old partners in their sacrificing ratio
questions.e: The incoming partner compensates old partners for their sacrificed share; premium for goodwill goes to old partners in the sacrificing ratio (old minus new ratio).

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bank balance sheets follow:
o: Schedule III of the Companies Act
Form A of the Third Schedule to the Banking Regulation Act
questions.e: Banking Regulation Act's Third Schedule: Form A (balance sheet) and Form B (profit and loss), with 16 schedules of notes. Companies use Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Income on NPAs is recognised by banks:
questions.e: RBI prudential norms require income recognition on NPAs only when actually received, reversing any previously accrued unrealised income. Standard assets follow accrual.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bills of exchange are negotiable under:
questions.e: The Negotiable Instruments Act governs promissory notes, bills of exchange and cheques — their negotiation, endorsement, crossing and dishonour. Accounting entries for bills follow from these legal features.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The current ratio's ideal benchmark is:
questions.e: The conventional 2:1 current ratio indicates comfortable short-term solvency; the quick ratio benchmark is 1:1. Banks use these in working-capital appraisal alongside MPBF.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Quick assets exclude:
questions.e: The acid test removes the least-liquid current assets — inventory and prepaids — from the numerator. A firm can show a healthy current ratio yet fail the quick test if stock is piled up.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Debt-equity ratio uses:
questions.e: Long-term debt over equity (shareholders' funds) measures leverage; below 2:1 is conventionally comfortable for industry. Proprietary ratio is the inverse perspective (funds to total assets).

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Interest coverage ratio is:
questions.e: EBIT/interest shows how many times operating earnings cover finance costs. Below 1.5-2 times signals distress — lenders watch its trend closely.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Average collection period equals:
questions.e: Collection period (days sales outstanding) translates the debtors turnover into days. Lengthening periods signal lax credit control or collection problems.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Return on capital employed uses:
o: Profit before interest and tax to capital employed
questions.e: ROCE = PBIT/Capital employed (equity plus long-term debt) measures operating efficiency of total long-term funds, before financing decisions distort it.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Earnings per share is:
o: (PAT minus preference dividend) to equity shares
PAT to total shares including preference
questions.e: EPS divides earnings available to equity holders by outstanding equity shares — the base for P/E valuation. Diluted EPS adjusts for convertibles and options.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The P/E ratio indicates:
o: Market price per rupee of earnings
questions.e: Price/EPS shows what investors pay for each rupee of earnings — a growth-expectation gauge. Its inverse is the earnings yield.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: DuPont analysis decomposes ROE into:
o: Net margin x asset turnover x leverage
questions.e: ROE = (Net profit/Sales) x (Sales/Assets) x (Assets/Equity), revealing whether returns come from pricing, efficiency or leverage — the diagnostic examiners love.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Fund-flow statements explain changes in:
questions.e: Fund flow tracks sources and applications of working capital (current assets minus current liabilities) between two balance sheets. 'Funds' here means working capital, not cash.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Issue of bonus shares in a fund-flow statement is:
o: Neither a source nor an application of funds
questions.e: Bonus issues capitalise reserves without moving working capital — a non-fund item, like depreciation or writing off goodwill. Only transactions altering working capital appear.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under AS-3, interest paid by a non-financial company is:
questions.e: AS-3 classifies interest/dividend paid as financing for non-financial enterprises (but operating for financial enterprises, whose business is money). Interest received is investing (operating for financial firms).

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Purchase of machinery for cash is:
questions.e: Capital expenditure sits in investing activities. Depreciation on that machinery later becomes an operating add-back — the classification pair examiners test together.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The indirect method of cash-flow starts from:
questions.e: The indirect method adjusts net profit for non-cash items and working-capital changes to reach operating cash flow. The direct method lists gross cash receipts and payments.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: An increase in creditors during the year:
questions.e: Rising payables mean cash retained — added back in operating activities. Rising receivables/inventory absorb cash and are deducted. This working-capital logic drives many numericals.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Future value of Rs.1,00,000 at 10 per cent for 2 years is:
questions.e: FV = 1,00,000 x (1.10)^2 = Rs.1,21,000 with annual compounding. Simple interest would give Rs.1,20,000 — the compounding difference is the exam's favourite trap.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Rule of 72 estimates:
o: Years to double money at a given rate
questions.e: Years to double = 72/interest rate (approx). At 9 per cent, money doubles in about 8 years — a quick sanity check for TVM answers.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: An annuity due differs from an ordinary annuity in:
o: Payments at the beginning of each period
questions.e: Annuity-due payments occur at period-start (rent in advance), ordinary annuities at period-end (loan EMIs typically). Each annuity-due payment compounds one period more.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NPV decision rule:
questions.e: Positive NPV means the project earns above the cost of capital, adding firm value. NPV is theoretically superior to IRR for mutually exclusive projects.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: IRR is the discount rate at which:
questions.e: IRR is the break-even discount rate; accept if IRR exceeds the cost of capital (hurdle rate). Multiple IRRs can arise with non-conventional cash flows.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Profitability index equals:
o: ARR divided by cost of capital
PV of inflows divided by initial investment
questions.e: PI above 1.0 mirrors positive NPV and ranks projects under capital rationing. It is a relative measure, unlike NPV's absolute rupee value.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Payback period ignores:
o: Time value of money and post-payback cash flows
questions.e: Payback's simplicity is its flaw — it ignores discounting and everything after payback. Discounted payback fixes the first flaw only.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Weighted average cost of capital uses:
questions.e: WACC weights cost of equity, debt (after tax), preference and retained earnings by market values — the economically relevant proportions for new decisions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Cost of debt is taken after tax because:
questions.e: Interest shields tax, so the effective cost is interest x (1 - tax rate). This tax shield is also why MM with taxes favours leverage.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Financial leverage is measured by:
questions.e: Degree of financial leverage = % change in EPS / % change in EBIT, computed as EBIT/EBT. Operating leverage is Contribution/EBIT; combined leverage is their product.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Modigliani-Miller with corporate taxes concludes:
o: Firm value rises with leverage due to the tax shield
questions.e: MM's 1963 tax correction: the interest tax shield makes levered firms more valuable, implying high (though not infinite, given distress costs) optimal debt.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The operating cycle equals:
o: Inventory days + receivable days - payable days
questions.e: The cash-conversion cycle measures days from paying for inputs to collecting from sales. Shorter cycles need less working capital — the target of receivables and inventory management.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: EOQ balances:
questions.e: Economic Order Quantity = sqrt(2AO/C) minimises total inventory cost where ordering and carrying costs cross. ABC analysis then focuses control on high-value items.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: In a direct forex quote:
o: The home currency is the price currency
questions.e: Direct quote: domestic currency per unit of foreign currency (Rs/USD). The foreign currency is the base (fixed at 1 unit); rupees are the variable price currency.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: TT selling rate is used for:
questions.e: TT (telegraphic transfer) buying/selling apply to clean inward/outward remittances; bill buying/selling rates apply to documentary (usance) transactions with an extra margin.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A cross rate is needed to quote:
questions.e: Cross rates derive non-dollar pairs via the dollar: INR/GBP = (INR/USD) x (USD/GBP), using the appropriate bid/offer sides so the bank keeps its spread.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Walter's dividend model recommends retention when:
o: Return on investment exceeds the cost of capital
questions.e: Walter's formula values the firm based on r versus k: if r > k (growth firm), retaining earnings maximises value; if r < k, distribute. Gordon's model similarly links value to dividend growth and required return.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: In the CAPM, beta measures:
questions.e: Beta captures sensitivity to market movements — systematic risk that cannot be diversified away. Expected return = Rf + beta x (Rm - Rf). A beta above 1 means the stock swings more than the market.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Miller-Orr model is used in:
questions.e: Miller-Orr sets upper and lower control limits for cash balances under uncertainty, triggering transfers to/from marketable securities. Baumol's model is the deterministic EOQ-analog for cash.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Factoring without recourse means:
o: The factor bears the default risk
The client bears the default risk
questions.e: Without recourse, the factor cannot claim back from the client if the debtor defaults — the factor absorbs credit risk (for a higher fee). With recourse, the client retains the risk.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Commercial papers' maturity range is:
questions.e: CPs are unsecured money-market instruments of 7 days to one year, issued by highly-rated corporates. NCDs and bonds cover longer tenures in the debt market.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A debenture trustee is appointed to:
questions.e: Debenture trustees (SEBI-regulated) hold the security on behalf of holders, monitor covenants and enforce rights on default. Listed NCD issues mandatorily need one.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Cumulative preference shares:
o: Are always redeemed in one year
Accumulate unpaid dividends for future payment
questions.e: Arrears on cumulative preference shares accumulate and must be cleared before any equity dividend. Non-cumulative preference shares lose the unpaid dividend for that year.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Rights issue is offered to:
o: Existing shareholders in proportion to holdings
questions.e: Rights issues give existing shareholders pre-emptive rights to subscribe proportionally, usually at a discount. Renunciation lets them sell the rights entitlement.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Sweat equity shares are issued to:
o: Employees/directors for value addition at a discount
questions.e: Sweat equity rewards employees/directors for know-how or value addition, issued at a discount or for non-cash consideration under Companies Act conditions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The ex-dividend date means:
o: Dividend is declared on this date
Buyers on/after this date don't get the declared dividend
Dividend is paid on this date
questions.e: Shares trade ex-dividend from the record-date-minus-settlement cycle; only holders before ex-date receive the dividend. The price typically drops by the dividend amount.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bonus shares:
o: Capitalise reserves without raising fresh funds
questions.e: Bonus issues convert reserves into share capital, increasing share count without cash inflow — the share price adjusts proportionally. They signal management confidence.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Stock split differs from bonus issue in that:
o: It reduces face value without touching reserves
questions.e: A split divides each share into smaller face-value shares (e.g., Rs.10 into two Rs.5 shares) with no reserve capitalisation; a bonus issue capitalises reserves keeping face value unchanged.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The accounting treatment of share premium is:
o: Credited to Securities Premium Account, usable only for specified purposes
questions.e: Premium on issue goes to Securities Premium (Section 52, Companies Act 2013), usable for bonus issues, buy-backs, writing off preliminary expenses or issue costs — not for dividends.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Buy-back of shares:
o: Reduces outstanding shares and may raise EPS
questions.e: Buy-backs return surplus cash, cut share count and can lift EPS and ROE. SEBI buy-back regulations govern listed-company offers (tender or open market).

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Operating leverage is high when:
o: Fixed operating costs are a large share of total cost
questions.e: High operating leverage (Contribution/EBIT) magnifies profit swings from sales changes — airlines and telecoms are classic cases. Combined with financial leverage it gives total risk.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Gordon growth model values a share as:
questions.e: Price = next year's dividend /(cost of equity - constant growth rate). It assumes perpetual constant growth below ke — the workhorse of dividend-discount valuation.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Zero-coupon bonds are issued:
o: At a deep discount with no periodic interest
questions.e: Zero-coupon (deep-discount) bonds pay no coupon; return comes from the discount to redemption value. STRIPS separate coupons from G-secs similarly.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Yield to maturity assumes:
o: Coupons are reinvested at the YTM rate
The bond is sold before maturity
questions.e: YTM is the IRR of the bond's cash flows, implicitly assuming coupon reinvestment at YTM — the reinvestment-risk caveat examiners probe.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Modified duration measures:
o: Percentage price change for a 1 per cent yield change
questions.e: Modified duration = Macaulay duration/(1+yield), giving price sensitivity. Higher duration means greater interest-rate risk — key for bond portfolio management.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A callable bond benefits:
o: The issuer, who can redeem early when rates fall
questions.e: Call options let issuers refinance when rates drop, so callable bonds carry higher yields to compensate investors for reinvestment risk. Puttable bonds favour investors.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Credit rating in India is regulated by:
questions.e: SEBI registers and regulates credit rating agencies (CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, etc.). Bank loans above thresholds need external ratings for capital-adequacy risk weights.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: An 'investment-grade' rating generally means:
questions.e: BBB- (S&P/Fitch scale) and above is investment grade; below is speculative/high-yield. Basel risk weights for bank exposures key off these ratings.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Venture capital is:
questions.e: VC funds take equity stakes in startups for high risk-return, exiting via IPO or buyback. SEBI's AIF regulations govern VC/PE funds in India.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Angel investors differ from VCs in:
o: Investing own money at the seed stage
questions.e: Angels invest personal funds in very early rounds; VCs manage pooled funds at later stages. Both take equity and mentorship roles.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The primary market is where:
o: New securities are issued to investors
questions.e: IPOs, FPOs and rights issues raise fresh capital in the primary market; the secondary market (exchanges) provides liquidity to existing holders.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Book building in an IPO:
o: Discovers price through investor bids in a price band
questions.e: Book building collects bids within a price band to discover the cut-off price, replacing fixed-price offers for most large IPOs. Anchor investors get pre-allocation.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: AS-3 (revised) deals with:
questions.e: AS-3 mandates cash-flow statements classified into operating, investing and financing activities. AS-9 covers revenue recognition, AS-19 leases, AS-2 inventories.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under AS-2, inventory is valued at:
o: Lower of cost and net realisable value
questions.e: AS-2's prudence rule values inventory at cost or NRV whichever is lower, using FIFO or weighted-average cost formulas. NRV is estimated selling price less completion/selling costs.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: FIFO in rising prices gives:
o: Higher profit and higher closing stock than weighted average
questions.e: FIFO charges older cheaper costs to production, leaving dearer recent costs in closing stock — inflating profit and inventory in inflation. Weighted average smooths this.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A provision for doubtful debts is:
o: A charge against profit shown as deduction from debtors
questions.e: The provision (a charge, not appropriation) follows prudence and the matching concept, presented netted against sundry debtors. General reserves, by contrast, are appropriations.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Preliminary expenses written off go to:
o: Securities premium or P&L as permitted
questions.e: Company-formation expenses are written off against securities premium or through P&L; they are fictitious assets until fully written off.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Calls in arrears are shown:
questions.e: Unpaid allotment/call money is deducted from called-up capital in the balance sheet; calls in advance appear as a current liability.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Forfeiture of shares is:
o: Cancellation for non-payment of calls, with amount credited to forfeited-shares account
questions.e: On forfeiture, share capital is debited and the forfeited-shares account credited with amounts already received; re-issue at a discount is limited to the forfeited amount.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Debentures issued as collateral security are:
o: Disclosed by note, not as a liability addition
questions.e: Collateral debentures are a contingent arrangement — noted below the balance sheet rather than added to debt, since the primary loan is already recognised.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The debt-service coverage ratio is:
questions.e: DSCR measures ability to service both interest and principal; lenders want 1.25-1.5 times. ISCR covers interest only.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Window dressing in financial statements means:
o: Year-end manipulation to show a better position
questions.e: Window dressing — e.g., postponing purchases to inflate the current ratio — is a key limitation of ratio analysis, alongside price-level and policy differences.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Common-size statements express:
o: Each item as a percentage of a base (sales or total assets)
questions.e: Vertical/common-size analysis standardises P&L items to sales and balance-sheet items to total assets, enabling cross-firm and trend comparison.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Trend analysis uses:
questions.e: Horizontal analysis indexes financial items to a base year (100) to reveal direction and pace of change — the companion to common-size vertical analysis.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Marginal costing treats fixed costs as:
o: Period costs charged to P&L, not to products
questions.e: Marginal (variable) costing charges only variable costs to units; fixed costs hit the period's P&L. Contribution = sales minus variable cost drives break-even and decision analysis.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Break-even point in units is:
o: Fixed costs divided by contribution per unit
questions.e: BEP units = Fixed cost/Contribution per unit; BEP sales = Fixed cost/PV ratio. Margin of safety = actual sales minus BEP sales.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The P/V ratio is:
questions.e: Profit-volume ratio shows contribution per rupee of sales; higher P/V means profits respond sharply to sales changes. BEP sales = fixed cost/PV ratio.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Standard costing compares:
o: Actual costs with pre-set standards to find variances
questions.e: Standard costing sets benchmarks for material, labour and overheads; variances (price, usage, efficiency) pinpoint control failures — the control arm of cost accounting.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A favourable material price variance means:
questions.e: Price variance = (standard price - actual price) x actual quantity; usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price. Favourable variances aid profit.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Budgetary control's first step is:
questions.e: The control cycle: plan (budgets), measure (actuals), compare (variances), correct. Flexible budgets adjust for activity levels, unlike fixed budgets.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Zero-based budgeting:
o: Justifies every expense from scratch each period
Adds inflation to last year's budget
questions.e: ZBB builds budgets from zero, ranking decision packages by priority — rigorous but time-consuming, versus incremental budgeting's last-year-plus approach.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Responsibility accounting assigns costs to:
questions.e: Cost centres control costs, profit centres control costs and revenues, investment centres also control asset investment (judged on ROI/RI) — aligning accountability with authority.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Transfer pricing is the price for:
o: Goods/services between divisions of the same firm
questions.e: Internal transfer prices affect divisional profit measurement; methods include market price, cost-plus and negotiated. Arm's-length rules govern cross-border transfer pricing for tax.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Gordon-Shapiro model assumes:
questions.e: The constant-growth DDM needs g < ke and stable growth — suited to mature dividend payers. Multi-stage models handle high-growth phases before settling to constant growth.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A rights issue's theoretical ex-rights price:
o: Blends the cum-rights price and subscription price
questions.e: TERP = (old shares x market price + new shares x subscription price)/total shares; the value of the right = market price - TERP. It anchors the rights' fair value.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Treasury stock refers to:
o: A company's own shares bought back and held
questions.e: Buy-back shares held in treasury can be reissued later. Indian law generally requires extinguishment of bought-back shares, limiting treasury-stock practice.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which sector contributes the largest share to India's Gross Value Added?
questions.e: The services sector contributes well over half of India's GVA, making it the largest contributor. Agriculture employs the largest share of workers but contributes under 20 per cent of output. This services-led structure is a defining feature of the Indian economy.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The New Industrial Policy that launched economic liberalisation in India was announced on:
questions.e: The New Industrial Policy of 24 July 1991 abolished industrial licensing for most industries and launched Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation. It was the policy response to the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis. The other dates are Independence Day, RBI's commencement and Republic Day.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: GDP at market prices equals:
o: GVA at basic prices minus net product taxes
GNP minus net factor income from abroad
GVA at basic prices plus net product taxes
questions.e: GDP at market prices is obtained by adding net product taxes (taxes less subsidies on products) to GVA at basic prices. GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad. Net national income further deducts depreciation from gross figures.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which price index is targeted by the RBI under the inflation-targeting framework?
questions.e: The RBI Act mandates CPI (Combined) inflation of 4 per cent with a tolerance band of plus/minus 2 per cent. WPI tracks wholesale prices with base 2011-12, while CPI (Combined) has base 2012. The MPC's repo decisions are anchored to the CPI target.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India commenced operations on:
questions.e: The RBI was established under the RBI Act, 1934 and commenced business on 1 April 1935. It was nationalised on 1 January 1949. Its Central Office is located in Mumbai.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee consists of:
o: Six members — three RBI officials and three government nominees
Five members, all from the RBI
Three members chaired by the Finance Minister
questions.e: The MPC has six members: the Governor as chair, the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer nominated by the Board, and three external members appointed by the government. Decisions are by majority with the Governor's casting vote, and at least four meetings are held each year.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: As decided in the August 2026 MPC review, the policy repo rate stood at:
questions.e: In its 3-5 August 2026 review the MPC held the repo rate at 5.25 per cent for the fourth consecutive time with a neutral stance. The SDF was 5.00 per cent and the MSF/Bank Rate 5.50 per cent. The RBI had earlier cut 125 bps cumulatively during 2025.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: In the RBI's interest-rate corridor, the floor is set by:
questions.e: The SDF (5.00 per cent) is the floor of the corridor at which banks park surplus funds overnight without collateral. The MSF (5.50 per cent) is the ceiling. The fixed reverse repo rate of 3.35 per cent is now largely a legacy rate.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Cash Reserve Ratio is currently:
o: 18 per cent of net demand and time liabilities
4 per cent of net demand and time liabilities
questions.e: CRR is 4 per cent of NDTL, maintained as cash balances with the RBI, and earns no interest. SLR is 18 per cent, maintained in approved securities which do earn interest. CRR changes directly affect lendable resources.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Treasury bills are issued in India with maturities of:
questions.e: Government of India T-bills are issued for 91, 182 and 364 days through auction by the RBI. They are zero-coupon money-market instruments. Dated securities have longer maturities starting from one year.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: SEBI was given statutory powers in the year:
questions.e: SEBI was set up in 1988 as a non-statutory body and given statutory powers through the SEBI Act, 1992, in the wake of the 1991 reforms. It regulates the securities market, mutual funds and intermediaries.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NABARD was established in the year:
questions.e: NABARD was set up in 1982 for agriculture and rural development refinance. SIDBI followed in 1990 for MSME, EXIM Bank in 1982 for foreign trade, and NHB in 1988 for housing finance.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: DICGC insures bank deposits up to:
o: Rs.5 lakh per depositor per bank
questions.e: DICGC, a wholly-owned RBI subsidiary, insures principal plus interest up to Rs.5 lakh per depositor per bank, aggregating all deposits held in the same right and capacity. The limit was raised from Rs.1 lakh effective 4 February 2020.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: FEMA replaced FERA in the year:
questions.e: The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 replaced the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, shifting the philosophy from regulation and criminality to management of forex with civil penalties. The rupee operates on a managed float.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The WTO replaced GATT in:
questions.e: The World Trade Organisation came into being on 1 January 1995 replacing GATT, with India as a founder member. The Uruguay Round concluded with the Marrakesh Agreement establishing the WTO.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under the revised MSME definition effective 1 April 2025, a micro enterprise has investment up to:
questions.e: The 2025 revision doubled limits: micro is investment up to Rs.2.5 crore and turnover up to Rs.10 crore; small is Rs.25 crore/Rs.100 crore; medium is Rs.125 crore/Rs.500 crore. Udyam registration is the gateway to MSME benefits.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The eight core industries carry what approximate weight in the IIP?
questions.e: The eight core industries — refinery products, electricity, steel, coal, crude oil, natural gas, cement and fertilisers — carry about 40.27 per cent weight in the Index of Industrial Production (base 2011-12). They are a leading indicator of industrial growth.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: In the Union Budget 2026-27, the fiscal deficit target is:
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 targets a fiscal deficit of 4.3 per cent of GDP, continuing the glide path from 6.4 per cent. Capital expenditure is Rs.12.2 lakh crore (3.1 per cent of GDP) and total expenditure about Rs.53.47 lakh crore.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The FRBM Act was enacted in:
questions.e: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 anchors deficit discipline for the central government. It sets targets for fiscal and revenue deficits and requires medium-term fiscal policy statements.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in:
questions.e: NITI Aayog was constituted on 1 January 2015, replacing the 65-year-old Planning Commission with a cooperative-federalism think tank. The Prime Minister chairs it.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NEFT settlement operates:
o: Only for amounts above Rs.2 lakh
Only on working days 8 am to 7 pm
questions.e: NEFT has operated 24x7 since December 2019, settling in half-hourly batches with no minimum or maximum amount. RTGS, for Rs.2 lakh and above, settles gross in real time and is also 24x7 since December 2020.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The minimum amount for an RTGS transaction is:
questions.e: RTGS is meant for large-value transfers with a minimum of Rs.2 lakh and no upper ceiling. Smaller or time-critical retail transfers use NEFT, IMPS or UPI.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: RBI's final Basel III market-risk directions for commercial banks take effect from:
questions.e: The RBI issued final Basel III market-risk capital directions in September 2026, with the new minimum requirements kicking in from 1 April 2027. They revise how banks compute capital for interest-rate, equity and forex risks in the trading book.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under Basel III as implemented in India, the minimum CRAR is:
questions.e: India prescribes a minimum CRAR of 9 per cent against Basel's 8 per cent, plus a 2.5 per cent capital conservation buffer, taking the effective minimum to 11.5 per cent including CCB. CET1 minimum is 5.5 per cent.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio is currently:
questions.e: SLR is 18 per cent of net demand and time liabilities, to be held in cash, gold or approved securities. Unlike CRR balances, SLR securities earn interest for the bank.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which of the following is a quantitative instrument of monetary policy?
questions.e: Open market operations — RBI purchase/sale of government securities — affect overall liquidity and are quantitative. Moral suasion, selective credit controls and margin requirements are qualitative/selective instruments.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The base year of the current GDP series in India is:
questions.e: The Central Statistics Office's current national-accounts series uses 2011-12 as the base year. The IIP also uses 2011-12, while CPI (Combined) uses 2012 and WPI uses 2011-12.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: GNP differs from GDP by:
questions.e: GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad (income earned by residents abroad minus income earned by non-residents domestically). Net exports are already part of GDP via the expenditure method.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Foreign institutional investors were first allowed into Indian capital markets in:
questions.e: FIIs were permitted to invest in Indian securities from September 1992 as part of capital-account liberalisation. FPI regulations consolidated the FII, sub-account and QFI regimes in 2014.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Narasimham Committee-I (1991) is associated with:
questions.e: The Narasimham Committee on the Financial System (1991) recommended interest-rate deregulation, entry of new private banks, prudential norms and DRTs. The second committee (1998) pushed for stronger banks and asset reconstruction companies.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which institution refinances MSME lending?
questions.e: SIDBI (1990) is the principal refinancer for MSME credit. NABARD serves agriculture and rural sectors, EXIM Bank serves foreign trade, and NHB serves housing finance.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: PMJDY accounts are primarily driven through:
questions.e: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana achieved last-mile coverage largely through the business-correspondent model, taking banking outlets to unbanked villages. BSBD accounts under PMJDY carry no minimum balance.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI's clean note policy relates to:
o: Withdrawal of soiled and mutilated notes from circulation
questions.e: The clean note policy ensures only good-quality currency circulates, with banks required to sort and withdraw soiled notes. The May 2023 withdrawal of Rs.2000 notes was conducted under this currency-management framework.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: India's foreign exchange reserves are custodied by:
questions.e: The RBI is the custodian of India's forex reserves under the RBI Act, managing them for safety, liquidity and returns while intervening in the forex market to curb excessive volatility.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Commercial paper in India has a minimum maturity of:
questions.e: Commercial paper, an unsecured money-market instrument issued by highly-rated corporates, has maturity from 7 days to one year. Certificates of deposit similarly start at 7 days.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: IRDAI was established under the IRDAI Act in:
questions.e: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India was set up under the IRDAI Act, 1999, headquartered in Hyderabad, opening the insurance sector to private and foreign players.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: PFRDA regulates:
o: Pension funds and the National Pension System
questions.e: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (2003, statutory 2013) regulates NPS and pension funds. Mutual funds are under SEBI, insurers under IRDAI.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The UPI system is operated by:
questions.e: The National Payments Corporation of India, an umbrella organisation for retail payments, operates UPI, RuPay, IMPS, NACH and AePS under RBI oversight.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which of the following deposits is repatriable in full?
questions.e: NRE deposits (principal and interest) are freely repatriable. NRO repatriation is capped at USD 1 million per financial year. FCNR(B) is also repatriable, being a foreign-currency deposit free of exchange risk for the depositor.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Interest on NRE deposits in India is:
o: Taxed as per slab with TDS
questions.e: Interest earned on NRE and FCNR(B) deposits is exempt from Indian income tax, while NRO interest is taxable. This exemption is a key attraction of NRE deposits.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Budget 2026-27 capex of Rs.12.2 lakh crore equals what share of GDP?
questions.e: The Rs.12.2 lakh crore capital expenditure is 3.1 per cent of GDP, the highest capex-to-GDP ratio. The fiscal deficit target of 4.3 per cent is separate — it is total borrowings over GDP.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Debt-to-GDP in Budget 2026-27 is estimated at 55.6 per cent, targeted to fall to 50 per cent by:
questions.e: The budget statement anchors the debt-to-GDP glide path: 55.6 per cent in FY27 declining to about 50 per cent by FY31, replacing the earlier pure deficit-number targeting with a debt anchor.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which committee recommended the inflation-targeting framework adopted in 2016?
questions.e: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended the 4 per cent CPI target with a plus/minus 2 per cent band, leading to the 2016 RBI Act amendments and the MPC. Narasimham covered banking reforms, Kelkar tax reforms.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bank Rate and MSF rate as of September 2026 are:
questions.e: Both Bank Rate and MSF stand at 5.50 per cent — 25 bps above the 5.25 per cent repo rate, forming the corridor ceiling. SDF at 5.00 per cent is the floor.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the RBI?
o: Accepting deposits from the general public
Acting as banker to the government
questions.e: The RBI does not do retail banking for the public; it banks the government and the banks. Currency issue, banker-to-government and bank regulation under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 are core RBI functions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI transfers its annual surplus to:
questions.e: Under Section 47 of the RBI Act, the central bank's surplus (after provisions) is transferred to the Government of India as dividend. The Bimal Jalan committee framework guides the economic-capital provisioning behind this transfer.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Scale-based regulation for NBFCs places the largest NBFCs in:
o: The Top Layer only by exception
questions.e: Scale-based regulation (2021) has four layers: Base, Middle, Upper and Top. NBFC-Upper Layer faces bank-like prudential norms; the RBI publishes the UL list annually.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The withdrawal of Rs.2000 banknotes was announced in:
questions.e: The RBI announced withdrawal of Rs.2000 notes on 19 May 2023 under the clean note policy; they remained legal tender during the exchange/deposit window. November 2016 was the demonetisation of Rs.500/1000 notes.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Certificates of Deposit are issued by:
o: Scheduled commercial banks and select financial institutions
questions.e: CDs are negotiable money-market instruments issued by scheduled commercial banks (excluding RRBs and LABs) and select all-India financial institutions, with maturity from 7 days to one year.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Economic Survey of India is published by:
questions.e: The Finance Ministry's Department of Economic Affairs tables the Economic Survey before the Budget, reviewing the year's developments — authored by the Chief Economic Adviser. It is distinct from the RBI's Annual Report.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'stagflation'?
o: High inflation with stagnant growth and unemployment
questions.e: Stagflation combines stagnant output, high unemployment and high inflation — a painful mix because rate cuts worsen inflation while rate hikes worsen growth. The 1970s oil shocks are the classic example. It challenges the simple Phillips-curve trade-off.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Phillips curve shows the relationship between:
questions.e: The Phillips curve posits an inverse short-run relationship between inflation and unemployment. Policymakers face a trade-off: pushing unemployment below its natural rate tends to raise inflation.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Revenue deficit is defined as:
questions.e: Revenue deficit captures the government borrowing to fund day-to-day consumption spending. Fiscal deficit minus interest payments gives the primary deficit. A zero revenue deficit means borrowings fund only capital formation.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Primary deficit equals:
questions.e: Primary deficit measures current-year borrowing excluding the burden of past debt servicing. It shows whether today's policies, ignoring inherited interest, are in deficit.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which tax is the largest source of the Centre's gross tax revenue in recent years?
questions.e: GST (CGST plus the Centre's share of IGST) has become the largest revenue source, ahead of corporation tax and income tax. Wealth tax was abolished in 2015.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The GST Council is chaired by:
questions.e: Article 279A creates the GST Council chaired by the Union Finance Minister with state finance ministers as members. Decisions need a three-fourths majority with the Centre holding one-third weight.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Disguised unemployment is most commonly found in:
questions.e: Disguised unemployment — more workers than needed, with near-zero marginal productivity — characterises family-labour Indian agriculture. Removing some workers would not reduce output, distinguishing it from open unemployment.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Human Development Index is published by:
questions.e: UNDP's Human Development Report publishes HDI combining life expectancy, education and per-capita income indices. It contrasts with pure GDP rankings by capturing wellbeing.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: India's demographic dividend refers to:
o: A rising share of working-age population relative to dependents
questions.e: The dividend is the growth boost from a bulge in the 15-64 age group with fewer dependents — but it pays off only with education, skills and jobs. The window is estimated to last till around 2055.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.e: Direct taxes (income tax, corporation tax) are levied on persons and cannot be shifted. GST, customs and excise are indirect taxes shifted to consumers. Direct taxes are progressive; indirect taxes tend to be regressive.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The 'twin balance sheet' problem referred to:
o: Stressed corporate balance sheets and stressed bank balance sheets
questions.e: The Economic Survey 2015-16 flagged over-leveraged corporates unable to invest alongside banks weighed down by NPAs — each worsening the other. The IBC and bank recapitalisation were the policy responses.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: India's current account in the balance of payments records:
o: Trade in goods and services plus transfers and income
questions.e: The current account covers goods, services, primary income and secondary income (remittances). Capital flows sit in the capital account. A deficit means the country spends more abroad than it earns.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A managed float exchange-rate system means:
o: The rate is pegged to the dollar
The RBI fixes the rate daily
The market sets the rate; the RBI intervenes only against volatility
questions.e: India follows a managed float: the rupee's level is market-determined, but the RBI buys/sells dollars to curb excessive volatility and disorderly moves, without targeting any level.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: FDI differs from FPI primarily in:
o: Lasting interest and management control versus passive investment
questions.e: FDI (10 per cent or more stake) implies lasting interest and often control; FPI is passive portfolio investment that can exit quickly. Hence FDI is 'sticky' while FPI flows are volatile — the 'hot money' distinction.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The base year for WPI in India is:
questions.e: WPI uses 2011-12 as base, while CPI (Combined) uses 2012. WPI covers only goods (no services), with manufactured products carrying the largest weight.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which measure of money supply is the broadest?
questions.e: M1 (currency plus demand deposits) is narrowest; M3 (M1 plus time deposits) is broad money; M4 adds post-office deposits to M3, making it broadest. RBI policy analysis focuses on M3.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Open market purchases of securities by the RBI:
questions.e: When the RBI buys government securities it pays banks, injecting durable liquidity. Sales absorb liquidity. OMOs are the main quantitative tool alongside LAF operations.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A cut in the CRR by the RBI:
questions.e: Lower CRR frees cash balances held with the RBI for lending, expanding money supply through the multiplier. A 1 per cent CRR cut releases roughly Rs.1.7 lakh crore at current NDTL levels.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The term 'sterilisation' in monetary policy means:
o: Offsetting forex intervention's liquidity impact via OMOs
questions.e: When the RBI buys dollars it injects rupees; sterilisation sells government securities to absorb that liquidity, keeping money supply on target. MSS bonds were earlier used for this purpose.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which market deals in unsecured overnight lending between banks?
questions.e: The call/notice money market is where banks borrow/lend overnight unsecured to square positions. The weighted average call rate is the operating target of monetary policy.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Treasury bills are:
o: Zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount
questions.e: T-bills are issued at a discount to face value and redeemed at par; the discount is the implicit interest. They carry no coupon, making them pure discount instruments.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The yield on a bond and its price move:
questions.e: This inverse relationship is the core of fixed-income maths: when market yields rise, existing bonds' prices fall to offer the higher yield, and vice versa. Duration measures the sensitivity.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Sovereign Green Bonds in India are issued:
o: By the Government of India as part of dated securities
By the RBI on its own account
questions.e: The government issues Sovereign Green Bonds within its dated-securities calendar (the H2 FY27 calendar includes 30-year SGrBs) to fund green infrastructure, with RBI conducting the auctions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The 10-year government bond yield is important because:
o: It benchmarks long-term borrowing costs across the economy
questions.e: The 10-year G-sec yield is the risk-free benchmark; corporate bond spreads, bank MCLR/base rates and mortgage pricing key off it. It reflects growth and inflation expectations.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which body regulates commodity derivatives markets in India?
questions.e: SEBI absorbed the Forward Markets Commission in 2015 and now regulates commodity derivatives alongside securities. The RBI regulates money and forex markets.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The National Stock Exchange commenced equity trading in:
questions.e: NSE started equity trading in November 1994 as India's first demutualised electronic exchange, ending BSE's open-outcry dominance. BSE itself dates to 1875.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Demat accounts in India are maintained by:
questions.e: NSDL and CDSL are the two depositories holding securities in electronic form; brokers and DPs are intermediaries. Dematerialisation became near-universal after the 2019 mandate.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A 'bull' market refers to:
questions.e: Bull markets show sustained price rises and confidence; bear markets show declines and pessimism. The terms come from how the animals attack — upwards and downwards.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Sensex comprises:
questions.e: The S&P BSE Sensex tracks 30 large, liquid BSE stocks; Nifty 50 tracks 50 NSE stocks. Both are free-float market-cap weighted indices.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which of the following is a development financial institution?
questions.e: DFIs like NABARD, SIDBI, EXIM Bank and NHB provide long-term refinance and development finance, unlike commercial banks which take deposits and lend across tenures.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Priority sector lending target for domestic scheduled commercial banks is:
questions.e: Domestic SCBs must direct 40 per cent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit to priority sectors, with sub-targets: 18 per cent agriculture (10 per cent to small/marginal farmers), 7.5 per cent micro enterprises, 12 per cent weaker sections.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: PSL shortfalls are parked by banks in:
o: RIDF with NABARD and similar funds
questions.e: Shortfalls go to the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (NABARD), or funds with SIDBI/NHB/MUDRA, earning below-market returns — the penalty that makes PSLCs attractive.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Priority Sector Lending Certificates allow:
o: Trading of PSL achievement without fresh lending
questions.e: PSLCs let surplus banks sell PSL credit to deficit banks in four categories (agriculture, small/marginal farmers, micro enterprises, general). They separate target compliance from actual lending.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The MUDRA scheme's 'Shishu' category covers loans up to:
questions.e: PMMY categories: Shishu up to Rs.50,000, Kishore Rs.50,001-5 lakh, Tarun Rs.5-10 lakh. Loans are collateral-free, refinanced by MUDRA Ltd.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: CGTMSE provides:
o: Credit guarantee for collateral-free MSE loans
questions.e: The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises covers collateral-free credit up to Rs.5 crore, with guarantee cover typically 75-85 per cent, encouraging banks to lend without collateral.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 provides resolution within:
questions.e: IBC mandates time-bound resolution — 330 days including legal proceedings — through the NCLT, with the Committee of Creditors approving plans by 66 per cent voting share.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme was launched in:
questions.e: The 2021 scheme integrated the banking, NBFC and digital-transactions ombudsman schemes into one, with a centralised receipt and processing centre and 'one nation, one ombudsman' coverage.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under the SARFAESI Act, banks can enforce security without court intervention for dues of:
questions.e: SARFAESI applies to secured debts of Rs.1 lakh and above where the account is NPA, after a 60-day demand notice under Section 13(2). Agricultural land is excluded from its ambit.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Debt Recovery Tribunals handle bank claims of:
questions.e: DRT jurisdiction under the RDDBFI Act, 1993 covers claims of Rs.20 lakh and above (raised from Rs.10 lakh in 2018); smaller claims go to civil courts or Lok Adalats.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: An asset is classified NPA when dues remain overdue for:
questions.e: The 90-day delinquency norm (interest/instalment overdue beyond 90 days, or CC/OD 'out of order') triggers NPA classification. SMA-0/1/2 buckets track 1-30, 31-60 and 61-90 day stress before that.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Sub-standard assets attract provisioning of:
o: 15 per cent on secured portion, 25 per cent on unsecured
questions.e: Sub-standard (NPA up to 12 months) needs 15 per cent on the secured portion and 25 per cent on the unsecured portion. Doubtful assets need 25-100 per cent by age; loss assets 100 per cent.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The 7 June 2019 RBI circular on stressed assets is known for:
o: The revised framework for resolution of stressed assets
questions.e: The 7 June 2019 circular replaced the earlier S4A/SDR schemes with a principles-based resolution framework: review within 30 days of default for Rs.100 crore-plus exposures and inter-creditor agreements.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Wilful defaulters are defined by:
o: Capacity to pay but diversion or siphoning of funds
questions.e: Wilful default covers deliberate non-payment despite capacity, diversion or siphoning of funds, or disposal of security without the lender's knowledge. Consequences include debarment from fresh finance.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The LAF corridor's width between SDF and MSF is:
questions.e: With SDF at 5.00 per cent and MSF at 5.50 per cent, the corridor is 50 bps wide around the 5.25 per cent repo rate. A narrow corridor reduces overnight rate volatility.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which of the following earns no interest for banks?
questions.e: CRR balances earn zero interest — the implicit tax on banks. SDF placements earn the SDF rate; SLR securities earn market coupons; MSF is a borrowing window at the MSF rate.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Reporting entities must file Cash Transaction Reports (CTRs) with FIU-IND for cash transactions above:
questions.e: CTRs cover all cash transactions above Rs.10 lakh (single or integrally connected) in a month; STRs have no threshold.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: PMLA was enacted in:
questions.e: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 criminalises laundering and provides for attachment of proceeds of crime. Banks' KYC/AML obligations flow from it and the RBI's KYC Directions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: CKYC assigns each customer:
questions.e: The Central KYC Records Registry issues a 14-digit CKYC number, letting customers reuse KYC across institutions. Reporting entities must upload KYC records to CERSAI's CKYCR.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Periodic KYC updation for high-risk customers is required at least once every:
questions.e: The risk-based cycle is 2 years for high-risk, 8 years for medium-risk and 10 years for low-risk customers. Simplified due diligence applies to small and BSBD accounts.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Lead Bank Scheme is implemented at the:
questions.e: Under the Lead Bank Scheme (1969), a designated bank leads credit planning for each district via the District Consultative Committee and the Annual Credit Plan — the original financial-inclusion architecture.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The fundamental banker-customer relationship on a deposit is:
questions.e: Money deposited becomes the bank's, and the bank owes a debt to the customer — hence deposits are liabilities in bank books. Trustee/beneficiary applies to safe custody, agent/principal to collections, bailee/bailor to pledged goods.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The banker's general lien is provided under:
o: Section 171 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872
questions.e: Section 171 gives bankers a general lien over securities deposited in the ordinary course of business for the general balance due. It does not extend to safe-custody articles or valuables left for a special purpose.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Clayton's rule applies to:
o: Appropriation of payments in a running account
questions.e: In the absence of express instructions, credits in a running account extinguish debits in chronological order — first-in, first-out. Borrowers can override it with specific appropriation instructions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A garnishee order is issued under:
o: Order 21 Rule 46 of the Civil Procedure Code
questions.e: A garnishee order attaches debts owed by a third party (the bank) to the judgment debtor. On receipt, the bank must freeze the credit balance and await court directions on payment.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under Section 4 of the NI Act, a promissory note is:
o: A written promise to pay a certain sum
An order to pay a third party
questions.e: Section 4 defines a promissory note as an unconditional written promise by the maker to pay. A bill of exchange (Section 5) is an order by the drawer; a cheque (Section 6) is a bill drawn on a banker payable on demand.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A cheque is defined under which section of the NI Act?
questions.e: Section 6 defines a cheque as a bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker, payable on demand. Section 13 defines 'negotiable instrument' generally, covering notes, bills and cheques.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Sections 123 to 131 of the NI Act deal with:
questions.e: Sections 123 (general crossing), 124 (special crossing), 126-131 cover crossing and the protection to paying and collecting bankers. Dishonour is Chapter XVII (Sections 138-142); noting and protest are Sections 99-104A.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: 'Not negotiable' crossing means:
o: The transferee cannot get a better title than the transferor
Only the payee can encash it over the counter
The cheque cannot be transferred at all
It is valid only for six months
questions.e: 'Not negotiable' under Section 130 does not block transfer but kills the holder-in-due-course protection — a thief or wrongful holder cannot pass good title. Transferability remains; negotiability is curtailed.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Payment in due course is defined under:
questions.e: Section 10 defines payment in due course — in good faith, without negligence, to the person in possession — which discharges the payer. Section 85 protects payment of crossed cheques; Section 131 protects collecting bankers.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under Section 138 NI Act, on dishonour the payee must first:
o: Demand payment in writing within 30 days of dishonour
File a civil suit within 7 days
questions.e: The 138 process: written demand within 30 days of receiving the return memo, 15 days for the drawer to pay, and complaint within one month after that. Skipping the demand notice invalidates prosecution.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Maximum punishment under Section 138 NI Act is:
o: Two years' imprisonment or fine up to twice the cheque amount
questions.e: Section 138 provides imprisonment up to two years or fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both. The 2018 amendment added interim compensation up to 20 per cent of the cheque amount during trial.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: An endorsement 'Pay to X only' is:
questions.e: Restrictive endorsement limits further negotiation ('pay to X only' / 'for collection'). Blank endorsement is a mere signature making it bearer; special endorsement names the endorsee; conditional endorsement makes payment depend on an event.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A holder in due course must have obtained the instrument:
o: Free of cost as a gift
With knowledge of a defect in title
For consideration, in good faith, before maturity, without notice of defect
questions.e: Section 9's holder in due course takes for value, in good faith, before maturity and without notice of title defects — and gets a title free from prior defects. Gifts and post-maturity takers don't qualify.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Positive Pay System applies to cheques of:
questions.e: RBI's Positive Pay requires key cheque details to be reconfirmed for cheques of Rs.50,000 and above (mandatory at Rs.5 lakh-plus at most banks), adding an authentication layer against cheque fraud.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: CTS-2010 refers to:
o: Cheque Truncation System with standardised cheque features
questions.e: CTS-2010 standardised cheque security features and enabled image-based clearing, ending physical movement of cheques. Non-CTS cheques were phased out of clearing.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: CASA ratio is computed as:
o: CASA deposits divided by total deposits
Term deposits divided by total deposits
Net profit divided by total deposits
Current deposits divided by savings deposits
questions.e: A high CASA ratio means cheaper funding since current accounts pay nil and savings pay regulated low interest. It is a key profitability and franchise-strength metric for banks.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bulk deposits are currently defined as single term deposits of:
questions.e: The bulk-deposit threshold was raised to Rs.3 crore (from Rs.2 crore) for scheduled commercial banks, excluding RRBs. Bulk deposits carry distinct rate and premature-withdrawal terms.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Differential interest rates on savings deposits were permitted from:
questions.e: The RBI deregulated savings-bank interest in October 2011, letting banks offer tiered rates on slabs. Earlier all banks paid the regulated 4 per cent.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: FCNR(B) deposits are denominated in:
questions.e: FCNR(B) accounts are maintained in designated foreign currencies (USD, GBP, EUR, JPY, etc.), so the depositor bears no rupee exchange risk. NRE/NRO are rupee-denominated.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: External benchmarking for floating-rate retail loans was mandated from:
questions.e: Since 1 October 2019, floating-rate personal/retail and MSME loans must link to an external benchmark (usually repo), replacing the opaque base-rate/MCLR regime for these segments and improving transmission.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A letter of credit is governed internationally by:
questions.e: The Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600), issued by the International Chamber of Commerce, governs LCs worldwide. Banks deal in documents, not goods — the autonomy principle.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A bank guarantee is a contract of guarantee under:
o: Sections 126-147 of the Indian Contract Act
questions.e: Guarantees — including performance and financial guarantees — are governed by Sections 126-147. A continuing guarantee (Section 129) can be revoked by notice as to future transactions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under a cash-credit facility, drawing power is based on:
o: Paid stock less margin, per stock statements
questions.e: Drawing power is computed from hypothecated stock (paid stock = stock minus unpaid creditors) less the stipulated margin, verified via monthly stock statements and periodic stock audit.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Hypothecation differs from pledge in that:
o: It applies only to immovable property
questions.e: In hypothecation the borrower retains possession of the movable security (e.g., inventory) while the bank holds a charge; in pledge, possession passes to the bank. Mortgages cover immovable property.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: An equitable mortgage is created by:
o: Deposit of title deeds in a notified town
questions.e: Equitable mortgage by deposit of title deeds needs no registration or stamp-heavy instrument, but the deposit must occur in a town notified under Section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act. Registered mortgages use a registered deed.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Limitation period for a loan document under the Limitation Act, 1963 is generally:
questions.e: Suits on loan documents generally face a three-year limitation, extendable by acknowledgement of debt in writing under Section 18 or part-payment under Section 19. Mortgage suits get twelve years.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Priority-sector sub-target for agriculture is:
questions.e: Within the 40 per cent PSL target: 18 per cent agriculture (including 10 per cent to small and marginal farmers), 7.5 per cent micro enterprises, 12 per cent weaker sections.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Weaker-sections PSL sub-target is:
questions.e: 12 per cent of ANBC must go to weaker sections (small/marginal farmers, artisans, SC/ST, SHGs, distressed borrowers etc.). The micro-enterprise sub-target is 7.5 per cent.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Udyam registration is:
o: The government portal for MSME registration
questions.e: Udyam (udyamregistration.gov.in) is the official MSME registration portal; the Udyam number with PAN/GST linkage is the gateway to priority-sector classification and subsidies.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Stand-Up India finances:
o: SC/ST and women entrepreneurs for greenfield enterprises
questions.e: Stand-Up India provides bank loans of Rs.10 lakh to Rs.1 crore to at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower per bank branch for greenfield ventures, with RuPay debit card and credit-history support.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Tandon Committee is associated with:
questions.e: The Tandon Committee (1974) framed working-capital lending norms — inventory/receivable holding levels and the MPBF method. The Chore Committee (1979) and Nayak Committee (for SSI) refined them.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Maximum Permissible Bank Finance under Method II of Tandon norms requires borrowers to bring:
o: 25 per cent of working-capital gap as margin
questions.e: Tandon Method II: 75 per cent of (current assets minus core current assets) as MPBF, with the borrower funding 25 per cent of the working-capital gap — enforcing borrower stake and current-ratio discipline.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A 'small account' under KYC norms can be opened with:
questions.e: Small accounts (per PML Rules) use simplified KYC with caps — aggregate credits Rs.1 lakh/year, balance Rs.50,000, withdrawals Rs.10,000/month — and must be upgraded with full KYC within 12 months (extendable).

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: BSBD accounts must have:
o: Cheque-book charges waived only for staff
questions.e: Basic Savings Bank Deposit Accounts — the no-frills vehicle including PMJDY accounts — carry no minimum balance, with a free RuPay debit card and limited free transactions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Cash Transaction Reports under PMLA are filed for:
o: Cash transactions of Rs.10 lakh and above in a month
questions.e: Banks report monthly cash transactions aggregating Rs.10 lakh-plus per customer to FIU-IND, plus all suspicious transactions (no threshold) and counterfeit currency reports.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Banking Ombudsman scheme is now part of:
questions.e: The 2021 integrated scheme subsumed the banking, NBFC and digital-payment ombudsman schemes with centralised receipt — 'one nation, one ombudsman' — covering deficiency in service.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The duty of secrecy of a banker has exceptions including:
questions.e: The Tournier principles recognise exceptions: compulsion of law (court orders, IT notices), public duty (fraud, treason), the bank's own interest (suing the customer), and express/implied customer consent.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Nomination facility for bank deposits is under:
o: Sections 45ZA-45ZF of the Banking Regulation Act
questions.e: Sections 45ZA-45ZF provide nomination for deposits, lockers and safe custody. The nominee receives as trustee for legal heirs — a classic exam trap distinguishing nominee from owner.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Deposit insurance premium is paid by:
o: Banks, and cannot be passed on to depositors
questions.e: Insured banks pay advance premium semi-annually (currently 12 paise per Rs.100 of assessable deposits, cap 15 paise) and are barred from passing it to depositors.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which deposits are NOT covered by DICGC?
questions.e: DICGC excludes deposits of foreign/central/state governments, inter-bank deposits, deposits outside India, and specifically exempted amounts. All individual savings, FD and RD deposits are covered.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A 'dormant' or inoperative account is one with no customer-induced transactions for:
questions.e: Accounts with no customer-induced debit/credit for two years are classified inoperative; banks must notify holders and re-activate only after due diligence. Unclaimed deposits over 10 years go to the RBI's DEA Fund.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Depositor Education and Awareness Fund receives:
questions.e: Balances unclaimed for 10 years or more are transferred to the DEA Fund maintained by the RBI; depositors can still reclaim from banks with interest.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Interest on savings deposits is credited:
o: Quarterly or as decided by the bank within RBI directions
questions.e: Banks compute savings interest on daily balances and credit it quarterly (or shorter intervals), per RBI directions. Deregulation lets banks set their own savings rates.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Premature withdrawal of term deposits:
o: May attract a penal interest as per the bank's policy disclosed upfront
questions.e: Banks may levy a penalty (typically 0.5-1 per cent) on premature closure per their board-approved policy disclosed at booking. Bulk deposits have stricter premature-withdrawal conditions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NRO deposits are taxable because:
o: They represent income of a resident for tax purposes in India
questions.e: NRO interest is taxable in India (with TDS, DTAA relief possible) since it is Indian-source income of a person resident here for account purposes, unlike exempt NRE/FCNR(B) interest.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: RFC accounts can be maintained by:
questions.e: Returning NRIs may park foreign-exchange earnings in Resident Foreign Currency accounts, preserving currency choice. Ordinary residents cannot open RFC accounts.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under simplified KYC, a 'small account' caps aggregate credits at:
questions.e: Small accounts opened with simplified KYC carry caps: aggregate credits Rs.1 lakh per year, maximum balance Rs.50,000, and withdrawals/transfers Rs.10,000 per month. Full KYC must be completed within 12 months (extendable). These caps make small accounts a favourite numerical MCQ.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Money laundering's three stages are:
questions.e: Placement introduces illicit cash into the system, layering obscures its trail through complex transactions, and integration returns it as apparently legitimate wealth. Smurfing is a placement technique using small deposits.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A demand draft is:
o: A cheque drawn by a customer
A negotiable instrument drawn by a bank on its branch
questions.e: A DD is a banker's order on its own branch/office to pay a sum on demand — effectively a bank-guaranteed instrument, hence preferred for fee payments. Validity is three months like cheques.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Cheques are valid for:
o: Six months from the date of issue
Three months from the date of issue
questions.e: Since April 2012, cheques, DDs and pay orders are valid for three months from the date of instrument (not from printing). Post-dated cheques become payable on the date written.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: SARFAESI Section 13(2) requires:
questions.e: The secured creditor must issue a 60-day demand notice under Section 13(2); only on non-compliance can it take measures under Section 13(4) — possession, sale, lease or management takeover. Borrowers can object under 13(3A).

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which asset is excluded from SARFAESI enforcement?
questions.e: Section 31 excludes agricultural land from SARFAESI. Residential, industrial and vehicle securities are covered, provided the debt is Rs.1 lakh-plus and the account is NPA.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Appeals against DRT orders lie to:
questions.e: The Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal hears appeals from DRTs, with further appeal to the High Court. SARFAESI actions are appealed to the DRT under Section 17 within 45 days.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Lok Adalats handle bank NPAs up to:
questions.e: Lok Adalats under the Legal Services Authorities Act settle compromise cases including NPAs up to Rs.20 lakh. Their awards are deemed civil-court decrees and are non-appealable.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: IBC's Committee of Creditors approves resolution plans by:
questions.e: CoC decisions need 66 per cent voting share (90 per cent for certain actions like liquidation). Financial creditors vote in proportion to their admitted claims.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Priority of government dues versus secured creditors under IBC was settled in favour of:
o: Secured financial creditors under Section 53 waterfall
questions.e: The Section 53 waterfall ranks secured financial creditors above government dues, upheld in Essar Steel. Workmen and employee dues for 24 months rank alongside dissenting secured creditors.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Provision Coverage Ratio is:
o: Provisions held as a percentage of gross NPAs
questions.e: PCR indicates cushioning against bad loans; RBI expects above 70 per cent including technical write-offs. Higher PCR means the balance sheet recognises stress upfront.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Technical write-off of an NPA means:
o: Removing it from the balance sheet while recovery continues
questions.e: Technical/prudential write-offs clean the balance sheet for fully-provided accounts but the bank's claim and recovery efforts continue — unlike a waiver, which extinguishes the debt.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: ARCs buy NPAs under:
questions.e: Asset Reconstruction Companies, registered with the RBI under SARFAESI, buy stressed assets issuing Security Receipts (typically 15:85 cash:SR). The 2021 NARCL is the public-sector bad bank.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NARCL is popularly known as:
questions.e: National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd aggregates large stressed assets (Rs.500 crore-plus exposures) from banks for resolution, with government-guaranteed security receipts backing the transfers.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Credit information companies in India are licensed by:
