questions.e: CICs (CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, CRIF High Mark) are licensed under the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005 by the RBI. Banks must report borrower data to all four.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A CIBIL score ranges from:
questions.e: Scores run 300-900; 750-plus is considered good for retail credit. The score blends payment history, utilisation, vintage and credit mix.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Tandon Committee prescribed inventory holding norms for:
questions.e: Tandon (1974) set maximum holding levels for raw materials, work-in-progress, finished goods and receivables by industry, plus the MPBF lending methods — the grammar of working-capital finance.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Core current assets in MPBF refer to:
o: The minimum current assets a firm must hold from long-term sources
questions.e: Core current assets are the permanent minimum locked in the operating cycle, to be funded from long-term sources — which is why Method II deducts them before computing MPBF.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bills discounting is:
o: A fund-based advance against usance bills
questions.e: Purchasing/discounting bills gives immediate funds to the holder against the acceptor's future payment — self-liquidating fund-based credit. LCs and guarantees are non-fund-based.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Deferred Payment Guarantees support:
o: Purchase of capital goods on deferred terms
questions.e: DPGs back instalment payments for machinery/capital goods bought on deferred credit, typically for industrial projects. They are non-fund-based until invoked.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Packing credit is:
o: Pre-shipment export finance in rupees or foreign currency
questions.e: Packing credit (pre-shipment) funds exporters against confirmed orders/LCs, available as rupee or PCFC (foreign currency) credit. Post-shipment finance covers the period after shipment till realisation.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The ECGC provides:
o: Export credit insurance to banks and exporters
questions.e: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation covers commercial and political risks on export credit, letting banks lend to exporters confidently. It is now ECGC Ltd, wholly government-owned.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: FEDAI is:
o: The association setting forex-market rules and benchmarks
questions.e: The Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India sets market conventions, benchmarks and codes for authorised dealers. FEMA (1999) is the governing statute; FEDAI provides the operating rulebook.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: An authorised dealer under FEMA is:
o: Licensed by the RBI to deal in foreign exchange
questions.e: Authorised Dealers (Category I/II/III) are licensed by the RBI under FEMA to handle forex transactions. Full-fledged money changers handle only specified non-trade transactions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Direct quote convention in India is:
o: Rupees per unit of foreign currency
questions.e: India quotes direct: e.g., Rs.95.89 per USD. TT buying/selling, bills buying/selling rates follow this convention; cross rates derive third-currency rates via the dollar.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: In forex dealing, the bank's buying rate is:
questions.e: The bid-ask spread is the dealer's margin: banks buy foreign currency cheaper (bid) and sell dearer (offer). TT rates apply to clean remittances; bill rates to documentary transactions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A forward premium means:
o: The spot rate is above forward
The forward rate is above the spot rate
questions.e: Forward premium/discount reflects the interest-rate differential between currencies (covered interest parity). Annualised premium = (forward - spot)/spot x (12/n) x 100.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NEFT operates on:
questions.e: NEFT nets transactions and settles in half-hourly batches (deferred net settlement), unlike RTGS which settles each transaction gross in real time.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: IMPS differs from NEFT mainly in:
questions.e: Immediate Payment Service settles instantly 24x7 through mobile/internet, while NEFT settles in batches. UPI rides on IMPS rails for person-to-person payments.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The maximum per-transaction limit typically associated with UPI P2P is:
questions.e: Standard UPI P2P cap is Rs.1 lakh per transaction (Rs.5 lakh for verified merchant categories like capital markets, insurance, and IPO applications as enabled). Banks may set lower internal caps.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: AePS enables:
questions.e: Aadhaar-enabled Payment System lets customers transact at BC outlets using Aadhaar plus biometric authentication — the backbone of last-mile financial inclusion.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act was enacted in:
questions.e: The DPDP Act, 2023 governs processing of digital personal data with consent, purpose limitation and breach-notification duties — directly relevant to banks' customer-data handling.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: RBI's outsourcing guidelines place ultimate responsibility for outsourced activities on:
questions.e: Outsourcing never outsources responsibility: the bank/NBFC board remains accountable, must do due-diligence, monitor vendors and ensure data localisation for payment data.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Two-factor authentication for card-not-present transactions in India uses:
o: OTP/3D Secure as the additional factor
questions.e: RBI mandates an additional factor (usually OTP) for domestic card-not-present transactions. Recurring e-mandates need additional-factor validation above Rs.15,000.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The fraud-reporting framework for banks uses:
o: FMR formats on the RBI portal within timelines
questions.e: Banks report frauds via Fraud Monitoring Returns on RBI's portal — FMR-1 within 21 days of detection for large frauds — with 100 per cent provisioning over four quarters.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Core Banking Solution means:
o: All branches on a single centralised database
questions.e: CBS networks branches into one database, enabling 'anywhere banking', centralised MIS and straight-through processing. It preceded the digital-payments revolution.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The 'banker to banks' function includes:
questions.e: As banker to banks, RBI holds banks' CRR balances, provides LAF/MSF liquidity and refinance, and supervises them — it does not compete for retail business.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: SLR securities are:
o: Approved securities including G-secs, T-bills and SDLs
questions.e: SLR can be held as cash, gold or unencumbered approved securities — dated G-secs, T-bills, state development loans and other RBI-notified instruments.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NDTL for CRR/SLR purposes excludes:
o: Inter-bank borrowings and specific exempt liabilities
questions.e: Net demand and time liabilities net out inter-bank liabilities and prescribed exemptions. Accurate NDTL computation (as per the fortnightly return) is the base for both ratios.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI's data-localisation directive requires:
o: Payment-system data to be stored only in India
questions.e: Since October 2018, all payment-system data must be stored in India (with a copy abroad permitted for cross-border processing). It covers card, UPI and PPI data.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Small finance banks must extend:
o: 75 per cent of ANBC to priority sectors
questions.e: SFBs carry a higher 75 per cent PSL target (versus 40 per cent for universal banks), reflecting their inclusion mandate. Payments banks cannot lend at all.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Payments banks cannot:
o: Accept deposits up to Rs.2 lakh
questions.e: Payments banks take deposits (Rs.2 lakh cap per customer) and offer payments/remittances but cannot lend or issue credit cards — a narrow-bank model.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The differentiated-licensing framework created:
o: Small finance banks and payments banks
questions.e: On-tap differentiated licences (2015-16) created SFBs and payments banks for inclusion. Universal-bank licensing also continues on-tap under RBI guidelines.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Priority-sector housing-loan caps in metros are:
o: Rs.35 lakh loan with Rs.45 lakh dwelling cost
questions.e: PSL housing caps: Rs.35 lakh loan (Rs.45 lakh cost) in metros; Rs.25 lakh loan (Rs.30 lakh cost) elsewhere. Loans within these count toward the housing PSL sub-category.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Education-loan collateral under the IBA model scheme: none up to:
questions.e: IBA model: no collateral up to Rs.4 lakh; third-party guarantee for Rs.4-7.5 lakh; tangible collateral above Rs.7.5 lakh. PM Vidyalaxmi extends collateral-free guarantee-backed loans up to Rs.7.5 lakh for meritorious students.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Moratorium on education loans covers:
questions.e: Repayment starts after course completion plus one year (or six months after getting a job, whichever is earlier); simple interest may be serviced during the moratorium.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The '4 Cs' of credit appraisal classically include:
questions.e: Character (integrity), Capacity (cash flows), Capital (stake) and Collateral (security) — sometimes plus Conditions — structure credit appraisal before ratios and projections.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A consortium advance differs from multiple banking in:
o: Common documentation and a lead bank versus separate arrangements
questions.e: Consortium lending shares appraisal, documentation and security via agreement among banks; multiple banking has independent bilateral limits, which RBI has discouraged for large exposures.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI's 2023 framework on compromise settlements:
o: Permits compromise for wilful defaulters only under strict board-approved conditions
questions.e: The 2023 framework standardised compromise/one-time settlements with transparent sacrifice computation, permitting wilful-defaulter compromises only with board oversight and cooling periods.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Evergreening of loans refers to:
o: Fresh lending to service old dues, hiding stress
questions.e: Evergreening — new loans to pay old ones — masks NPAs and is penalised by RBI inspection. Related-party and circular lending are red flags in credit supervision.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The 'out of order' status for CC/OD accounts triggers when:
o: Outstanding exceeds limit/DP continuously or no credits for 90 days
questions.e: An account is 'out of order' if the balance stays above the sanctioned limit/drawing power, or if there are no credits (other than interest) for 90 days — either makes it NPA.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Agricultural advances become NPA when overdue for:
o: Two crop seasons for short-duration crops, one for long-duration
questions.e: Crop loans follow harvest cycles: overdue beyond two crop seasons (short-duration) or one crop season (long-duration), not the flat 90-day norm — recognising agriculture's seasonality.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Restructured standard accounts under the 2019 framework:
o: Retain standard tag only if the resolution plan succeeds
questions.e: The 7 June 2019 framework allows standard classification during implementation, but failure triggers NPA classification with accelerated provisioning — discipline through consequence.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Banking Regulation Act was originally enacted as the Banking Companies Act in:
questions.e: The Banking Companies Act, 1949 (renamed the Banking Regulation Act in 1966) empowers the RBI to license, inspect and regulate banks — the statutory root of Indian banking supervision.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Retail banking is characterised by:
o: High volumes and small ticket sizes
questions.e: Retail banking serves individuals/small businesses with standardised, high-volume, low-ticket products delivered through branches, BCs and digital channels. Granularity diversifies risk but raises operating costs.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The CASA ratio indicates:
o: The share of low-cost deposits in total deposits
questions.e: Current and savings accounts are the cheapest funds; a higher CASA ratio lowers cost of deposits and lifts NIM. It is a core retail-franchise metric.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Maximum LTV for housing loans up to Rs.30 lakh is:
questions.e: RBI LTV caps: up to 90 per cent for loans up to Rs.30 lakh, 80 per cent for Rs.30-75 lakh, 75 per cent above Rs.75 lakh — balancing access with collateral cushion.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Interest on self-occupied housing loans is deductible up to:
questions.e: Section 24(b) allows up to Rs.2 lakh interest deduction for self-occupied property; principal repayment qualifies under 80C (Rs.1.5 lakh overall). Let-out property has different treatment.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: External benchmarking of floating retail loans links them to:
o: Repo rate or other RBI-specified external benchmarks
questions.e: Since October 2019, floating retail/MSME loans must reference repo, T-bill or other external benchmarks with a spread, ensuring policy transmission. Reset clauses pass through rate changes.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Prepayment penalty on floating-rate retail loans:
o: Cannot be levied as per RBI directions
questions.e: RBI bars prepayment penalties on floating-rate loans to individuals, aiding balance transfers. Fixed-rate loans may carry charges per the sanction terms.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Credit utilisation ratio is:
o: Outstanding balances to total credit limits
questions.e: Using a high share of available limits (above 30 per cent) hurts credit scores, signalling credit hunger. Low utilisation with timely payments builds scores.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A good CIBIL score is generally:
questions.e: Scores range 300-900; 750-plus unlocks better rates and approvals. Payment history carries the largest weight, followed by utilisation and vintage.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Minimum due on a credit card:
o: Does not avoid interest on the remaining balance
questions.e: Paying only the minimum (typically 5 per cent) keeps the account current but interest accrues on the full outstanding (often 36-49 per cent annualised) and the interest-free period is lost.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The interest-free period on credit cards can extend up to:
questions.e: Purchases at the billing cycle's start get the longest float — cycle days plus the payment grace period — provided the previous balance was fully paid.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Debit cards differ from credit cards in that:
o: They access the customer's own funds
questions.e: Debit cards pull from the linked account — no credit, no interest. Only credit products (cards, loans) build bureau credit history.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: EMI under reducing-balance method:
o: Charges interest on the original principal throughout
Is always higher than flat-rate EMI
Charges interest only on the outstanding principal
questions.e: Reducing-balance interest falls as principal amortises, making it the fair comparison metric. Flat rates understate true cost — a classic exam comparison.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: PM Vidyalaxmi scheme provides:
o: Collateral-free guarantee-backed education loans up to Rs.7.5 lakh
questions.e: PM Vidyalaxmi (2024) offers meritorious students collateral-free loans up to Rs.7.5 lakh with government credit guarantee, plus interest subvention for eligible families.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Auto loans are typically secured by:
questions.e: The financed vehicle is hypothecated — the borrower keeps possession while the bank holds a registered charge. Tenures run 3-7 years with LTV around 80-90 per cent.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Personal loans are:
o: Unsecured with higher rates reflecting credit risk
questions.e: Clean personal loans price the absence of collateral into higher rates and rely on bureau scores and income multiples for underwriting.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme account tenure is:
questions.e: SCSS runs 5 years (extendable once by 3), offering above-market rates with quarterly payouts — a retiree staple alongside PMVVY.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: PPF's tax treatment is:
o: EEE — exempt at investment, interest and withdrawal
questions.e: Public Provident Fund enjoys exempt-exempt-exempt status with 80C deduction, tax-free interest and maturity — the benchmark safe long-term retail product with a 15-year horizon.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NPS Tier I versus Tier II:
o: Tier I is restricted retirement savings; Tier II is voluntary with full liquidity
Tier II has the tax benefit
questions.e: Tier I locks funds till retirement (with partial conditional withdrawals) and gives 80CCD tax benefits; Tier II is a liquid add-on without exclusive tax benefits.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: At NPS maturity, the tax-free lump-sum limit is:
questions.e: Up to 60 per cent can be withdrawn tax-free; at least 40 per cent must annuitise. The annuity income is taxable in the year received.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Additional NPS deduction under 80CCD(1B) is:
questions.e: Section 80CCD(1B) gives an extra Rs.50,000 deduction for NPS beyond the Rs.1.5 lakh 80C ceiling — over and above the 10 per cent salary limit under 80CCD(1).

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: ELSS funds have a lock-in of:
questions.e: Equity Linked Savings Schemes lock investments for 3 years — the shortest among 80C options — with market-linked returns and 80C deduction up to Rs.1.5 lakh.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: SIP's rupee-cost averaging means:
o: More units when NAV is low, fewer when high
questions.e: Fixed instalments buy more units in dips and fewer at peaks, averaging purchase cost and imposing discipline — though it cannot eliminate market risk.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NAV of a mutual fund is:
o: (Assets minus liabilities) divided by units outstanding
questions.e: Net Asset Value per unit values the portfolio daily net of liabilities and expenses, divided by units — the price for subscriptions and redemptions in open-ended funds.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Direct mutual fund plans differ from regular plans in:
o: Lower expense ratio, excluding distributor commission
questions.e: Direct plans skip distributor commission, so their expense ratio is lower and long-term returns higher; the portfolio is identical to the regular plan.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: SEBI categorises mutual fund schemes to:
o: Ensure one scheme per category per fund house
questions.e: Categorisation norms (2017) permit only one scheme per category per AMC (with defined exceptions), curbing duplication and making comparison honest.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Liquid funds invest in:
questions.e: Liquid and overnight funds park in very-short-term debt (T-bills, CP, CDs) for safety and next-day liquidity — the corporate-treasury parking slot.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Modified duration of a debt fund indicates:
o: Sensitivity of NAV to interest-rate changes
questions.e: Higher modified duration means NAV swings more with rate moves — long-duration funds gain most when rates fall and lose most when rates rise.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Term insurance is:
o: Pure protection with the highest cover per rupee of premium
questions.e: Term plans pay only on death within the term — no maturity value — making cover cheapest. Endowment and money-back bundle savings at higher cost.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: ULIPs have a lock-in of:
questions.e: Unit Linked Insurance Plans lock in for 5 years, splitting premium into mortality charges, fund management and investment — market-linked insurance-cum-investment.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Free-look period for life insurance is:
questions.e: IRDAI's 30-day free-look lets policyholders return the policy for a refund (minus charges) if terms disappoint — a key consumer-protection disclosure.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Third-party motor insurance is:
o: Mandatory under the Motor Vehicles Act
questions.e: Third-party liability cover is compulsory for all motor vehicles; own-damage cover is optional. Insurers cannot refuse TP cover.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Health insurance waiting period for pre-existing diseases is typically:
o: Up to 3-4 years as per policy terms
questions.e: PED waiting periods (now capped by IRDAI at 3 years for most products) delay coverage of declared pre-existing conditions; specific ailments and initial 30-day waits also apply.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Claim settlement ratio of an insurer indicates:
o: Claims settled as a percentage of claims received
questions.e: Higher claim-settlement ratios signal reliable payout behaviour — a prime comparison metric alongside solvency ratio when choosing insurers.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: IRDAI is headquartered in:
questions.e: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India, set up under the IRDAI Act 1999, is headquartered in Hyderabad, regulating insurers, brokers and agents.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The rule-of-100 in asset allocation suggests:
questions.e: The crude glide path cuts equity exposure with age (a 30-year-old holds ~70 per cent equity). Target-date funds automate similar glides.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Rebalancing a portfolio means:
questions.e: Market moves drift weights from targets; periodic rebalancing (calendar or threshold-based) sells winners and buys laggards — systematic contrarian discipline.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: An emergency fund should cover:
o: 3-6 months of expenses in liquid instruments
questions.e: The liquidity buffer precedes investing, parked in savings, liquid funds or sweep-in deposits — accessible without market or penalty risk.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Risk capacity differs from risk appetite in that:
o: Capacity is financial ability; appetite is psychological willingness
questions.e: Capacity (income stability, horizon, dependents) is objective; appetite (comfort with volatility) is behavioural. Suitability must respect the lower of the two.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A nominee under bank nomination is:
o: A trustee for the legal heirs, not the owner
questions.e: Per Sections 45ZA-45ZF of the Banking Regulation Act and court rulings (Vandana v Armaan line), the nominee receives as trustee; succession law decides ownership. Wills and trusts complete estate planning.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A will is:
o: Revocable during the testator's lifetime with no stamp duty
questions.e: Wills are revocable, need no stamp duty or mandatory registration (registration adds evidentiary strength), and cover all assets — the simplest estate-transfer tool.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Private trusts in estate planning help:
o: Provide for minors or special-needs beneficiaries
questions.e: Trusts ring-fence assets for beneficiaries who cannot manage them, with trustees bound by fiduciary duty — useful for minor children or dependents with disabilities.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Systematic Transfer Plans:
o: Shift money systematically between schemes of a fund house
questions.e: STPs move fixed sums periodically (e.g., liquid to equity), phasing entry like an SIP funded from an existing corpus. SWPs do the reverse for regular income.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The first step in financial planning is:
o: Fact-finding — income, expenses, assets, liabilities, goals
questions.e: Fact-finding grounds everything: without the balance sheet, cash flows and goal horizons, product selection is guesswork. Risk profiling follows, then allocation.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Goal-based investing assigns:
o: Each goal a horizon, inflation assumption and dedicated portfolio
questions.e: Education, retirement and home purchase get separate portfolios matched to horizon and inflation (education inflation exceeds CPI) — preventing short-goal money from riding equity volatility.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Diversification eliminates:
questions.e: Holding 15-20 uncorrelated securities or diversified funds washes out firm-specific shocks; market-wide systematic risk remains and is priced via beta.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The efficient frontier shows:
o: Maximum expected return for each risk level
questions.e: Portfolios below the frontier are suboptimal; the optimal risky portfolio plus the risk-free asset gives the capital-market line. It is the visual core of modern portfolio theory.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Loss aversion (behavioural finance) means:
o: Losses hurt more than equal gains please
questions.e: Prospect theory's loss aversion explains panic selling and disposition effects (selling winners, holding losers). Awareness plus automation (SIPs, rebalancing) counters it.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bancassurance is:
o: Banks distributing insurance as corporate agents
questions.e: Banks act as corporate agents for insurers, earning fee income — but mis-selling of ULIPs/endowment as 'deposits' is a conduct risk the RBI and IRDAI penalise.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Banking Ombudsman under the integrated scheme covers:
questions.e: The RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 gives 'one nation, one ombudsman' coverage with centralised receipt — including digital-transaction complaints.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Video-KYC for account opening was permitted by the RBI in:
questions.e: The January 2020 amendment to KYC Directions allowed V-CIP (video-based customer identification), compressing digital onboarding to minutes alongside Aadhaar e-KYC.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: SWP in mutual funds is used to:
o: Withdraw fixed sums periodically for regular income
questions.e: Systematic Withdrawal Plans redeem fixed amounts periodically — popular for retirees drawing income from debt/hybrid funds while the balance stays invested.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Capital gains on equity funds held over 1 year (LTCG) are taxed at:
o: 12.5 per cent above the Rs.1.25 lakh annual exemption
questions.e: Post-July-2024 rules: listed-equity LTCG at 12.5 per cent beyond Rs.1.25 lakh yearly exemption; STCG (under 1 year) at 20 per cent. Debt-fund taxation follows slab rates.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Sovereign Gold Bonds' tenor and premature exit:
o: 8 years with exit from the 5th year
questions.e: SGBs run 8 years with premature redemption allowed after 5 years on interest-payment dates, plus exchange tradability. They pay 2.5 per cent interest and track gold prices.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Gold ETF versus physical gold:
o: ETF gives gold exposure without storage or purity risk
questions.e: Gold ETFs hold demat units backed by physical gold — no making charges, theft or purity worries, with high liquidity. Expense ratios are the only drag.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The PPF interest rate is:
o: Set quarterly by the government, 7.1 per cent since April 2020
Fixed for 15 years at account opening
questions.e: Small-savings rates are reset quarterly; PPF has held 7.1 per cent since April 2020. Interest is tax-free and the 15-year tenure extends in 5-year blocks.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: EPF interest rate for FY25 was:
questions.e: EPFO retained 8.25 per cent for FY25 (as for FY24). EPF enjoys EEE treatment for most employees within contribution limits.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NPS annuity income is:
questions.e: The mandatory 40 per cent annuity purchase generates pension taxable as salary/income each year; only the 60 per cent lump sum is tax-free.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Atal Pension Yojana guarantees:
o: Pension of Rs.1,000-5,000 monthly from age 60
questions.e: APY (for unorganised workers 18-40) guarantees a defined monthly pension from 60, with government co-contribution for eligible early joiners.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: PMJJBY provides:
o: Rs.2 lakh life cover at Rs.436 annual premium
questions.e: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana gives Rs.2 lakh term cover (18-50 years) via auto-debit; PMSBY gives Rs.2 lakh accident cover at Rs.20/year.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: PMSBY premium is:
questions.e: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana's Rs.20 yearly premium covers accidental death/disability up to Rs.2 lakh for ages 18-70 — the flagship micro-insurance pair with PMJJBY.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY covers:
o: Rs.5 lakh per family per year for secondary/tertiary care
questions.e: PM-JAY gives cashless hospitalisation cover of Rs.5 lakh per family yearly to deprived households (SECC-based), now extended to all senior citizens 70-plus.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Retail loan underwriting primarily relies on:
o: Bureau scores, income multiples and collateral coverage
questions.e: Scorecards blend CIBIL, FOIR (fixed obligations to income ratio), LTV and vintage analytics. Granular portfolios are managed statistically, unlike corporate relationship lending.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: FOIR in retail underwriting stands for:
questions.e: FOIR caps total EMIs as a share of net income (typically 40-50 per cent), ensuring repayment capacity beyond the specific loan's EMI.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Vintage analysis in retail credit tracks:
o: Delinquency by loan origination cohort over time
questions.e: Vintage curves show how each origination month's loans season — early delinquency spikes flag underwriting slippage. It is the core portfolio-monitoring tool for retail books.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Balance transfer of a home loan:
o: Shifts the outstanding to another lender, usually for better terms
Converts it to a personal loan
questions.e: Borrowers refinance with a new lender offering lower spreads; the new lender does fresh due diligence and the old loan is foreclosed. No prepayment penalty applies on floating-rate loans.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Top-up home loans:
o: Additional borrowing against the same property's margin
questions.e: Top-ups leverage the property's appreciated value/margin for additional secured borrowing at near-home-loan rates — cheaper than personal loans.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Reverse mortgage is designed for:
o: Senior citizens to draw income against home equity
questions.e: Seniors (60-plus) mortgage their home to receive periodic payments while continuing to reside; settlement occurs on death or sale. It monetises illiquid housing wealth.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Loan against securities provides:
o: Overdraft against pledged shares/mutual funds with LTV haircuts
questions.e: LAS gives revolving credit against demat securities with regulatory LTV caps and mark-to-market margin calls — cheaper than personal loans for the invested.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Gold loans' LTV cap is:
o: 75 per cent of the gold's value
questions.e: RBI caps gold-loan LTV at 75 per cent, with assaying and auction procedures on default. NBFC gold lenders follow the same ceiling.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Kisan Credit Card limit is assessed on:
o: Scale of finance for the crop x area plus allied activities
questions.e: KCC uses district scale-of-finance per acre for crops plus limits for allied activities and consumption, with interest subvention bringing effective rates to 4 per cent for prompt payers.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Interest subvention makes prompt-paying crop loans effectively:
o: 4 per cent per annum up to Rs.3 lakh
questions.e: The 2 per cent subvention plus 3 per cent prompt-repayment incentive on the 7 per cent base rate yields 4 per cent effective for short-term crop loans up to Rs.3 lakh.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Agri Jewel loans are:
o: Crop loans against gold ornaments for agricultural purposes
questions.e: Farmers pledge gold for agricultural-needs credit, often quicker than land-record-based loans — classified as agricultural advances for PSL.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Priority-sector classification of education loans:
questions.e: All education loans (domestic and abroad) count toward priority-sector targets under the education category, regardless of ticket size.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Housing loans for PSL in non-metros: loan cap and cost cap:
o: Rs.25 lakh loan, Rs.30 lakh dwelling cost
questions.e: Non-metro PSL housing: Rs.25 lakh loan on Rs.30 lakh cost; metros Rs.35 lakh on Rs.45 lakh. Loans beyond these still get PSL only for the EWS/LIG segments per extant rules.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: DRI scheme (Differential Rate of Interest) lends at:
o: 4 per cent to the weakest borrowers
questions.e: Public-sector banks must lend 1 per cent of previous-year advances at 4 per cent to SC/ST and weaker sections under DRI — the oldest directed-lending concessional window.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: SHG-Bank Linkage Programme pioneered by:
questions.e: NABARD's 1992 SHG-bank linkage model made India the world's largest microfinance outreach, with SHGs' savings-linked credit now a PSL weaker-section mainstay.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Microfinance (RBI 2022 framework) caps borrower indebtedness with:
o: FOIR-based household income assessment, not a fixed loan cap
questions.e: The harmonised microfinance directions use household income and FOIR (50 per cent cap) rather than ticket caps, applying uniformly to banks, NBFC-MFIs and SFBs.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Business Correspondents are:
o: Bank agents providing last-mile services with ICT devices
questions.e: BCs (individuals, kirana stores, CSCs) extend deposits, remittances and credit origination to unbanked areas on the bank's behalf, under board-approved BC policies.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The BC's transactions are:
o: Real-time and reflected in the bank's books
questions.e: BC transactions through micro-ATMs/handheld devices hit the CBS in real time; the bank remains fully liable to the customer for BC acts.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Financial literacy centres are run by:
questions.e: RBI requires banks to run Financial Literacy Centres (FLCs) conducting camps on savings, credit discipline, digital banking and grievance redress.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The 'no-frills' account is now called:
questions.e: BSBD replaced the no-frills nomenclature, standardising zero-minimum-balance savings with defined free services across banks.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: AePS transactions need:
questions.e: AePS works on feature phones via BC micro-ATMs using Aadhaar and fingerprint/iris — no card or phone needed — enabling DBT and last-mile cash.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) primarily uses:
questions.e: DBT credits subsidies directly to Aadhaar-linked accounts through the Aadhaar Payments Bridge, cutting leakage — the JAM trinity's payoff.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The JAM trinity is:
questions.e: Jan Dhan accounts, Aadhaar identity and mobile connectivity form the inclusion stack behind DBT, UPI and digital onboarding.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: UPI AutoPay is used for:
questions.e: UPI AutoPay handles recurring collections (subscriptions, EMIs, mutual-fund SIPs) with pre-debit notifications and mandate limits.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: E-mandates above Rs.15,000 need:
o: Additional factor authentication at setup and pre-debit notification
questions.e: RBI's recurring-payment framework requires AFA for mandates above Rs.15,000 plus 24-hour pre-debit notification with opt-out — balancing convenience and control.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Credit-card billing disputes are resolved through:
questions.e: Chargeback lets issuers reverse disputed transactions through network rails for fraud, non-delivery or duplication — the cardholder's core purchase protection.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Card tokenisation in India:
o: Replaces card details with tokens for online transactions
questions.e: RBI mandated tokenisation (no merchant storage of card data) from 2022, with card-on-file tokenisation securing e-commerce without exposing PAN data.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Co-branded credit cards:
o: Issued by a bank with a partner brand sharing rewards economics
questions.e: Co-brand partnerships (airlines, e-commerce, fuel) split interchange and reward costs, driving acquisition through the partner's customer base.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The total expense ratio (TER) of a mutual fund:
o: Is capped by SEBI on a slab basis of AUM
questions.e: SEBI caps TER by AUM slabs (higher for the first Rs.500 crore), with additional allowances for B-30 city inflows — protecting investors from fee drag.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: B-30 in mutual funds refers to:
o: Beyond-top-30 cities getting extra TER incentive
questions.e: Additional TER up to 30 bps is allowed for inflows from beyond-top-30 cities to deepen geographic penetration of mutual funds.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Index funds versus ETFs:
o: Both passive; ETFs trade intraday on exchanges, index funds transact at NAV
questions.e: Both track indices passively; ETFs need demat and trade live (with tracking error plus price spreads), while index funds subscribe/redeem at end-of-day NAV.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Tracking error measures:
o: Deviation of a fund's returns from its benchmark
questions.e: Lower tracking error means tighter index replication — the key quality metric for passive funds alongside TER.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A hybrid aggressive fund holds:
questions.e: SEBI categories: aggressive hybrid 65-80 per cent equity; conservative hybrid 10-25 per cent; balanced advantage dynamically managed. Equity taxation needs 65 per cent-plus equity.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Arbitrage funds are treated as:
o: Equity for taxation (65 per cent-plus equity)
questions.e: Arbitrage funds hold hedged equity qualifying for equity taxation while behaving like debt — a tax-efficient parking slot for 1-3 year horizons.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Overnight funds invest in:
questions.e: Overnight funds hold 1-day-maturity instruments — the safest debt category, virtually immune to interest-rate and credit risk.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Credit-risk funds:
o: Invest at least 65 per cent in below-highest-rated papers
questions.e: Credit-risk funds chase yield in AA-and-below paper (min 65 per cent), carrying genuine default risk — Franklin Templeton's 2020 wind-ups are the cautionary tale.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Gilt funds invest in:
questions.e: Gilt funds hold only sovereign paper — zero credit risk but full interest-rate (duration) risk, shining when rates fall.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The '4 per cent rule' in retirement planning suggests:
o: Withdrawing ~4 per cent yearly for a 25-30 year corpus life
questions.e: The Bengen rule's 4 per cent initial withdrawal (inflation-adjusted) is a starting heuristic; Indian planners adapt it for higher inflation and return assumptions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Human-life-value in insurance needs analysis:
questions.e: HLV = present value of future income the family depends on, less self-maintenance — the economic-value method for sizing life cover, refined by needs analysis.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: In September 2026 the RBI recognised the Unified Fintech Forum (UFF) as:
o: A Self-Regulatory Organisation for the FinTech sector (SRO-FT)
questions.e: UFF is the second entity to receive SRO-FT recognition under the RBI's framework, after the FinTech Association for Consumer Empowerment (FACE) in August 2024. The move aims to strengthen self-regulation, industry governance and responsible growth in India's fintech ecosystem.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: As reported in September 2026, global rating agencies' expectations for the RBI's policy repo rate (held at 5.25% since August 2026, MPC next meeting 5-7 October 2026) are:
o: S&P expects one 25-bps hike to 5.5% in FY27; Fitch expects 25-bps hikes in October 2026 (to 5.5%) and early 2027 (to 5.75%)
S&P expects a 100-bps cut; Fitch expects no change until 2028
Both agencies expect the repo rate to stay at 5.25% through 2028
S&P expects two 50-bps hikes before December 2026
questions.e: S&P Global Ratings expects a single 25-basis-point hike to 5.5% during FY27, while Fitch Ratings expects a 25-bps increase in October 2026 followed by another to 5.75% in early 2027, citing strong demand and rising inflation (Fitch sees retail inflation reaching 5.5% in December 2026).

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The UFBU deferred the 28–30 September 2026 bank strike after which assurance from the IBA?
o: A high-level committee on the five-day-week (all Saturdays holiday) demand
questions.e: On 27 September 2026 the UFBU deferred the 28–30 September strike after the IBA assured a high-level IBA–UFBU committee to deliberate on declaring all Saturdays holidays; the five-day-week demand dates to the March 2024 wage settlement.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: As per RBI data released in September 2026, NRI deposit flows during April–July 2026 were:
questions.e: RBI data showed NRI deposit flows surged nearly sixfold to $36.2 billion in April–July 2026, bolstered by attractive domestic interest-rate differentials.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: SIDBI withdrew its Rs 6,000-crore bond offering in September 2026 because:
o: Hardening domestic yields made pricing unfavourable
questions.e: SIDBI pulled its three-year Rs 6,000-crore bond issuance in September 2026 as hardening domestic yields created unfavourable pricing conditions for corporate debt.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: What was India’s rank in the September 2026 Ipsos consumer-confidence survey of 30 countries?
questions.e: India retained the top rank among 30 countries with a consumer-confidence score of 66.9 in September 2026 (Ipsos), up 1.6 points; the Employment sub-index gained 3.7 points.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: UPI transactions in August 2026, as per NPCI data released in September 2026:
o: 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore
questions.e: UPI processed a record 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore in August 2026 — about 791 million a day — per NPCI data released in September 2026.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The 11th AIIB Board of Governors meeting on 28 September 2026 is being held in:
questions.e: FM Nirmala Sitharaman is in Qatar (27–29 September 2026) for the 11th AIIB Board of Governors meeting in Doha, attending as India’s Governor; India is the AIIB’s second-largest shareholder.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: A Reuters poll (18–28 Sep 2026) found how many of 61 economists expecting a 25 bps repo-rate hike at the RBI’s 5–7 Oct MPC meeting?
questions.e: 35 of 61 economists expected a 25 bps hike to 5.50% — the first since February 2023 — with August CPI inflation at 4.82%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI’s policy repo rate and stance as of September 2026 are:
questions.e: The MPC has held the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance since the August 2026 policy; the next decision is due 7 October 2026.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: India’s CPI inflation in August 2026, as reported ahead of the October MPC meeting, was:
o: 4.82%, above the RBI’s 4% target for the third straight month
questions.e: August CPI inflation accelerated to 4.82%, driven by energy and food costs — a key input for the October policy decision.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under NPCI’s revised UPI framework effective 15 October 2026, the MDR on merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000 is:
o: A flat Rs 5 for all merchant payments
questions.e: NPCI set 0.4% MDR capped at Rs 300 for merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000; about 96% of person-to-merchant transactions and small merchants (up to Rs 1 lakh/month) stay at zero MDR.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under the UPI MDR framework effective 15 October 2026, what is the maximum MDR on a single transaction of Rs 75,000 or more?
questions.e: MDR is 0.4% on specified person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: India’s Index of Industrial Production (IIP) grew by what percentage year-on-year in August 2026?
questions.e: IIP grew 8% y/y in August 2026 (data released 28 Sep), beating the 6.5% Reuters poll estimate and accelerating from 7.4% in July.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under the Gig Workers Social Security and Welfare Bill, 2026 (passed by the Rajya Sabha on 29 Sep 2026), platform companies must contribute what share of transaction value toward provident fund?
questions.e: Platforms contribute 2% of transaction value; ESIC is the implementing agency for the ’7.7 crore gig workers covered.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Pashudhan Bima Portal launched on 28 September 2026 by the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying is a single digital platform for:
questions.e: It covers policy issuance, claim processing, monitoring and reporting for livestock insurance under the Livestock Insurance Scheme.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The ’Shram Samvad’ labour-code awareness campaign launched by the Labour Ministry on 28 September 2026 runs for:
questions.e: A 90-day mega campaign covering industrial clusters across 316 districts in all 36 states/UTs.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under the UPI MDR framework, a flat Rs 5 MDR applies to which of the following categories?
o: Railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs
questions.e: Specified categories — railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agri inputs — attract a flat Rs 5 MDR; P2P transfers remain free.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee is scheduled to meet on:
questions.e: The MPC meets 5-7 October 2026; markets are watching for a possible 25-bps repo-rate hike to 5.50%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: August 2026 CPI inflation at 4.82% implies:
o: Inflation is below the RBI's 4% target
Inflation stayed above the 4% target for a third straight month
The 6% upper tolerance band was breached
questions.e: At 4.82%, CPI stayed above the RBI's 4% target for the third consecutive month.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: August 2026 IIP growth of 8.0%, with manufacturing at 9.0%, indicates:
questions.e: IIP grew 8.0% year-on-year in August 2026; manufacturing at 9.0% outpaced the headline number.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The proposed MDR challenged before the Supreme Court applies to specified UPI merchant transactions above:
questions.e: The challenge targets the MDR framework for specified UPI merchant transactions above Rs 2,000; the Court refused interim stay on 29 Sep 2026.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Nomura's projection of a 5.75% terminal repo rate assumes:
questions.e: Nomura projected 25-bps hikes in October and December - a market forecast, not a decided policy move.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: If the RBI hikes 25 bps in October as polled, it would be the first repo-rate hike since:
questions.e: The last hike cycle ended in February 2023.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The UPI MDR matter returns to the Supreme Court next on (as reported):
questions.e: The next hearing was reported for 13 October 2026.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: On 30 September 2026, Bank of America Securities forecast the RBI's terminal repo rate at:
questions.e: BofA expects 25 bps in October plus 75 bps thereafter — 100 bps through H1 2027 — taking the terminal repo rate to 6.25%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Blue Bond launched by Sagarmala Finance Corporation is rated AA+ by:
questions.e: The 10-year Blue Bond is rated AA+ by ICRA and CARE and was arranged by SBI Capital Markets.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: IndusInd Bank's GCC Banking vertical integrates all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Foreign-currency accounts via GIFT City IBU
questions.e: The vertical integrates digital banking, employee banking, commercial cards, FEMA/capital-account solutions and foreign-currency accounts via its IBU at GIFT City.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: SEBI's board on 30 September 2026 cleared an overhaul of rules governing:
questions.e: SEBI's board cleared the overhaul of portfolio management and settlement rules.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The FPI outflow of about Rs 9,200 crore in September 2026 was from:
questions.e: FPIs offloaded Rs 9,200 crore of Fully Accessible Route bonds in September, snapping a five-month buying spree.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The PM-DHARA scheme approved on 1 October 2026 has an outlay of:
questions.e: The Cabinet approved Rs 1.86 lakh crore for PM-DHARA's intra-state transmission networks with battery storage.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The wheat MSP for 2027-28, after the Rs 25 hike, is:
questions.e: The MSP for wheat is now Rs 2,610 per quintal; pulses and oilseeds got hikes of up to Rs 675 per quintal.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI's October 2026 MPC meeting is scheduled for:
questions.e: The MPC meets 5–7 October 2026 with the repo rate currently at 5.25%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Foreign investors withdrew about $2.7 billion from Indian equities in which month?
questions.e: FPIs withdrew $2.7 billion from Indian equities in September 2026 amid global rate concerns.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The windfall tax cut announced on 1 October 2026 applies to exports of:
questions.e: The government cut the windfall tax on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) exports.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI's current repo rate going into the 5–7 October 2026 MPC meeting is:
questions.e: The repo rate is at 5.25%; the market expects a 25 bps hike to 5.50%, the first since February 2023.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: BofA's India Viewpoint (September 2026) expects the RBI to change its stance in December to:
questions.e: BofA expects the stance to switch to 'calibrated tightening' in December alongside 100 bps of hikes through H1 2027.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: An increase in the repo rate by the RBI typically leads to:
o: a fall in banks' cost of funds
a rise in MCLR/EBLR-linked lending rates
questions.e: Higher repo raises banks' cost of funds; MCLR and EBLR-linked loans reprice upward, tightening credit conditions.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: According to the Reuters poll (18–28 September 2026), how many of the 61 economists expected a 25 bps hike in October?
questions.e: 35 of 61 economists (about 57%) expected the October 25 bps hike to 5.50%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Nomura's forecast for average CPI inflation in FY27 is:
questions.e: Nomura forecasts FY27 CPI at 5.2% y/y and FY28 at 4%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: CPI inflation in August 2026 (4.82%) exceeded the RBI's medium-term target for the:
questions.e: August was the third straight month above the 4% target, driven by energy and food costs.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: After the 5–7 Oct 2026 MPC meeting, the repo rate stands at:
questions.e: 25 bps hike; stance changed to Calibrated Tightening; SDF 5.25%, MSF 5.75%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate after the October 2026 MPC is:
questions.e: SDF = repo (5.50%) − 25 bps.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: PFRDA's Certificate of Appointment as Sponsor of a pension fund is granted under:
o: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act
questions.e: The route Bank of Baroda used in October 2026 to become the second PSB in the pension fund business.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: In the pension fund management company, Bank of Baroda's shareholding is:
questions.e: Baroda BNP Asset Management holds the remaining 19.90%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: India's defence exports in FY 2025–26 crossed:
questions.e: Reported in October 2026 current-affairs compilations.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Chakshu portal, which crossed 30 crore visits, is run by:
questions.e: For reporting suspected fraud calls and messages.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The SME Growth Fund's government commitment is:
questions.e: The Cabinet approved a Rs 10,000-crore commitment to an AIF under the SGF framework on 6 October 2026.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The proposed new threshold for launching GST prosecution is:
questions.e: The 57th GST Council recommended raising it from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Gross GST collections in H1 FY2026-27 were approximately:
questions.e: April–September 2026 gross collections reached Rs 12.46 lakh crore, up 11.6% year-on-year.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which body will serve as the apex authority for integrated transport planning?
questions.e: The Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) was approved as an SPV by the Cabinet on 6 October 2026.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Each JOSH team comprises:
questions.e: Five NCC cadets and five MY Bharat volunteers work under a designated Class-I officer.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: India's TB treatment coverage, per the Health Minister (8 Oct 2026), is:
questions.e: Treatment coverage reached 92% against 78% globally; incidence declined 21% against 12% globally.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI's special dollar window announced on 10 October 2026 is open to:
questions.e: The three state oil marketers can buy dollars directly from the RBI's forex reserves from 12 October, easing spot-market pressure.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: From the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026, banks must maintain daily CRR of at least:
questions.e: Raised from 90% to 99%; the prescribed CRR itself remains 3% of deposits.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The RBI's open market operation sale of government securities on 13 October 2026 is worth:
questions.e: The sale is meant to drain surplus banking-system liquidity.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: After the October 2026 MPC meeting, the repo rate stands at:
questions.e: A 25-basis-point hike — the first increase since 2023 — with the stance moved to 'calibrated tightening'.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: In October 2026 the RBI revised its FY27 real GDP growth forecast to:
questions.e: Raised from 6.7%; growth in Q2 FY27 is projected at 7.2%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: On 10 October 2026 the RBI cut the position limit for exchange-traded rupee currency derivatives to:
questions.e: Cut from $100 million; dealers may no longer rebook rupee FX derivatives.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The 57th GST Council meeting was held on 8 October 2026 at:
questions.e: Chaired by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The GST Council scrapped arrest powers under GST and raised the prosecution threshold to:
questions.e: Raised from Rs 1 crore — the biggest decriminalisation push in GST's history.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The general penalty under GST was reduced from Rs 25,000 to:
questions.e: Announced after the 57th GST Council meeting on 8 Oct 2026.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under the new GST refund rules, the acknowledgement period for refund claims is cut to:
questions.e: Cut from 15 days; 90% of eligible refunds are to be sanctioned within 3 working days of acknowledgement.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Going forward, GST rate changes will be decided:
questions.e: The Council also plans a faceless tax-administration framework under CGST for FY28.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: GST registered taxpayers (September 2026) and gross collections (Apr–Sep 2026) stand at:
questions.e: Taxpayers rose from about 60 lakh in 2017; the process reforms take effect 1 April 2027.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bihar's MSME Policy 2026 targets how many families self-reliant through entrepreneurship?
questions.e: 45,000 entrepreneurs are being developed with Rs 3,500 crore.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The SC/ST share among Bihar's 45,000 planned MSME entrepreneurs is:
questions.e: Plus 10,000 EBC, 9,500 women, 9,000 youth and 2,500 minority.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Under the MSME Policy 2026, in-state procurement share will be:
questions.e: Announced 9 Oct 2026.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bihar's five-year industrial investment target via PPP is:
questions.e: With 20,000 MW of power to industry in the same period.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bihar expects what share of the Centre's Rs 10,000-crore MSME allocation?
questions.e: About Rs 1,000 crore for the state.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Bihar's agri-feeder solarisation target announced 9 Oct 2026 is:
questions.e: Alongside ropeways at 20 important locations in two years.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which measure of central tendency is most affected by extreme values?
questions.e: The arithmetic mean uses every observation in its sum, so a single very large or very small value pulls it strongly. The median and mode depend on position or frequency, making them resistant to extremes.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical relationship between mean, median and mode is:
questions.e: Karl Pearson's empirical rule states Mean - Mode = 3(Mean - Median) for moderately skewed distributions. It lets you estimate one measure from the other two when the distribution is not perfectly symmetric.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which of the following is the best measure for comparing consistency of two datasets with different means?
questions.e: Coefficient of variation = (SD/mean) x 100 is a relative, unit-free measure, so it can compare variability across datasets with different means or units. Absolute measures like SD or range cannot do this fairly.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The correlation coefficient r lies between:
questions.e: Pearson's r is bounded between -1 (perfect negative linear relationship) and +1 (perfect positive). Values near 0 indicate no linear relationship. It is unit-free and symmetric in x and y.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: If r = 0.8 between advertisement spend and sales, the coefficient of determination is:
questions.e: The coefficient of determination is r squared = 0.8 x 0.8 = 0.64. It means 64% of the variation in sales is explained by advertisement spend in this linear model.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The two regression lines always intersect at:
questions.e: Both regression lines (y on x and x on y) pass through the point of means (x-bar, y-bar). This is a standard property used to verify regression computations in exams.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: For independent events A and B, P(A and B) equals:
questions.e: Independence means the occurrence of one does not affect the other, so the joint probability is the product of the marginal probabilities. The addition rule applies to unions, not intersections.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In a normal distribution, approximately what percentage of observations lie within +/- 2 standard deviations?
questions.e: The empirical rule for the normal curve: about 68% within +/-1 sigma, 95% within +/-2 sigma, and 99.7% within +/-3 sigma. These fixed percentages are heavily tested.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which sampling method divides the population into homogeneous groups before random selection?
questions.e: Stratified sampling first partitions the population into homogeneous strata (e.g., loan size bands) and then samples randomly within each. It is ideal for heterogeneous bank portfolios and reduces sampling error.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The components of a time series do NOT include:
questions.e: A time series decomposes into Trend, Seasonal, Cyclical and Irregular components (Y = T+S+C+I or multiplicative). The regression coefficient is a modelling output, not a time-series component.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Quartile deviation is equal to:
questions.e: Quartile deviation, also called the semi-interquartile range, is (Q3 - Q1)/2. It measures the spread of the middle 50% of data and is resistant to outliers.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Bayes' theorem is primarily used for:
questions.e: Bayes' theorem updates prior probabilities into posterior probabilities when new evidence arrives. Banks use it in credit scoring and fraud models to revise default probabilities.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The binomial distribution applies when:
o: There are repeated independent trials with two outcomes
questions.e: Binomial conditions: fixed n, independent trials, exactly two outcomes (success/failure) with constant p. Loan default/no-default across a portfolio is the classic banking example.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Positive skewness implies:
questions.e: In a right-tailed (positively skewed) distribution the tail pulls the mean up most, so Mean > Median > Mode. Income and loan-size data are typically positively skewed.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The product of the two regression coefficients (b_yx and b_xy) equals:
questions.e: Since b_yx = r(sy/sx) and b_xy = r(sx/sy), their product is r squared. This identity is a favourite exam trap for checking regression arithmetic.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which average is appropriate for computing average growth rates?
questions.e: Growth compounds multiplicatively, so the geometric mean (nth root of the product) gives the correct average growth rate — the basis of CAGR calculations.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Moving averages in time-series analysis are used to:
o: Smooth out fluctuations and reveal trend
questions.e: Moving averages average out seasonal and irregular movements, exposing the underlying trend. Longer moving averages give smoother but less responsive trend lines.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: If P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5 for mutually exclusive events, P(A or B) is:
questions.e: For mutually exclusive events P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.4 + 0.5 = 0.9. No subtraction is needed because the intersection is empty.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The standard deviation of a constant value (e.g., all observations = 10) is:
questions.e: With no variation around the mean, every deviation is zero, so the standard deviation is 0. SD measures spread; a constant has none.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Kurtosis measures:
questions.e: Kurtosis describes how peaked or flat a distribution is relative to normal: leptokurtic (peaked, fat tails), mesokurtic (normal), platykurtic (flat). Skewness, not kurtosis, measures asymmetry.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In hypothesis testing, a Type I error is:
questions.e: Type I error (alpha) rejects a true null hypothesis — a false positive. Type II error (beta) accepts a false null — a false negative. Reducing one generally increases the other for fixed n.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which diagram is most suitable for showing the trend of deposits over 10 years?
questions.e: A line graph (historigram) shows how a variable evolves over time, making trends visible. Pie charts show composition, histograms show frequency distribution, scatter plots show bivariate relationships.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The harmonic mean is most appropriate for averaging:
o: Rates like speed or price per unit
questions.e: The harmonic mean (n / sum(1/x)) correctly averages rates — e.g., average speed over equal distances or average cost per share. Arithmetic mean would overstate such rates.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: If the coefficient of variation of Branch A is 8% and Branch B is 15%, which is more consistent?
questions.e: Lower CV means lower relative variability, hence greater consistency. Branch A's 8% CV shows its performance varies less relative to its mean than Branch B's 15%.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The addition rule of probability P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) is needed because:
questions.e: Simply adding P(A) + P(B) double-counts the intersection, so it must be subtracted once. Only for mutually exclusive events (empty intersection) can you add directly.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Maslow's hierarchy of needs, in correct ascending order, is:
questions.e: Maslow's order is Physiological -> Safety -> Social (belongingness) -> Esteem -> Self-actualisation. Lower needs must be reasonably satisfied before higher needs motivate behaviour.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Herzberg's two-factor theory distinguishes between:
questions.e: Herzberg found hygiene factors (pay, policy, working conditions) only prevent dissatisfaction, while motivators (achievement, recognition, responsibility) create satisfaction. The two operate on separate continua.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Theory X and Theory Y were propounded by:
questions.e: Douglas McGregor's Theory X assumes people are lazy and need control; Theory Y assumes people are self-motivated and seek responsibility. A manager's assumptions shape their leadership style.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: According to Vroom's expectancy theory, motivation equals:
questions.e: Vroom's model is multiplicative: Motivation = Expectancy (effort->performance) x Instrumentality (performance->reward) x Valence (value of reward). If any factor is zero, motivation collapses.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Adams' equity theory states that employees compare:
o: Their salary with the CEO's salary only
Their input-output ratio with others' ratios
questions.e: Adams argued people compare their own input-output (effort-reward) ratio with referent others. Perceived inequity creates tension, leading them to adjust effort, seek raises, or leave.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The 9,9 style in Blake and Mouton's Managerial Grid represents:
o: High concern for people, low for production
High concern for both people and production
questions.e: The 9,9 'team management' style combines maximum concern for people with maximum concern for production, and is presented as the ideal. 1,1 is impoverished, 9,1 is authority-compliance, 1,9 is country-club.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Fiedler's contingency theory holds that leadership effectiveness depends on:
o: Leader-member relations, task structure and position power
questions.e: Fiedler identified three situational variables: leader-member relations, task structure, and position power. Task-oriented leaders suit very favourable or unfavourable situations; relationship-oriented leaders suit moderate ones.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Kirkpatrick's four levels of training evaluation, in order, are:
questions.e: Kirkpatrick's sequence is Reaction (did they like it) -> Learning (what did they learn) -> Behaviour (did on-job behaviour change) -> Results (business impact). Each level is harder but more valuable to measure.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: BARS in performance appraisal stands for:
questions.e: BARS anchors each point of a rating scale with specific behavioural examples of good and poor performance. It reduces subjectivity compared to simple graphic rating scales.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Management by Objectives (MBO) was popularised by:
questions.e: Peter Drucker introduced MBO: superiors and subordinates jointly set goals, and performance is appraised against them. It shifts appraisal from traits to measurable results.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: 360-degree feedback collects performance input from:
o: Superiors, peers, subordinates, self and customers
questions.e: 360-degree appraisal gathers ratings from all around the employee — boss, peers, juniors, self, and sometimes customers — giving a rounded view and reducing single-rater bias.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: OCTAPACE culture, used in HRD climate surveys, does NOT include:
questions.e: OCTAPACE stands for Openness, Confrontation, Trust, Authenticity, Proaction, Autonomy, Collaboration, Experimentation. It is the classic Indian instrument for measuring HRD climate.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which training method is an off-the-job method?
questions.e: Vestibule training simulates the work environment away from the actual job (e.g., mock branch counters). Job rotation, coaching and understudy assignments are all on-the-job methods.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Alderfer's ERG theory differs from Maslow mainly because:
o: Needs can operate simultaneously and regress
questions.e: ERG (Existence, Relatedness, Growth) allows multiple needs to motivate at once and includes frustration-regression — if growth is blocked, relatedness needs intensify. Maslow's hierarchy is strictly sequential.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Reinforcement theory of motivation is associated with:
questions.e: B.F. Skinner's reinforcement theory says behaviour is shaped by its consequences: positive reinforcement, negative reinforcement, punishment and extinction. It focuses on observable behaviour, not inner needs.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Hersey-Blanchard situational leadership prescribes matching style to:
questions.e: The situational model says use telling (S1), selling (S2), participating (S3) or delegating (S4) styles according to the follower's competence and commitment (maturity) for the task.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which of the following is a hygiene factor as per Herzberg?
questions.e: Company policy, supervision, salary, working conditions and job security are hygiene factors — their absence dissatisfies, but their presence only brings neutrality. Recognition, achievement and responsibility are motivators.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Training Needs Analysis is conducted at which levels?
questions.e: TNA is three-tiered: organisational analysis (where training is needed strategically), task analysis (what the job requires), and person analysis (who needs it). Skipping TNA is why many training programmes fail.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Ohio State leadership studies identified which two dimensions?
questions.e: Ohio State researchers found leaders vary on initiating structure (task focus) and consideration (people focus) independently — a leader can be high on both, unlike earlier either-or views.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which appraisal method uses multiple exercises and multiple assessors?
questions.e: Assessment centres put candidates through simulations, group discussions, in-baskets and role plays observed by several trained assessors — the most valid but most expensive appraisal/selection method.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: McClelland's theory of needs emphasises:
questions.e: David McClelland identified three learned needs: nAch (achievement), nPow (power), nAff (affiliation). High nAch individuals prefer moderately challenging goals with personal responsibility and feedback.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Job enrichment, as per Herzberg, means:
o: Adding motivators like responsibility and growth to the job
Adding more tasks of the same level
questions.e: Job enrichment builds motivators (achievement, recognition, responsibility, advancement) into the job vertically. Merely adding similar tasks is job enlargement, which does not motivate.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which leadership style is most appropriate in a crisis requiring quick decisions?
questions.e: In emergencies, autocratic (telling) leadership enables fast, unambiguous decisions. Participative styles are better for commitment and creativity but are too slow when time is critical.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Succession planning in banks primarily addresses:
questions.e: Succession planning identifies and develops internal talent for critical roles, ensuring leadership continuity — vital for PSBs facing large-scale retirements.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: E-HRM refers to:
o: Electronic Human Resource Management using technology
questions.e: E-HRM is the application of web-based and digital technology to HR processes — e-recruitment, e-learning, HR portals, and increasingly HR analytics for data-driven workforce decisions.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which is an example of a self-actualisation need for a banker?
questions.e: Self-actualisation is realising one's full potential — leading a complex project or innovating a process. Security and canteen are lower-order (safety/physiological) needs.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Hawthorne studies, foundational to human relations, were led by:
questions.e: Elton Mayo's Hawthorne experiments showed productivity rose when workers felt observed and valued — the 'Hawthorne effect' — founding the human-relations movement in management.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A grievance procedure in banks is important because it:
o: Provides a formal channel to resolve employee complaints fairly
questions.e: A fair, time-bound grievance procedure lets employees raise issues without fear, preventing small complaints from becoming disputes and sustaining morale and industrial peace.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Performance appraisal is primarily used for all EXCEPT:
questions.e: Appraisal feeds promotions, training needs, increments and feedback — but CRR is a monetary-policy instrument set by RBI's MPC, entirely unrelated to HR appraisal.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which motivation theory is a 'process' theory rather than a 'content' theory?
questions.e: Content theories (Maslow, Herzberg, McClelland, Alderfer) list what motivates; process theories (Vroom, Adams, Skinner, Locke) explain how motivation works. Expectancy theory models the cognitive process of choosing effort levels.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The 5 Cs of credit appraisal are:
questions.e: The classic 5 Cs are Character (integrity), Capacity (repayment ability), Capital (own stake), Collateral (security), and Conditions (economic environment). All five must be satisfactory for a sound advance.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under the Tandon Committee norms, the first method of lending computes MPBF as:
questions.e: Tandon's Method 1: MPBF = 75% of (Current Assets minus Core Current Assets). Method 2 subtracts all current liabilities (other than bank borrowings) from 75% of current assets; the Chore Committee pushed Method 2.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An account is classified as NPA when interest/instalment remains overdue for more than:
questions.e: Under RBI's IRAC norms, a term-loan account becomes NPA when interest or instalment is overdue for more than 90 days. The 90-day norm has been the standard since 2004.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Provision required for the secured portion of a sub-standard asset is:
questions.e: Sub-standard assets (NPA up to 12 months) attract 15% provision on the secured portion and 25% on the unsecured portion. Doubtful assets attract 25/40/100% by age bucket.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Nayak Committee (1992) recommended which method for SSI working capital?
questions.e: The Nayak Committee recommended the turnover method for SSIs: working-capital requirement at 20% of projected annual turnover (25% for new units), with bank finance at 75% of that requirement.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: DSR (Debt Service Coverage Ratio) is computed as:
questions.e: DSCR measures cash available for debt service: (PAT + non-cash charges + interest) divided by (interest + principal instalments). Lenders normally want it at or above 1.25-1.5.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under SARFAESI, a secured creditor issues the demand notice under:
questions.e: Section 13(2) of SARFAESI requires a 60-day demand notice to the borrower before enforcement of security interest. The borrower can appeal to the DRT under Section 17.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Debts Recovery Tribunals have jurisdiction over debts of:
questions.e: DRTs (under the RDB Act, 1993) entertain applications where the debt is Rs.20 lakh or more. Smaller dues go to Lok Adalats or civil courts.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which committee recommended the second method of lending?
questions.e: The Chore Committee (1980) recommended shifting to the second method of lending (75% of current assets minus current liabilities) and penal interest for excess borrowings, tightening Tandon's framework.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A wilful defaulter is one who:
o: Fails due to genuine business losses
Diverts/siphons funds or doesn't pay despite capacity
questions.e: Wilful default covers diversion or siphoning of funds, disposal of security without knowledge, or non-payment despite adequate cash flows. Genuine business failure is not wilful default.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The RBI's prudential framework for resolution of stressed assets was issued in:
questions.e: The June 7, 2019 circular replaced earlier schemes (SDR, S4A, 5/25). It mandates a 30-day review period and 180-day implementation timeline with an inter-creditor agreement.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Commercial Paper in India is issued at:
questions.e: CP is a short-term unsecured promissory note issued at a discount to face value, with minimum denomination Rs.5 lakh. The discount represents the investor's return.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Factoring differs from forfaiting mainly in that:
o: Forfaiting is for domestic trade only
Factoring is with recourse, forfaiting is without recourse
questions.e: Domestic factoring is typically with recourse to the seller if the buyer defaults; forfaiting (used in exports) is without recourse — the forfaiter bears the full risk.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Expected Loss in credit risk measurement equals:
questions.e: EL = Probability of Default x Loss Given Default x Exposure at Default. It is the statistical average loss priced into lending margins; unexpected loss needs capital.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The compliance function in banks, per RBI guidelines, must be:
o: Independent with a Chief Compliance Officer
questions.e: RBI mandates an independent compliance function headed by a CCO, with a Board-approved compliance policy, annual compliance plan and compliance-risk assessment.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: GRC framework in banks stands for:
questions.e: GRC integrates Governance, Risk management and Compliance into one framework so that controls, risk appetite and regulatory obligations are managed coherently.
