questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under the Companies Act 2013, the maximum directors without special resolution is:
questions.e: Section 149 caps the board at 15 directors; exceeding 15 needs a special resolution. This frequently-tested number also appears in BRBL questions.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Cash credit differs from a term loan mainly because:
o: It is a running facility against working-capital security
questions.e: Cash credit is a revolving working-capital limit operated like a current account against hypothecation of stock/receivables, while term loans are fixed-tenor facilities for capital expenditure.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Credit derivatives like CDS are used by banks to:
o: Transfer credit risk to another party
questions.e: A credit default swap transfers the credit risk of a borrower to the protection seller for a premium. RBI permits banks limited participation in CDS markets.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Central Fraud Registry is maintained by:
questions.e: RBI's Central Fraud Registry (CFR) is a web-based searchable database of frauds reported by banks, accessible to banks for due diligence before lending.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In consortium lending, the arrangement is:
o: Multiple banks jointly finance with a common appraisal
One bank lends the full amount
questions.e: In consortium lending, several banks jointly fund a large borrower under common appraisal, documentation and sharing of security — used when exposure exceeds a single bank's appetite.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: RBI's fit-and-proper norms for bank directors primarily ensure:
o: Directors meet integrity, expertise and track-record standards
questions.e: Fit-and-proper criteria screen directors for integrity, professional competence, financial soundness and absence of disqualifications — a corporate-governance safeguard.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Provision on standard assets for commercial real estate exposure is:
questions.e: Standard-asset provisioning is 0.40% generally but higher for riskier segments — 1% for commercial real estate (and housing loans above thresholds). Always verify the current slab before the exam.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The first charge on a borrower's current assets for working-capital finance is usually by:
questions.e: Working-capital stock and receivables are charged by hypothecation — the borrower retains possession while the bank has the charge. Pledge needs possession transfer; mortgage is for immovable property.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Early warning signals in credit monitoring do NOT include:
questions.e: Timely servicing is a sign of health, not stress. Delays in statements, excesses, cheque bounces, diversion signals and auditor qualifications are classic early-warning signals of account stress.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: India follows which system of exchange-rate quotation?
questions.e: India uses direct quotation: foreign currency is the unit, e.g., USD/INR = 83.50 means one US dollar costs Rs.83.50. In indirect quotation the home currency would be the unit.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A Nostro account is:
o: Our account with a foreign bank in foreign currency
A foreign bank's account with us in rupees
questions.e: Nostro = 'our account with you' — the Indian bank's foreign-currency account maintained with an overseas correspondent bank. Vostro is the mirror: their rupee account with us.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Forward premium is annualised by the formula:
questions.e: Annualised premium/discount = (Forward - Spot)/Spot x (12/months) x 100. If forward exceeds spot, the foreign currency is at a premium; below spot, at a discount.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under FEMA, foreign-exchange contraventions are:
questions.e: FEMA 1999 decriminalised forex violations — contraventions attract civil penalties up to three times the amount involved. FERA 1973 had treated them as criminal offences.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under the LRS, Tax Collected at Source (TCS) applies on foreign remittances exceeding:
o: Rs.7 lakh in a financial year
Rs.10 lakh in a financial year
Rs.2.5 lakh in a financial year
Rs.25 lakh in a financial year
questions.e: Since 1 October 2023, TCS (20%, or 5% for education/medical) applies on LRS remittances above Rs.7 lakh per financial year per individual.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which NRI account is maintained in foreign currency with no exchange risk for the depositor?
questions.e: FCNR(B) deposits are denominated in designated foreign currencies, so the depositor faces no rupee depreciation risk; the bank bears the exchange risk. NRE/NRO are rupee accounts.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Documentary credits are governed internationally by:
questions.e: UCP 600 (Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits, ICC) governs letters of credit. URDG 758 covers demand guarantees; ISBP supplements UCP; INCOTERMS define delivery terms.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The ECGC of India primarily provides:
questions.e: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation covers exporters and banks against commercial and political risks in export credit — it is India's export credit agency, not a deposit insurer (that is DICGC).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An Authorised Dealer Category-I can:
o: Undertake all forex transactions permitted under FEMA
questions.e: AD Category-I (usually banks) may handle the full range of forex business — current and capital account transactions per FEMA. FFMCs and AD Cat-II/III have restricted licences.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: TT selling rate is derived from the interbank rate by:
questions.e: Banks add FEDAI-prescribed exchange margins to the interbank rate for selling forex to customers (TT selling = interbank + margin), and deduct margins for buying. The spread is the dealer's profit.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: If a customer cancels a forward purchase contract, the bank covers itself by:
questions.e: Cancellation reverses the original deal: a cancelled purchase contract means the bank sells the currency, so the bank applies the TT selling rate (opposite of the original purchase direction).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: SWIFT is:
o: A messaging network for financial institutions
questions.e: SWIFT is a Belgium-based cooperative messaging network carrying payment instructions between banks worldwide. It transmits messages; settlement happens through correspondent banking or RTGS.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Mirror accounts in forex accounting represent:
o: Nostro balances in the bank's own books
questions.e: The mirror account is the bank's own-book record of its Nostro account with the correspondent — the debit/credit mirror of the correspondent's statement, used for reconciliation.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Interest earned on NRO deposits in India is:
o: Fully taxable in India, with TDS
Taxed only if the NRI visits India
questions.e: Unlike NRE interest (exempt), NRO deposit interest is fully taxable in India and subject to TDS (DTAA relief may apply).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: External Commercial Borrowings in India are regulated by:
questions.e: RBI's ECB framework governs maturity periods, all-in-cost ceilings, recognised lenders, and permitted end-uses. Automatic and approval routes apply by sector and amount.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: UCP 600 Article on 'complying presentation' requires documents to be examined within:
questions.e: Under UCP 600, banks have a maximum of 5 banking days after presentation to determine compliance. The old UCP 500 allowed 7 days — a favourite exam trap.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A bill of lading serves as all EXCEPT:
questions.e: A bill of lading is a receipt, a document of title, and evidence of the carriage contract — but it is not an insurance policy. Banks insist on separate marine insurance documents.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Cross rate USD/INR 83.50 and EUR/USD 1.08 gives EUR/INR approximately:
questions.e: EUR/INR = EUR/USD x USD/INR = 1.08 x 83.50 = 90.18. Cross rates are derived by multiplying (or dividing) two rates sharing a common currency.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Unlike FERA, violations under FEMA are treated as:
o: Offences triable only by the Supreme Court
questions.e: FEMA (1999) decriminalised forex violations: contraventions are civil offences with monetary penalties, unlike FERA (1973) which treated them as criminal offences.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which account can a returning NRI maintain in foreign currency in India?
questions.e: The Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) account lets returning NRIs park foreign-currency assets in India. EEFC is for exporters' earnings; NRE/NRO are for non-residents.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In a direct quote USD/INR 83.20/83.30, the spread is:
questions.e: Spread = ask - bid = 83.30 - 83.20 = 0.10 (10 paise). The dealer buys dollars at 83.20 and sells at 83.30; the spread is the profit margin.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: LIBOR's replacement benchmark for USD is:
questions.e: After LIBOR's discontinuation, USD contracts transitioned to SOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate). India's MIBOR continues for rupee markets.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An Indian exporter wanting to hedge a 3-month USD receivable should:
questions.e: The exporter will receive dollars and fears rupee appreciation — so sell USD forward (lock in the rate). A forward sale is the classic export hedge.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Pre-shipment export credit in foreign currency is called:
questions.e: PCFC (Pre-shipment Credit in Foreign Currency) lets exporters borrow in foreign currency at international rates before shipment; post-shipment has its own rupee/foreign-currency variants.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The maximum usance normally allowed for import bills under UCP is:
questions.e: UCP 600 does not cap usance periods; tenor is a matter of the credit terms agreed between buyer and seller. RBI's trade-credit rules (not UCP) govern import financing periods.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Deemed exports under FTP are:
o: Supplies within India treated as exports for specified benefits
questions.e: Deemed exports are domestic supplies (e.g., to EOUs, SEZ developers, mega power projects) that earn specified FTP benefits though goods don't leave India.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An irrevocable letter of credit:
o: Cannot be amended/cancelled without beneficiary consent
Can be cancelled by the buyer anytime
questions.e: An irrevocable LC is a firm bank undertaking that cannot be amended or cancelled without the agreement of all parties including the beneficiary — the foundation of LC security.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In forex dealing, 'value date' means:
questions.e: Value date is when funds actually change hands: spot = T+2 (two business days), cash/tom = T+0/T+1, forwards = future agreed date. Deal date is when the rate is agreed.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A 'Loro' account refers to:
o: Our account with a foreign bank
A third bank's account referenced in correspondence
questions.e: Loro ('theirs') is how bank A refers to bank B's Nostro account with bank C — a third-party account in correspondence. Nostro = ours with you; Vostro = yours with us.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Exchange Earners' Foreign Currency (EEFC) account holders may retain:
questions.e: EEFC accounts let exporters and other earners retain 100% of forex earnings in foreign currency, with no interest, for paying import/fx obligations.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The FEDAI in India:
o: Prescribes rules for interbank forex deals and exchange margins
questions.e: The Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India frames market-conduct rules for ADs — including exchange-margin guidelines and code of conduct — complementing RBI regulation.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Back-to-back LCs are used when:
o: An intermediary uses the import LC as basis for an export LC
questions.e: In merchanting trade, the intermediary gets an export LC issued backed by the import LC received from the ultimate buyer — the first LC serves as security for the second.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Currency futures in India are traded on:
questions.e: Currency futures and options are exchange-traded on NSE, BSE and MSEI in pairs like USD-INR, EUR-INR, GBP-INR, JPY-INR, with standardised lots and daily mark-to-market.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A stronger rupee (appreciation) makes Indian exports:
questions.e: Rupee appreciation means foreigners need more of their currency per rupee, making Indian goods costlier abroad — hurting export competitiveness but cheapening imports.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The 'clean' instrument in forex remittance means:
questions.e: Clean remittances (e.g., TTs for services, family maintenance) move without shipping/trade documents attached, unlike documentary collections backed by bills of exchange and shipping papers.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An integrated treasury combines:
o: Forex, money market and securities desks
questions.e: An integrated treasury pools the forex, domestic money-market and securities operations so funding, trading and risk are managed centrally for efficiency and control.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A positive maturity gap (RSA > RSL) means:
questions.e: With more rate-sensitive assets than liabilities, rising rates reprice assets upward faster than liabilities, expanding the net interest margin. The reverse holds for a negative gap.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Duration gap is defined as:
questions.e: DGAP = duration of assets minus leverage-adjusted duration of liabilities. A positive DGAP means economic value of equity falls when interest rates rise.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Macaulay duration of a bond measures:
o: The price change for a 1% yield move
The time to the first coupon
The weighted average time to receipt of the bond's cash flows
The average maturity of the issuer's liabilities
questions.e: Macaulay duration is the cash-flow-weighted average time to receipt; modified duration (= Macaulay/(1+y/m)) measures price sensitivity to yield changes.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) comprises:
questions.e: LAF is RBI's daily window where banks borrow via repo and park surplus via reverse repo/SDF. MSF is the penal overnight window; OMO is outright purchase/sale.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate acts as:
o: The floor of the policy corridor
The ceiling of the policy corridor
questions.e: SDF (introduced 2022, replacing fixed-rate reverse repo) is the floor — banks park surplus with RBI without collateral. MSF is the ceiling; repo sits in between.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A bank's trading book contains:
o: Positions held for short-term trading profit
questions.e: The trading book holds instruments held for short-term resale or hedging trading positions, marked to market daily. The banking book holds loans and HTM investments at amortised cost.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Value at Risk (VaR) at 99% confidence over 10 days means:
o: Loss will not exceed VaR on 99% of 10-day periods
questions.e: VaR is a quantile: losses exceed the VaR number only 1% of the time over the horizon. It is not the worst-case loss — tail risk beyond VaR needs expected shortfall/stress tests.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Back-testing of VaR models compares:
questions.e: Back-testing counts how often actual trading losses exceeded the VaR estimate. Too many exceptions indicate the model understates risk and needs recalibration.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An interest-rate swap typically exchanges:
questions.e: A plain-vanilla IRS swaps fixed-for-floating interest payments on a notional principal (which is not exchanged). It converts the interest-rate character of liabilities or assets.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In a currency swap, parties exchange:
o: Principal and interest in different currencies
questions.e: A cross-currency swap exchanges principal at inception and maturity plus interest streams in two currencies — used to hedge long-term FX exposure or raise cheaper foreign funding.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The buyer of a call option on USD/INR benefits when:
questions.e: A USD call gives the right to buy dollars at the strike. If the rupee depreciates (USD/INR rises), the option is in-the-money — the classic importer hedge.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Option premium is paid by:
questions.e: The option buyer pays the premium to the writer (seller) for the right without obligation. Maximum loss for the buyer is limited to the premium paid.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Delta of an option measures:
o: Change in option price per unit change in underlying
questions.e: Delta is the first derivative of option price to the underlying price — the hedge ratio. Gamma measures delta's change; theta measures time decay; vega measures volatility sensitivity.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Basis risk in hedging arises when:
o: Spot and futures prices move differently
questions.e: Basis = spot - futures. If the basis changes unexpectedly between hedge initiation and lifting, the hedge leaves residual risk — this divergence is basis risk.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A long hedge using futures is appropriate for:
questions.e: A long hedge (buy futures) locks in purchase prices — suitable for someone who must buy later and fears prices rising. Short hedges protect sellers against falling prices.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Treasury bills in India are issued for maturities of:
questions.e: Government of India T-bills are issued for 14, 91, 182 and 364 days at a discount through auction. They are the benchmark short-term risk-free instruments.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The yield curve is normally:
questions.e: Normally longer maturities carry higher yields (term premium for risk and time). An inverted curve (short > long) often signals expected rate cuts or recession.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Stop-loss limits in treasury are meant to:
o: Cap the maximum loss on a position
questions.e: Stop-loss limits force dealers to square off positions once losses hit a preset threshold, preventing small losses from becoming catastrophic. They are a key market-risk control.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Arbitrage in treasury means:
o: Risk-free profit from price differences across markets
questions.e: Arbitrage exploits simultaneous price differences for the same instrument in different markets — e.g., currency arbitrage across centres — earning near-risk-free spreads.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The structural liquidity statement buckets:
o: Assets and liabilities by residual maturity
questions.e: The maturity ladder slots all cash inflows and outflows into time buckets (1-14 days, 15-28 days, etc.), revealing gaps where outflows exceed inflows — the core liquidity-risk view.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: RBI's LCR requirement for banks is a minimum of:
questions.e: Liquidity Coverage Ratio = HQLA / net 30-day cash outflows must be at least 100% — banks must hold enough high-quality liquid assets to survive 30 days of stress.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: NSFR (Net Stable Funding Ratio) requires:
o: Available stable funding >= required stable funding over one year
Daily cash balance of Rs.100 crore
questions.e: NSFR >= 100% ensures long-term assets are funded with stable liabilities over a one-year horizon, curbing excessive maturity transformation.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Macaulay duration of a zero-coupon bond equals:
questions.e: With no interim coupons, the weighted-average time to cash flows is simply the maturity itself. Coupon bonds have duration shorter than maturity.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A forward rate agreement (FRA) is used to:
o: Lock in a future interest rate
questions.e: An FRA is an OTC contract locking in an interest rate for a future period on a notional principal — banks use it to hedge upcoming borrowing/lending rate risk.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The 'banking book' interest-rate risk is measured by:
o: Earnings perspective (NII) and economic value perspective (EVE)
questions.e: IRRBB is assessed via both the earnings perspective (impact on NII over 12 months) and the economic value perspective (impact on EVE) — RBI's framework requires both.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Dealer limits in a treasury are approved by:
o: The Board / ALCO within the risk policy
questions.e: The Board sets the treasury policy with per-dealer, per-currency and stop-loss limits, monitored by mid-office and overseen by ALCO/RMC — never self-approved by dealers.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A negative duration gap implies that when interest rates rise:
questions.e: Negative DGAP means liabilities are longer-duration than assets, so rising rates reduce liability values more — economic value of equity increases. (Earnings view: negative repricing gap hurts NII.)

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Money-market mutual funds invest mainly in:
questions.e: Liquid/money-market funds hold T-bills, CP, CD and short-term instruments with maturity up to 91 days (liquid) — that is why banks' treasury desks track them.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The primary objective of ALM is to:
o: Manage interest-rate and liquidity risk while optimising NII
questions.e: ALM balances risk and return: it manages mismatches in repricing and maturity to protect NII and economic value while meeting liquidity needs — risk is managed, not eliminated.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Basel III minimum Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio is:
questions.e: Basel III requires CET1 of 4.5% of RWA, plus the 2.5% capital conservation buffer (total CET1 7%). Tier 1 minimum is 6% and total capital 8% before buffers.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Including the capital conservation buffer, Basel III total capital requirement is:
questions.e: 8% minimum total capital + 2.5% CCB = 10.5%. India adds its own overlay: minimum CRAR 9% plus 2.5% CCB = 11.5%.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: India's minimum CRAR requirement (excluding CCB) is:
questions.e: RBI requires minimum CRAR of 9% — one percentage point above Basel's 8% global floor. With the 2.5% CCB, Indian banks effectively need 11.5%.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Risk-weighted assets for market-risk capital charge are computed as:
questions.e: RWA = capital charge x 12.5 (the reciprocal of 8%), converting the market-risk capital requirement into risk-weighted-asset equivalents for the CRAR denominator.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under Basel III, the leverage ratio is a:
questions.e: The 3% leverage ratio (Tier 1 / total exposure) constrains balance-sheet growth regardless of risk weights, backstopping the risk-based framework. D-SIBs face 4% in India.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: D-SIBs currently designated in India include:
questions.e: RBI's Domestic Systemically Important Banks are SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank (in buckets with additional CET1 surcharges of 0.60%, 0.20% and 0.20% respectively).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The three pillars of Basel II are:
o: Minimum capital, supervisory review, market discipline
questions.e: Basel II's pillars: Pillar 1 (minimum capital requirements), Pillar 2 (supervisory review/ICAAP-SREP), Pillar 3 (market discipline via disclosure). Basel III retained and strengthened them.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The standardised approach for credit risk uses:
o: External credit ratings mapped to risk weights
questions.e: Under the standardised approach, exposures are risk-weighted per tables linked to external ratings (e.g., AAA corporate 20%, unrated 100%). IRB approaches use internal PD/LGD/EAD.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Foundation IRB differs from Advanced IRB in that:
o: Banks estimate only PD; LGD/EAD are supervisory
Banks estimate PD, LGD and EAD
questions.e: In Foundation IRB banks supply their own PD while LGD and EAD use supervisory values; in Advanced IRB banks estimate all three. Both need RBI approval.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: RAROC stands for and is used to:
o: Rate of return on cash; for liquidity
Real annual return on credit; for NPAs
Random return on capital; for trading
Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital; price loans for risk
questions.e: RAROC = risk-adjusted income / economic capital. Comparing RAROC with the hurdle rate tells whether a loan earns enough for the risk capital it consumes — the basis of risk-based pricing.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Operational risk under Basel III's final framework is measured by:
questions.e: Basel III final replaced AMA/BIA/TSA with the single Standardised Measurement Approach: capital = Business Indicator Component x Internal Loss Multiplier.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The countercyclical capital buffer ranges from:
questions.e: The CCyB (0-2.5% of RWA in CET1) is built up in credit booms and released in downturns. RBI has kept India's CCyB at zero, activating only if systemic risk warrants.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: ICAAP is:
o: The bank's internal capital adequacy assessment process
questions.e: The Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process is the bank's own forward-looking evaluation of capital needs under Pillar 2, covering risks beyond Pillar 1, reviewed by RBI under SREP.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A credit rating migration matrix shows:
o: Probabilities of ratings moving between grades
questions.e: Migration matrices give historical probabilities of an obligor moving from one rating grade to another (including default) over a horizon — key input for portfolio credit-risk models.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Securitisation's 'true sale' criterion ensures:
o: Assets are legally isolated from the originator
questions.e: True sale means the asset transfer is legally complete and bankruptcy-remote from the originator, so investors bear only asset risk. Without it, capital relief is denied.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The minimum retention requirement (MRR) in securitisation requires originators to retain:
o: At least 10% of book value (5% for certain assets)
questions.e: RBI's MRR (10% of book value; 5% for receivables with original maturity up to 24 months) forces skin-in-the-game so originators don't securitise and forget.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Large Exposures Framework caps a bank's exposure to a single counterparty at:
questions.e: RBI's LEF limits single-counterparty exposure to 20% of Tier 1 capital (extendable to 25% with board approval in exceptional cases) and groups to 25%, curbing concentration risk.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) is triggered by breaches in:
o: CRAR, net NPA and leverage ratios
questions.e: RBI's revised PCA framework uses three parameters — capital (CRAR), asset quality (net NPA ratio) and leverage — with risk thresholds triggering progressively tougher restrictions.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which risk is NOT covered under Pillar 1 minimum capital?
questions.e: Pillar 1 covers credit, market and operational risk. Reputational, strategic and concentration risks are Pillar 2 risks assessed under ICAAP/SREP.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The output floor under Basel III final (Basel IV) is set at:
questions.e: Modelled RWA cannot fall below 72.5% of standardised-approach RWA — the output floor limits the capital benefit of internal models, phased in from 2023.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Tier 2 capital includes:
questions.e: Tier 2 (gone-concern capital) includes subordinated debt, perpetual cumulative preference shares and general provisions (up to 1.25% of RWA). Equity and retained earnings are CET1.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds are characterised by:
questions.e: AT1 bonds are perpetual, with coupon discretion and write-down/conversion triggers at the point of non-viability — the Yes Bank AT1 write-down is the famous Indian case.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: HQLA in the LCR must consist mainly of:
o: Level 1 assets like cash and G-secs
questions.e: Level 1 HQLA — cash, RBI balances, and SLR-eligible G-secs — get 100% weight with no haircut. Level 2 assets face haircuts and a 40% cap.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Stress testing in banks is used to:
o: Assess resilience to extreme but plausible shocks
questions.e: Stress tests apply severe-but-plausible scenarios (rate spikes, defaults, liquidity freezes) to capital and earnings, informing contingency planning and ICAAP buffers.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The three lines of defence model places risk management in:
questions.e: First line = business units owning risk; second line = risk management and compliance setting frameworks; third line = internal audit providing independent assurance.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Country risk comprises:
questions.e: Country risk = sovereign risk (foreign government default) + transfer risk (inability to convert/repatriate due to exchange controls), plus political and contagion elements.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Credit concentration risk is best mitigated by:
questions.e: Single/group borrower caps, sector limits and geographic diversification prevent one default from threatening solvency — the rationale for the Large Exposures Framework.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A bank's economic capital differs from regulatory capital because it:
o: Reflects the bank's own risk assessment at its chosen confidence level
questions.e: Economic capital is internally modelled unexpected loss at the bank's target solvency standard (e.g., 99.97%); regulatory capital is the RBI-prescribed minimum. They often differ materially.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Wrong-way risk in derivatives means:
o: Exposure rises precisely when counterparty creditworthiness falls
questions.e: Wrong-way risk is adverse correlation between exposure and counterparty quality — e.g., selling protection to a bank whose health moves with the reference asset.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision is hosted by:
questions.e: BCBS operates under the Bank for International Settlements in Basel, Switzerland. Its standards (Basel I/II/III) are implemented nationally — in India by RBI.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Risk appetite statement of a bank is approved by:
questions.e: The Board approves the risk appetite — the quantum and type of risk the bank will take to meet strategy — and senior management implements it through limits and policies.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In the standardised approach, the risk weight for unrated corporate exposures is:
questions.e: Unrated corporates attract 100% risk weight under the standardised approach. Rated exposures vary: AAA 20%, A 50%, BBB 100%, below BB 150%.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Net Stable Funding Ratio became effective for Indian banks from:
questions.e: RBI implemented NSFR from 1 October 2021 (after deferrals), requiring available stable funding to cover required stable funding at 100% over one year.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A 'point of non-viability' (PONV) trigger applies to:
questions.e: AT1 and Tier 2 instruments carry contractual PONV triggers allowing write-down or conversion to equity if the bank becomes non-viable — the loss-absorption that defines gone-concern capital.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: RBI's September 2026 final directions on market-risk capital adopt:
questions.e: The September 2026 directions implement Basel III market-risk capital via the simplified standardised approach (interest-rate, equity, FX risk) effective 1 April 2027, with a trading/banking book boundary.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The current ratio is computed as:
questions.e: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities; the conventional bank norm is 1.33:1. Quick ratio excludes inventory; absolute liquid ratio uses only cash and marketable securities.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A proprietary ratio of 0.6 indicates:
o: 60% of assets funded by owners' funds
questions.e: Proprietary ratio = proprietors' funds / total assets. 0.6 means owners fund 60% of assets — higher is safer for long-term solvency, complementing the debt-equity ratio.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Interest coverage ratio below 1 implies:
questions.e: Interest coverage = EBIT / interest. Below 1 means operating profit cannot even cover interest — a red flag for lenders. Banks look for 2-3x coverage.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The DuPont identity decomposes ROE into:
o: Net margin x asset turnover x leverage
questions.e: DuPont: ROE = (Net profit/Sales) x (Sales/Assets) x (Assets/Equity). It reveals whether returns come from operational efficiency or financial leverage.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Higher inventory turnover indicates:
questions.e: Inventory turnover = COGS / average inventory; higher means stock converts to sales faster, freeing working capital. Abnormally high can also signal understocking.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Debtors collection period is computed as:
questions.e: Average collection period = (average debtors / net credit sales) x 365 days. Longer periods tie up working capital and raise default risk.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A steadily rising ROCE for a company generally signals:
o: Improving efficiency in generating profits from capital employed
questions.e: ROCE = PBIT/Capital employed; a rising trend means each rupee of capital is generating more operating profit — better capital efficiency.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL) equals:
questions.e: DOL = Contribution (sales - variable cost) / EBIT. High fixed costs magnify profit sensitivity to sales changes — the operating-risk measure.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Degree of Financial Leverage (DFL) equals:
questions.e: DFL = EBIT / EBT (earnings before tax). It captures how fixed interest charges magnify EPS sensitivity to EBIT changes — the financial-risk measure.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Combined leverage (DCL) is:
questions.e: DCL = DOL x DFL = Contribution/EBT, showing total EPS sensitivity to sales changes. Both leverages multiply, not add.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Cost of debt used in WACC is taken:
o: After tax: interest x (1 - tax rate)
questions.e: Interest is tax-deductible, so the effective cost is kd(1-t). This tax shield is why debt is cheaper than equity and central to MM-with-taxes.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: As per CAPM, cost of equity equals:
questions.e: CAPM: ke = risk-free rate + beta x market risk premium. Beta measures systematic risk; diversifiable risk earns no premium in the model.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A beta of 1.5 means the stock:
o: Is 50% more volatile than the market
questions.e: Beta 1.5 implies the stock moves 1.5x the market — 50% more systematic risk. Beta 1 = market risk; beta 0 = risk-free; negative beta moves inversely.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: WACC is the:
o: Weighted average of debt and equity costs; the project hurdle rate
questions.e: WACC = (E/V)ke + (D/V)kd(1-t). Projects earning above WACC create shareholder value; NPV discounts cash flows at WACC.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: MM theory WITHOUT taxes concludes:
o: Capital structure is irrelevant to firm value
questions.e: Modigliani-Miller (1958) no-tax: firm value depends only on operating cash flows, not debt-equity mix. With taxes, the interest shield makes debt valuable (trade-off theory).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Operating cycle = Inventory days + Receivables days. Net operating cycle subtracts:
questions.e: Net operating (cash conversion) cycle = inventory + receivable days - payable days. Longer cycles need more working-capital finance — the logic behind MPBF norms.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Fund flow statement analyses changes in:
questions.e: The fund flow statement explains sources and applications of working capital between two balance-sheet dates — complementing the cash flow statement (AS-3), which tracks cash.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Cash flow from operations is preferred by lenders for DSCR because:
o: It shows actual cash available for debt service
questions.e: Operating cash flow reflects real cash generation after working-capital changes — what actually services debt — unlike accounting profit which includes non-cash items.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Diluted EPS differs from basic EPS because it additionally includes:
o: Potential equity shares such as convertibles and ESOPs
questions.e: Diluted EPS divides earnings by (equity shares + dilutive potential shares like convertible debentures, warrants and ESOPs), showing the worst-case per-share figure.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Dividend payout ratio =
questions.e: Payout = dividend / profit after tax; retention = 1 - payout. Growth g = ROE x retention ratio in the sustainable-growth model.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Price-Earnings ratio =
questions.e: P/E = market price per share / EPS. High P/E implies growth expectations; it is the most-used relative valuation multiple.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Book value per share is:
questions.e: BVPS = equity (net worth) / outstanding shares. P/B compares market price to this accounting value — below 1 may signal undervaluation or distress.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The acid-test (quick) ratio excludes:
questions.e: Quick assets = current assets minus inventory (and prepaid expenses) — only near-cash items. The 1:1 norm tests immediate liquidity.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Gross profit margin =
questions.e: GP margin = (sales - COGS)/sales. It reflects production/pricing efficiency before operating expenses, interest and tax.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Capital gearing ratio compares:
questions.e: Capital gearing = equity share capital+reserves : preference+debentures. High gearing means heavy fixed-charge capital — riskier in downturns.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which ratio best measures long-term solvency?
questions.e: Debt-equity (long-term debt / equity) gauges the permanent financing mix and long-term solvency; the conventional norm is 2:1 for industry.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Trend analysis of financial statements is also called:
questions.e: Horizontal analysis compares line items across periods (trends); vertical analysis expresses each item as a percentage of a base (common-size statements) within one period.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Window dressing of financial statements refers to:
o: Manipulating accounts to show a better position
questions.e: Window dressing means cosmetic accounting manipulation (e.g., postponing purchases, channel stuffing) to flatter the balance sheet — a fraud red flag for analysts.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A high degree of operating leverage is risky because:
o: Small sales drops cause large EBIT falls
questions.e: High fixed costs mean EBIT swings violently with sales — great in booms, dangerous in slumps. That is why DOL measures business risk.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Retained earnings as a source of finance is:
o: Internal and cheapest in flotation terms
questions.e: Retained earnings are internal equity with no flotation cost and no obligation — the cheapest source, though shareholders expect returns on it (opportunity cost = ke).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Net Present Value is computed as:
questions.e: NPV = discounted future cash inflows minus the initial investment. Accept if NPV > 0 — it directly measures the absolute addition to shareholder wealth.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Internal Rate of Return is the discount rate at which:
questions.e: IRR solves NPV = 0. Accept projects where IRR exceeds the cost of capital. Multiple IRRs can arise with non-conventional cash flows — then prefer NPV.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Payback period's main weakness is that it:
o: Ignores time value of money and post-payback flows
questions.e: Simple payback counts years to recover cost, ignoring discounting and cash flows after payback. Discounted payback fixes the first flaw but not the second.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Profitability Index =
questions.e: PI = PV of future inflows / initial outlay. Accept if PI > 1. It is a relative measure — useful for ranking under capital rationing where NPV's absolute scale misleads.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In case of conflict between NPV and IRR for mutually exclusive projects:
questions.e: NPV measures absolute wealth creation and handles reinvestment at the cost of capital; IRR's reinvestment-at-IRR assumption and scale issues make NPV the superior rule in conflicts.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Sunk costs in capital budgeting should be:
questions.e: Sunk costs are past and irreversible — they cannot change whatever the decision, so including them distorts analysis. Only incremental future cash flows matter.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under the indirect method of cash-flow preparation, an increase in inventory during the year is:
o: Deducted from operating profit as a cash outflow
questions.e: A rise in inventory locks up cash, so it is deducted from PAT under operating activities; a fall in inventory is added back.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Opportunity cost of using owned land for a project should be:
o: Included at its market value forgone
questions.e: Using owned land sacrifices its next-best use (sale/rent). This forgone value is a real incremental cost of the project and must be included.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Risk-adjusted discount rate method handles project risk by:
o: Adding a risk premium to the discount rate
questions.e: Riskier cash flows are discounted at cost of capital + risk premium. Higher discounting shrinks PV — a simple, widely-used risk adjustment, though it compounds risk over time.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Certainty equivalent approach adjusts:
o: Cash flows downward for risk, then discounts at risk-free rate
questions.e: Certainty equivalents convert risky cash flows to their certain equivalents (multiplying by coefficients < 1) and discount at the risk-free rate — separating risk adjustment from time value.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A project with conventional cash flows has:
questions.e: Conventional cash flows (one sign change: outflow then inflows) yield a unique IRR. Non-conventional flows (multiple sign changes) can produce multiple IRRs.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Average Rate of Return (ARR) uses:
questions.e: ARR = average accounting profit / average investment. It is simple but flawed — it uses profit not cash and ignores time value, so it is the weakest appraisal method.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Capital rationing means:
questions.e: With limited capital, firms rank acceptable projects — PI (or NPV per rupee) guides selection to maximise total NPV within the budget constraint.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Sensitivity analysis in capital budgeting:
o: Tests how NPV changes with key variables
questions.e: Sensitivity analysis varies one input at a time (sales, cost, discount rate) to find NPV's break-even points — identifying which assumptions the decision hinges on.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Scenario analysis differs from sensitivity analysis because it:
questions.e: Scenario analysis builds consistent stories (base, optimistic, pessimistic) changing several variables together, unlike sensitivity's one-at-a-time approach.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Decision-tree analysis is most useful for:
o: Sequential decisions with probabilities at each stage
questions.e: Decision trees map sequential choices and chance nodes (e.g., expand if pilot succeeds), rolling back expected values — ideal for staged investments with abandonment options.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Real options in capital budgeting include:
o: Options to expand, abandon or defer a project
questions.e: Real options value managerial flexibility — expand if successful, abandon if not, defer timing. Traditional NPV understates projects with such flexibility.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The reinvestment assumption of IRR is that intermediate cash flows are reinvested at:
questions.e: IRR implicitly assumes reinvestment at the IRR — unrealistic for high IRRs. NPV assumes reinvestment at the cost of capital, which is why NPV wins conflicts.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Incremental cash flows exclude:
questions.e: Only cash flows that change because of the project count. Sunk costs are past; allocated fixed overheads continue regardless — both must be excluded.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A replacement decision should compare:
o: Incremental cash flows of new vs old
Old machine cost with new machine cost
questions.e: Replacement analysis compares the differential cash flows — operating savings, tax shields, salvage values — of keeping versus replacing, discounted appropriately.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: If NPV = Rs.50,000 at 10% and Rs.-10,000 at 15%, IRR is approximately:
questions.e: By interpolation: IRR = 10 + (50,000/(50,000+10,000)) x 5 = 10 + 4.17 = 14.17%. IRR lies closer to the rate with the smaller absolute NPV.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Discounted payback is superior to simple payback because it:
questions.e: Discounted payback discounts cash flows before cumulating, fixing simple payback's time-value flaw. It still ignores post-payback flows, unlike NPV.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Which method gives a percentage return measure?
questions.e: IRR expresses return as a percentage rate, intuitive for managers comparing with cost of capital. NPV gives absolute rupees; PI gives a ratio.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Working-capital investment in a project is treated as:
o: A cash outflow at start, recovered at end
questions.e: Net working capital tied up is a time-0 outflow; it is released (inflow) when the project ends. Ignoring it overstates project returns.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Equivalent annual annuity is used to compare:
o: Mutually exclusive projects with unequal lives
questions.e: EAA converts each project's NPV into an annualised equivalent, allowing fair comparison of different-lived alternatives — superior to the flawed shortest-common-life replication.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The cost of capital for a project should reflect:
o: The risk of the project's cash flows
questions.e: Discount rates must match project risk, not the firm's average — a risky new venture needs a higher hurdle than the firm's WACC. Using WACC for all projects misprices risk.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Post-completion audit of projects helps to:
questions.e: Comparing actual vs projected cash flows reveals systematic biases (optimism in sales, cost underestimation), improving future forecasts and accountability.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A project with PI of 1.25 means:
o: Every rupee invested returns Rs.1.25 in PV terms
questions.e: PI 1.25 = PV of inflows is 1.25x the outlay — a 25% PV surplus per rupee invested. Accept since PI > 1 (equivalent to NPV > 0).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Monte Carlo simulation in capital budgeting:
o: Generates a probability distribution of NPV from random inputs
questions.e: Monte Carlo samples thousands of random input combinations per their distributions, producing an NPV distribution — showing not just expected value but the probability of loss.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The 'abandonment option' adds value when:
o: Management can exit a failing project and recover salvage
questions.e: The right to abandon truncates downside — if cash flows disappoint, exit and salvage. This flexibility has positive option value that static NPV misses.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A forward contract is:
o: OTC, customised and binding on both parties
questions.e: Forwards are over-the-counter, tailor-made, and obligate both parties to perform at maturity — unlike options which give a right. Their customisation creates counterparty risk.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Futures differ from forwards mainly because futures are:
questions.e: Futures trade on exchanges with standard lots/dates, daily MTM settlement and margins via a clearing house — eliminating the counterparty risk of OTC forwards.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The writer of a put option:
o: Has the obligation to buy if exercised
questions.e: The put writer receives the premium but must buy the underlying at the strike if the holder exercises. Writers have obligations; buyers have rights.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Intrinsic value of a call option =
questions.e: Intrinsic value is the in-the-money amount: spot minus strike for calls (floored at zero). Option price = intrinsic value + time value.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Theta of an option measures:
questions.e: Theta is the daily erosion of option value as expiry nears — time decay accelerates for at-the-money options. Long option holders fight theta; writers collect it.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Vega measures sensitivity to:
questions.e: Vega = change in option price per 1% change in implied volatility. Higher volatility raises both call and put values since it increases the chance of finishing in-the-money.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Black-Scholes model values:
questions.e: The classic Black-Scholes formula prices European options (exercisable only at expiry) on non-dividend-paying underlyings using spot, strike, rate, time and volatility.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A collar strategy (long put + short call) is used to:
o: Protect downside cheaply by capping upside
questions.e: Buying a protective put funded by selling a call creates a zero/low-cost collar — downside protected below the put strike, gains capped at the call strike.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In a plain-vanilla interest-rate swap, the notional principal is:
questions.e: IRS notionals are reference amounts for computing interest — only net interest differences change hands. Currency swaps, by contrast, do exchange principals.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Hedging with derivatives aims to:
questions.e: Hedgers use derivatives to offset an existing exposure (export receivable, bond portfolio), sacrificing upside to remove downside — the opposite of speculation.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The dividend discount model values a share as:
questions.e: Gordon model: P0 = D1/(ke-g) for constant-growth dividends. It suits mature dividend-paying firms; high-growth firms need multi-stage DCF.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Terminal value in DCF commonly uses:
questions.e: Beyond the forecast horizon, remaining cash flows are valued as a growing perpetuity. Terminal value often dominates total DCF value — a key sensitivity.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Enterprise Value (EV) =
questions.e: EV = equity market value + debt + minority interest - cash. EV/EBITDA compares firms independent of capital structure, unlike P/E.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A conglomerate merger is between:
questions.e: Conglomerate mergers combine unrelated businesses (diversification motive). Horizontal = competitors; vertical = supply-chain stages.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Synergy in M&A means:
o: Combined value exceeds sum of parts
questions.e: Synergy — revenue, cost or financial — is the value created by combination. Paying more than standalone value + synergy destroys shareholder wealth.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A poison pill defence against takeovers:
o: Dilutes the acquirer's stake via discounted share issue
questions.e: Poison pills (shareholder rights plans) let existing shareholders buy shares cheaply if a bidder crosses a threshold, making the takeover prohibitively expensive.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A white knight in takeovers is:
o: A friendly acquirer sought by target management
questions.e: Targets facing hostile bids invite a white knight — a preferred acquirer — to outbid the raider on friendlier terms.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under the Companies Act 2013, mergers require approval of:
questions.e: Schemes of merger/amalgamation need National Company Law Tribunal sanction (plus shareholder/creditor majorities) — the statutory route for bank and corporate mergers.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Greenmail as a takeover defence means:
o: Target buys back the raider's stake at a premium
questions.e: Greenmail = the target repurchases the hostile bidder's shares at a premium to make them go away — controversial since it rewards the raider.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Venture capital typically invests in:
questions.e: VCs fund startups past the seed stage with equity for high growth, exiting via IPO or acquisition. Angel investors come earlier; private equity targets mature firms.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Mezzanine finance is:
questions.e: Mezzanine sits between debt and equity — subordinated debt with warrants or conversion rights, offering higher returns for higher risk in LBOs and growth funding.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A SPAC is:
o: A shell company raising IPO money to acquire a private firm
questions.e: Special Purpose Acquisition Companies list as cash shells and then merge with a target — a faster public-listing route, though with investor-protection concerns.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Free cash flow to firm (FCFF) =
o: EBIT(1-t) + depreciation - capex - change in WC
questions.e: FCFF = after-tax operating profit + non-cash charges - capital expenditure - working-capital investment — the cash available to all investors, discounted at WACC.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The P/B multiple is most meaningful for:
questions.e: Price-to-book suits asset-heavy businesses (banks, NBFCs) where balance-sheet value anchors worth. It is meaningless for asset-light or negative-equity firms.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Descriptive, predictive and prescriptive analytics represent:
questions.e: Descriptive (what happened), predictive (what will happen), prescriptive (what should we do) — increasing sophistication, used in credit scoring and fraud analytics.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Crowdfunding for startups in India is regulated for:
o: Equity crowdfunding is restricted; donation/reward models operate
questions.e: SEBI has not permitted public equity crowdfunding; donation/reward-based platforms operate while equity/debt fundraising must follow private-placement norms.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An angel investor differs from a VC mainly in:
o: Investing own money at earlier stages
questions.e: Angels invest personal wealth in very early (seed) rounds; VCs deploy pooled fund money at later stages with formal due diligence and board seats.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The payback of green bonds is distinguished by:
questions.e: Green bonds are standard bonds whose use-of-proceeds is ring-fenced for green projects with impact reporting — pricing is otherwise market-driven.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In DCF valuation, WACC is used to discount:
questions.e: FCFF belongs to all capital providers, so it is discounted at WACC (blended cost). FCFE (to equity holders) is discounted at cost of equity.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A leveraged buyout (LBO) is financed primarily with:
o: Debt secured on the target's assets
questions.e: LBOs use heavy debt — often secured against the target's own assets and cash flows — with a small equity cheque, amplifying returns (and risk) for sponsors.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was constituted on:
questions.e: RBI was established under the RBI Act 1934 and commenced operations on 1 April 1935. It was nationalised in 1949.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 42 of the RBI Act empowers RBI to prescribe:
questions.e: Section 42 governs the Cash Reserve Ratio for scheduled banks. The 2006 amendment removed the 3% floor and 20% ceiling, giving RBI full flexibility.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: SLR for scheduled banks is maintained under:
questions.e: Section 24 of the BR Act requires banks to maintain SLR (currently 18%) in cash, gold or approved securities. Section 42 RBI Act is CRR.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Banking is defined in which section of the BR Act?
questions.e: Section 5(b) defines 'banking' as accepting deposits for lending/investment, repayable on demand or otherwise. Section 6 lists permissible business.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 17 of the BR Act requires banks to transfer to the statutory reserve fund:
questions.e: Every banking company must transfer at least 25% of its annual net profit to the reserve fund before declaring dividends — the statutory plough-back.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under Section 9 of the BR Act, non-banking assets must be disposed of within:
questions.e: Immovable property acquired in satisfaction of debts (non-banking assets) must be disposed of within 7 years (extendable by RBI by up to 5 years) — banks are not estate agents.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 8 of the BR Act:
questions.e: Section 8 bars banking companies from trading in goods (buying/selling/bartering), except in realisation of security — banking is financial intermediation, not commerce.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: RBI's power to inspect banks flows from:
questions.e: Section 35 empowers RBI to inspect any banking company and its books. Section 35A lets RBI issue directions to banks generally or specifically.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 26 of the BR Act requires a return on unclaimed deposits within:
questions.e: Banks file the Section 26 return within 30 days after each calendar year-end; balances unclaimed for 10+ years go to RBI's DEAF.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under Sections 45ZA-45ZF of the Banking Regulation Act, nomination for a deposit account can be made in favour of:
questions.e: The BR Act nomination facility is available only for individuals (a minor can be nominated with a guardian named); non-individuals cannot be nominees.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 20 of the BR Act restricts:
o: Loans against own shares and to directors
questions.e: Section 20 bars advances against the bank's own shares; Section 20A restricts loans to directors and firms where directors are interested — classic governance safeguards.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Banking Regulation Act originally applied as:
questions.e: Enacted as the Banking Companies Act 1949, it was renamed the Banking Regulation Act in 1966 when extended to cooperative banks.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Minimum capital requirements for banking companies are in:
questions.e: Section 11 prescribes minimum paid-up capital and reserves (Rs.5 lakh for Indian banks with multi-state presence, varying by area) — since superseded by RBI licensing norms.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 35A of the BR Act empowers RBI to:
questions.e: Section 35A is RBI's omnibus power to issue directions to banks in public interest or to prevent detrimental conduct — the basis of most RBI circulars.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Moratorium on a banking company can be imposed under:
questions.e: RBI may apply to the government for a moratorium (up to 6 months) under Section 45 while framing a reconstruction/amalgamation scheme — used in Yes Bank (2020) and Lakshmi Vilas Bank.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The preamble of the RBI Act states its objective as:
o: Regulating currency and securing monetary stability
questions.e: The preamble mandates RBI to regulate the issue of bank notes, keep reserves for monetary stability, and operate the currency and credit system to the country's advantage.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 22 of the RBI Act gives RBI:
questions.e: Section 22 confers the monopoly of bank-note issue (except Re 1 notes/coins issued by Government of India). Section 24 fixes note denominations.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under Section 19 of the BR Act, a bank's subsidiary holdings are:
o: Restricted to specified purposes and limits
questions.e: Section 19 permits subsidiaries only for specified purposes (e.g., businesses under Section 6) within holding limits — preventing banks from running unrelated empires.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: RBI can supersede a bank's board under:
questions.e: Section 36ACA lets RBI supersede the board of a banking company for up to 12 months in public interest — invoked for several weak banks and NBFCs.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation insures deposits up to:
questions.e: DICGC cover is Rs.5 lakh per depositor per bank (principal + interest), raised from Rs.1 lakh in February 2020. It covers all commercial and eligible cooperative banks.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Priority-sector lending certificates (PSLCs) are traded on:
questions.e: PSLCs trade on RBI's e-Kuber portal in four categories (agriculture, small/marginal farmers, micro enterprises, general) — letting surplus banks sell to deficit banks.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Ombudsman complaints about banks now go to:
questions.e: The 2021 Integrated Ombudsman unified the banking, NBFC and digital-transactions schemes with centralised receipt (CRPC) and appeal to RBI's Executive Director.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 45W of the RBI Act empowers RBI to regulate:
questions.e: Section 45W (with definitions in 45U) gives RBI authority over derivatives, repo and money-market instruments — the legal basis for forex-derivative and interest-derivative directions.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A scheduled bank is one:
o: Included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act
questions.e: Scheduled banks are those in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act 1934 (paid-up capital + reserves >= Rs.5 lakh and satisfying RBI) — eligible for RBI refinance and membership benefits.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Cash reserve under Section 18 of the BR Act applies to:
questions.e: Section 18 imposes a 3% cash reserve on non-scheduled banks (demand and time liabilities), while scheduled banks follow Section 42 of the RBI Act.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 29 of the BR Act mandates:
o: Balance sheet and P&L in prescribed forms
questions.e: Section 29 requires accounts in the Third Schedule forms (Form A balance sheet, Form B P&L); Section 30 mandates audit; Section 31 requires publication.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: RBI's monetary policy committee has:
questions.e: MPC has 6 members — 3 RBI officials (Governor as chair with casting vote) and 3 government nominees — deciding the policy repo rate by majority.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The flexible inflation-targeting framework mandates CPI inflation of:
questions.e: The government-set target is 4% CPI (combined) with a +/-2% tolerance band. Breaches for three consecutive quarters require RBI to report to the government.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Bank Rate and MSF rate are:
o: Aligned — MSF is linked to Bank Rate
questions.e: The Marginal Standing Facility rate equals the Bank Rate (a penal overnight window). Both sit above the repo rate as the corridor ceiling.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Open Market Operations (OMO) by RBI involve:
questions.e: OMOs are outright secondary-market purchases/sales of government securities to inject or absorb durable liquidity — distinct from repo (temporary) operations.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 138 of the NI Act deals with:
o: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency of funds
questions.e: Section 138 criminalises cheque bounce due to insufficient funds. The payee must issue a written demand within 30 days of return and the drawer gets 15 days to pay before prosecution.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Protection to a collecting banker is available under:
questions.e: Section 131 protects a collecting banker who credits a customer in good faith and without negligence. Section 85 protects the paying banker; Section 10 defines payment in due course.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A 'holder in due course' under the NI Act is one who:
o: Takes it for consideration, in good faith, before maturity
questions.e: Section 9: a holder in due course takes a negotiable instrument for consideration, in good faith and without notice of defects, before maturity — getting title free of prior defects.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Material alteration of a negotiable instrument:
o: Renders it void against non-consenting parties
questions.e: Under Section 87, material alteration (amount, date, payee) without consent voids the instrument except against the alterer and subsequent consenting parties.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A cheque crossed 'A/c Payee' instructs the paying banker to:
o: Pay cash across the counter to anyone
Credit the amount only to the payee's bank account
questions.e: An 'A/c Payee' crossing directs that payment be made only by credit to the payee's account, making the cheque non-transferable in practice.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Section 118 of the NI Act lays down:
questions.e: Section 118 presumes consideration, date, time of acceptance/transfer and holder status — the complainant need not prove these; the accused must rebut them.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under the NI Act, a cheque is an instrument that is always:
questions.e: Section 6 defines a cheque as a bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker and payable on demand — 'payable on demand' is its essential trait.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The validity period of a cheque in India is:
questions.e: RBI reduced cheque validity from 6 months to 3 months from the date of issue (April 2012) to curb fraud and align with CTS.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Payment in due course (Section 10) requires payment:
o: In good faith, without negligence, to the person in possession
questions.e: Payment in due course must follow the apparent tenor, be in good faith and without negligence, to the person in possession entitled to receive it — the paying banker's shield.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An 'account payee' crossing:
o: Is a direction to collect only for the payee's account
questions.e: Account-payee crossing (a banking practice, not in the NI Act text) directs the collecting bank to credit only the named payee's account — the strongest practical safeguard.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under the Indian Contract Act, a proposal is defined in:
questions.e: Section 2(a) defines proposal (offer); 2(b) acceptance; 2(d) consideration; 2(h) contract. Section 10 lists essentials of a valid contract.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Consideration under Section 2(d) must be:
o: At the desire of the promisor, lawful and real
questions.e: Consideration need not be adequate (courts don't weigh value) but must be at the promisor's desire, lawful, real and not past (with exceptions like Section 25).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Free consent (Section 14) is vitiated by all EXCEPT:
questions.e: Coercion (15), undue influence (16), fraud (17), misrepresentation (18) and mistake (20-22) vitiate free consent. Proper independent advice actually supports valid consent.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A contract with a minor is:
questions.e: Per Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose, agreements with minors are void from the start — though minors can be beneficiaries and necessaries supplied can be claimed from their property (Section 68).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Surety's liability under a contract of guarantee is:
o: Co-extensive with principal debtor unless agreed otherwise
questions.e: Section 128: the surety's liability is co-extensive with the principal debtor's — the creditor may proceed against the surety without first exhausting remedies against the debtor.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A contract of indemnity is defined in:
questions.e: Section 124 defines indemnity (promising to save another from loss); Section 126 defines guarantee; 148 bailment; 182 agency. Bank guarantees are the everyday example.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Bailment under Section 148 requires:
o: Delivery of goods for a purpose with return/redelivery
questions.e: Bailment = delivery of goods by one person to another for some purpose, on condition they be returned or disposed of per directions — e.g., pledged goods, safe custody.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An agent's authority to bind the principal flows from:
questions.e: Section 182 defines agent and principal; Section 188-189 set the agent's authority. Acts within authority bind the principal (Section 226-227).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Contingent contracts are defined in:
questions.e: Section 31: a contingent contract depends on a collateral uncertain event (e.g., insurance). Section 32 governs enforcement; Section 36 covers impossible events.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Liquidated damages vs penalty (Section 74) — Indian position:
o: Reasonable compensation up to the named sum, penalty label not decisive
questions.e: Section 74 allows reasonable compensation not exceeding the sum named, regardless of the penalty label — courts assess actual loss (Fate Chand v. Balkishan Dass).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Quasi-contracts are covered by:
questions.e: Sections 68-72 impose obligations resembling contracts without agreement — necessaries for minors, money paid by an interested person, finder of goods, etc.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Novation under Section 62 means:
o: Substitution of a new contract for the old
questions.e: Novation substitutes a new contract — with new parties or terms — extinguishing the original. It requires all parties' consent.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Limitation Act prescribes for suits on bills of exchange:
questions.e: Suits on bills of exchange/promissory notes: 3 years from due date. Mortgage suits: 12 years. Banks diarize limitation to avoid time-barred debts.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: An agreement in restraint of trade is:
o: Void under Section 27 with narrow exceptions
questions.e: Section 27 voids agreements restraining lawful trade/profession, except sale of goodwill and (post-2013 amendments context) reasonable employee non-competes during employment.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Acceptance of a proposal must be:
questions.e: Section 7: acceptance must be absolute, unqualified and communicated in the prescribed manner. Conditional acceptance is a counter-offer.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: SARFAESI applies to secured debts of:
o: Rs.1 lakh and above where the account is NPA
questions.e: SARFAESI covers secured debts of Rs.1 lakh and above (and 20%+ of principal outstanding) where security interest is created and the account is classified NPA. Agricultural land is excluded.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under SARFAESI Section 13(4), on default the secured creditor may:
o: Take possession, sell, assign or manage the secured asset
questions.e: After the 60-day notice, Section 13(4) permits taking possession, sale/lease/assignment, taking over management, or appointing a manager — without court intervention.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Appeal against SARFAESI action lies to the DRT under:
questions.e: Section 17 lets the aggrieved borrower/guarantor appeal to the DRT within 45 days of measures taken, on deposit of 50% (DRT may reduce to 25%) of the debt.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Central Registry under SARFAESI (CERSAI) registers:
questions.e: CERSAI (Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest) records mortgages and security interests, preventing multiple financing on the same asset.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Assistance of the District Magistrate under SARFAESI is sought under:
questions.e: Section 14 empowers the CMM/DM to assist secured creditors in taking possession of secured assets — a frequently tested procedural section.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Lok Adalats can settle bank dues up to:
questions.e: Debt Recovery Tribunals handle Rs.20 lakh+; Lok Adalats (under the Legal Services Authorities Act) settle smaller bank dues up to Rs.20 lakh with awards deemed civil-court decrees.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: IBC's Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process must normally complete within:
questions.e: CIRP: 180 days + one 90-day extension, with an overall outer limit of 330 days including litigation time. Beyond that, liquidation follows.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under IBC, the Committee of Creditors approves a resolution plan with:
questions.e: CoC decisions need 66% of voting share (financial creditors weighted by debt). Liquidation needs 66% too; earlier the threshold was 75%.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Moratorium under IBC Section 14:
o: Prohibits suits, asset transfers and recovery actions during CIRP
questions.e: The Section 14 moratorium freezes institution/continuation of suits, asset alienation and recovery enforcement — giving the resolution professional calm-time to find a buyer.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Financial creditor initiates CIRP under IBC:
questions.e: Section 7 = financial creditor application; Section 8-9 = operational creditor (after 10-day demand notice); Section 10 = corporate applicant itself. Minimum default threshold is Rs.1 crore.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The waterfall for distribution in liquidation is in IBC:
questions.e: Section 53 sets the priority waterfall: insolvency costs, secured creditors, workmen, employees, unsecured financial creditors, government dues, and finally equity.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Consumer commissions' pecuniary jurisdiction under CPA 2019: District Commission up to:
questions.e: CPA 2019: District up to Rs.50 lakh, State Rs.50 lakh-2 crore, National above Rs.2 crore. The 1986 Act had lower slabs (20 lakh/1 crore).

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The CCPA under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 can:
o: Investigate unfair trade practices and order recalls/refunds
questions.e: The Central Consumer Protection Authority investigates, orders discontinuation of unfair practices, product recalls and refunds — with penalties for misleading ads and endorsements.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under PMLA, suspicious transaction reports (STRs) must reach FIU-IND within:
questions.e: Banks file STRs within 7 days of the suspicion arising; Cash Transaction Reports (over Rs.10 lakh) and counterfeit reports go monthly by the 15th.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: KYC/AML guidelines for banks are issued by RBI under:
o: PMLA and RBI's Master Direction on KYC
questions.e: RBI's Master Direction on KYC (updated periodically) operationalises PMLA obligations — CDD, beneficial-ownership identification, ongoing monitoring and record-keeping.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Mortgage by deposit of title deeds is called:
questions.e: Section 58(f), Transfer of Property Act: depositing title deeds with intent to create security = equitable mortgage — no registration needed in notified towns, making it the bankers' favourite.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: In an English mortgage:
o: Ownership is transferred with a buy-back condition
questions.e: English mortgage (Sec 58(e)): mortgagor transfers ownership absolutely with a condition of retransfer on repayment — used in some corporate loans.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Registration of charges with the RoC under Companies Act 2013 (Section 77) must be within:
questions.e: Charges created by companies must be registered with the Registrar within 30 days (extendable with fees). Unregistered charges are void against liquidators/creditors.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The IT Act 2000 gives legal validity to:
questions.e: The IT Act grants electronic records and digital/electronic signatures the same legal validity as paper — the foundation of e-banking, e-contracts and e-filings.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: RTI Act 2005 applies to:
questions.e: RTI covers public authorities — government bodies and substantially financed entities. Private banks are generally outside RTI, though RBI as regulator is covered.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: A 'wilful defaulter' under RBI norms faces:
o: Debarment from fresh finance and publication of name
questions.e: Wilful defaulters are barred from additional facilities, launching ventures for 5 years, and accessing capital markets; lenders publish their names — the strictest credit-discipline tool.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code consolidated earlier laws including:
o: SICA, RDDBFI provisions and Presidency Towns Insolvency Act
questions.e: IBC 2016 replaced the Sick Industrial Companies Act, parts of RDDBFI and the old provincial insolvency acts — creating one time-bound insolvency framework.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Fast-track CIRP under IBC applies to:
questions.e: Fast-track insolvency for small companies and startups: 90 days with a single 45-day extension — half the standard timeline.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under the Partnership Act 1932, registration of a firm is:
questions.e: Registration is optional, but unregistered firms cannot sue to enforce contractual rights (Section 69) — so banks prefer lending to registered firms.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: LLP combines:
questions.e: The LLP Act 2008 gives partners limited liability (like a company) with internal flexibility of a partnership — popular for professional firms.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: NABARD was set up in 1982 on the recommendation of the:
questions.e: The Sivaraman Committee (1979) recommended a dedicated apex refinance institution for agriculture and rural development, leading to NABARD's creation on 12 July 1982.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Under KCC, the effective interest for prompt-paying farmers on crop loans up to Rs.3 lakh is:
questions.e: Crop loans up to Rs.3 lakh carry 7% with a 3% prompt-repayment subvention — effective 4%. Allied activities (fisheries/dairy) get up to Rs.2 lakh under KCC.

questions.subject: CAIIB
questions.q: Priority-sector lending target for banks is:
