questions.q: Housing loans qualifying for priority sector are subject to:
o: Prescribed loan-amount and per-unit cost caps
questions.e: Only housing loans within RBI-prescribed amount and dwelling-unit cost caps (higher for metros) count as PSL — targeting affordable housing, not luxury homes.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Under the MSME definition, enterprises are classified by:
o: Investment in plant & machinery/equipment and annual turnover
questions.e: The 2020 definition (limits enhanced in 2025) classifies micro, small and medium enterprises by twin criteria — investment and turnover — replacing the old manufacturing/services split. Udyam registration is the single-window enrolment.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Drawings made by the proprietor for personal use:
o: Are recorded as a business expense
questions.e: Drawings are debited to the capital/drawings account and reduce capital; they are not a business expense.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: 'Debit the receiver, credit the giver' applies to:
questions.e: Personal accounts (debtors, creditors): debit the receiver, credit the giver. Real accounts (assets): debit what comes in, credit what goes out. Nominal (income/expenses): debit expenses/losses, credit incomes/gains.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: 'Debit what comes in, credit what goes out' applies to:
questions.e: Real accounts record assets: debit on acquisition (what comes in), credit on disposal (what goes out). Cash, machinery and stock are real accounts.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: 'Debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains' applies to:
questions.e: Nominal accounts capture income and expenditure for the period (salaries, rent, interest) and are closed to the Profit & Loss Account at year-end.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The going concern concept assumes:
o: The business will continue for the foreseeable future
The business will close this year
questions.e: Going concern justifies charging depreciation over useful life and classifying assets/liabilities as long-term. If it fails, accounts are drawn up on liquidation basis.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The prudence (conservatism) convention means:
o: Provide for anticipated losses, never anticipate profits
Record assets at market value always
questions.e: Prudence underlies NPA provisioning, provision for doubtful debts and stock valued at cost-or-market-price-whichever-is-lower. It guards against overstating financial strength.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: A trial balance primarily checks:
questions.e: The trial balance verifies that total debits equal total credits, but it cannot detect errors of omission, principle, original entry, or compensating errors.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Which error is NOT disclosed by a trial balance?
o: An error of principle (e.g. capital expenditure debited to revenue)
A casting error in a ledger
Omission of one leg of an entry
questions.e: Errors of principle, omission of both legs, compensating errors and errors of original entry keep debits equal to credits, so the trial balance still tallies.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Depreciation is:
o: A non-cash allocation of an asset's cost over its useful life
The same as amortisation of goodwill in all cases
questions.e: Depreciation spreads cost (matching concept) without cash outflow; it is added back in cash-flow statements. Land is generally not depreciated.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Under the straight-line method of depreciation:
o: An equal charge is made every year
questions.e: Straight-line: (cost − scrap) ÷ useful life each year. Written-down-value applies a fixed percentage to the diminishing balance, giving higher early charges.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Banks prepare their balance sheet as per:
o: Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013
The Third Schedule of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
questions.e: Banking companies follow the BR Act's Third Schedule vertical formats for balance sheet and P&L, unlike other companies which follow Companies Act Schedule III.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Under Section 17 of the BR Act, banks must transfer to the statutory reserve:
o: 25% of net profit before declaring dividend
questions.e: Section 17 requires transfer of at least 25% (the practice: 25%) of net profit to the reserve fund before any dividend. The reserve strengthens the capital base.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The current ratio is:
o: Total assets divided by total liabilities
Current assets divided by current liabilities
questions.e: Current ratio tests short-term solvency; 2:1 is the traditional benchmark. Quick ratio excludes inventory and prepaid expenses for a stricter test.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The debt–equity ratio measures:
o: Long-term solvency — long-term debt relative to equity
questions.e: D/E = long-term debt ÷ shareholders' funds. A lower ratio means less financial risk; lenders prefer moderate leverage so equity cushions their exposure.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Return on equity (ROE) is:
o: Profit after tax divided by shareholders' funds
questions.e: ROE measures returns to owners; ROA uses total assets. Banks target ROE through leverage and NIM, constrained by capital adequacy.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The interest coverage ratio is:
questions.e: Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest; it shows how comfortably operating profit services interest. DSCR additionally covers principal instalments.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Contribution in marginal costing is:
questions.e: Contribution = sales − variable cost; P/V ratio = contribution ÷ sales. Break-even sales = fixed cost ÷ P/V ratio — the no-profit-no-loss level.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: A cash-flow statement (AS-3/Ind AS-7) classifies flows into:
questions.e: Operating (core business cash), investing (assets/investments), financing (debt/equity/dividends). It explains why profit and cash differ.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Basel III minimum CRAR for Indian banks, including the capital conservation buffer, is:
questions.e: RBI requires 9% CRAR plus a 2.5% capital conservation buffer = 11.5% effective, with CET1 at 8% (5.5% + 2.5%). Breaching the buffer restricts distributions.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) minimum including buffer is:
questions.e: CET1 — equity and disclosed reserves, the highest-quality capital — must be 5.5% plus the 2.5% buffer = 8%. Tier 1 overall is 7% + 2.5% buffer.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) requires:
o: HQLA of at least 100% of 30-day net cash outflows
questions.e: LCR = high-quality liquid assets ÷ stressed 30-day outflows ≥ 100%. NSFR (≥100%) covers structural funding over one year.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Risk weight for Government of India securities is:
questions.e: Sovereign exposures carry 0% risk weight, so government securities need no capital backing — one reason banks hold large G-sec portfolios for SLR.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: RTGS is meant for transfers of:
o: ₹2 lakh and above, settled gross in real time
questions.e: RTGS settles large-value transfers individually in real time, 24×7×365 since December 2019. NEFT handles smaller values in half-hourly batches, also 24×7.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: NEFT settles transactions:
questions.e: NEFT is a deferred net-settlement system in 48 half-hourly batches daily, 24×7, with no RBI-prescribed minimum or maximum. IMPS is instant 24×7.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: UPI was launched by NPCI on:
questions.e: UPI (11 April 2016) enables instant inter-bank transfers via VPA/QR/mobile number. Later additions: UPI Lite, 123Pay, AutoPay, and Tap & Pay with My UPI (September 2026).

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: AePS transactions are authenticated through:
questions.e: Aadhaar-enabled Payment System uses biometric authentication for balance enquiry, cash withdrawal and transfers at BC outlets — key for rural last-mile banking.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: NACH is used for:
o: Bulk electronic debits and credits like salaries, EMIs and subsidies
questions.e: National Automated Clearing House handles bulk, repetitive transactions — salary credits, dividend payments, EMI debits and DBT subsidies — replacing paper ECS.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: BBPS is:
o: A standardised bill-payment system operated under NPCI
questions.e: Bharat Bill Payment System offers interoperable bill payments (electricity, telecom, gas, etc.) through agents, apps and bank branches with instant confirmation.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: e-RUPI, launched in August 2021, is:
questions.e: e-RUPI is a cashless, contactless voucher for specific purposes (e.g. healthcare, subsidies), redeemable without a bank account by the beneficiary.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Under RBI's zero-liability framework, a customer reporting an unauthorised electronic transaction within 3 working days gets:
questions.e: Report within 3 working days: zero liability; 4–7 days: graded liability (capped); beyond 7 days: liability per bank policy. Banks must credit shadow reversal within 10 days of notification.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The RBI mandated an additional factor of authentication for domestic card-not-present (online) transactions in:
questions.e: RBI's February 2009 circular required additional authentication (e.g., OTP/3D Secure) for interactive e-commerce card transactions.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The Business Correspondent model was permitted by the RBI in:
questions.e: The January 2006 BC guidelines let banks use intermediaries (bank mitras, CSPs) with biometric devices for doorstep banking — the backbone of rural financial inclusion.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: PMJDY was launched on:
questions.e: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (28 August 2014) gave every unbanked household a zero-balance account with RuPay card, ₹10,000 overdraft (eligible holders) and ₹2 lakh accident cover for accounts opened after 28 August 2018.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: PMJDY accounts offer an overdraft of up to:
questions.e: Eligible PMJDY holders (satisfactory operation for 6 months, etc.) can get an overdraft up to ₹10,000. The ₹2 lakh figure is the accident insurance cover for newer accounts.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: DBT payments ride on:
o: Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts via the Aadhaar Payments Bridge
questions.e: Direct Benefit Transfer credits subsidies directly to Aadhaar-seeded accounts through APB/NACH, cutting leakages. JAM (Jan Dhan–Aadhaar–Mobile) is the delivery trinity.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: PM Vishwakarma (September 2023) supports:
o: Traditional artisans and craftspeople with collateral-free loans and skilling
questions.e: PM Vishwakarma gives 18 traditional trades (carpenters, potters, etc.) recognition, skilling, toolkit incentives and collateral-free enterprise loans in two tranches.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The BCSBI is associated with:
o: Codes for fair treatment of bank customers
questions.e: The Banking Codes and Standards Board of India (2006) issued the Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers and to MSEs, setting fair-practice benchmarks later absorbed into RBI's Charter of Customer Rights.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The Reserve Bank–Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS) came into force on:
questions.e: RB-IOS (12 November 2021) merged the Banking, NBFC and digital-transactions ombudsman schemes into 'one nation, one ombudsman', covering banks, NBFCs, system participants and credit information companies.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Under RB-IOS, a customer can approach the Ombudsman after:
o: The bank fails to resolve the complaint within 30 days
questions.e: The complaint must first go to the regulated entity; if unresolved/rejected after 30 days (or the customer is unsatisfied), the CMS portal (cms.rbi.org.in) route opens, within one year of the bank's reply.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Maximum compensation under RB-IOS is:
o: ₹20 lakh, plus ₹1 lakh for mental agony/harassment
questions.e: The Ombudsman can award up to ₹20 lakh for consequential loss plus ₹1 lakh for mental agony/harassment. In October 2025 the RBI proposed raising this to ₹30 lakh and covering state co-operative banks.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Appeal against an Ombudsman award lies with:
o: The Appellate Authority (Executive Director-level at RBI)
questions.e: Either party aggrieved by the Ombudsman's award/closure may appeal within 30 days to the RBI's Appellate Authority (an Executive Director), whose decision is reasoned and binding subject to legal remedies.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: The 7 Ps of bank marketing include:
o: Product, price, place, promotion, people, process, physical evidence
questions.e: Booms & Bitner's 7 Ps extend the classic 4 Ps for services. In banking — an intangible promise — people (staff), process (delivery) and physical evidence (branch, app) dominate differentiation.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Segmentation of bank customers is usually done on:
o: Demographic, geographic, psychographic and behavioural bases
questions.e: Banks segment by demographics (age, income), geography, psychographics (lifestyle) and behaviour (usage, loyalty) to target products like youth accounts, senior-citizen deposits or MSME loans.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Cross-selling in banks primarily aims at:
o: Increasing share of wallet and fee income per customer
questions.e: Cross-selling (CASA + insurance + mutual funds + lockers) deepens relationships, raises switching costs and boosts fee income — but must follow suitability and misselling norms.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Bancassurance refers to:
o: Banks distributing insurance products as corporate agents
questions.e: As corporate agents, banks sell insurers' policies earning commission (fee income). IRDAI caps the number of tie-ups; misselling norms and suitability apply.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: DBF November 2026: the Principles & Practices of Banking paper is on:
questions.e: Per IIBF: Indian Economy & Indian Financial System — 1 November 2026; PPB — 22 November; Accounting & Financial Management — 28 November; Retail Banking & Wealth Management — 29 November 2026.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: DBF passing criteria are:
o: 50 marks per paper, or 45 per paper with 50% aggregate
questions.e: Each 100-mark paper needs 50 to pass; alternatively 45+ in each paper with 50% aggregate overall. There is no negative marking, and case-study MCQs feature in every paper.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: DBF first-attempt examination fee is:
questions.e: IIBF charges ₹3,500 + GST for the first DBF attempt; attempts two to five cost ₹1,300 + GST each. DBF is open to non-members with 12th-standard eligibility.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: DBF is open to:
questions.e: Unlike JAIIB (for members), DBF is IIBF's flagship qualification for non-members — students and career entrants with 12th-standard education can enrol, making it a banking career gateway.

questions.subject: DBF
questions.q: Which DBF paper covers accounting ratios, final accounts and capital adequacy?
questions.e: AFM (28 November 2026) covers accounting concepts, final accounts, ratio analysis and financial management including capital adequacy — the most numerical of the four papers.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The first stage of the money laundering process, in which illicit cash is introduced into the financial system, is called
questions.e: Placement is the first stage: criminal proceeds are introduced into the financial system (cash deposits, smurfing, currency exchange). Layering then separates funds from source, and integration returns them in apparently legitimate form. Front-line bank staff detect most placement attempts.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Smurfing in money laundering refers to
o: Using trade invoices to move value
Breaking a large sum into many small deposits below reporting thresholds
Investing laundered money in real estate
questions.e: Smurfing (also called structuring) splits a large amount into many small deposits to evade threshold-based reporting like CTRs. This is a placement-stage typology. Shell companies belong to layering, and real estate investment is typically integration.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following is a layering technique?
o: Opening an account with fake KYC documents
Multiple wire transfers through shell companies across jurisdictions
Large cash deposit of sale proceeds
questions.e: Layering creates distance between crime and money through complex transaction chains — wire transfers, shell companies, multiple jurisdictions. Fake KYC at account opening and cash deposits are placement; buying property is integration.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Investment of laundered funds in real estate so that they appear as legitimate wealth is an example of
questions.e: Integration is the final stage: laundered money re-enters the economy as apparently legitimate assets (real estate, businesses, luxury goods). Placement introduces the money; layering obscures the trail.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Money laundering is distinguished from terrorist financing mainly because
o: Terrorist financing always uses large sums while laundering uses small sums
Money laundering cleans dirty money while terrorist financing often directs clean money to an illegal purpose
Money laundering is a predicate offence
Terrorist financing is not covered by FATF Recommendations
questions.e: TF often uses legitimately-earned (clean) money directed to an unlawful purpose — the flow is 'reverse money laundering'. Sums can be tiny, so detection is harder. FATF Recommendations cover both ML and TF.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The FATF was established in 1989 by
questions.e: The Financial Action Task Force was set up by the G-7 at the 1989 Paris summit as the global AML standard-setter. It is not a UN body; the Basel Committee sets banking supervision standards.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Palermo Convention (2000), which underpins the PMLA, is formally known as
o: UN Convention on Financing of Terrorism
UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime
questions.e: The Palermo Convention (2000) is the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime; India enacted the PMLA to implement its obligations. The Vienna Convention (1988) targeted drug trafficking, and UNCAC (2003) targets corruption.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: UNODC estimates that the amount of money laundered globally each year is approximately
questions.e: UNODC's widely-cited estimate is that 2–5% of global GDP (hundreds of billions to over a trillion dollars) is laundered annually, which is why AML is a systemic financial-integrity issue, not merely a policing one.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A 'predicate offence' under the PMLA means
o: An offence punishable only by fine
An offence committed by a reporting entity
An offence committed after money laundering
The underlying scheduled offence that generated the proceeds of crime
questions.e: The predicate (scheduled) offence is the underlying crime — e.g. drug trafficking, fraud, corruption — whose proceeds are then laundered. The PMLA offence (s.3) is stand-alone: handling those proceeds is itself a crime.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three classic stages of money laundering?
questions.e: The classic model is placement → layering → integration. Prosecution is a law-enforcement outcome, not a laundering stage. Exam questions frequently test whether candidates can map a typology to the right stage.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Rapid movement of funds in and out of an account with no apparent economic purpose is a red flag typically associated with
questions.e: Layering shows up as complex, rapid, economically pointless movements designed to confuse the audit trail. Simple large cash deposits signal placement; long-term holding in assets signals integration.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Cash couriers carrying currency across borders are mainly used in which stage?
questions.e: Physical smuggling of cash into another jurisdiction is a placement technique — the money has not yet entered the financial system. Once deposited and moved electronically, it enters layering.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The term 'structuring' is synonymous with
o: Smurfing deposits to avoid reporting thresholds
questions.e: Structuring = smurfing = breaking transactions into smaller amounts to evade threshold reporting (e.g. CTR at ₹10 lakh). Shell companies and trade mis-invoicing are layering tools; real estate is integration.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Loans taken against the criminal's own laundered deposits are a typology of
questions.e: Borrowing against laundered deposits (back-to-back loans) is a classic integration technique: the criminal receives 'clean' loan funds while the dirty deposit sits as collateral. The loan looks legitimate.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which agency publishes the estimate that 2–5% of global GDP is laundered?
questions.e: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) publishes the 2–5% of GDP estimate. FATF sets standards; IMF/World Bank assess financial systems but this figure is UNODC's.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Trade-based money laundering typically involves
o: Over- and under-invoicing of goods to move value across borders
questions.e: TBML moves value disguised as legitimate trade through over/under-invoicing, phantom shipments, multiple invoicing and mis-described goods. It is a layering typology, distinct from placement techniques like smurfing.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A casino chip purchase followed by redemption for a cheque is an example of
questions.e: Casinos are a placement channel: cash buys chips, and redeemed chips produce a 'clean' cheque or bank credit. The funds then enter the system for layering. Such channels are why casinos are reporting entities in many jurisdictions.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Hawala transactions are most closely associated with
o: Informal value transfer outside the formal financial system
questions.e: Hawala is an informal money value transfer system (MVTS) operating outside formal banking through trusted brokers settling net balances. It is abused for both ML and TF, and FATF addresses MVTS under its Recommendations.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The offence of money laundering under PMLA requires
o: Only a cash transaction above ₹10 lakh
A conviction for the predicate offence first
Proof that proceeds are linked to a scheduled offence, with the accused projecting them as untainted
questions.e: Section 3 makes the offence stand-alone: handling proceeds of crime and projecting them as untainted is enough; a prior conviction for the predicate offence is not required. This was affirmed in Vijay Madanlal Choudhary (2022).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which international convention of 1988 first targeted drug-trafficking proceeds and influenced AML law?
questions.e: The 1988 Vienna Convention (UN Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs) first criminalised laundering of drug proceeds. Palermo (2000) widened this to organised crime; Merida (2003) is the anti-corruption convention.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Shell companies are primarily used in which laundering stage?
questions.e: Shell companies with no real business are classic layering vehicles: they hold accounts, receive wires and create opaque ownership chains. Placement introduces funds; integration converts them to usable assets.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Round-tripping of funds — sending money abroad and bringing it back as 'foreign investment' — is a form of
questions.e: Round-tripping layers funds through offshore jurisdictions and integrates them as apparently legitimate foreign investment. It exploits investment incentives while disguising the money's origin.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The main reason banks are called the 'frontline' in AML is that
o: Nearly every placement attempt touches the formal financial system through a bank
questions.e: Banks are gatekeepers: placement almost always requires a bank account or channel, so CDD, monitoring and reporting by banks are the system's first line of defence. Investigation of predicate offences is the police/ED's job.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following transactions is most likely to indicate placement?
o: An NRI remitting funds through banking channels
A company paying salaries by NEFT
A customer making structured cash deposits of ₹9.5 lakh on consecutive days
questions.e: Structured cash deposits just below the ₹10 lakh CTR threshold are a textbook placement red flag (smurfing). Salary payments, legitimate NRI remittances and GST payments have clear economic rationale.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The 'integration' stage is hardest to detect because
o: The funds are indistinguishable from legitimate money by then
questions.e: By integration, layered funds have acquired apparently legitimate form (property, investments, business income), so they blend with lawful money. That is why prevention concentrates on placement and layering.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Correspondent banking channels can be abused for laundering mainly through
o: Nested correspondent relationships and payable-through accounts
questions.e: Nested correspondents (downstream clients of a respondent using the channel) and payable-through accounts let unknown third parties move money through a correspondent — the classic cross-border layering risk.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A 'mule' in money laundering terminology is
o: A person who transfers illicit funds on behalf of criminals
questions.e: Money mules are individuals recruited (often through job scams) to receive and forward illicit funds, giving criminals distance from the transactions. Banks watch for mule-like account behaviour.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Purchase of high-value art, jewellery and luxury goods with criminal proceeds is typically
questions.e: Luxury assets are integration vehicles: portable, high-value stores of wealth that convert dirty money into apparently legitimate possessions. Placement is the cash entry; structuring is deposit-splitting.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Vienna Convention relates to which predicate crime category?
questions.e: The 1988 Vienna Convention targeted drug trafficking — the original predicate crime for AML law. Corruption came under UNCAC (Merida, 2003); terrorism financing under UNSC Resolution 1373 (2001).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which statement about the three-stage model is correct?
o: The stages are a conceptual model; schemes may skip or blend stages
Every laundering scheme must pass through all three stages in order
questions.e: The model is analytical, not a legal checklist — schemes often compress or repeat stages. Placement is the riskiest stage (closest to the crime and cash), which is why detection focuses there.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Benami transactions are relevant to AML because
o: They conceal true ownership, aiding the layering and concealment of proceeds
They are only a tax issue
questions.e: Benami arrangements — property held by one person but paid for by another — conceal beneficial ownership, a core laundering technique. India prohibits them under the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The phrase 'proceeds of crime' under PMLA includes
o: Property derived directly or indirectly from criminal activity related to a scheduled offence, or its value
questions.e: Section 2(1)(u) defines proceeds of crime broadly: any property (movable or immovable, in India or abroad) derived from a scheduled offence, or its value — including equivalent property attached under the 2015 amendment.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following is a predicate offence category in the PMLA Schedule?
questions.e: The PMLA Schedule lists serious crimes: NDPS (drugs), UAPA (terror), Arms Act, Companies Act s.447 fraud, corruption, etc. Minor civil or traffic matters are not scheduled offences.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Layering is most effective for criminals when it uses
o: Multiple accounts, jurisdictions and instruments to confuse the audit trail
questions.e: Layering works by complexity and distance — many accounts, countries, shell entities and instruments. A single domestic account leaves a clear trail, defeating the purpose.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: An 'attempted transaction' that appears suspicious
o: Can be ignored by the bank
Need not be reported since no money moved
Must be reported in an STR since the Rules cover attempts
questions.e: The Rules expressly cover suspicious transactions 'including attempted transactions' — a failed laundering attempt is still reportable in an STR. Ignoring attempts would blind the system to detected-but-blocked crime.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The primary objective of India's PMLA is to
o: Prevent money laundering and provide for confiscation of property derived from it
questions.e: The PMLA's long title states its object: preventing money-laundering and providing for confiscation of property derived from, or involved in, money-laundering. Forex regulation is FEMA's domain.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which body sets the global AML/CFT standards that India's PMLA framework implements?
questions.e: The FATF's 40 Recommendations are the global standard; India's PMLA, FIU-IND and RBI KYC Directions implement them domestically. RBI/SEBI/IRDAI are sectoral regulators.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: In the PNB–Nirav Modi case (2018), the fraud primarily involved
o: Fraudulent Letters of Undertaking (LoUs) misused through the SWIFT–CBS gap
questions.e: The ~₹13,850 crore PNB fraud used fraudulently issued LoUs: SWIFT messages were sent without entering them in the core banking system, letting overseas branches extend buyer's credit. It is a landmark Indian enforcement case.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Terrorist financing is often described as 'reverse money laundering' because
o: Clean or legitimate funds are directed towards an illegal purpose
questions.e: TF frequently starts with clean money (donations, business income, charity) and ends in crime — the reverse flow of laundering. This makes TF harder to detect via transaction monitoring alone.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'integration'?
o: Using laundered funds to acquire apparently legitimate assets
questions.e: Integration = the criminal enjoys the money as apparently legitimate wealth (assets, investments, businesses). Introducing cash is placement; obscuring the trail is layering; reporting is the bank's duty.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A customer who refuses to provide KYC documents and insists on urgency is exhibiting
questions.e: Reluctance to provide identification, use of aliases, and pressure for urgency are classic customer red flags. Transaction red flags concern the pattern of money movement; geographic flags concern jurisdictions.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The offence of money laundering is defined in which section of the PMLA?
questions.e: Section 3 defines the offence of money laundering — attempting, assisting, being knowingly party to, or actually involved in any process connected with proceeds of crime and projecting it as untainted. Section 4 provides punishment; Section 5 covers provisional attachment.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under Section 3 of PMLA, a person is guilty of money laundering if he
o: Projects proceeds of crime as untainted property
questions.e: The essence of Section 3 is projecting or claiming proceeds of crime as untainted property (along with concealment, possession, acquisition or use). Mere large deposits or procedural lapses are not the Section 3 offence.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Punishment for money laundering under Section 4 of PMLA is
o: Only a fine up to ₹5 lakh
Rigorous imprisonment of not less than 3 years up to 7 years, plus fine
questions.e: Section 4 prescribes rigorous imprisonment of not less than 3 years extending to 7 years, and fine. Where proceeds relate to NDPS offences (para 2, Part A of the Schedule), imprisonment may extend to 10 years.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Where the proceeds of crime relate to NDPS offences, the maximum punishment under PMLA Section 4 extends to
questions.e: For NDPS-linked proceeds (paragraph 2 of Part A of the Schedule), Section 4 allows rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years instead of the normal 7-year maximum. This is a favourite exam distractor.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Provisional attachment of property under Section 5 of PMLA can be ordered for a period of
questions.e: Section 5 empowers the Director (or authorised Deputy Director) to provisionally attach property for 180 days from the date of the order, on reasons to believe recorded in writing. The Adjudicating Authority then decides on confirmation.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The authority that confirms attachment or retention of property under Section 8 of PMLA is
questions.e: The Adjudicating Authority under Section 8 confirms provisional attachment/retention after hearing; on confirmation the property vests in the Central Government. The Appellate Tribunal (s.25) hears appeals against the Authority's orders.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under Section 5 of PMLA, the Director must forward the attachment order and material to the Adjudicating Authority within
questions.e: Section 5 requires the Director to forward a copy of the attachment order along with the material to the Adjudicating Authority within 30 days, keeping the provisional attachment under judicial oversight.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The 'burden of proof' provision under PMLA is contained in
questions.e: Section 24 reverses the burden: where a person is accused of money laundering, the Authority/Court presumes the proceeds of crime are involved in money laundering unless the contrary is proved. This departs from the normal 'innocent until proven guilty' rule.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The twin conditions for bail in PMLA cases are prescribed in
questions.e: Section 45(1) imposes twin conditions: the court must be satisfied there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty AND is not likely to commit any offence while on bail. Struck down in Nikesh Tarachand Shah (2017), it was revived by the Finance Act, 2018.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Powers of ED officers to summon persons, enforce attendance and compel production of documents are given by
questions.e: Section 50 gives ED officers powers of a civil court — discovery, inspection, enforcing attendance, compelling production of records, examining on oath; proceedings are deemed judicial proceedings. Section 25 creates the Appellate Tribunal.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Appeals against orders of the Adjudicating Authority under PMLA lie to
questions.e: Section 25 establishes the Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals against the Adjudicating Authority's orders; further appeal lies to the High Court and then the Supreme Court. Direct High Court appeal skips the statutory hierarchy.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The PMLA received presidential assent on
questions.e: The PMLA was passed in 2002 and received assent on 17 December 2002; it was brought into force on 1 July 2005 along with the PML Rules. The 2023 dates are the VDA and professionals notifications.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which amendment made Section 447 (fraud) of the Companies Act, 2013 a scheduled offence under PMLA?
questions.e: The Finance Act, 2018 inserted Section 447 of the Companies Act (punishment for fraud) into the PMLA Schedule and also revived the Section 45(1) bail provision. The 2015 amendment addressed equivalent property abroad.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Notification S.O. 1072(E) dated 7 March 2023 brought under PMLA
o: Virtual digital asset service providers as reporting entities
questions.e: S.O. 1072(E) (7.3.2023) designated five categories of VDA activity under PMLA, making VDA service providers — including offshore providers serving India — reporting entities required to register with FIU-IND.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Notification S.O. 2036(E) dated 3 May 2023 relates to
o: Practising CA/CS/CMA brought under PMLA for specified client financial transactions
questions.e: S.O. 2036(E) (3.5.2023) notified that financial transactions carried out by practising chartered accountants, company secretaries and cost accountants on behalf of clients (property deals, managing client money/assets/accounts, company formation/management) are designated activities under s.2(1)(sa)(vi).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following client transactions by a practising CA is NOT covered by S.O. 2036(E)?
o: Buying and selling of immovable property for a client
Managing client money, securities or other assets
Creation or management of companies for a client
Routine statutory audit of financial statements
questions.e: The notification covers five specified financial transactions (property, client money/assets, account management, organising contributions, company/LLP/trust creation and management). Routine audit work is not among the notified activities.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The PMLA is enforced by
o: The Directorate of Enforcement under the Department of Revenue
questions.e: The Directorate of Enforcement (ED), under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, enforces the PMLA. RBI regulates banks; SEBI regulates securities markets; CBI investigates general crimes.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: In Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India (2022), the Supreme Court
o: Transferred PMLA trials to consumer courts
Upheld the core PMLA provisions including Sections 5, 8, 17, 19 and 24
questions.e: On 27 July 2022 the Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of the PMLA's core provisions — attachment (s.5), confirmation (s.8), search/seizure (s.17), arrest (s.19) and burden of proof (s.24). It did not strike down the Act.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The term 'reporting entity' is defined in PMLA under
questions.e: Section 2(1)(wa) defines 'reporting entity' (banking companies, FIs, intermediaries, persons carrying on designated business/profession). Section 2(1)(sa) defines 'designated business or profession'; (ha) defines 'client'; (u) defines 'proceeds of crime'.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: 'Designated business or profession' is defined in PMLA under
questions.e: Section 2(1)(sa) defines 'person carrying on designated business or profession', whose sub-clause (vi) lets the Central Government notify additional activities — the route used for VDA providers (2023) and CA/CS/CMA professionals (2023).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The term 'client' under PMLA Section 2(1)(ha) means
o: A person engaged in a financial transaction or activity with a reporting entity, including one on whose behalf another acts
questions.e: The definition is deliberately wide: any person engaged in a financial transaction with a reporting entity, including beneficial owners on whose behalf the transaction is done — so CDD reaches beyond the named customer.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: 'Proceeds of crime' is defined in PMLA under
questions.e: Section 2(1)(u): property derived or obtained, directly or indirectly, as a result of criminal activity relating to a scheduled offence, or the value of such property. Sections 3 and 4 deal with the offence and punishment.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Attachment of 'equivalent property' situated abroad was enabled by
questions.e: The Finance Act, 2015 amended PMLA to allow attachment of equivalent property in India/abroad where proceeds of crime are held outside India — closing the offshore-parking loophole.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Adjudicating Authority under PMLA can, after confirmation of attachment,
o: Order confiscation vesting the property in the Central Government and restore property to victims with quantifiable loss
questions.e: Section 8: on confirmation, the property vests in the Central Government (confiscation); the Authority may also take possession and restore confiscated property to a claimant who suffered quantifiable loss — as illustrated by the ₹66.33 crore released to PNB in June 2025.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which PMLA amendment enlarged the reporting-entity net and introduced NPO-related concepts?
questions.e: The Prevention of Money-laundering (Amendment) Act, 2012 significantly widened reporting entities and added concepts including non-profit organisations, aligning India with revised FATF standards.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A person who only knowingly assists another in concealing proceeds of crime, without touching the money himself,
o: Is liable only under the IPC
Is guilty under Section 3, which covers knowingly assisting
questions.e: Section 3 expressly covers one who 'knowingly assists or knowingly is a party' to laundering — physical handling of the money is not required. Concealment itself is listed among the covered processes.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2019 in relation to PMLA mainly
o: Made further amendments including clarificatory and procedural changes
questions.e: The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2019 carried further PMLA amendments (procedural and clarificatory). The Act, FIU-IND and the Adjudicating Authority all continue.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under PMLA, 'money laundering' as defined in Section 2(1)(p)
o: Has the same meaning as in Section 3
questions.e: Section 2(1)(p) defines 'money-laundering' as having the meaning assigned in Section 3 — the definition clause simply cross-refers to the offence section. Tax evasion and insider trading are separate offences.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Scheduled offences under the PMLA are organised in the Schedule under:
questions.e: The PMLA Schedule lists predicate offences in Parts A (serious offences like NDPS, Arms Act), B and C (IPC offences above thresholds).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The five VDA activities notified under S.O. 1072(E) include
o: Exchange between VDA and fiat, exchange between VDAs, transfer, safekeeping/administration, and participation in issuance-related financial services
questions.e: The notification lists five activities: (i) exchange VDA↔fiat, (ii) exchange VDA↔VDA, (iii) transfer of VDAs, (iv) safekeeping/administration, (v) participation in financial services related to an issuer's offer/sale of VDAs.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Offshore VDA service providers catering to the Indian market
o: Are covered as reporting entities and must register with FIU-IND
questions.e: The March 2023 framework expressly covers offshore VDA service providers serving India — they must register with FIU-IND and comply with PMLA verification, record-keeping and reporting obligations.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Nikesh Tarachand Shah (2017) judgment related to PMLA concerned
questions.e: Nikesh Tarachand Shah v. Union of India (2017) struck down the twin conditions for bail in Section 45(1) as unconstitutional; the Finance Act, 2018 revived the provision with amendments.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which statement about Section 24 PMLA is correct?
o: The Authority/Court shall presume proceeds of crime are involved in money laundering unless the contrary is proved
The prosecution must prove the accused's guilt beyond doubt with no presumptions
questions.e: Section 24 creates a statutory presumption — a reverse burden — against the accused regarding the tainted character of the property. Bail is Section 45; attachment is Section 5.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The PMLA long title states its object as
o: Preventing money-laundering and providing for confiscation of property derived from or involved in money-laundering
questions.e: The long title: 'An Act to prevent money-laundering and to provide for confiscation of property derived from, or involved in, money-laundering and for matters connected therewith.' Forex is FEMA's domain.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: How many activities did S.O. 2036(E) notify for practising CA/CS/CMA under PMLA?
questions.e: Five: (i) buying/selling immovable property; (ii) managing client money, securities or other assets; (iii) management of bank, savings or securities accounts; (iv) organisation of contributions for companies; (v) creation/operation/management of companies, LLPs or trusts, and buying/selling business entities.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A 'relevant person' under S.O. 2036(E) includes
o: Individuals holding certificates of practice under the CA Act 1949, CS Act 1980 and Cost and Works Accountants Act 1959
questions.e: Explanation 1 defines 'relevant person' as individuals with certificates of practice under the three professional statutes, practising individually or through firms. Lawyers/legal professionals were kept out.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under Section 5 PMLA, provisional attachment requires
o: Reasons to believe recorded in writing by the Director that the person is in possession of proceeds of crime
questions.e: The Director (or authorised Deputy Director) must have 'reason to believe' — recorded in writing — that a person is in possession of proceeds of crime. No prior conviction is needed; attachment is a preventive, provisional measure.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The PMLA (Amendment) Act, 2009 primarily
o: Expanded the scope of the Act including the Schedule of offences
questions.e: The 2009 amendment broadened the Act's scope, including expanding scheduled offences. FIU-IND was created in 2004; VDA coverage came in 2023; CKYC is an RBI/CERSAI initiative.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which court/tribunal hears appeals from the PMLA Appellate Tribunal's orders?
questions.e: Orders of the Appellate Tribunal (s.25) can be appealed to the High Court, and thereafter to the Supreme Court — the standard statutory appellate ladder under PMLA.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 were notified on
questions.e: The Rules were notified on 1 July 2005 — the same day the PMLA came into force — giving effect to the Section 12 record-keeping and reporting obligations. The 2016 date is the RBI KYC Master Direction.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under Rule 7 of the PML Rules, the Principal Officer is
o: A management-level officer designated to furnish information to the Director, FIU-IND
The branch manager of every branch
questions.e: Rule 7 requires each reporting entity to designate a Principal Officer at management level who is responsible for furnishing CTRs, STRs and other reports to FIU-IND. It is an entity-level, not branch-level, designation.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Overall compliance with PMLA obligations at the management level is the responsibility of the
questions.e: Rule 8 requires a Designated Director — a person at board/management level — to ensure overall compliance with PMLA obligations. The Principal Officer (Rule 7) handles the actual furnishing of reports.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Cash Transaction Reports (CTRs) must be furnished to FIU-IND for cash transactions above
questions.e: CTR covers all cash transactions above ₹10 lakh (or equivalent foreign currency), plus integrally connected series below ₹10 lakh each that aggregate above ₹10 lakh within a month. The ₹5 lakh threshold belongs to CBWTR.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A series of integrally connected cash transactions, each below ₹10 lakh but aggregating above ₹10 lakh within a month,
o: Must be reported in the CTR
Must be reported only as STR
questions.e: The Rules expressly include such structured series in the CTR — this is the anti-smurfing provision. Each transaction is below the threshold, but the connected series is reportable.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: CTRs are due to FIU-IND by
questions.e: CTR is a monthly report due by the 15th of the succeeding month. Contrast: STR/CCR are event-driven, due within 7 working days.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Suspicious Transaction Reports must be filed
o: For suspicious transactions regardless of value, including attempted transactions
questions.e: STR has no monetary threshold — any transaction (cash or non-cash, completed or attempted) giving reasonable ground of suspicion of ML/TF is reportable. This 'no threshold' feature is a favourite exam trap.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: An STR must be furnished within
o: 7 working days of being satisfied that the transaction is suspicious
questions.e: Rule-based timelines: STR within 7 working days of the reporting entity being satisfied about suspicion. The clock starts at satisfaction, not at the transaction date.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Counterfeit Currency Reports (CCRs) are due within
questions.e: CCR — where forged/counterfeit notes are used as genuine or forgery facilitates the transaction — is due within 7 working days of occurrence. Like STR, it is event-driven rather than monthly.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Cross Border Wire Transfer Reports (CBWTRs) cover transfers above
questions.e: CBWTR covers cross-border wire transfers above ₹5 lakh (or equivalent), filed monthly. The ₹10 lakh figure is the CTR threshold — a common distractor.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: NPO Transaction Reports (NTRs) are filed for receipts by non-profit organisations above
questions.e: NTR covers transactions involving receipts by NPOs above ₹10 lakh, filed monthly — reflecting FATF's concern about terrorist-financing abuse of the non-profit sector (Recommendation 8).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Records of transactions under Rule 10 must be preserved for
o: 5 years from the date of the transaction
questions.e: Rule 10: transaction records — 5 years from the date of the transaction. Identity records of clients/beneficial owners — 5 years after the business relationship ends. The two limbs have different starting points.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Records evidencing the identity of clients and beneficial owners must be preserved for
o: 5 years after the business relationship has ended or the account is closed
questions.e: Identity records are kept for 5 years after the relationship ends or the account closes, whichever is later — longer in practice than transaction records, since relationships can last decades.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The prohibition on informing the client that a report is being furnished to FIU-IND is called the prohibition of
questions.e: Tipping off — alerting the customer that an STR/CTR is filed or contemplated — is prohibited; it would let the suspect destroy evidence or flee. Section 12 of PMLA correspondingly immunises good-faith reporting.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A banker who reports a suspicious transaction to FIU-IND in good faith
o: Breaches banker-customer confidentiality and is liable
Is protected: reporting is not treated as breach of confidentiality
questions.e: Section 12 immunity: furnishing information in good faith to FIU-IND is not a breach of confidentiality obligations. The banker cannot be sued for the disclosure — but tipping off the client remains prohibited.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: FIU-IND was established in
questions.e: FIU-IND was set up in 2004 under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, as India's central agency for receiving, analysing and disseminating suspect-transaction intelligence. Its statutory teeth came with PMLA (2005).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: FIU-IND functions under the administrative control of
o: The Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
questions.e: FIU-IND is under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance (like the ED). RBI is the banking regulator; MHA handles internal security and UAPA sanctions administration.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The electronic gateway through which reporting entities file reports to FIU-IND is called
questions.e: FINnet is FIU-IND's reporting gateway for CTR/STR/CCR/CBWTR/NTR filing. SFMS is the messaging system for interbank communication; CKYCR is the KYC registry.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Egmont Group is
o: The global network of Financial Intelligence Units for secure information exchange
questions.e: The Egmont Group connects 170+ FIUs worldwide, enabling secure intelligence exchange (via the Egmont Secure Web). FIU-IND shares and receives ML/TF intelligence through this channel.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a report filed with FIU-IND?
questions.e: FIU-IND receives CTR, STR, CCR, CBWTR and NTR. CRR is a monetary-policy instrument reported to RBI — the similar acronym is a deliberate distractor.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A cash deposit of ₹12 lakh in a savings account must be reported in
questions.e: Single cash transaction above ₹10 lakh → CTR (monthly, by 15th). It is not automatically suspicious (no STR unless suspicion factors exist), not counterfeit (CCR), and not NPO-related (NTR).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A customer deposits ₹4 lakh in cash on three occasions in a month into the same account. The bank should
o: Ignore it since each is below ₹10 lakh
Report the integrally connected series in the CTR
questions.e: The series is integrally connected and aggregates ₹12 lakh within a month — reportable in the CTR. Whether an STR is also warranted depends on suspicion, but the CTR obligation is clear.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: An attempted wire transfer that the bank blocked because it appeared to fund terrorism should be
o: Reported in an STR within 7 working days of being satisfied
questions.e: Attempted suspicious transactions are expressly STR-reportable. The 7-working-day clock runs from satisfaction of suspicion. Police reporting may follow separately, but the FIU obligation stands.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Counterfeit notes detected at the cash counter must be reported in the CCR
questions.e: CCR is event-driven: within 7 working days of occurrence, with no monetary threshold. Monthly 15th applies to CTR/CBWTR/NTR.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which report has no monetary threshold?
questions.e: STR is suspicion-based with no threshold — even a ₹5,000 attempted transaction can be STR-worthy. CTR (₹10L), CBWTR (₹5L) and NTR (₹10L) are all threshold-based.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Designated Director under Rule 8 must be
o: A person at board/management level ensuring overall PMLA compliance
questions.e: Rule 8: the Designated Director is nominated at the level of the board or top management to own overall compliance with PMLA obligations — distinct from the Principal Officer who files reports.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Customer due diligence requirements under the PML Rules are primarily in
questions.e: Rule 9 prescribes client due diligence (identification, verification, beneficial ownership). Rule 3 covers record maintenance, Rule 10 retention, Rule 7 the Principal Officer.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under the PML Rules, 'beneficial owner' for a company means the natural person holding
o: More than 10% of shares/capital/profits or exercising control
questions.e: Company: more than 10% of shares, capital or profits, or control through other means. The 25% figure is the older international norm; India tightened it to 10% (2023 amendment).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: For a partnership firm, the beneficial-owner threshold is
o: More than 10% of capital or profits
questions.e: Partnership: natural persons entitled to more than 10% of capital or profits. Trusts use 10% or more for beneficiaries; unincorporated associations use more than 15%.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: For a trust, which of the following must be identified as beneficial owner?
o: The author, trustee, beneficiaries with 10% or more interest, protector, and persons exercising ultimate control
questions.e: Trusts are opaque vehicles, so the Rules require identifying the full control chain: author/setlor, trustee, qualifying beneficiaries (10%+), protector, and anyone with ultimate effective control.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: For an unincorporated association or body of individuals, the beneficial-owner threshold is
questions.e: Unincorporated association/BOI: more than 15% ownership or entitlement. Company and partnership use more than 10%; trusts use 10% or more for beneficiaries.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Where no natural person is identified as beneficial owner, the Rules treat as beneficial owner
questions.e: Fallback: if no natural person is identified through ownership/control, the senior managing official is deemed the beneficial owner — ensuring there is always an identified natural person.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A company listed on a recognised stock exchange is
o: Generally exempt from the beneficial-owner identification drill
questions.e: Listed companies (and their subsidiaries) are exempt from the BO look-through because market disclosure and regulation already ensure transparency. They remain subject to CTR/STR obligations.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Politically exposed persons were formally defined in the PML Rules in
questions.e: The March 2023 amendments inserted formal PEP and NPO definitions into the PML Rules, aligning India with FATF expectations on EDD for PEPs.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Non-profit organisations were defined in the PML Rules in
questions.e: The March 2023 amendment defined NPOs in the Rules, alongside the NTR reporting framework and DARPAN registration requirements for NPO clients.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following persons is a PEP?
questions.e: PEPs are individuals entrusted with prominent public functions (domestic or foreign), plus family members and close associates — the corruption-proceeds risk category requiring EDD.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: EDD for PEPs includes
o: Senior management approval, establishing source of wealth/funds, and enhanced ongoing monitoring
questions.e: PEP relationships demand enhanced due diligence: senior management sign-off, source of wealth/funds established, and heightened monitoring — the FATF-mandated treatment for corruption-risk clients.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A reporting entity that fails to maintain records or furnish reports under PMLA is liable to
o: Monetary penalty imposed by the Director, FIU-IND
questions.e: Section 13 PMLA empowers the Director, FIU-IND to impose monetary penalty for failure to maintain records, furnish information, or comply with Rules — a direct compliance incentive for banks.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The FIU-IND's core functions include
o: Receiving, analysing and disseminating suspect-transaction information and maintaining the national database
questions.e: FIU-IND is India's financial intelligence unit: it collects CTR/STR/CCR/CBWTR/NTR, analyses them, disseminates intelligence to enforcement agencies, and maintains the national database. Licensing and rates are RBI's domain.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following entities is a 'reporting entity' under PMLA?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(wa) covers banking companies, financial institutions, intermediaries, and persons carrying on designated business/profession — the full net of entities with Rule 7/8, record and reporting duties.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The phrase 'integrally connected' in CTR rules is aimed at
o: Smurfing/structuring designed to evade the ₹10 lakh threshold
questions.e: The series rule defeats structuring: splitting deposits to stay below ₹10 lakh each still triggers CTR when the connected monthly aggregate crosses ₹10 lakh.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A non-profit organisation receiving ₹15 lakh should be
o: Reported in the monthly NTR and the NPO's DARPAN registration verified
questions.e: NPO receipts above ₹10 lakh go in the monthly NTR; banks must also verify the NPO's registration details (DARPAN) as part of CDD, given TF-abuse risks in the sector.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Tipping-off provisions exist primarily to
o: Prevent the suspect from being alerted, which could lead to destruction of evidence or flight
questions.e: Alerting a suspect defeats investigation — funds get moved, evidence destroyed. The prohibition preserves the integrity of the intelligence and enforcement chain.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The RBI Master Direction on KYC was issued on
questions.e: The Master Direction — KYC (DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16) was issued on 25 February 2016, consolidating KYC/AML guidelines for banks. It was repealed for commercial banks in November 2025.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The RBI (Commercial Banks — Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 were notified on
questions.e: Notified 28 November 2025 (RBI/2025-26/101), the 2025 Directions repealed the 2016 Master Direction for commercial banks, folding in all intervening amendments into one framework.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The 2016 KYC Master Direction was replaced for commercial banks by the 2025 Directions, which means
o: Only cooperative banks follow KYC now
The 2016 framework stands repealed for commercial banks and the 2025 Directions apply
questions.e: The 2025 Directions expressly repealed the 2016 Master Direction for commercial banks — KYC obligations continue under the new instrument. The exam tests this transition, not any dilution of KYC.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an officially valid document (OVD) for KYC?
questions.e: OVDs: passport, driving licence, voter ID, MGNREGA job card, NPR letter, Aadhaar. A library card is not an OVD — exam distractors often use plausible-looking non-documents.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Periodic updation of KYC for high-risk customers is required every
questions.e: High-risk: every 2 years; medium-risk: every 8 years; low-risk: every 10 years. The 2-8-10 ladder is one of the most-tested numerical facts in the exam.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Periodic updation of KYC for medium-risk customers is required every
questions.e: Medium-risk customers: KYC updated every 8 years. High-risk 2 years, low-risk 10 years — the middle value belongs to medium risk.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Periodic updation of KYC for low-risk customers is required every
questions.e: Low-risk: every 10 years. The June 2025 amendment additionally gives low-risk individuals one year beyond the due date (or until 30 June 2026, whichever is later) to complete updation.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under the June 2025 KYC amendments, low-risk individual customers whose KYC is due get
o: One year after the due date or until 30 June 2026, whichever is later
questions.e: The 12 June 2025 amendment (effective 1 January 2026) gives low-risk individuals one year after the due date or until 30 June 2026, whichever is later — easing compliance without weakening standards.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The June 2025 amendments allow banks to obtain KYC self-declarations from customers
questions.e: Banks may collect self-declarations through business correspondents, sparing customers — especially in rural areas — a branch visit. This is part of the customer-convenience package of the June 2025 changes.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under the June 2025 amendments, banks must send customers
o: Three advance intimations before the due date and three reminders after
questions.e: Three advance intimations before KYC falls due plus three reminders after — the RBI's prescription to end surprise account-freezing for KYC non-compliance.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: CDD at the UCIC level was introduced by the RBI in
questions.e: The November 2024 amendment requires CDD at the Unique Customer Identification Code level, giving the bank a single consistent KYC view of the customer across all accounts and relationships.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Simplified Due Diligence (SDD) was formally introduced for specified categories in
questions.e: The 22 May 2025 amendment introduced SDD — reduced documentation for specified low-risk categories — balancing financial inclusion with AML rigour.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Aadhaar face authentication as a KYC identification mode was enabled by
questions.e: The second KYC amendment of 2025 permitted Aadhaar face authentication, adding a biometric option alongside OTP-based e-KYC and physical verification.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Banks were made responsible for their CKYCR uploads by the amendment dated
questions.e: The 29 December 2025 amendment fixed responsibility on banks for uploading KYC records to the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) — closing the accountability gap on registry data quality.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: CDD is required for occasional transactions above
questions.e: Occasional (walk-in, non-account-based) transactions of ₹50,000 and above trigger CDD even without an account relationship — the threshold for one-off transactions.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: V-CIP is treated under the KYC Directions as
o: On par with face-to-face customer identification
questions.e: Video-based Customer Identification Process — a live audio-video interaction by an authorised official — is legally on par with face-to-face CIP, provided the session is live and the customer is in India.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: In a V-CIP session, the bank official must capture
o: The customer's live photograph, the OVD, and the customer's live location
questions.e: V-CIP requires capturing the customer's live image, the officially valid document shown on camera, and live location — the three anchors that make video identification equivalent to in-person verification.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for
o: PEPs, customers from high-risk jurisdictions, and complex/unusually large transactions
questions.e: EDD applies to high-risk categories: PEPs, FATF-listed-country links, complex or unusually large transactions, and correspondent banking. Standard customers get standard CDD.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: EDD measures include
o: Senior management approval, establishing source of wealth/funds, enhanced ongoing monitoring
questions.e: EDD = senior management approval for the relationship, source of wealth/funds established, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. It intensifies — never waives — diligence.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Customer Acceptance Policy under KYC Directions requires that
o: No account is opened in anonymous, fictitious or benami names
Any person can open an account without documents
Accounts can be opened anonymously with numbers only
questions.e: Anonymous, fictitious and benami accounts are prohibited; accounts open only after proper identification. This is the first pillar of the KYC framework.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Risk categorisation of customers under the KYC Directions is into
questions.e: Three buckets — high, medium, low — driving the 2/8/10-year periodic updation cycle and the intensity of monitoring. The exam frequently pairs categories with their timelines.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Ongoing monitoring of transactions under the KYC framework should be
o: Risk-based, proportionate to the customer's risk profile
questions.e: Monitoring intensity follows risk: high-risk customers get enhanced ongoing monitoring; low-risk get simplified treatment. Uniform monitoring wastes resources and misses real risk.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following customers would typically be classified high-risk?
o: A salaried employee with regular credits
A PEP with complex cross-border transactions
A student with a scholarship account
questions.e: PEPs with complex cross-border activity are textbook high-risk. Salaried, pension and student profiles with clean patterns are typically low-risk.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The four pillars of the KYC framework are
o: Customer acceptance policy, CDD, risk management and monitoring, training/internal control
questions.e: The Directions rest on: customer acceptance policy, customer due diligence, risk management/transaction monitoring, and training, internal control and record management.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: For a company customer, the bank must obtain
o: Only the PAN of the company
Certificate of incorporation, MOA/AOA, board resolution and POA for authorised persons, plus BO identification
Nothing beyond the account opening form
questions.e: Legal-person CDD: incorporation documents, constitutional documents (MOA/AOA), board resolution authorising account opening and operation, POA for operators, and beneficial-owner identification.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Small accounts (relaxed KYC) under the RBI framework are subject to
o: Balance and transaction caps with periodic review
questions.e: Small accounts (e.g. for those without OVDs) operate with balance/turnover caps and are monitored; they are a financial-inclusion measure, not an AML blind spot.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC in non-face-to-face mode
o: Must be accepted by banks for account opening
questions.e: The June 2025 amendments require banks to accept Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC in non-face-to-face mode — a major inclusion push, especially for remote onboarding.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The inclusion of persons with disabilities in KYC processes was addressed by the amendment of
questions.e: The 23 May 2025 amendment addressed KYC accessibility for persons with disabilities — an exam favourite because it is recent and specific.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: If a customer does not furnish KYC documents on periodic updation, the bank should
o: Follow the prescribed reminder/escalation process, with partial freezing only after due notice
questions.e: The Directions (and the June 2025 reminder regime) require a graded process — intimations and reminders — before any restrictive action; arbitrary freezing invites regulatory censure.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The UCIC (Unique Customer Identification Code) helps banks by
o: Giving a single customer-level view of KYC across all relationships
questions.e: UCIC-level CDD (Nov 2024) unifies the customer's KYC status across accounts, loans and services — preventing inconsistent or duplicated KYC within the same bank.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which risk category gets Simplified Due Diligence?
questions.e: SDD (May 2025) is for specified low-risk categories — reduced documentation where ML/TF risk is demonstrably low. High-risk customers get EDD, the opposite treatment.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Transaction monitoring systems in banks primarily aim to
o: Detect unusual patterns for STR/CTR purposes
questions.e: Monitoring detects anomalies — structuring, rapid movement, profile-inconsistent activity — feeding the STR decision process and threshold reports. It is a detection, not sales, tool.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A walk-in customer doing a one-time transfer of ₹75,000
o: Triggers CDD as an occasional transaction above ₹50,000
questions.e: ₹75,000 exceeds the ₹50,000 occasional-transaction threshold → CDD applies. EDD needs additional high-risk factors, not just the amount.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The KYC Directions apply to
o: All regulated entities including banks, NBFCs and other REs as specified
questions.e: The KYC Directions (and the 2025 Commercial Banks Directions for their segment) apply to regulated entities broadly — banks, NBFCs, and others specified — not a single bank group.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Record management under the KYC framework requires
o: Systematic maintenance and retrieval of KYC/transaction records per prescribed retention
questions.e: Records must be maintained systematically and retrievable, with retention per the PML Rules (5 years) — the compliance backbone for audits, FIU queries and investigations.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Training under the KYC/AML framework should
o: Be ongoing, covering front-line staff, with updates on typologies and regulatory changes
questions.e: The Directions mandate ongoing staff training — front-line staff must recognise red flags and know reporting lines; typologies and rules change, so training must too.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The board-approved KYC/AML policy of a bank should be reviewed
o: Periodically, to reflect regulatory changes and emerging risks
questions.e: Policies need periodic review — the 2016→2025 transition, the 2025 amendments, and new typologies (VDA, digital KYC) all require policy updates.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following is a valid combination under the periodic updation ladder?
questions.e: 2-8-10: high 2, medium 8, low 10. Any other pairing is wrong — the exam rotates these numbers across options.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A low-risk customer's KYC fell due in March 2025. Under the June 2025 amendment, the latest permissible updation is
o: One year after the due date or 30 June 2026, whichever is later
questions.e: Low-risk individuals get one year beyond the due date, or until 30 June 2026, whichever is later — here that means the later of March 2026 and June 2026, i.e. June 2026.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Business correspondents under the June 2025 framework may
questions.e: BCs may collect self-declarations for KYC updation — extending reach without diluting standards. Account approval, credit decisions and STR filing remain the bank's responsibility.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The 2025 Commercial Banks KYC Directions consolidated
o: The 2016 Direction plus all intervening amendments into one framework
questions.e: The 2025 Directions repealed the 2016 Master Direction for commercial banks and folded in every amendment (UCIC, SDD, face authentication, CKYCR responsibility, etc.) — one current rulebook.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The FATF was established in
questions.e: FATF was set up by the G-7 in Paris in 1989. The 40 Recommendations followed in 1990; the 8 Special Recommendations on TF came in October 2001.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: India became a full member of the FATF in
questions.e: India joined FATF as a full member in 2010 after observer status and assessment. Its 2024 mutual evaluation placed India on regular follow-up.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The FATF's 40 Recommendations were first issued in
questions.e: The original 40 Recommendations date to 1990; they were revised in 1996 and 2003, consolidated in 2012, and their text is periodically updated.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The 8 Special Recommendations on Terrorist Financing were issued in
questions.e: After 9/11, FATF issued 8 Special Recommendations on TF in October 2001 (a 9th, on cash couriers, in 2004); they were later merged into the consolidated 40.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: FATF Recommendation 10 deals with
questions.e: Rec 10 = CDD measures. Rec 11 = record-keeping; Rec 16 = wire transfers; Rec 24/25 = beneficial ownership transparency. The Rec numbers are heavily tested.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The FATF Recommendation that mandates reporting of suspicious transactions to the FIU is
questions.e: Rec 20 mandates reporting of suspicious transactions to the FIU — India's STR obligation under PMLA implements it. Rec 21 then prohibits tipping off.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: FATF Recommendation 21 covers
questions.e: Rec 21: financial institutions must not tip off customers about STR filings, and are protected when reporting in good faith — mirrored in PMLA Section 12.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The FATF Recommendation requiring complete originator and beneficiary information with wire transfers is
o: Complete originator and beneficiary information to accompany wire transfers
questions.e: Rec 16 (wire transfers): accurate originator and beneficiary information must travel with the transfer; missing info is itself a red flag and a compliance failure.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: FATF Recommendation 6 relates to
o: Targeted financial sanctions related to terrorism and terrorist financing
questions.e: Rec 6 = TFS for terrorism/TF (UNSCRs 1267/1373/1988); Rec 7 = TFS for proliferation financing. Rec 6 implementation guidance was updated in June 2026.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 deal with
o: Transparency and beneficial ownership of legal persons and legal arrangements
questions.e: Rec 24 (legal persons) and Rec 25 (legal arrangements like trusts) require countries to ensure adequate, accurate and timely BO information — India's 10%/15% thresholds implement this.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: As of the June 2026 FATF statement, the 'black list' (call for action) comprises
questions.e: The High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action are Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, and Myanmar — unchanged at the June 2026 plenary.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following was ADDED to the FATF grey list in June 2026?
questions.e: June 2026: Bosnia and Herzegovina and Iraq were added to the grey list; Algeria and Namibia were removed. The list then comprised 22 jurisdictions under increased monitoring.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following was REMOVED from the FATF grey list in June 2026?
questions.e: Algeria and Namibia were removed in June 2026 after addressing strategic deficiencies; Bosnia and Herzegovina and Iraq were added. Nepal and Kenya remained listed.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: As of 19 June 2026, the FATF grey list comprised
