questions.e: 22 jurisdictions under increased monitoring as of 19 June 2026. Transactions with grey-listed jurisdictions attract enhanced due diligence by banks.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Grey-listing by FATF results in
o: Enhanced due diligence on business relationships and transactions involving the listed jurisdiction
questions.e: Grey listing = increased monitoring + EDD obligations; it is not a sanction or freeze. Black-list (call for action) triggers countermeasures.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Mutual evaluations by FATF assess
o: Both technical compliance (laws in place) and effectiveness (11 Immediate Outcomes)
questions.e: The methodology has two limbs: technical compliance with the 40 Recommendations, and effectiveness across 11 Immediate Outcomes. India's 2024 MER put it on regular follow-up.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: India's 2024 FATF mutual evaluation outcome was
questions.e: India's 2024 MER resulted in 'regular follow-up' — a strong outcome indicating an effective AML/CFT regime. Grey/black listing applies to deficient jurisdictions.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The UN Security Council Resolution establishing the Al-Qaida/ISIL sanctions regime is
o: Sanctions against Al-Qaida/ISIL and associated individuals/entities
questions.e: UNSCR 1267 (1999) established the Al-Qaida sanctions regime; ISIL listings were split into Resolution 2253 (2015). Banks screen customers against these consolidated lists.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The UN Security Council Resolution establishing the separate Taliban sanctions regime is
questions.e: UNSCR 1988 (2011) split the Taliban from the 1267 regime into its own sanctions list. RBI's 7 September 2026 instruction updated banks on this list.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: UN Security Council Resolution 1373 (2001)
o: Requires states to criminalise terrorist financing and freeze terrorist assets
questions.e: UNSCR 1373, adopted after 9/11, obliges all states to criminalise TF, freeze terrorist funds without delay, and deny safe haven — implemented in India via UAPA Section 51A.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Section 51A of the UAPA deals with
o: Freezing of funds/assets of designated terrorists and organisations
questions.e: UAPA s.51A operationalises UN sanctions: banks screen, verify matches, freeze without prior notice, and report. It is the TF-freezing counterpart to PMLA's attachment machinery.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under the MHA procedure for UAPA Section 51A, on finding a match with a designated list, the bank must verify within
questions.e: Verification within 5 working days of detecting a potential match; if verified, a freeze order follows within 24 hours — without prior notice to the customer.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Once a UAPA Section 51A match is verified, the freeze order must be obtained
o: Within 24 hours, without prior notice to the customer
questions.e: 24 hours, without prior notice — prior notice would let funds flee. The bank also files an STR with FIU-IND on the frozen relationship.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: After freezing under UAPA Section 51A, the bank must
o: File an STR with FIU-IND and report to the authorities
questions.e: Freezing is followed by STR filing and reporting up the chain (to the MHA's IS-I Division via prescribed channels). Informing the customer first would be tipping off.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The UAPA was originally enacted in
questions.e: The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act dates to 1967; major amendments (2004, 2008, 2012, 2019) expanded its terror-financing and designation provisions.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The WMD Act, 2005 through Section 12A provides for
o: Freezing of funds/assets related to proliferation financing
questions.e: Section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction Act extends the freeze-and-report machinery to proliferation financing, complementing FATF Recommendation 7.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: FATF Recommendation 7 covers targeted financial sanctions related to
questions.e: Rec 7 = TFS for proliferation of WMD (UNSCRs 1718/1737 regimes); Rec 6 = TFS for terrorism/TF. India's WMD Act s.12A implements Rec 7 domestically.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Non-profit organisations are a TF concern under FATF
questions.e: Rec 8 requires countries to ensure NPOs are not misused for TF — the basis for India's NTR reporting and DARPAN-registration checks on NPO clients.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Screening of customer databases against UN-designated lists should be done
o: At onboarding and on an ongoing basis as lists are updated
questions.e: Screening is continuous: at onboarding and whenever lists update (RBI circulates UN list changes, e.g. the September 2026 Taliban update). One-time screening misses later designations.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A 'false positive' in sanctions screening means
o: A name match that on investigation is not the designated person
questions.e: Name matches need verification (within 5 working days under s.51A) precisely because common names generate false positives; freezing on an unverified match would be unlawful.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The FATF 'Immediate Outcomes' number
questions.e: 11 Immediate Outcomes measure effectiveness in mutual evaluations (e.g. IO.3 supervision, IO.4 preventive measures, IO.9 TF investigation). The 40 is the Recommendations count.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which FATF Recommendation requires countries to criminalise terrorist financing?
questions.e: Rec 5: criminalise TF consistent with the TF Convention. Rec 10 = CDD, Rec 20 = STR reporting, Rec 40 = other forms of international cooperation.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Designated non-financial businesses and professions (DNFBPs) under FATF include
o: Casinos, real estate agents, dealers in precious metals/stones, lawyers, accountants, TCSPs
questions.e: DNFBPs — casinos, real-estate agents, precious-metal dealers, lawyers, accountants, trust/company service providers — must apply CDD, record-keeping and STR duties; India's 2023 notifications extended PMLA to some of these.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The June 2026 update to FATF Recommendation 6 guidance concerned
o: Implementation of targeted financial sanctions related to terrorism/TF
questions.e: FATF updated its Rec 6 implementation guidance in June 2026 — TFS for terrorism/TF. Exam-relevant as a current-affairs anchor for the sanctions chapter.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Nepal's presence on the FATF grey list (as of June 2026) means Indian banks should
o: Apply enhanced due diligence to Nepal-linked relationships and transactions
questions.e: Grey-list jurisdiction = EDD, not prohibition. Banks calibrate monitoring, source-of-funds checks and senior oversight for Nepal-linked business.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Egmont Group's secure channel for FIU information exchange is called
questions.e: The Egmont Secure Web (ESW) is the closed network through which FIUs exchange intelligence. FINnet is FIU-IND's domestic reporting gateway; SWIFT/SFMS are payment messaging systems.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Terrorist financing differs from money laundering in detection because
o: It may use small, legitimate-looking amounts with no placement stage
questions.e: TF can move tiny sums of clean money, so threshold-based monitoring misses it; detection relies on behavioural red flags, NPO scrutiny, MVTS monitoring and sanctions screening.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Charities and NPOs are vulnerable to TF abuse through
o: Diversion of donations, sham charities, and commingling of legitimate and terrorist funds
questions.e: FATF typologies: donations diverted, charities as fronts, commingling — hence Rec 8, NTR reporting above ₹10 lakh, and DARPAN verification of NPO clients.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under UAPA Section 51A, the freezing action is taken
o: After giving the customer 30 days' notice
Without prior notice to the designated person
questions.e: Without prior notice — the element of surprise prevents dissipation of funds. The order is an executive freeze under the MHA procedure, subject to later review/unfreezing mechanisms.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which Indian Act criminalises terrorist financing as required by UNSCR 1373?
questions.e: The UAPA (ss. 17, 40 and related provisions, plus s.51A freezing) criminalises TF and implements UNSCR 1373. PMLA covers laundering of crime proceeds including TF-linked funds as predicate-linked property.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A bank receives the RBI circular updating the UNSC Taliban list. The first action is to
o: Screen the customer database against the updated list
questions.e: Screen first against the updated designations; only verified matches get frozen (within 24 hours) plus STR. Blanket freezing of a nationality's accounts would be unlawful and discriminatory.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: In correspondent banking, a 'nostro' account is
o: Our account with you (with the foreign bank)
questions.e: Nostro = our account with you (the Indian bank's account with its foreign correspondent); vostro = your account with us (the foreign bank's account with the Indian bank). The Latin tags are classic exam material.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A 'vostro' account is
o: Our account with the foreign bank
The foreign respondent bank's account with us
questions.e: Vostro = your account with us. Correspondent banking AML risk concentrates here: the correspondent may not know the respondent's underlying customers (nested relationships).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The highest AML risk in correspondent banking comes from
o: Nested correspondent relationships and payable-through accounts
questions.e: Nested correspondents let a respondent's downstream clients use the channel opaquely; payable-through accounts let the respondent's customers draw directly on the correspondent account — both demand EDD.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: EDD for a correspondent banking relationship includes
o: Understanding the respondent's business, assessing its AML controls and supervision, senior management approval
questions.e: Correspondent EDD: know the respondent institution, evaluate its AML/CFT controls and supervision quality, document responsibilities, and get senior management approval before establishing the relationship.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The industry standard principles for correspondent banking AML were issued by
questions.e: The Wolfsberg Group (major international banks) issued Correspondent Banking Principles — the industry benchmark for respondent due diligence, alongside FATF guidance.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A payable-through account allows
o: Only the correspondent's staff to transact
The respondent bank's customers to draw directly on the correspondent account
questions.e: Payable-through accounts give the respondent's customers direct drawing rights on the correspondent — effectively sub-accounts for unknown third parties, hence the EDD requirement.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under FATF Recommendation 16, a wire transfer must carry
o: Complete and accurate originator and beneficiary information
questions.e: Rec 16: originator and beneficiary information must travel with the wire; incomplete information is a red flag and banks should consider restricting or reporting such transfers.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Trade-based money laundering commonly uses
o: Over/under-invoicing, multiple invoicing, phantom shipments and mis-described goods
questions.e: TBML disguises value movement as trade: inflated or deflated invoices, repeated invoicing of one shipment, shipments that never existed, and mis-described goods.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Multiple invoicing of the same shipment is a typology of
questions.e: Invoicing the same goods several times justifies multiple cross-border payments for one real shipment — a TBML technique that moves value while looking like trade.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Notification S.O. 1072(E) (7 March 2023) designated as reporting entities
o: Virtual digital asset service providers for five specified activities
questions.e: Five VDA activities (fiat↔VDA exchange, VDA↔VDA exchange, transfer, safekeeping/administration, issuance-related services) became designated business under PMLA, with FIU-IND registration mandatory.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: VDA service providers under PMLA must
o: Register with FIU-IND and comply with verification, record-keeping and reporting obligations
questions.e: As reporting entities, VDA providers must register with FIU-IND and follow the full PMLA stack: CDD, record maintenance, and CTR/STR-type reporting — including offshore providers serving India.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Which of the following is a VDA-related red flag for a bank?
o: A customer holding a PPF account
Frequent fiat-to-crypto conversions inconsistent with the customer's profile via unregistered exchanges
questions.e: Profile-inconsistent crypto conversions, especially through unregistered/offshore exchanges, plus mixer/privacy-coin use, are VDA red flags. Normal investments and salary credits are not.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: CKYC stands for
o: Central KYC — the centralised KYC records system
questions.e: Central KYC: a centralised registry (CKYCR) giving each customer a single KYC identifier usable across the financial sector (banks, securities, insurance, pension).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) is managed by
questions.e: CERSAI (Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest) operates the CKYCR; its portal is ckycindia.in. Banks upload KYC records there within 10 days of establishing a relationship.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The KYC Identifier issued by CKYCR is
questions.e: The CKYC identifier is 14 digits, communicated to the customer in writing and usable across financial sector entities to fetch the KYC record instead of repeating KYC.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Banks must upload KYC records to CKYCR within
o: 10 days of establishing the account-based relationship
questions.e: 10 days from commencement of the account-based relationship (scanned copies + data); updates must be reflected within 7 days. The 29 December 2025 amendment fixed responsibility for uploads on banks.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: If a customer already has a CKYC identifier and the information is unchanged, the bank may
o: Download the KYC record from CKYCR instead of fresh KYC
questions.e: The registry's purpose is reusability: download the existing CKYC record when data is unchanged — one of CKYC's core efficiency benefits, tested via the operating guidelines v1.5 (Dec 2025).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Aadhaar e-KYC is provided by
questions.e: The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) provides e-KYC (OTP/biometric-based paperless verification) used by banks for instant, paperless onboarding.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Offline Aadhaar XML allows
o: Sharing masked Aadhaar details via secure XML/QR with a share code, without biometrics
questions.e: Offline Aadhaar (XML/QR) lets customers share masked, digitally-signed KYC details with a share code — no biometrics, no UIDAI server hit — a privacy-preserving KYC option.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: V-CIP requires the customer to be
o: In India during the live session
questions.e: V-CIP: live audio-video with the customer physically in India, conducted by an authorised official; pre-recorded videos are not permitted.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: For a company, the beneficial owner is the natural person holding
o: More than 10% of shares, capital or profits, or exercising control
questions.e: Company threshold: more than 10% (shares/capital/profits) or control through other means. 'More than 10%' excludes exactly-10% holdings — a precision the exam tests.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: For a trust, beneficiaries qualify as beneficial owners at
questions.e: Trust beneficiaries: 10% or more interest (note: 'or more' — unlike the company's 'more than 10%'), plus author, trustee, protector and persons with ultimate control.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under the PMLA rules, the beneficial-ownership threshold for a company is shareholding of more than:
questions.e: Beneficial owner: >10% for companies, >10% for trusts, >15% for partnership firms and unincorporated associations.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: If no natural person is identified as beneficial owner, the fallback is
questions.e: Senior managing official is deemed the beneficial owner when ownership/control analysis identifies no natural person — the Rules always end with an identified person.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: PEPs were formally defined in the PML Rules in
questions.e: March 2023 amendments defined PEPs (domestic and foreign, plus family/close associates) in the PML Rules, triggering EDD: senior management approval, source of wealth/funds, enhanced monitoring.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under the PML Rules, a 'politically exposed person' is:
o: An individual entrusted with a prominent public function in a foreign country
questions.e: PEPs are individuals entrusted with prominent public functions abroad (heads of state, senior politicians, senior judicial/military officers) plus family and close associates.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: EDD for a PEP relationship requires
o: Senior management approval, source of wealth/funds established, enhanced ongoing monitoring
questions.e: PEP EDD: senior management sign-off, establish source of wealth and source of funds, enhanced ongoing monitoring — because PEP-linked funds may be corruption proceeds.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A 'customer red flag' includes
o: Reluctance to provide KYC documents and use of aliases
questions.e: Customer red flags: evasiveness about identity, aliases, PO boxes, reluctance to meet, PEP links. Salary credits, bill payments and FD renewals are normal behaviour.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A 'transaction red flag' includes
questions.e: Structuring just below the CTR threshold is the textbook transaction red flag. Regular EMIs, genuine remittances and tax payments have clear economic rationale.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A 'geographic red flag' includes
questions.e: Geographic red flags: high-risk jurisdictions (FATF-listed), offshore centres with weak supervision, conflict zones. Domestic routine transactions are not geographic flags.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Round-tripping of funds is
o: Sending funds abroad and bringing them back as apparent foreign investment to disguise origin
questions.e: Round-tripping layers money offshore and integrates it as 'foreign investment' — disguising domestic criminal proceeds as legitimate inbound investment.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: In the PNB fraud case, ED's provisional attachment was approximately
questions.e: ED attached about ₹2,324.97 crore in the Nirav Modi/Mehul Choksi case; the fraud itself was ~₹13,850 crore via fraudulent LoUs; ₹66.33 crore was later released to PNB (June 2025).

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: In June 2025, a special PMLA court released to PNB attached assets worth
questions.e: ₹66.33 crore of attached assets were released/restored to PNB — illustrating Section 8's restoration of confiscated property to victims with quantifiable loss.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The PNB–Nirav Modi fraud was disclosed in
questions.e: PNB disclosed the ~₹13,850 crore LoU fraud in February 2018 — India's landmark trade-finance control failure, rooted in the SWIFT–CBS disconnect.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The IIBF Certificate Examination in AML/KYC comprises
questions.e: 120 MCQs for 100 marks in 2 hours, in English, no negative marking, 60% to pass — the pattern consistently reported for this IIBF certificate exam.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The pass mark for the IIBF AML/KYC certificate exam is
questions.e: 60% (60 marks out of 100). With no negative marking, attempting all 120 questions is the rational strategy.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The exam fee for the IIBF AML/KYC certificate (plus GST) is
questions.e: As listed by IIBF: ₹1,100 for members, ₹1,600 for non-members, plus GST. The official study material is the Macmillan 2023 edition book.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: There is negative marking in the IIBF AML/KYC certificate exam
questions.e: No negative marking — attempt every question. This is explicitly stated in the exam pattern and shapes exam strategy.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The medium of the IIBF AML/KYC certificate exam is
questions.e: The exam is conducted in English only — unlike JAIIB/CAIIB which offer Hindi. Prepare terminology in English.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The official study book for the IIBF AML/KYC certificate exam is published by
questions.e: IIBF lists the Macmillan-published study book (2023 edition) as the official course material for the Certificate Examination in AML/KYC.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: In the exam, when unsure between options, the best approach is to choose the answer that
o: Strengthens detection, due diligence and reporting
questions.e: The exam rewards the compliance-first instinct: more diligence, more monitoring, more reporting. Options that weaken controls are almost always wrong.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: A 'mule account' shows which pattern?
o: Money received and quickly forwarded, inconsistent with the holder's profile
questions.e: Mule accounts receive illicit funds and forward them rapidly, with activity inconsistent with the holder's profile — a placement/layering red flag banks monitor for.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The Financial Intelligence Unit – India (FIU-IND) functions under the:
o: Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.e: FIU-IND is the national agency for receiving and analysing suspicious transaction reports, under the Department of Revenue.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: The CKYC Operating Guidelines version 1.5 is dated
questions.e: CKYC Operating Guidelines v1.5 (Dec 2025) detail upload/download/dissemination duties — including that updates about a customer are disseminated to REs availing registry services.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Information updated about a customer in CKYCR is
o: Disseminated by the Registry to reporting entities availing its services for that customer
questions.e: A key CKYCR function: updated KYC records are pushed to REs that use the registry for that customer — keeping KYC current across the financial sector.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under the RBI's draft Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026, issued in September 2026, the proposed maximum duration of a temporary debit hold on amounts suspected to be linked to money-mule activity or cyber-enabled fraud is:
questions.e: The draft SOP proposes that the hold must be lifted within 60 days unless law enforcement directs otherwise. It follows the Supreme Court's 4 August 2026 order directing the RBI to prescribe the procedure; public comments were invited until 2 October 2026, with proposed commencement on 1 April 2027.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under the RBI's draft standard operating procedure for suspected money-mule accounts (September 2026), the proposed timeline sequence is:
o: Customer gets 20 calendar days to establish legitimacy, bank gets 10 days to assess, then referral to police with 30 days for a formal restraint order
Bank freezes the account indefinitely and informs the customer later
Customer gets 60 days, bank gets 30 days, police gets 90 days
No timelines are prescribed in the draft
questions.e: The draft gives the customer 20 calendar days to prove the legitimacy of the transaction (identity, context, source of funds); the bank then has 10 calendar days to assess the explanation and lift the hold if satisfactory. If suspicion persists, the case is referred to the jurisdictional police through the NCRP/CFCFRMS portal, and law enforcement has 30 days to issue a formal statutory restraint order — banks cannot keep funds frozen indefinitely.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: By the RBI's September 2026 amendment to the KYC directions, Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) dealing with urban and rural co-operative banks:
o: May submit certified copies of KYC documents, a facility previously available to NRIs and PIOs
Are exempted from all KYC requirements
Must appear in person before the co-operative bank's board
Can no longer open accounts with co-operative banks
questions.e: The amendment, effective immediately and issued under the PMLA, 2002, extends the certified-copy facility to FPIs: the copy may be attested by an authorised official of an overseas branch of a scheduled commercial bank registered in India, a notary public abroad, a court magistrate/judge, or the Indian Embassy/Consulate — removing the need for in-person comparison of copies with originals.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: As defined in the RBI's draft KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, a 'money mule account' is:
o: An account used, knowingly or unknowingly, to move the proceeds of cyber fraud
Any account with a balance above Rs 10 lakh
An account dormant for over two years
An account opened through a business correspondent
questions.e: The draft defines a money-mule account as one used 'knowingly or unknowingly' to move the proceeds of cyber fraud, and inserts a detailed SOP on suspected mule accounts as a new annex to the KYC Directions, 2025. The draft was issued after the Supreme Court's 4 August 2026 order in the suo motu digital-arrest-scams proceedings.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: On 24 Sep 2026 the RBI imposed a Rs 3.10 lakh penalty on Ola Financial Services for:
o: Breach of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules reporting timelines
Failure to file STRs with FIU-IND
questions.e: The RBI penalised Ola Financial Services Rs 3.10 lakh for KYC non-compliance under section 30(1) read with section 26(6) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

questions.subject: AML / KYC
questions.q: Under which statute did the RBI penalise Ola Financial Services in September 2026?
questions.e: The Rs 3.10 lakh penalty for KYC non-compliance was imposed under section 30(1) read with section 26(6) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In a Core Banking Solution, a customer is treated as a customer of the
o: branch where the account was opened
questions.e: CBS centralises all accounts in a single database, so the relationship belongs to the bank rather than any one branch. This is what makes 'anywhere banking' possible across branches and channels.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: CIF in a CBS environment stands for
questions.e: The Customer Information File holds the single customer view — personal details, KYC status and every relationship with the bank. It powers AML screening, relationship pricing and cross-selling.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Which of these is NOT a widely used CBS platform in Indian banks?
questions.e: Finacle (Infosys/EdgeVerve), BaNCS (TCS) and Flexcube (Oracle) are the dominant CBS products in India. Microsoft Windows is an operating system, not a core banking application.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The primary benefit of CBS for management reporting is
o: a single source of truth for reports
questions.e: Because every transaction posts to one central database, management reports draw consistent, real-time data. This single source of truth enables centralised risk, compliance and ADF reporting.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In CBS, day-to-day branch transactions are processed in
questions.e: CBS runs online transaction processing, updating the central database the moment a debit or credit is entered. Batch jobs are reserved for end-of-day work like interest application and standing instructions.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: EOD/BOD in a CBS context refers to
o: end of department / beginning of department
questions.e: End-of-day and beginning-of-day processes run interest, charges, standing instructions, NPA marking and statutory reports as scheduled batches. They execute after online transaction hours close.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The maker-checker concept in CBS means
o: the branch manager does all entries
one user initiates and a different user authorises a transaction
questions.e: Maker-checker segregates duties: the maker enters the transaction and a different checker authorises it. This is a fundamental preventive application control against error and fraud.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A CDM differs from an ATM in that a CDM
questions.e: A Cash Deposit Machine accepts cash deposits with instant or near-instant credit, while an ATM primarily dispenses cash. Many modern machines combine both functions.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: India's ATM switching network NFS is operated by
questions.e: The National Financial Switch, India's largest ATM-switching network, is operated by NPCI. It interconnects ATMs of member banks for interoperable cash withdrawals.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: IDRBT, the institution that set up the INFINET network for banks, is located in:
questions.e: The Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology (IDRBT), Hyderabad — set up by the RBI — built INFINET, the closed user-group network for banks and FIs.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: SFMS in Indian banking stands for
questions.e: The Structured Financial Messaging System is the secure domestic messaging backbone for NEFT, RTGS and government transactions. It is India's counterpart to SWIFT for domestic payment traffic.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: MPLS is preferred for CBS branch connectivity mainly because it
o: provides private, QoS-managed paths for critical traffic
questions.e: Multi-Protocol Label Switching creates private virtual paths with quality-of-service guarantees, giving CBS transactions predictable latency and security. Banks use it to link branches and data centres reliably.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: VSAT connectivity in banking is used to
questions.e: Very Small Aperture Terminal links use satellite communication to reach branches where terrestrial lines are unavailable or unreliable. They were historically important for rural branch computerisation.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The OSI model has
questions.e: OSI defines seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation and Application. The TCP/IP model collapses these into four layers.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In the OSI model, routing and IP addressing happen at the
questions.e: Layer 3, the Network layer, handles logical addressing (IP) and routing packets across networks. The Data Link layer below it handles MAC addressing within a LAN.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: TCP differs from UDP in that TCP is
questions.e: TCP establishes a connection, sequences segments and retransmits lost data, guaranteeing delivery — essential for CBS and payment messages. UDP skips handshakes for speed, suiting DNS and streaming.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: IPv4 addresses are
questions.e: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (about 4.3 billion unique addresses), written as four dotted octets. IPv6 expanded this to 128 bits to solve address exhaustion.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: HTTPS traffic by default uses port
questions.e: Port 443 carries HTTPS (HTTP over TLS), while port 80 is plain HTTP. Banking portals must use 443 so customer sessions are encrypted.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Port 22 is associated with
questions.e: SSH (Secure Shell) on port 22 gives encrypted remote administration, replacing insecure Telnet on port 23. FTP uses port 21 and SMTP uses port 25.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: DNS primarily resolves
questions.e: The Domain Name System translates human-readable names like www.rbi.org.in into IP addresses. It runs over UDP port 53.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A switch differs from a hub because a switch
o: forwards frames only to the destination port using a MAC table
broadcasts every frame to all ports
questions.e: A hub repeats every incoming frame to all ports, wasting bandwidth and leaking traffic. A switch learns MAC addresses and forwards selectively, which is faster and more secure.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A router operates primarily at the
questions.e: Routers forward packets between different networks using IP addresses at Layer 3. Switches stay within a LAN at Layer 2 using MAC addresses.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A gateway is used to
o: translate between different protocols or networks
questions.e: Gateways sit at network boundaries and convert between dissimilar protocols or architectures. A router connects similar IP networks; a gateway bridges different worlds.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In a star topology, failure of the central device
questions.e: Every node in a star connects through the central hub or switch, creating a single point of failure. Mesh topologies avoid this with redundant paths.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Which topology offers the highest fault tolerance?
questions.e: A full mesh connects every node to every other node, so any single link failure leaves alternate paths. The cost is the large number of links required.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: MAN in networking stands for
questions.e: A Metropolitan Area Network spans a city — larger than a LAN, smaller than a WAN. Bank networks connecting branches across a city are typically MANs.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: DHCP is used to
o: automatically assign IP addresses to devices
questions.e: The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol leases IP addresses, subnet masks and gateway/DNS settings to devices joining a network. It avoids manual addressing errors.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The Presentation layer of OSI handles
o: encryption, compression and data format translation
questions.e: Layer 6 translates between application and network formats, handling encryption/decryption and compression. TLS operates around this layer.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Packet switching differs from circuit switching in that packet switching
o: splits data into packets that share network resources
dedicates a path for the whole call
questions.e: Packet switching chops data into packets that travel independently and share links efficiently — the basis of the internet. Circuit switching reserves a dedicated path, as in traditional telephone calls.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Latency in a network refers to
questions.e: Latency is the time delay for a packet to travel from source to destination. CBS branch performance depends on low latency as much as on bandwidth.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A firewall's primary function is to
o: filter network traffic according to security policy
questions.e: Firewalls inspect packets and allow or deny them based on rules for addresses, ports and protocols. They sit at network boundaries as preventive controls.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The three-tier CBS architecture consists of
questions.e: The presentation tier serves user interfaces, the application tier runs business logic, and the database tier holds the central RDBMS. This separation lets banks scale and secure each tier independently.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Data migration is critical in CBS implementation because
o: vendors do it free of charge
dirty legacy master data corrupts the new system
questions.e: Migrating customer masters, balances and histories from legacy systems is the top failure point in CBS rollouts. Cleansing, reconciling and validating migrated data decides go-live success.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The General Ledger in CBS is updated
o: by every financial transaction as double-entry
questions.e: Every CBS transaction posts balanced debit and credit entries to the General Ledger in real time. The trial balance must tally daily, and breaks are investigated immediately.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Automated Data Flow (ADF) as required by RBI means
o: regulatory returns generated straight from source systems without manual intervention
questions.e: RBI's ADF project requires banks to produce regulatory returns directly from their CBS/source systems. It eliminates manual aggregation errors and is a favourite exam phrase.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An OLTP system like CBS is optimised for
questions.e: Online Transaction Processing handles thousands of small concurrent debits/credits with ACID guarantees. Analytical workloads belong to OLAP data warehouses instead.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Business Correspondents extend banking through
o: agents with handheld/micro-ATM devices in unbanked areas
questions.e: The BC model uses local agents equipped with biometric micro-ATMs to offer deposits, withdrawals and remittances beyond branch reach. It is central to financial inclusion.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A modem's function is to
o: modulate/demodulate signals between digital devices and analog lines
questions.e: Modem stands for modulator-demodulator: it converts digital computer signals for transmission over analog telephone lines and back. Routers and switches do not perform this conversion.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Which device connects a LAN to a WAN?
questions.e: A router forwards traffic between the LAN and the WAN using IP routing. Hubs and repeaters only extend signals within one network segment.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: SMTP, used for sending email, operates on port
questions.e: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol sends mail on port 25 (submission often on 587). POP3 (110) and IMAP (143) retrieve mail, while DNS uses port 53.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: RDP, used for remote desktop administration, uses port
questions.e: Remote Desktop Protocol listens on TCP port 3389. Exposing it to the internet without controls is a common attack vector banks must guard.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Centralised KYC/AML screening in CBS is enabled by
questions.e: Because the Customer Information File aggregates every relationship of a customer bank-wide, sanctions and AML screening run once centrally. Branch-level registers could never give this consolidated view.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A DBMS is preferred over a flat file system mainly because it provides
o: data integrity, security and concurrent access
questions.e: A DBMS enforces integrity constraints, access control and concurrent multi-user access that flat files cannot. It also removes the redundancy and inconsistency of duplicated files.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In an RDBMS, data is organised as
o: tables of rows and columns linked by keys
questions.e: The relational model stores data in tables (relations) where rows are tuples and columns are attributes, linked through primary and foreign keys. SQL is its standard language.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A primary key must be
questions.e: A primary key uniquely identifies each row and cannot contain nulls or duplicates. Only one primary key is allowed per table.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A foreign key
o: uniquely identifies rows in its own table
references the primary key of another table to enforce referential integrity
questions.e: Foreign keys create relationships between tables and prevent orphan rows — you cannot insert a loan for a non-existent customer. This is referential integrity in action.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A candidate key is
o: a duplicate of the primary key
any attribute set that could uniquely identify rows
questions.e: Candidate keys are all minimal attribute sets capable of unique identification; one of them is chosen as the primary key. A super key is any superset of a candidate key.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Atomicity in ACID means a transaction is
questions.e: Atomicity guarantees that either all operations of a transaction complete or none do — a fund transfer cannot debit one account without crediting the other. Failed transactions are fully rolled back.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Consistency in ACID means
o: a transaction moves the database from one valid state to another
questions.e: Consistency ensures every transaction preserves database rules and constraints, like balance non-negativity. A transaction that would violate integrity is rejected.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Isolation in ACID means
o: only one user may log in
concurrent transactions execute without interfering with each other
questions.e: Isolation makes concurrent transactions behave as if they ran serially, preventing lost updates and dirty reads. Locking and multiversion methods implement it.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Durability in ACID means
questions.e: Once committed, a transaction's effects are permanent — typically via write-ahead logging to stable storage. A power failure after commit must not lose the CBS entry.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: First Normal Form (1NF) requires
o: every determinant to be a key
atomic values and no repeating groups
questions.e: 1NF forbids multi-valued cells and repeating groups: each cell holds one atomic value and each row is uniquely identifiable. Higher normal forms build on this foundation.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Second Normal Form (2NF) additionally requires
o: no partial dependency on a composite key
questions.e: 2NF is 1NF plus the rule that every non-key attribute must depend on the whole primary key, not part of it. Partial dependencies are removed into separate tables.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Third Normal Form (3NF) additionally requires
o: no transitive dependency of non-key attributes
questions.e: 3NF is 2NF plus the elimination of transitive dependencies — non-key attributes must depend only on the key, not on other non-key attributes. This kills most update anomalies.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) states that
o: every determinant must be a candidate key
questions.e: BCNF strengthens 3NF: for every functional dependency X → Y, X must be a candidate key. It fixes edge cases with overlapping candidate keys that 3NF misses.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An insertion anomaly occurs when
o: new data cannot be added without other unrelated data
a row is inserted too slowly
a table has too many indexes
questions.e: In an unnormalised design you cannot, say, add a new branch until a customer from it exists — there is nowhere else to store branch data. Normalization gives each fact its own table.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A deletion anomaly occurs when
o: deleting one fact unintentionally loses another needed fact
questions.e: If the only row mentioning a product is deleted along with a customer, the product record vanishes too. Proper decomposition keeps independent facts in independent tables.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An update anomaly arises because
o: the same fact stored in many rows must be changed everywhere
questions.e: Redundant storage means changing, say, a branch address in one row but missing another leaves the database inconsistent. Normalization stores each fact once.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In an ER diagram, a diamond shape represents a
questions.e: Chen notation draws entities as rectangles, attributes as ovals and relationships as diamonds. The ER model is then mapped to relational tables.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: CREATE, ALTER and DROP belong to
questions.e: Data Definition Language commands define and modify schema objects like tables and indexes. DML manipulates rows, DCL manages permissions and TCL manages transactions.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE belong to
questions.e: Data Manipulation Language commands read and change the rows inside tables. They are the workhorses of CBS application queries.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: GRANT and REVOKE belong to
questions.e: Data Control Language commands grant or withdraw privileges on database objects. They implement the authorization leg of AAA inside the DBMS.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: COMMIT, ROLLBACK and SAVEPOINT belong to
questions.e: Transaction Control Language manages transaction boundaries: COMMIT makes changes permanent, ROLLBACK undoes them, SAVEPOINT sets partial rollback points. They deliver ACID atomicity.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An INNER JOIN returns
o: only rows with matching values in both tables
questions.e: INNER JOIN keeps only the rows whose join keys match in both tables. LEFT JOIN additionally keeps all left-table rows, and CROSS JOIN produces every combination.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A LEFT JOIN returns
o: all rows from the left table plus matches from the right
questions.e: LEFT (OUTER) JOIN preserves every row of the left table, filling NULLs where the right table has no match. It is the standard way to find customers without loans, for example.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A CROSS JOIN returns
o: the cartesian product of both tables
questions.e: CROSS JOIN pairs every row of the first table with every row of the second — m × n rows. It is rarely wanted in banking queries and usually signals a missing join condition.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A database view is
o: a stored SELECT query presenting a virtual table
questions.e: Views simplify complex queries and enforce security by exposing only permitted columns and rows. Most views store no data themselves; they execute their query on access.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Creating an index on a table generally
o: slows down both reads and writes
speeds up reads but slows down writes
questions.e: Indexes are lookup structures that accelerate SELECT and join performance but must be maintained on every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE. Over-indexing hurts CBS transaction throughput.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A database trigger
o: fires automatically on INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE
questions.e: Triggers are stored procedures the DBMS executes automatically when specified data events occur. Banks use them for audit logging and enforcing complex business rules.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: UNION differs from UNION ALL in that UNION
o: removes duplicate rows from the combined result
questions.e: UNION merges result sets and eliminates duplicates (adding sort/hash work), while UNION ALL keeps every row and runs faster. Both require compatible column lists.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The Database Administrator (DBA) is primarily responsible for
o: physical design, backup, performance and security of databases
questions.e: The DBA handles installation, storage design, backup/recovery, tuning and access control — the operational side. The Data Administrator instead owns enterprise data policy and definitions.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The Data Administrator (DA), unlike the DBA, focuses on
o: enterprise-wide data policy, standards and ownership
questions.e: The DA governs what data means, who owns it and the standards for its use across the organisation. The DBA implements the physical databases that hold it.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A data warehouse is characterised as
questions.e: Inmon's definition: warehouses organise data by subject, integrate sources consistently, keep history over time and are not updated in place. They feed OLAP analytics, unlike OLTP CBS systems.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: ETL stands for
questions.e: ETL pipelines extract data from source systems like CBS, transform (cleanse, conform) it, and load it into the warehouse. ETL quality decides MIS trustworthiness.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: OLAP differs from OLTP in that OLAP
o: runs complex analytical queries over historical data
questions.e: Online Analytical Processing supports multidimensional analysis and reporting on warehouse data. OLTP instead handles high volumes of small concurrent transactions.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The data dictionary (system catalog) stores
o: metadata: table definitions, constraints and privileges
questions.e: The dictionary is data about data — schemas, data types, relationships and access rights. Auditors consult it to understand the database structure.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A deadlock occurs when
o: two transactions each wait for a lock held by the other
questions.e: In a deadlock neither transaction can proceed, so the DBMS breaks it by timeout or by choosing a victim to roll back. Good application design minimises lock holding time.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A dirty read is
o: reading uncommitted data of another transaction
questions.e: If transaction A reads data that transaction B has modified but not committed, and B rolls back, A acted on phantom data. Proper isolation levels prevent this.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Two-phase locking ensures serializability through
o: a growing phase acquiring locks followed by a shrinking phase releasing them
questions.e: In 2PL a transaction first acquires all needed locks (growing phase) and only then releases them (shrinking phase). This discipline guarantees the schedule is serializable.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The CAP theorem states a distributed system can guarantee only two of
questions.e: When network partitions occur, a distributed store must choose between consistency and availability. Bank designers weigh this trade-off in distributed CBS and payment architectures.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The waterfall SDLC model is characterised by
o: strictly sequential phases with sign-off before the next begins
questions.e: Waterfall flows requirements → design → code → test → deploy in order, revisiting earlier phases only at cost. It suits well-understood, stable requirements but struggles with change.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Boehm's spiral model is best described as
questions.e: Each spiral loop addresses the highest risks through prototyping and stakeholder review before committing further. It fits large, high-risk banking system projects.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Agile/Scrum delivers software through
o: one big release after two years
time-boxed sprints pulling work from a product backlog
questions.e: Scrum teams deliver working increments every sprint (typically 2–4 weeks), reprioritising from the backlog. Banks increasingly use it for digital-channel development.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) is
o: business users verifying the system meets requirements before sign-off
questions.e: UAT is the business's final gate: real users run real scenarios and formally accept the system. No CBS module goes live without UAT sign-off.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Confidentiality in the CIA triad means
o: information is disclosed only to authorised parties
questions.e: Confidentiality protects information from unauthorised disclosure through access controls and encryption. Breaching it means the wrong eyes saw the data.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Integrity in the CIA triad means
o: information is accurate and protected from unauthorised modification
questions.e: Integrity ensures data remains correct and trustworthy — no unauthorised creation, alteration or deletion. Hashing and digital signatures are its classic technical controls.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Availability in the CIA triad means
o: systems and data are accessible when needed by authorised users
questions.e: Availability keeps CBS, ATMs and payment channels running despite failures or attacks. Redundancy, DR sites and DDoS defences protect it.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: AAA in security stands for
questions.e: Authentication proves who you are, authorization decides what you may do, and accounting logs what you did. Together they form the access-control lifecycle.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Which is a valid second authentication factor?
o: employee ID printed on a card
questions.e: Factors are something you know, have or are; the username is merely an identifier, not a factor. An OTP on a separate device adds a 'have' factor to the password's 'know' factor.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Discretionary Access Control (DAC) means
o: owners decide who gets access to their objects
access follows security labels assigned by the system
questions.e: In DAC, the data owner grants or revokes permissions at their discretion — like file sharing settings. MAC instead enforces system-wide labels regardless of owner wishes.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) assigns permissions based on
questions.e: RBAC groups permissions into roles (teller, supervisor, auditor) and assigns users to roles. It enforces least privilege and simplifies reviews when staff change jobs.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A virus differs from a worm in that a virus
o: spreads without any host file or user action
needs a host program and usually user action to spread
questions.e: Viruses attach to host files and need execution to propagate, while worms self-replicate across networks unaided. Both are malware, but their propagation mechanics differ.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A Trojan horse is malware that
o: disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users
questions.e: Trojans pose as useful programs — fake apps, cracked software — to get users to install them. Unlike viruses they do not infect other files; they open backdoors for attackers.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Ransomware's primary mechanism is
o: encrypting victim data and demanding payment for the key
questions.e: Ransomware encrypts files or systems and extorts payment for decryption keys, often with data-theft double extortion. Offline immutable backups are the standard defence.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Spyware is designed to
o: secretly monitor user activity and steal information
questions.e: Spyware captures keystrokes, credentials and browsing without consent. Keyloggers targeting net-banking credentials are a classic banking example.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A botnet is
o: a network of compromised machines controlled by an attacker
questions.e: Botnets are armies of infected devices (bots) commanded via C2 servers to launch DDoS attacks or spam. Banks defend with DDoS scrubbing and endpoint controls.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Phishing is
o: fraudulent messages impersonating trusted entities to steal credentials
questions.e: Phishing lures victims through fake bank emails, SMS or calls to fake sites or malicious links. Spear phishing personalises the attack; whaling targets senior executives.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Vishing and smishing are phishing variants using
questions.e: Vishing uses voice calls (often fake 'bank officer' calls) and smishing uses SMS with malicious links. Both exploit trust in the bank's brand.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack
o: secretly intercepts communication between two parties
questions.e: MITM attackers position themselves between, say, a customer and the banking site, eavesdropping or altering traffic. TLS, certificate validation and avoiding public Wi-Fi counter it.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: SQL injection attacks target
o: poorly validated application inputs to manipulate database queries
questions.e: Attackers inject SQL fragments into input fields, potentially dumping or altering database contents. Parameterised queries and input validation are the standard defences.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A zero-day vulnerability is one that
o: is unknown to the vendor with no patch available
questions.e: Zero-day means defenders have had zero days to fix it — the flaw is known to attackers first. Rapid patch management and virtual patching mitigate the exposure window.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) is characterised by
questions.e: APTs are typically state-sponsored campaigns that dwell in networks for months, moving laterally toward high-value data. Detection needs threat hunting and behavioural analytics, not just signatures.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In a SIM-swap fraud, the attacker
o: gets the victim's mobile number reissued to their own SIM to intercept OTPs
questions.e: By socially engineering the telecom operator, fraudsters port the victim's number and receive OTPs for net-banking and UPI. Unexpected loss of mobile signal is the classic warning sign.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Card skimming involves
o: devices fitted on ATMs/POS to capture card data and PINs
questions.e: Skimmers read the magnetic stripe while hidden cameras or fake keypads capture the PIN. EMV chip cards, which never expose a cloneable stripe, largely defeat it.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A preventive control example is
questions.e: Preventive controls stop incidents before they occur — firewalls, MFA, encryption. Detective controls (IDS, log reviews) find incidents, and corrective controls (backups, IR) recover from them.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An IDS differs from an IPS in that an IDS
o: detects and alerts on suspicious activity without blocking
questions.e: Intrusion Detection Systems monitor and raise alerts, while Intrusion Prevention Systems sit inline and actively block threats. Banks typically deploy both, tuned to minimise false positives.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A DMZ (demilitarized zone) in network design
o: hosts public-facing servers isolated from the internal network
questions.e: The DMZ sits between the internet and the internal LAN, holding web and mail servers that outsiders must reach. If a DMZ server is compromised, the internal network stays segmented.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A VPN provides
o: an encrypted tunnel over untrusted networks
questions.e: Virtual Private Networks encrypt traffic between endpoints across the public internet, protecting confidentiality in transit. Banks use them for remote access and branch backup links.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A SOC (Security Operations Centre) primarily
o: monitors, detects and responds to security events round the clock
questions.e: The SOC is the bank's 24x7 security watch floor, triaging SIEM alerts and coordinating incident response. RBI expects banks to run or subscribe to one.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: SIEM tools
o: aggregate and correlate logs to detect security incidents
questions.e: Security Information and Event Management platforms centralise logs from firewalls, servers and applications and correlate them into actionable alerts. They feed the SOC's monitoring.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: VAPT stands for
questions.e: Vulnerability Assessment scans for known weaknesses; Penetration Testing actively exploits them like an attacker would. RBI mandates periodic VAPT of internet-facing banking applications.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: DLP (Data Loss Prevention) tools
o: prevent sensitive data from leaving the organisation unauthorised
questions.e: DLP inspects outbound email, web and USB traffic for patterns like card numbers or customer data and blocks or quarantines violations. It enforces data-handling policy technically.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Symmetric encryption differs from asymmetric in that symmetric uses
o: one shared secret key for both encryption and decryption
a public and private key pair
questions.e: Symmetric ciphers like AES use one shared key and are fast, suiting bulk data encryption. Asymmetric (RSA, ECC) uses key pairs for key exchange and signatures but is computationally heavier.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: AES-256 refers to
o: the Advanced Encryption Standard with a 256-bit key
questions.e: AES is the global standard symmetric cipher; the 256-bit key variant offers the highest strength. It protects data at rest in CBS databases and HSMs.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: DES is considered obsolete because
o: its 56-bit key is brute-forceable with modern computing
questions.e: Data Encryption Standard's 56-bit effective key can be cracked in hours today. Banks must use AES or Triple-DES only as a legacy bridge, never for new systems.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In RSA, data encrypted with the public key can be decrypted only by
o: the holder of the matching private key
questions.e: RSA's key pair is mathematically linked: public-key encryption gives confidentiality to the private-key holder. The reverse — private-key 'encryption' — creates digital signatures verifiable by anyone.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A cryptographic hash function like SHA-256
o: produces a fixed-size digest that cannot be reversed to the input
questions.e: Hashes are one-way: the same input always yields the same digest, but the digest reveals nothing about the input. They underpin password storage and digital signatures.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: MD5 is unsuitable for security use because
o: collision attacks let attackers forge matching hashes
questions.e: Researchers demonstrated practical MD5 collisions, so attackers can craft different inputs with identical hashes. Use SHA-256 or stronger for integrity and signatures.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A digital signature provides
questions.e: Signing hashes the message and encrypts the hash with the sender's private key; verification with the public key proves origin and detects tampering. The signer cannot later deny sending it.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In PKI, a Certification Authority (CA)
o: issues and vouches for digital certificates binding keys to identities
questions.e: CAs verify identity and issue certificates that bind a public key to an owner. India's Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA) licenses CAs under the IT Act.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: TLS/SSL primarily protects data
o: in transit between client and server
questions.e: Transport Layer Security encrypts the channel — the padlock on HTTPS banking — defeating eavesdropping and MITM. Data at rest instead needs disk/database encryption.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: SPF, DKIM and DMARC are email controls that
o: authenticate senders to fight spoofing and phishing
questions.e: SPF authorises sending servers, DKIM cryptographically signs mail, and DMARC tells receivers how to handle failures. Together they stop attackers spoofing the bank's domain.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A honeypot in cybersecurity is
o: a decoy system designed to attract and study attackers
questions.e: Honeypots mimic real systems to lure attackers, revealing their tools and tactics without risking production. Any interaction with them is malicious by definition.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Zero Trust architecture is based on the principle
o: never trust, always verify — every access is authenticated regardless of location
questions.e: Zero Trust assumes breach and verifies every user, device and request continuously with least-privilege access. It replaces the old 'trusted internal network' perimeter mindset.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Privileged Access Management (PAM) controls
o: administrator and super-user accounts with elevated rights
questions.e: PAM vaults privileged credentials, enforces just-in-time elevation and records admin sessions. Compromised admin accounts are the fastest path to full domain takeover.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A WAF (Web Application Firewall) protects against
o: application-layer attacks like SQL injection and XSS
questions.e: WAFs inspect HTTP traffic for attack patterns targeting web applications — injection, cross-site scripting, bots. They shield internet-banking portals at Layer 7.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: RBI's Cyber Security Framework for banks was issued in
questions.e: The framework came via RBI circular of 2 June 2016, following the Gopalakrishna Committee's 2011 recommendations. IIBF still lists it explicitly, so study it historically and check current directions.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Under the 2016 Cyber Security Framework, banks must have a cyber-security policy that is
o: distinct from the broader IT policy and board-approved
questions.e: RBI required a standalone, board-approved cyber-security policy separate from the general IT policy. It must address risk assessment, baseline controls and incident response.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The 2016 framework requires cyber incidents to be reported to RBI within
questions.e: Unusual cyber-security incidents must reach RBI within 2–6 hours of detection, reflecting how fast attacks spread. CERT-In's separate 6-hour rule runs in parallel.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: RBI's dedicated cyber-security subsidiary set up in 2016 is
questions.e: The Reserve Bank Information Technology Pvt. Ltd. (ReBIT) was established to strengthen RBI's cyber posture and that of regulated entities. IDRBT (1996) is the older research institute.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Baseline controls under RBI's cyber framework include
o: asset inventory, patch management and access control
questions.e: You cannot protect what you do not know: inventory, timely patching and strict access control form the minimum baseline. Gap assessments measure the bank against these.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: RBI's Master Direction on IT Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance was issued on
questions.e: The IT Governance Directions of 7 November 2023 consolidated RBI's IT expectations. They took effect on 1 April 2024, replacing older scattered circulars.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The IT Governance Directions 2023 became effective from
questions.e: RBI gave banks about five months to comply, with effectiveness from 1 April 2024. The directions apply to scheduled commercial banks and other regulated entities.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Which is NOT one of the five focus areas of the IT Governance Directions 2023?
questions.e: The five areas are IT Governance, IT Infrastructure & Services, IT Risk Management, Information System Audit and IT Services Outsourcing. Marketing has no place in an IT governance direction.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Under the IT Governance Directions, banks must maintain a policy on
questions.e: The directions explicitly require a board-approved data migration policy with controls for completeness, accuracy and reconciliation. Migrations are high-risk events regulators watch closely.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The directions prohibit
o: manual modification or deletion of data without audit trails
questions.e: Direct manual edits to production data bypass application controls, so RBI mandates audit trails and maker-checker for any such intervention. Untraceable changes are a supervisory red flag.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The Gopalakrishna Committee (2011) is associated with
o: technology, electronic payments and information security in banks
questions.e: The Working Group on Information Security, Electronic Banking, Technology Risk Management and Cyber Frauds (2011) laid the foundation for RBI's cyber framework. Its report led to the 2016 circular.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: COBIT is a governance framework published by
questions.e: Control Objectives for Information and Related Technologies (COBIT), from ISACA, aligns IT with business goals through governance and management objectives. It is the classic exam answer for IT governance frameworks.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: ITIL is primarily concerned with
questions.e: The Information Technology Infrastructure Library codifies service strategy, design, transition, operation and continual improvement. Banks map their IT service management to ITIL.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 specifies requirements for
questions.e: ISO 27001 defines how to establish, operate and improve an ISMS, with Annex A controls; the 2022 revision reorganised them into four themes. Certification is a common bank assurance signal.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The six functions of NIST CSF 2.0 are
o: Plan, Do, Check, Act, Stop, Go
Input, Process, Output, Store, Send, Receive
Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover
Buy, Build, Test, Deploy, Run, Retire
questions.e: NIST's Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 added Govern to the original five: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover. It organises outcomes rather than prescribing specific technologies.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: PCI DSS applies to organisations that
o: store, process or transmit cardholder data
questions.e: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard is contractual (via card schemes) and mandates controls around card data. Tokenisation and network segmentation are common compliance strategies.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The primary objective of an IS audit is to
o: provide assurance that IT controls safeguard assets and support business objectives
questions.e: IS audit independently evaluates whether IT governance, controls and processes protect information assets and deliver value. Findings go to management and the audit committee.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A risk-based IS audit
o: focuses effort on areas of highest IT risk
questions.e: Risk-based auditing allocates scarce audit resources where failure hurts most — CBS, payment systems, cyber defences. It starts from the bank's risk assessment, not a fixed checklist.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: CAATs (Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques) let auditors
o: analyse entire populations of data with software
questions.e: Tools like ACL or IDEA test 100% of transactions instead of small samples, finding anomalies sampling would miss. Parallel simulation reprocesses live data through audit software.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An embedded audit module is
o: audit code built into the application to capture transactions continuously
questions.e: Embedded modules (like SCARF) log specified transactions as they occur for later audit analysis. They enable continuous auditing rather than periodic snapshots.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The test data technique in IS audit
o: processes dummy transactions through the live system to verify controls
questions.e: Auditors feed fictitious transactions (valid and invalid) into the production system in a controlled way. Correct handling proves input and processing controls work.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Auditor independence means the auditor
o: is free from conflicts and reports objectively
questions.e: Independence — in fact and appearance — plus professional ethics underpin audit credibility. Auditors must not audit systems they designed or operate.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Input controls are designed to ensure
o: data entered is accurate, complete and authorised
questions.e: Field validations, reasonableness checks, duplicate detection and authorisation at data entry stop garbage at the source. 'Garbage in, garbage out' makes input controls foundational.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Processing controls ensure
o: transactions are processed completely, accurately and only once
questions.e: Run-to-run totals, sequence checks and duplicate-transaction detection verify processing integrity. They catch errors between input acceptance and output generation.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Output controls primarily address
o: distribution of reports only to authorised recipients
questions.e: Output controls govern who receives reports, how sensitive outputs are protected and how exceptions are followed up. A perfect system fails if its reports leak.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: General (IT) controls differ from application controls in that general controls
o: cover the IT environment as a whole — access, change, operations
questions.e: General controls (logical access, change management, backup) create the foundation; application controls operate within specific CBS modules. Weak general controls undermine all application controls.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The 'three lines of defence' model places IS audit in the
questions.e: First line is business operations owning risks, second line is risk/compliance oversight, and third line is independent internal audit. IS audit's independence puts it firmly in the third line.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A Key Risk Indicator (KRI) is
o: a metric signalling rising risk exposure
questions.e: KRIs like failed-login rates or unpatched-critical counts give early warning before losses materialise. Thresholds trigger escalation to risk committees.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: For IT outsourcing, RBI requires banks to retain
o: ultimate responsibility plus right-to-audit clauses over vendors
questions.e: Outsourcing never outsources accountability: contracts must grant the bank and RBI access and audit rights over the provider. Concentration and exit risks must be managed.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: CISA certification is awarded by
questions.e: The Certified Information Systems Auditor credential from ISACA is the global benchmark for IS audit professionals. Its domains mirror the IS audit lifecycle taught in this module.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: For audit evidence to be reliable it must be
o: sufficient, relevant and obtained from trustworthy sources
questions.e: Good evidence is sufficient in quantity, relevant to the objective and reliable — independent external sources beat internal say-so. Auditors document it in working papers.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
