questions.q: Change management control requires that program changes be
o: tested, approved and documented before deployment
questions.e: Segregating development from production, testing changes and obtaining approvals prevents unauthorised or buggy code reaching CBS. Emergency changes still need post-facto review.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An audit trail must be
o: complete, tamper-evident and retained for review
questions.e: Audit trails record who did what and when, enabling reconstruction of events for audit and forensics. The IT Governance Directions stress their completeness and protection.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: ReBIT's role includes
o: strengthening cyber security of RBI and regulated entities
questions.e: ReBIT builds cyber-resilience tools, threat-intelligence sharing and security assessments for the financial sector. It operationalises RBI's cyber strategy.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The CSITE cell set up by RBI in 2015
o: monitors cyber threats and shares intelligence with banks
questions.e: The Cyber Security and Information Technology Examination cell conducts focused IT examinations of banks. It complements the broader supervisory framework.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Which standard covers Business Continuity Management Systems?
questions.e: ISO 22301 specifies BCMS requirements — policy, BIA, strategies, exercising and continual improvement. ISO 9001 covers quality and 14001 the environment.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In the CITAP pathway, CISB sits alongside
o: IT Security and Prevention of Cyber Crimes & Fraud Management examinations plus mandatory training
questions.e: IIBF's revised CITAP (reimagining DISA) requires three certificate exams — CISB, IT Security, and Prevention of Cyber Crimes & Fraud Management — followed by mandatory training. CISB is the technology-foundation leg.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A gap assessment against RBI's cyber framework
o: compares current controls with required controls to identify shortfalls
questions.e: Gap assessments systematically map existing controls to framework requirements, producing remediation plans. Boards track closure of gaps as a governance metric.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Cryptographic controls under the IT Governance Directions cover
o: key management, encryption standards and HSM usage
questions.e: Banks must govern encryption algorithms, key lifecycles and hardware security modules centrally. Weak or unmanaged cryptography silently voids other controls.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The IT Governance Directions require an Information Security policy that is
questions.e: Board approval gives the security policy authority, and periodic review keeps it aligned with evolving threats and regulations. RBI examines both existence and effectiveness.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Concurrent audit of CBS transactions primarily provides
questions.e: Concurrent (continuous) auditors examine transactions as they occur using system data, catching frauds and errors early. It complements rather than replaces periodic statutory audit.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Which sampling approach tests every transaction in a population?
questions.e: CAATs make full-population testing feasible, eliminating sampling risk for computerised data. Auditors still sample where judgment or physical verification is needed.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: CTS-2010 standards relate to
o: cheque truncation with standardised cheque features
questions.e: Cheque Truncation System 2010 mandated standardised cheque security features (watermark, void pantograph) for image-based clearing. It stopped the physical movement of cheques between banks.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In a 9-digit MICR code, the first three digits denote the:
questions.e: MICR: first 3 digits = city, next 3 = bank, last 3 = branch — enabling high-speed electronic sorting of cheques.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: NACH is primarily used for
o: bulk electronic debits and credits like salaries and EMIs
questions.e: National Automated Clearing House handles bulk, repetitive transactions — salary credits, utility debits — with mandate management. NPCI operates it as the successor to ECS.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: NEFT operates in
questions.e: NEFT nets transactions and settles them in half-hourly batches, economising on liquidity versus RTGS. It runs 24x7x365 since 16 December 2019 with no minimum or maximum amount.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The RTGS system settles each transaction:
o: Individually, on a gross basis, in real time
Once at the end of the day
questions.e: RTGS = Real-Time Gross Settlement: each instruction is settled individually and irrevocably in real time (minimum Rs.2 lakh, no maximum).

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Gross settlement in RTGS eliminates
o: interbank settlement risk from intraday net exposures
questions.e: Because each transfer settles individually and finally in central-bank money, no exposure builds up between banks intraday. Net systems instead economise on liquidity at the cost of some settlement risk.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: IMPS was launched in India in
questions.e: Immediate Payment Service (2010, NPCI) gave India 24x7 instant retail transfers via mobile using MMID or account+IFSC. It was the direct ancestor of UPI.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The retail instant-payment system whose success paved the way for UPI was:
questions.e: IMPS (launched 2010 by NPCI) proved 24x7 instant mobile transfers; UPI (2016) built on that rails experience with VPA-based push/pull payments.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In UPI, VPA stands for
questions.e: The Virtual Payment Address (e.g. name@bank) maps to the underlying account, so payers never share account numbers. It works with two-factor authentication: device binding plus UPI PIN.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A UPI 'collect request' is an example of
questions.e: In a pull transaction the payee requests and the payer approves — the merchant-initiated collect flow. Push payments are payer-initiated, like scanning a QR to pay.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: UPI Lite is designed for
o: small-value offline-capable transactions from an on-device wallet
questions.e: UPI Lite holds a small balance on the device for low-value payments without hitting the bank's core systems each time. It reduces load and works in poor connectivity.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: UPI 123Pay enables digital payments
o: on feature phones via IVR, missed call, app or sound
questions.e: 123Pay brings UPI to the 40-crore feature-phone base through four technology options. It extends financial inclusion beyond smartphone users.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: *99# in Indian banking provides
o: USSD-based mobile banking on any phone
questions.e: The *99# USSD service works on basic GSM phones without internet, offering balance, transfers and merchant payments. NPCI operates it for financial inclusion.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: AePS (Aadhaar-enabled Payment System) authenticates using
questions.e: AePS lets customers transact at BC micro-ATMs using Aadhaar number plus fingerprint/iris authentication. It underpins DBT and last-mile banking.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: RuPay is
questions.e: RuPay is India's domestic card scheme, keeping card transaction processing within the country. It competes with Visa and Mastercard rails for Indian issuance.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: NFS in the ATM context stands for
questions.e: The National Financial Switch interconnects member banks' ATMs for interoperable withdrawals. NPCI operates it as the country's largest ATM network.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: NETC FASTag uses
o: RFID tags for electronic toll collection
questions.e: National Electronic Toll Collection links RFID FASTags to bank accounts/wallets for cashless tolling. NPCI operates the NETC program.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: e-RUPI is
questions.e: e-RUPI vouchers are person- and purpose-specific, redeemable without a bank account via SMS/QR. Government uses them for targeted benefit delivery like vaccination or scholarships.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: BBPS (Bharat Bill Payment System)
o: standardises recurring bill payments through agents and apps
questions.e: BBPS provides interoperable bill collection — electricity, telecom, gas — through a network of agents and digital apps. NPCI's BBPS unit operates the central platform.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Tokenisation of card data replaces
o: the PAN with a merchant-specific token
questions.e: RBI's tokenisation framework substitutes a non-sensitive token for the 16-digit PAN in stored credentials. A breach of token data is useless to attackers.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: EMV chip cards are safer than magnetic-stripe cards because
o: the chip generates a unique cryptogram per transaction
questions.e: EMV chips perform dynamic authentication — each transaction carries a one-time cryptogram that cannot be replayed. Cloned stripe data cannot produce valid chip transactions.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Under RBI's PPI framework, full-KYC PPIs differ from minimum-KYC PPIs in
questions.e: Full-KYC wallets/prepaid cards enjoy higher balances and full functionality including fund transfer. Minimum-KYC instruments carry lower caps and restricted use.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In correspondent banking, a 'loro' account is:
o: An account a bank holds with the RBI
A foreign bank's rupee account maintained with us
An account maintained by a third bank on behalf of another bank
A synonym for a nostro account
questions.e: Loro ('theirs'): an account a third-party bank maintains on behalf of another bank. Nostro = our account with them; vostro = their account with us.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: SWIFT provides
questions.e: The Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication carries payment instructions between banks globally. It is messaging, not settlement — actual funds move via correspondent accounts.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A 'cooling period' in internet banking is a control that
o: restricts newly added payees for a defined period
questions.e: After adding a new beneficiary, transfers are blocked or capped for the cooling window (often 24 hours). This blunts account-takeover frauds that add mule payees.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: MyUPI, launched around September 2026, is
o: an enhanced UPI app platform with automated support and payment controls
questions.e: MyUPI is NPCI's platform giving a unified dashboard of UPI transactions and AutoPay mandates across banks and apps, with a Safety Switch to decline suspicious debits, UPI-number delink and 24x7 AI-powered support. It was unveiled by the RBI Governor at the Global Fintech Fest in September 2026.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: UPI Tap & Pay (September 2026) allows
o: PIN-free NFC payments up to Rs. 5,000
questions.e: Tap & Pay uses NFC for quick in-person payments without entering the UPI PIN up to Rs. 5,000. Above that, PIN authentication applies as before.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: FiMI, introduced alongside MyUPI in September 2026, is
o: NPCI's Small Language Model powering MyUPI's AI-assisted customer support
questions.e: FiMI — Finance Model for India — is NPCI's small language model behind MyUPI's 24x7 AI support and safety features, unveiled by the RBI Governor at the Global Fintech Fest 2026. It shows NPCI embedding AI into the UPI experience.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: RBI's 2018 data-localisation circular requires
o: payment system data to be stored only in India
all bank data to be stored abroad
questions.e: All data relating to payment systems operated in India must be stored in India, with foreign copies deleted or also localised. It was a landmark assertion of data sovereignty.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Account Aggregators (2021 framework) enable
o: consent-based sharing of financial data with regulated entities
questions.e: The AA framework lets customers share bank, securities and insurance data with lenders or advisors through encrypted, revocable consent. NBFC-AAs licensed by RBI operate the rails.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: India's CBDC retail pilot (e-rupee) began in
questions.e: RBI launched the retail digital rupee pilot on 1 December 2022 after the wholesale pilot in November 2022. It tests sovereign digital currency alongside UPI.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: In AI/ML-based fraud detection, models primarily
o: score transactions in real time against learned behavioural patterns
questions.e: ML models learn normal customer behaviour and flag anomalies — unusual amounts, locations or velocities — for step-up authentication or blocking. They complement rule-based systems.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A blockchain/DLT's core security property is
o: a tamper-evident distributed ledger with consensus
questions.e: Distributed ledgers replicate records across nodes and use consensus plus cryptographic chaining to resist tampering. Banks explore them for trade finance and settlement use cases.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: NPCI was incorporated in
questions.e: NPCI was incorporated in December 2008 as a Section 8 not-for-profit company promoted by RBI and major banks, operational from 2009. It now runs UPI, IMPS, NACH, RuPay, NFS, AePS, NETC and CTS.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Cloud adoption in banks raises the regulatory concern of
o: data residency, concentration and exit risk
questions.e: Regulators worry about where cloud data physically resides, over-dependence on few providers and the ability to exit. RBI's outsourcing and IT governance directions address these directly.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: 5G and IoT expand the banking attack surface mainly through
o: many more connected endpoints with uneven security
questions.e: Billions of IoT devices and always-on 5G connections multiply entry points, many with weak default security. Network segmentation and device identity become critical controls.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Quantum-safe (post-quantum) cryptography matters because
o: future quantum computers could break RSA/ECC, so migration must start early
questions.e: Large-scale quantum computers would break current public-key cryptography via Shor's algorithm. IDRBT's research centre prepares the banking sector for eventual migration.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: E-mandates / UPI AutoPay are used for
o: recurring payments like subscriptions and EMIs with pre-authorised debits
questions.e: Customers pre-authorise recurring debits up to a set limit, authenticated once with additional-factor authentication. It digitises the old ECS/NACH mandate flow.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Device binding in mobile banking
o: ties the banking app to one registered device as an authentication factor
questions.e: Device binding registers the handset's identifiers so the app refuses to run on unknown devices. Combined with MPIN/biometrics it gives strong two-factor authentication.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An MPIN is
questions.e: The Mobile PIN authenticates mobile/UPI transactions as the 'knowledge' factor. It must never be shared, and banks never ask for it on calls.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: QR-code-based UPI payments work because
o: the code encodes the payee's VPA/account for the payer's app to read
questions.e: The merchant's QR encodes their payment address; the customer's app decodes it and initiates a normal UPI push with PIN. It needs no POS hardware, aiding small merchants.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A Business Continuity Plan (BCP) differs from a Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) in that BCP
o: keeps the whole business operating during disruption, while DRP restores IT
questions.e: BCP is the umbrella: alternate sites, manual workarounds and communication that keep banking services alive. DRP is its IT subset — restoring systems, networks and data.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A Business Impact Analysis (BIA) identifies
o: critical processes and the impact of their disruption over time
questions.e: BIA maps critical functions, their dependencies and how losses grow with downtime. Its outputs — RTO, RPO, MTD — drive the entire continuity strategy.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is
o: the amount of data loss allowed
the maximum acceptable downtime for a process
questions.e: RTO answers 'how fast must we be back?' — the deadline for restoring a process after disruption. RPO separately answers 'how much data may we lose?'

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Recovery Point Objective (RPO) defines
o: the maximum tolerable data loss measured in time
questions.e: An RPO of one hour means backups/replication must ensure no more than an hour's transactions are lost. Tighter RPOs demand synchronous replication and cost more.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) is
o: the absolute deadline beyond which the business cannot survive
questions.e: MTD is the outer survival limit; the RTO must always sit comfortably inside it. Breaching MTD risks regulatory action and customer flight.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: An incremental backup copies
o: only data changed since the last full backup
only data changed since the last backup of any kind
questions.e: Incremental backups are fast and small but restore needs the full plus every incremental in sequence. Differential backups instead copy all changes since the last full backup.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A differential backup copies
o: all changes since the last full backup
questions.e: Differentials grow through the week but restore needs only the full plus the latest differential. Banks choose the mix balancing backup windows against restore speed.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The 3-2-1 backup rule means
questions.e: Keep three copies of data, on two different media, with one copy offsite/offline. It protects against hardware failure, ransomware and site disasters simultaneously.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A hot DR site
o: is fully equipped and synchronised for near-instant failover
questions.e: Hot sites run live replicated systems, giving the fastest recovery at the highest cost. Warm sites have hardware ready but need setup; cold sites are just space.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: DR drills are conducted to
o: validate that recovery procedures actually work within RTO/RPO
questions.e: Untested plans fail: drills prove failover works, staff know roles and RTOs are achievable. RBI expects periodic testing with documented lessons learned.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The Information Technology Act, 2000 received Presidential assent on
questions.e: The IT Act was passed on 9 June 2000 and came into force on 17 October 2000. The 2008 amendment took effect on 27 October 2009.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The IT (Amendment) Act, 2008 became effective from
questions.e: The 2008 amendments — adding sections like 43A, 66A–66F, 69A/69B — took effect on 27 October 2009. They substantially expanded cyber-crime and intermediary provisions.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Section 10A of the IT Act provides that
questions.e: Section 10A (added in 2008) confirms contracts formed electronically are enforceable. It underpins net-banking agreements and online acceptances.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Section 43 of the IT Act deals with
o: unauthorised access and damage to computer systems — civil liability
questions.e: Section 43 imposes civil compensation liability for unauthorised access, data theft, malware introduction and disruption. Section 66 makes graver cases criminal.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Section 43A of the IT Act concerns
o: compensation for failure to protect sensitive personal data
questions.e: Section 43A makes body corporates possessing sensitive personal data liable to compensate negligence in maintaining reasonable security practices. It was India's first data-protection liability provision.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Under the IT Act, hacking with dishonest intent is punishable under
questions.e: Section 66 criminalises computer-related offences committed dishonestly or fraudulently (acts under Section 43 done with such intent), with up to 3 years' imprisonment. Section 43 alone is civil.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Identity theft (stealing passwords, OTPs, card data) is punishable under IT Act
questions.e: Section 66C punishes fraudulent use of another's electronic signature, password or unique identification feature (up to 3 years). Section 66D covers cheating by personation using computer resources.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Cheating by personation using a computer resource (e.g. fake bank websites) falls under
questions.e: Section 66D targets phishing-style frauds where criminals impersonate banks or officials online (up to 3 years). It is the core provision against fake banking portals.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Cyber terrorism under the IT Act is covered by
questions.e: Section 66F punishes acts threatening India's unity, integrity, security or sovereignty through computers — punishable up to life imprisonment. It is the gravest cyber offence in the Act.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Section 66A of the IT Act was
o: struck down by the Supreme Court in Shreya Singhal (2015)
questions.e: The Supreme Court held Section 66A (offensive online messages) unconstitutional for vagueness violating free speech. Police occasionally still invoke it — itself a noted exam trap.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Power to issue directions for interception/monitoring of information is in IT Act
questions.e: Section 69 allows government interception/monitoring/decryption for sovereignty, security and public-order grounds with safeguards. Sections 69A/69B cover blocking and traffic-data monitoring.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Section 69A of the IT Act empowers
o: the government to block public access to online information
questions.e: Section 69A provides the legal basis for blocking websites and apps, with a committee review procedure. It is frequently in the news and hence exam-relevant.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: CERT-In is established under IT Act
questions.e: Section 70B designates CERT-In as the national nodal agency for cyber incident response. Its directions — including 6-hour incident reporting — bind service providers.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: CERT-In was established in
questions.e: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team became operational in January 2004 under MeitY. It issues advisories, coordinates incident response and mandates reporting timelines.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: CERT-In's 2022 directions require incident reporting within
questions.e: Specified cyber incidents must be reported to CERT-In within 6 hours of detection. The directions also mandate 180-day log retention with NTP-synced timestamps.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Under CERT-In directions, logs must be retained for
questions.e: Service providers, intermediaries and data centres must keep ICT logs for 180 days within India. Time sources must sync to NTP servers like those of NIC or NPL.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Disclosure of information in breach of lawful contract is punishable under IT Act
questions.e: Section 72A punishes disclosure of information obtained while providing services under a lawful contract (up to 3 years). Section 72 covers breach of confidentiality by those empowered under the Act.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Section 79 of the IT Act gives intermediaries
o: safe harbour from liability for third-party content, subject to due diligence
questions.e: Intermediaries (ISPs, platforms) are shielded from user-content liability if they observe due diligence and act on takedown orders. Losing safe harbour exposes them to direct liability.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA)
o: licenses and supervises Certifying Authorities issuing DSCs
questions.e: Under Sections 17–25 of the IT Act, the CCA licenses CAs, certifies their keys and maintains the national PKI root. DSC issuance flows through CCA-licensed CAs.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Aadhaar e-Sign under the IT Act framework provides
o: online electronic signatures authenticated via Aadhaar
questions.e: e-Sign lets Aadhaar holders sign documents online using Aadhaar authentication through licensed providers. It carries the same legal validity as other electronic signatures.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Appeals against orders under the IT Act lie to
questions.e: The Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) hears IT Act appeals after the Cyber Appellate Tribunal's functions were merged into it in 2017. IT Act Section 62 then gives a further appeal to the High Court within 60 days.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act received Presidential assent on
questions.e: The DPDP Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023) was assented on 11 August 2023. Its phased commencement follows subordinate rules; candidates should check current Gazette status.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Under the DPDP Act, the individual to whom personal data relates is the
questions.e: The Data Principal owns the rights; the Data Fiduciary determines purpose and means of processing. Processors act only on the fiduciary's behalf — terminology the exam tests directly.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Lawful processing under the DPDP Act generally requires
o: free, specific, informed and unconditional consent of the Data Principal
questions.e: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, with notice of data sought and purpose. Certain legitimate uses are exempted from the consent requirement.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Rights of Data Principals under the DPDP Act include
o: access, correction, erasure, grievance redressal and nomination
questions.e: Principals can obtain summaries of processing, correct or erase data, seek grievance redressal and nominate representatives. These mirror global privacy rights adapted to India.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The Data Protection Board of India under the DPDP Act
o: adjudicates breaches and can impose penalties
questions.e: The Board inquires into breaches, directs remedial measures and levies penalties graded by severity. Appeals go to TDSAT and then the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Maximum penalty under the DPDP Act for serious breaches is
questions.e: Penalties are graded up to Rs. 250 crore per contravention for the gravest breaches like failure to prevent data breaches. The Board considers gravity, duration and mitigation.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: Under the DPDP Act, personal data breaches must be
o: notified to the Board and affected Data Principals
questions.e: Fiduciaries must notify the Data Protection Board and each affected principal of breaches. Notification timelines and manner follow the subordinate rules.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: The DPDP Act exempts processing for
o: state security, legal proceedings and certain research/archival purposes
questions.e: Exemptions cover sovereignty/security, legal/regulatory functions and specified research, archival or statistical purposes. Commercial processing otherwise needs consent or legitimate use.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: A warm DR site differs from a hot site in that a warm site
o: has hardware ready but needs configuration and data restore
questions.e: Warm sites keep infrastructure in place but require software setup and data restoration before cutover — cheaper than hot, slower to activate. Cold sites provide only space and power.

questions.subject: Certified Information System Banker
questions.q: ISO 22301 is the international standard for
questions.e: ISO 22301 specifies BCMS requirements: policy, BIA, strategies, exercising and continual improvement. Banks align their BCP programs to it for supervisory comfort.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Certified Banking Compliance Professional (CBCP) course is offered jointly by IIBF and which other professional body?
o: Institute of Company Secretaries of India
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
questions.e: CBCP is offered jointly by the Indian Institute of Banking & Finance and the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI). It combines an online examination with three days of classroom training.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: What is the pass mark for the CBCP online examination of 100 marks?
questions.e: The CBCP online examination carries 100 marks and the pass mark is 50. The classroom training component separately requires 25 out of 50 marks.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: What is the pass mark for the CBCP classroom training component?
questions.e: The classroom training component of CBCP is evaluated for 50 marks, with a pass mark of 25. Both the online exam and training must be cleared for the certificate.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: According to the Basel Committee, compliance risk is the risk of legal or regulatory sanctions, material financial loss, or loss of reputation arising from:
o: failure to comply with laws, regulations and rules
questions.e: The Basel Committee's 2005 paper defines compliance risk as the risk of legal or regulatory sanctions, material financial loss or loss of reputation resulting from failure to comply with laws, regulations, rules and codes of conduct.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI requires the compliance function in banks to be:
o: merged with the business development vertical
headed by the Chief Financial Officer
questions.e: RBI mandates that the compliance function be permanent, independent of business lines, adequately resourced, and headed by a Chief Compliance Officer who reports to the Board or Audit Committee.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Chief Compliance Officer of a bank generally reports to:
o: the Board or the Audit Committee of the Board
questions.e: The CCO must have an independent reporting line to the Board or the Audit Committee of the Board, never to business heads, so that compliance findings cannot be suppressed by revenue pressures.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: In the three lines of defence model, the compliance function sits in the:
questions.e: The first line is the business (branch staff following rules daily); the second line is risk management and compliance (setting policies, monitoring adherence); the third line is internal audit (independently verifying the first two).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: In the three lines of defence model, internal audit is the:
questions.e: Internal audit is the third line of defence: it independently verifies the effectiveness of the first line (business) and the second line (risk/compliance).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a responsibility typically assigned to the compliance function?
o: Reporting breaches to senior management and the Board
Sanctioning loans and fixing interest rates
questions.e: Compliance sets policies, monitors adherence, trains staff and reports breaches; it does not sanction loans or fix interest rates — those are business decisions the compliance function oversees from an independent position.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, under which compliance officers file reports, was enacted in:
questions.e: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act was enacted in 2002. Compliance officers ensure filing of cash transaction reports and suspicious transaction reports with FIU-IND under its provisions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Suspicious transaction reports are filed by banks with:
questions.e: Banks file cash transaction reports and suspicious transaction reports with FIU-IND (Financial Intelligence Unit – India), the national agency for receiving and analysing financial intelligence on money laundering.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Banking Codes and Standards Board of India was registered in:
questions.e: BCSBI was registered on 18 February 2006 on the recommendation of the S.S. Tarapore Committee, with RBI Governor Y.V. Reddy as its first chair.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: BCSBI was dissolved in:
questions.e: RBI dissolved the Banking Codes and Standards Board of India on 28 September 2021, absorbing its consumer-protection role into the central bank's Consumer Education and Protection framework.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following codes was published by BCSBI?
o: Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers
questions.e: BCSBI published the Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers and the Code of Bank's Commitment to Micro and Small Enterprises — voluntary codes of fair banking practice.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which statute provides the framework for RBI to impose monetary penalties on banks for non-compliance?
o: Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code
Section 46(4) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
questions.e: Section 46(4) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 empowers RBI to impose penalties on banks for contravention of the Act's provisions or RBI directions — the compliance function's most feared stick.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Customer due diligence under KYC norms primarily requires banks to:
o: verify the customer's identity and understand the nature of business
sell insurance products to the customer
questions.e: Customer due diligence requires identifying and verifying the customer (and beneficial owners), and understanding the purpose and intended nature of the banking relationship — the foundation of AML compliance.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The compliance-risk assessment of a bank should be refreshed:
o: at least annually and whenever new products or regulations appear
questions.e: Compliance-risk assessments must be refreshed at least annually and whenever the bank launches new products, enters new geographies or absorbs new regulation, with findings reported to the Board.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Whistle-blower mechanisms in banks are typically owned for independence by:
questions.e: The compliance function typically owns the vigil/whistle-blower mechanism's independence so staff can report suspected breaches without fear of retaliation from business lines.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'regulatory liaison' as a compliance activity?
o: Coordinating with RBI and other regulators on inspections and reporting
Negotiating loan interest rates with borrowers
questions.e: Regulatory liaison is the compliance function's coordination with regulators — managing inspections, responding to queries, filing returns on time and tracking regulatory commitments.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A bank launches a new digital product without compliance sign-off and no loss occurs. Under the compliance-risk definition, this is:
o: a compliance-risk event because the risk turns on the possibility of sanction
not a compliance event since there was no loss
questions.e: Compliance risk turns on the possibility of legal or regulatory sanction, not actual loss. Launching without compliance sign-off is a compliance-risk event even with zero financial damage.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Ultimate responsibility for compliance in a bank rests with:
o: the Board of Directors and senior management
questions.e: While the compliance function advises and monitors, ultimate responsibility for compliance rests with the Board and senior management — the CCO's independence does not transfer accountability.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which RBI committee's recommendation led to the creation of BCSBI?
questions.e: BCSBI was set up on the recommendation of the S.S. Tarapore Committee (Committee on Procedures and Performance Audit of Public Services), which RBI constituted in 2004.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Transaction monitoring in an AML programme is designed to:
o: detect unusual patterns that may indicate money laundering
questions.e: Transaction monitoring uses rule-based and behavioural analytics to detect unusual patterns — structuring, rapid movement of funds, mule activity — that may indicate money laundering or terrorist financing.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following is a second-line-of-defence activity?
o: The compliance team testing whether branches follow KYC norms
External statutory audit of financial statements
A teller following the cash-handling manual
questions.e: The compliance team testing branch adherence to KYC norms is classic second-line work: setting standards and monitoring the first line's compliance. The teller is first line; statutory audit is external.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: FIMMDA and FEDAI codes of conduct belong to which layer of the compliance universe?
questions.e: Codes from industry bodies like FIMMDA (fixed income markets) and FEDAI (foreign exchange dealers) are self-regulatory standards — the third layer of the compliance universe, below statutes and RBI directions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Foreign Exchange Management Act was enacted in:
questions.e: FEMA was enacted in 1999 (in force from 1 June 2000), replacing FERA 1973 and shifting violations from criminal offences to civil penalties.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Information Technology Act, relevant for digital-banking compliance, was enacted in:
questions.e: The Information Technology Act, 2000 provides the legal framework for electronic contracts, digital signatures and cyber offences — essential compliance knowledge for digital banking.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of these is a compliance obligation under the Companies Act framework for banks?
o: Related-party transaction disclosures and board governance norms
Fixing the savings bank interest rate
questions.e: Listed banks must comply with Companies Act governance norms including related-party transaction approvals and disclosures — monitored by the compliance function alongside banking regulations.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A compliance officer discovers a regulatory breach at a branch. The correct first step is to:
o: hide it to protect the branch's rating
wait for the RBI inspection to find it
report it through the defined escalation channel to senior management
questions.e: Compliance breaches must be reported promptly through defined escalation channels to senior management and, where required, to the regulator. Concealment compounds the offence and destroys the function's credibility.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The 'regulatory calendar' maintained by compliance tracks:
o: due dates of RBI returns, disclosures and inspection responses
questions.e: The regulatory calendar lists every return, disclosure and inspection-response due date. Slippage invites penalties that RBI publishes, making the calendar a core compliance tool.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following conflicts of interest must a compliance function manage?
o: Staff trading in securities of companies the bank lends to
questions.e: Personal trading by staff in securities of borrower companies creates insider-trading and conflict-of-interest risks that compliance must police through trading restrictions and disclosures.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Outsourcing of banking activities creates compliance risk because:
o: the bank remains responsible for the outsourced activity's compliance
questions.e: RBI's outsourcing guidelines make clear that outsourcing does not diminish the bank's obligations — the bank remains responsible for compliance of outsourced activities and must supervise vendors.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Basel Committee paper that defines the compliance function in banks is titled:
o: Principles for effective risk data aggregation
Core principles for effective banking supervision
Compliance and the compliance function in banks
questions.e: The Basel Committee's April 2005 paper 'Compliance and the compliance function in banks' is the canonical international statement on the compliance function's mandate and independence.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following is an indicator of a weak compliance culture?
o: Business heads overriding compliance objections routinely
Independent reporting line for the CCO
questions.e: Routine override of compliance objections by business heads signals a weak compliance culture — the other options indicate a strong one.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under PMLA, banks must preserve transaction records for:
questions.e: Banks must maintain records of transactions and customer identification for five years from the date of the transaction (and five years after the business relationship ends for KYC records) under PMLA rules.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The compliance function of a bank should have:
o: unfettered access to information and personnel across the bank
a dotted reporting line to the CEO only
questions.e: An effective compliance function needs unfettered access to information, records and personnel across all units — without it, monitoring and testing are impossible.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following is a 'conduct risk' that compliance monitors?
o: A borrower defaulting on a loan
Mis-selling of financial products to customers
questions.e: Conduct risk — how the bank and its staff behave toward customers — covers mis-selling, unfair practices and poor complaint handling, and is squarely within compliance's remit.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI's penalties for non-compliance are published because:
o: public disclosure creates deterrence and market discipline
it is required by the Press Council
questions.e: RBI publishes penalties imposed on banks to create deterrence across the system and enable market discipline — a reputational cost that compliance exists to prevent.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The compliance testing programme of a bank typically covers:
o: all branches and units on a risk-based cycle
questions.e: Compliance testing covers all branches and business units, prioritised on a risk-based cycle — high-risk areas tested more frequently than low-risk ones.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following best captures the relationship between compliance and internal audit?
o: Compliance is second line; audit independently verifies as third line
questions.e: Compliance (second line) sets policies and monitors adherence; internal audit (third line) independently verifies that both the first and second lines are effective. They are distinct by design.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A bank employee must complete CBCP training evaluation. The classroom training pass mark is 25/50. This component tests:
o: practical application through case studies and exercises
questions.e: The three-day classroom training uses case studies, exercises and practical application of compliance concepts, evaluated for 50 marks with a 25-mark pass threshold.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of these is a regulatory reporting obligation monitored by compliance?
o: Timely submission of fraud reports to RBI
questions.e: Frauds must be reported to RBI within prescribed timelines — a classic compliance-monitored regulatory reporting obligation. The others are not regulatory reports.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Institute of Company Secretaries of India partners IIBF for CBCP because:
o: company secretaries bring governance and legal-compliance expertise
questions.e: ICSI's expertise in corporate governance, legal compliance and board processes complements IIBF's banking domain knowledge — the rationale for the joint CBCP offering.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following would the compliance function classify as a 'near miss'?
o: A profitable quarter for the bank
A fraud that caused a ₹1 crore loss
A control failure detected and fixed before any breach occurred
questions.e: A near miss is a control failure caught before it caused a breach or loss. Tracking near misses is a leading indicator of compliance-risk health.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Compliance risk differs from operational risk in that:
o: compliance risk centres on legal/regulatory sanction and reputation; operational risk on loss from failed processes, people, systems or external events
compliance risk only covers credit losses
operational risk is a subset of compliance risk
questions.e: Compliance risk centres on sanctions and reputation from rule breaches; operational risk covers losses from failed internal processes, people, systems or external events. They overlap but are distinct risk types.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The first Chief Compliance Officers were mandated for Indian banks by RBI in:
questions.e: RBI's September 2020 circular mandated appointment of Chief Compliance Officers with prescribed rank, tenure and reporting lines, strengthening the compliance function's independence.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which document should a compliance officer consult first when a new RBI circular is issued?
o: The circular itself and the bank's mapping of applicable rules to products
questions.e: The compliance officer reads the circular itself, maps its requirements to the bank's products and processes, assesses gaps, and drives implementation — the standard regulatory-change workflow.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A 'compliance certificate' submitted periodically to the Board typically confirms:
o: that the bank has complied with applicable regulatory requirements during the period
questions.e: Periodic compliance certificates to the Board (often quarterly) confirm adherence to applicable regulatory requirements and flag exceptions — a key Board oversight tool.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Banking Regulation Act, which compliance officers must master, applies primarily to:
questions.e: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 governs banking companies operating in India — licensing, management, capital, and RBI's supervisory powers over them.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI's inspection reports (risk-based supervision) are coordinated on the compliance side by:
o: the compliance function, which tracks and closes inspection findings
questions.e: Compliance tracks inspection findings, ensures time-bound rectification, and reports closure to the Board — a core regulatory-liaison duty.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Certified Treasury Professional (CTP) course is offered jointly by IIBF and:
questions.e: The Certified Treasury Professional course is run by IIBF jointly with FIMMDA (Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association of India). The classroom training must be completed within 15 months of clearing the online exam.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which module of the CTP syllabus covers money-market operations?
questions.e: Module I covers financial markets and the role of treasury; Module II covers money-market operations; Module III covers investments — the three-module structure in the official syllabus.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Confirmation and settlement of treasury deals is handled by the:
questions.e: Dealers in the front office execute trades; the mid office measures risk and monitors limits; the back office confirms and settles deals.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Risk measurement and limit monitoring in a dealing room is the job of the:
questions.e: The mid office measures risk, monitors limits and performs ALM gap analysis — the control layer between dealing and settlement.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The key organisational control in a treasury is to:
o: let dealers confirm their own trades
segregate front, mid and back offices
questions.e: Front office (dealers), mid office (risk) and back office (settlement) must be segregated so no one person controls a trade end-to-end — the core dealing-room control.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which institution guarantees settlement of money-market and forex trades in India?
questions.e: CCIL (Clearing Corporation of India, established 2001) guarantees settlement of money-market and foreign-exchange trades, eliminating counterparty risk for participants.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Borrowing for a period of 7 days in the interbank market is classified as:
questions.e: Call money is overnight (one day); notice money is 2–14 days; term money is beyond 14 days. These definitions are frequently tested.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Treasury Bills are issued in tenors of:
questions.e: The three T-bill tenors are 91 days, 182 days and 364 days — issued by the Government of India through RBI auctions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Commercial Paper in India is issued in minimum denominations of:
questions.e: Commercial Paper is an unsecured money-market instrument issued by highly rated corporates, in denominations of ₹5 lakh and multiples thereof.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A repo transaction involves:
o: selling securities with an agreement to repurchase
questions.e: In a repo, securities are sold with an agreement to repurchase — the seller borrows cash against collateral. Reverse repo is the mirror image.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Marginal Standing Facility allows banks to:
o: borrow overnight from RBI against SLR securities in emergencies
questions.e: MSF (Marginal Standing Facility) lets scheduled commercial banks borrow overnight from RBI against SLR securities beyond the LAF window, at a penal rate — the emergency funding tap.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: CBLO has been replaced in India by:
questions.e: CBLO was discontinued and replaced by tri-party repo (TREPS) on the CCIL platform for collateralised borrowing and lending.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Certificates of Deposit in India have a maturity period ranging from:
questions.e: CDs issued by scheduled commercial banks and select FIs have maturities of 7 days to 1 year and are freely transferable by endorsement.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Borrowing short-term and deploying funds long-term to earn the rate spread is:
o: a legitimate treasury strategy within approved limits
questions.e: Running a maturity mismatch (borrowing short, lending long) is the classic treasury arbitrage that earns the spread — legitimate within approved limits.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The most sensitive daily indicator of systemic liquidity watched by treasuries is:
questions.e: The overnight call-money rate is the pulse of systemic liquidity — the treasury watches it to decide daily borrowing and lending.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Primary Dealers in the Indian market primarily:
questions.e: Primary dealers are RBI-registered entities that underwrite and make markets in government securities, supporting the G-sec market's liquidity.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: When market interest rates rise, existing bond prices generally:
questions.e: Bond prices and yields move inversely: when market yields rise, existing fixed-coupon bonds become less attractive and their prices fall.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Yield to maturity of a bond represents:
o: the total return if the bond is held till maturity
questions.e: Yield to maturity is the total return an investor earns if the bond is held till maturity, factoring coupon payments and capital gain/loss on redemption.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Duration of a bond measures:
o: the bond's price sensitivity to interest-rate changes
questions.e: Duration measures the weighted-average time to receive a bond's cash flows and its price sensitivity to interest-rate changes — the core interest-rate risk metric.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Modified duration tells a dealer the bond's:
o: approximate percentage price change for a 1% yield change
questions.e: Modified duration converts duration into an approximate percentage price change per 1% change in yield — directly usable for risk limits.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: PV01 in treasury risk management stands for:
o: change in portfolio value for a 1 basis point yield move
questions.e: PV01 (price value of a basis point) is the change in a portfolio's value for a one-basis-point (0.01%) move in yields — the standard trading-desk risk unit.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Convexity of a bond measures:
o: the curvature of the price-yield relationship
questions.e: Convexity captures the curvature of the price-yield relationship — the second-order effect that duration alone misses, important for large rate moves.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The 'dirty price' of a bond is the:
questions.e: The dirty (full) price includes accrued interest since the last coupon; the clean price excludes it. Settlement happens at the dirty price.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The key difference between a forward and a futures contract is:
o: Forwards are customised OTC contracts; futures are standardised and exchange-traded
Forwards are standardised; futures are customised
questions.e: A forward is a customised OTC contract to buy/sell at a future date at a pre-agreed price; a future is standardised, exchange-traded and marked to market daily.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Buying a call option gives the buyer:
o: the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell, for a premium
questions.e: The option buyer pays a premium for the right — not the obligation — to buy (call) or sell (put) the underlying; the writer bears the obligation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: In an interest-rate swap, the parties exchange:
o: fixed and floating interest cash flows on a notional principal
questions.e: An interest-rate swap exchanges cash flows — typically fixed-rate payments for floating-rate payments — on a notional principal, without exchanging the principal.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Value at Risk (VaR) measures:
o: the maximum expected loss at a given confidence level
questions.e: VaR estimates the maximum expected loss over a given horizon at a given confidence level (e.g., 99%) — the standard market-risk metric.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Back-testing in risk management means:
o: comparing VaR predictions with actual outcomes
questions.e: Back-testing compares VaR predictions with actual outcomes to validate the risk model — too many exceptions mean the model understates risk.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Daylight and overnight limits in forex dealing refer to:
o: caps on intraday and overnight forex exposures
questions.e: Daylight limits cap intraday forex exposure; overnight limits cap positions carried past the trading day — both core dealer controls.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Statutory Liquidity Ratio is maintained in:
questions.e: SLR is maintained in cash, gold or approved securities (mainly government securities) — the statutory liquidity buffer every bank must hold.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: NDS-OM is RBI's electronic trading platform for:
questions.e: NDS-OM (Negotiated Dealing System – Order Matching) is RBI's electronic platform for trading government securities.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: FIMMDA and FEDAI in treasury markets:
o: set market conventions for fixed income (FIMMDA) and forex (FEDAI)
questions.e: FIMMDA publishes valuation benchmarks and codes for the fixed-income market; FEDAI sets rules for forex dealing — both are self-regulatory organisations for treasury markets.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Asset-Liability Management (ALM) gap analysis measures:
o: maturity and repricing mismatches between assets and liabilities
the difference between two dealers' salaries
questions.e: ALM gap analysis matches the maturity and repricing profiles of assets and liabilities to measure liquidity and interest-rate risk — the mid office's core report.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: If a bank has a positive interest-rate sensitivity gap, it means:
o: net interest income will fall when rates rise
net interest income will rise when rates rise
the bank will make a loss
questions.e: A positive gap (rate-sensitive assets > rate-sensitive liabilities) means rising rates increase net interest income; falling rates hurt it.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A bank's treasury may be organised:
o: either as a profit centre or a cost centre
questions.e: Treasury can be organised as a profit centre (earning trading income) or a cost centre (pure funding) — the exam tests that both models exist and profits must survive risk measurement.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following is a refinance window available to banks?
questions.e: Export refinance from RBI (and refinance windows of NABARD and SIDBI) provides banks low-cost funds to on-lend to priority borrowers — part of the treasury's funding toolkit.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: To arrive at the settlement (dirty) price of a bond, a dealer must:
o: add accrued interest to the clean price
questions.e: The clean price excludes accrued interest; settlement happens at the dirty (full) price = clean price + accrued interest.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Inter-bank participation certificates are used to:
o: share short-term loan assets between banks
questions.e: Inter-bank participation certificates let banks share short-term loan assets — with risk (participation with risk) or without (risk-free) participation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Stress testing a treasury portfolio involves:
o: test the dealing room's air conditioning
estimate losses under extreme interest-rate moves
questions.e: Stress tests shock the portfolio with extreme rate moves (e.g., ±200 bps parallel shifts) to estimate losses beyond normal VaR — the forward-looking risk discipline.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The correct confirmation discipline for treasury deals is:
o: the dealer confirms his own trades
an independent back-office confirmation matched to the deal ticket
questions.e: Every treasury deal needs an independent back-office confirmation (via SWIFT/NDS) matched against the front-office ticket — the control that catches errors and fraud.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A Contingency Funding Plan is:
o: pre-planned actions to survive a liquidity crisis
questions.e: The contingency funding plan lists actions — asset sales, emergency borrowing lines, deposit mobilisation — to survive a liquidity crisis. Every treasury must have one.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: After passing the CTP online examination, the classroom training must be completed within:
questions.e: The 15-month window runs from the date of passing the online CTP exam; the certificate is issued only after the classroom training is completed and cleared.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: In money-market parlance, 'O/N' means a tenor of:
questions.e: O/N (overnight) covers today to tomorrow; tom-next, spot-next and longer tenors follow. Money-market tenors are precise exam vocabulary.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The writer of an option receives:
o: the premium and the obligation to perform if exercised
questions.e: The writer (seller) of an option collects the premium and bears the obligation to perform if the buyer exercises — the mirror image of the buyer's right.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Mark-to-market accounting for the trading book means the bank:
o: revalues positions at current market prices
questions.e: Mark-to-market revalues trading positions at current market prices daily, so profits and losses reflect reality — the accounting discipline for the trading book.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Taking a 'short' position in a security means:
o: buying a security expecting its price to rise
selling a security expecting its price to fall
questions.e: A long position profits when prices rise; a short position profits when prices fall. Dealers use both within approved limits.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: One basis point equals:
questions.e: Basis points are the standard unit for rate moves: 1 bp = 0.01%. A 25 bp hike = 0.25%.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The yield curve is:
o: a graph of yields against maturity
questions.e: The yield curve plots yields against maturity; its shape (normal, inverted, flat) encodes market expectations about future rates — essential context for every treasury decision.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: An inverted yield curve is generally interpreted as signalling:
questions.e: An inverted yield curve (short rates above long rates) has historically preceded recessions — the market pricing in future rate cuts and weak growth.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: In a treasury quote, 'bid' and 'offer' mean respectively:
questions.e: The bid is the price at which the dealer buys; the offer (ask) is the price at which the dealer sells. The spread between them is the dealer's margin.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: UCP 600 came into force on:
questions.e: UCP 600 (ICC Publication No. 600) came into force on 1 July 2007, replacing UCP 500, and contains 39 articles.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: How many articles does UCP 600 contain?
questions.e: UCP 600 comprises 39 articles — the complete rulebook for documentary credits.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under UCP 600, a letter of credit is:
o: Credits are revocable unless stated otherwise
All credits are irrevocable even without indication
questions.e: Article 2 states that a credit is irrevocable even if there is no indication to that effect — all UCP 600 credits are irrevocable by default.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which bank issues a letter of credit and gives the primary payment undertaking?
questions.e: The issuing bank (buyer's bank) issues the credit and undertakes to pay the beneficiary against a complying presentation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A confirming bank in an LC transaction:
o: adds its own independent payment undertaking
questions.e: A confirming bank adds its own independent payment undertaking to the issuing bank's — the beneficiary then has two banks' promises.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The principle of independence in UCP 600 means:
o: banks deal with documents and not with goods or the underlying contract
questions.e: Articles 4 and 5 enshrine the independence principle: banks deal with documents, not with the goods, services or the underlying sales contract.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under UCP 600, banks have a maximum of how many banking days to examine documents?
questions.e: Article 14 requires banks to examine documents within a maximum of five banking days following presentation — the examination clock.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Documents under an LC must normally be presented within how many days of shipment?
questions.e: Article 14(d) requires documents to be presented not later than 21 calendar days after shipment, and in any event within the credit's expiry.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under UCP 600's examination standard, data in documents must be:
o: not conflicting with the credit or other documents
questions.e: Data in documents need not be identical, but must not conflict with data in the credit or other documents — the 'not conflicting' standard of Article 14(d).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: An amendment to a letter of credit requires the agreement of:
o: the issuing bank, the confirming bank (if any) and the beneficiary
questions.e: Article 10: an amendment needs the agreement of the issuing bank, the confirming bank (if any) and the beneficiary before it is effective.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Transferable letters of credit are governed by which UCP 600 article?
questions.e: Article 38 governs transferable credits: the credit may be transferred in whole or part to a second beneficiary (usually once), at the applicant's request.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: ISBP 745 is:
o: the ICC's standard practice for examining documents
questions.e: ISBP 745 (International Standard Banking Practice) is the ICC's checklist of how documents should be examined under UCP 600.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: eUCP deals with:
o: electronic records and presentation under UCP 600
questions.e: The eUCP (supplement to UCP 600) governs electronic records and electronic presentation of documents.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Documentary collections are governed by:
questions.e: URC 522 (ICC Publication 522, 1995) governs collections — the remitting, collecting and presenting banks' roles — in 21 articles.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under URC 522, the difference between D/P and D/A is:
o: D/P is for domestic trade only
D/P releases documents against payment; D/A against acceptance of a draft
questions.e: In D/P (documents against payment), the collecting bank releases documents only against payment; in D/A (documents against acceptance), against the buyer's acceptance of a time draft.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: In a documentary collection, the key risk for the exporter is that:
o: banks act as agents with no payment undertaking
questions.e: Unlike an LC, a collection carries no bank payment undertaking — the banks act as agents for collection, and payment depends on the buyer.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Bank guarantees in international trade are governed by:
questions.e: URDG 758 (2010) is the ICC's uniform rules for demand guarantees; ISP98 governs standby letters of credit.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A standby letter of credit is essentially:
o: a guarantee-like undertaking drawn only on default
questions.e: Standby LCs back an obligation and are drawn only on default — they function like guarantees and follow ISP98 (or UCP 600 if so stated).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The distinction between pre-shipment and post-shipment export credit is:
o: Pre-shipment finances manufacture and shipment; post-shipment bridges the period after shipment
questions.e: Pre-shipment (packing) credit finances the manufacture/procurement and shipment of export goods; post-shipment credit bridges the period after shipment until the buyer pays.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: PCFC refers to:
o: export credit denominated in foreign currency
questions.e: PCFC (pre/post-shipment credit in foreign currency) lets exporters borrow in foreign currency, often at lower international rates, avoiding rupee-interest cost.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which institution insures Indian exporters against non-payment risks?
questions.e: ECGC (Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India, 1957) insures exporters and lending banks against commercial and political risks of non-payment.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: EXIM Bank of India was established in:
questions.e: EXIM Bank (established 1982) finances project exports, extends lines of credit to foreign governments and supports Indian companies' overseas ventures.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Forfaiting is:
o: discounting medium-term export receivables on a non-recourse basis
questions.e: Forfaiting discounts medium-term export receivables (backed by bank guarantee/aval) on a non-recourse basis — the exporter gets cash and sheds the risk.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: International factoring typically covers:
o: short-term receivables on a usually non-recourse basis
questions.e: International factoring assigns short-term export receivables to a factor, usually non-recourse — suited to open-account and short-credit trade.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: INCOTERMS 2020 contains how many delivery terms?
questions.e: INCOTERMS 2020 (ICC) defines 11 delivery terms — EXW, FCA, FOB, CFR, CIF, CPT, CIP, DPU, DAP, DDP — allocating costs and risk between buyer and seller.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A common misconception about Incoterms is corrected by remembering:
o: they define delivery obligations, not payment
questions.e: Incoterms define who pays freight/insurance and where risk passes — they are not payment instruments and do not oblige any bank to pay.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under FOB terms:
o: risk passes when goods are on board the vessel
the seller bears all risk to destination
questions.e: Under FOB (Free On Board), risk passes when goods are loaded on board the vessel; the seller clears export formalities and the buyer arranges freight and insurance.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under CIF terms, the seller must:
o: the seller pays cost, insurance and freight to destination
questions.e: CIF (Cost, Insurance and Freight) obliges the seller to pay freight and minimum insurance to the destination port; risk still passes on shipment.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: FEMA came into force on:
questions.e: FEMA 1999 came into force on 1 June 2000, replacing FERA 1973 — violations became civil offences with monetary penalties instead of criminal prosecution.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under FEMA, appeals against orders of the Adjudicating Authority lie to:
questions.e: Section 19 of FEMA provides appeals to the Appellate Tribunal (which also hears SAFEMA and PMLA appeals) against Adjudicating Authority orders.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Authorised Dealer Category I banks may handle:
o: all current and capital account transactions
questions.e: AD Category I banks handle all current and capital account transactions; Category II handles specified non-trade transactions; Category III handles select forex business.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Export proceeds must normally be realised within:
questions.e: Export proceeds must generally be realised and repatriated to India within 9 months from the date of shipment (6 months for SEZ units).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Liberalised Remittance Scheme cap per resident individual per financial year is:
questions.e: The LRS cap is USD 250,000 per financial year per resident individual for permitted current/capital account transactions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under UCP 600 Article 16, refusal of documents must be notified:
o: by the 5th banking day via telecommunication, stating all discrepancies
questions.e: Article 16 requires a single refusal notice by telecommunication (or other expeditious means) no later than the close of the fifth banking day, stating all discrepancies and the disposition of documents.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: If an issuing bank misses the Article 16 refusal requirements, the consequence is:
o: it is precluded from claiming those discrepancies
questions.e: The preclusion rule: a bank that fails to refuse correctly (late notice, missing discrepancies) loses the right to claim those discrepancies — strictly enforced by courts.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Bank-to-bank reimbursement claims under LCs are governed by:
questions.e: URR 725 (ICC Publication 725) governs bank-to-bank reimbursements; the reimbursing bank must honour a complying claim within three banking days.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Courts will restrain payment under an LC only in case of:
o: mere breach of the underlying contract
questions.e: Fraud is the narrow exception to the independence principle — courts can restrain payment only where fraud is clearly established; mere breach of contract is not enough.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A back-to-back letter of credit is:
o: a separate second credit issued on the strength of the first
questions.e: A back-to-back LC is a second, separate credit issued against the security of the first — used by intermediaries; it is not a transfer under Article 38.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which document evidences shipment of goods under an LC?
questions.e: The bill of lading is the transport document evidencing shipment; combined with the invoice, packing list, insurance policy and certificate of origin, it forms the standard LC document set.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A 'red clause' letter of credit authorises:
o: the issuing bank to refuse documents
the applicant to cancel the credit
the negotiating bank to make advances to the beneficiary before shipment
the advising bank to confirm the credit
questions.e: A red clause LC authorises the nominated/negotiating bank to advance funds to the beneficiary before shipment — pre-shipment finance built into the credit.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A 'green clause' LC differs from a red clause LC in that:
o: advances are made against warehoused goods as well as pre-shipment
questions.e: A green clause LC extends the red clause facility to advances against goods warehoused pending shipment, not just pre-shipment advances.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under a revolving letter of credit:
o: the credit amount is reinstated after each drawing up to the agreed limit
