the beneficiary must be changed each time
the credit can never be amended
questions.e: A revolving LC reinstates the available amount after each utilisation — suited to regular, repeated shipments between the same parties.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The 'negotiating bank' under an LC is the bank that:
o: negotiates (purchases) the beneficiary's documents and drafts
questions.e: The nominated negotiating bank purchases the documents/drafts from the beneficiary, giving the exporter immediate funds, and claims reimbursement from the issuing bank.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: In international trade, 'avalisation' refers to:
o: a bank adding its guarantee to a bill of exchange
questions.e: Avalisation is a bank's guarantee endorsement (aval) on a bill of exchange or promissory note — common in forfaiting structures.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The maximum tenor generally associated with forfaiting transactions is:
questions.e: Forfaiting covers medium-term receivables, typically 6 months to 5–7 years — suited to capital-goods exports.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following documents is NOT normally required under a documentary credit for manufactured goods?
questions.e: Commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, insurance policy and certificate of origin are standard LC documents; a birth certificate is never one.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: An 'evergreen clause' in a bank guarantee provides for:
o: automatic extension of validity unless the bank gives notice
questions.e: An evergreen clause auto-extends a guarantee's validity for successive periods unless the guarantor bank gives non-renewal notice — the beneficiary stays protected.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under FEMA, an Authorised Dealer Category II may handle:
o: specified non-trade current account transactions like remittances and forex for travel
questions.e: AD Category II entities (including select NBFCs and full-fledged money changers) handle specified non-trade transactions — travel, remittances, etc.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Directorate of Enforcement adjudicates:
questions.e: FEMA contraventions are adjudicated by the Directorate of Enforcement with civil monetary penalties; appeals lie to the Appellate Tribunal and High Court.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A usance (time) LC differs from a sight LC in that payment is:
o: deferred to a future date per the tenor of the draft
questions.e: A sight LC pays on complying presentation; a usance LC pays at a future date (e.g., 90 days after bill of lading date) per the draft's tenor.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under the revised MSME definition effective 1 April 2025, a MEDIUM enterprise is one with investment up to:
o: Rs.125 crore investment and Rs.500 crore turnover
Rs.250 crore investment and Rs.1,000 crore turnover
questions.e: Budget 2025 revision: micro Rs.2.5 cr/10 cr, small Rs.25 cr/100 cr, medium Rs.125 cr investment and Rs.500 cr turnover.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under the 2025 revision, a small enterprise is defined as investment up to:
questions.e: Small enterprises: investment up to ₹25 crore and turnover up to ₹100 crore from 1 April 2025.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under the 2025 revision, a medium enterprise has turnover up to:
questions.e: Medium enterprises: investment up to ₹125 crore and turnover up to ₹500 crore from 1 April 2025.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: MSME classification under the 2025 definition requires:
o: both the investment and turnover limits must be met
questions.e: The 2025 revision uses a composite test: the enterprise must satisfy BOTH the investment and the turnover limit of its category.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: For MSME classification, export turnover is:
questions.e: Export turnover is excluded from the turnover computation, so export-intensive units are not pushed into higher categories by export sales.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The 2025 MSME definition applies:
o: different limits for manufacturing and services
the same limits for manufacturing and services
questions.e: The revised definition applies uniformly to manufacturing and service enterprises — the old sectoral distinction is gone.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: MSME registration in India is done on:
questions.e: MSME registration runs on the Udyam portal, integrated with GST and income-tax databases for verification.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act was enacted in:
questions.e: The MSMED Act was enacted in 2006, replacing the earlier SSI framework and providing the statutory basis for MSME classification and the 45-day payment rule.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: CGTMSE was set up by:
questions.e: CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises) was set up by the Government of India and SIDBI to guarantee collateral-free credit.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The CGTMSE credit guarantee ceiling per borrower from 1 April 2025 is:
questions.e: From 1 April 2025, the CGTMSE guarantee ceiling rose from ₹5 crore to ₹10 crore per borrower (Circular 250/2024-25).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The extent of CGTMSE guarantee cover is:
questions.e: CGTMSE coverage ranges from 75% to 90% by borrower category — 85% for micro enterprises up to ₹5 lakh, higher for women, North-East and SC/ST borrowers.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The CGTMSE Annual Guarantee Fee (AGF) currently ranges at:
questions.e: The Annual Guarantee Fee was revised downward to a range of 0.37% to 1.20% per annum on the guaranteed amount.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Banks may not take collateral for MSE loans up to:
questions.e: RBI's February 2026 Master Direction bars banks from taking collateral security for MSE loans up to ₹20 lakh — they must be covered by CGTMSE instead.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A micro borrower needs ₹15 lakh under PMMY. The applicable category is:
questions.e: PMMY (launched 8 April 2015) has four categories: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001–₹5 lakh), Tarun (₹5–₹10 lakh) and Tarun Plus (₹10–₹20 lakh).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The MUDRA category introduced in October 2024 for successful Tarun repayers is:
questions.e: Tarun Plus (₹10–₹20 lakh) is available from 24 October 2024 to borrowers who have successfully repaid a previous Tarun loan.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: MUDRA is:
o: a direct lender to micro borrowers
a SIDBI subsidiary that refinances micro-unit lending
questions.e: MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) is a SIDBI subsidiary that refinances micro-unit lending; it does not lend directly to borrowers.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under Stand-Up India, each bank branch must finance:
o: one SC/ST and one woman entrepreneur per branch
questions.e: Stand-Up India (2016) mandates every bank branch to finance at least one SC/ST and one woman entrepreneur, ₹10 lakh–₹1 crore, for greenfield enterprises.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under the MSMED Act, buyers must pay MSME suppliers within:
questions.e: The 45-day rule (Section 15, MSMED Act): buyers must pay MSME suppliers within 45 days (15 days if no agreement); delayed payment attracts compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Interest payable on delayed payments to MSMEs is:
o: three times the RBI bank rate
questions.e: Delayed payment to MSMEs attracts interest at three times the RBI bank rate, compounded monthly — a strong deterrent built into the MSMED Act.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Section 43B(h) of the Income-tax Act provides that:
o: disallows the deduction until actual payment to the MSME
questions.e: Section 43B(h) disallows the buyer's deduction for sums payable to MSMEs until actual payment is made — aligning tax incentives with prompt payment.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Delayed-payment complaints by MSMEs are filed on the:
questions.e: The MSME Samadhaan portal lets MSEs file delayed-payment complaints, which go to the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council for conciliation/arbitration.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: TReDS is:
o: an RBI-regulated platform for auctioning MSME receivables
questions.e: TReDS (Trade Receivables Discounting System) is an RBI-regulated electronic platform where MSME receivables are auctioned to financiers — faster working-capital realisation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Nayak Committee norm for MSME working capital assessment is:
questions.e: The Nayak Committee norm: working-capital assessment at 20% of projected annual turnover for units with turnover up to ₹5 crore, with 25% margin (bank finance 75%).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: DSCR in credit appraisal stands for:
questions.e: DSCR (Debt Service Coverage Ratio) = cash available for debt service ÷ debt obligations. Lenders look for comfort above 1.25–1.5.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Within the 18% agriculture target, the sub-target for lending to small and marginal farmers is:
questions.e: RBI raised the small-and-marginal-farmer sub-target in phases from 8% to 10% of ANBC, reaching 10% in FY 2023-24; it sits inside the 18% agriculture target.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The priority-sector sub-target for micro enterprises is:
questions.e: Micro enterprises carry an 8% sub-target within priority sector (7.5% achieved in stages); the question tests the micro-enterprise emphasis.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: CGTMSE guarantee cover applies to:
o: term loans and working capital to MSEs
questions.e: CGTMSE covers term loans and working-capital facilities (fund-based and non-fund-based) to micro and small enterprises — the standard MSE credit suite.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: When a CGTMSE-covered loan defaults, the correct procedure is:
o: the lender initiates recovery; CGTMSE settles the guaranteed portion per claim rules
questions.e: The claim process requires the lender to first initiate recovery action; CGTMSE settles the guaranteed portion (75% upfront in many cases) after invocation formalities.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI's Master Direction on lending to the MSME sector (consolidating collateral-free norms) was issued in:
questions.e: The February 2026 Master Direction consolidated MSME lending rules: no collateral up to ₹20 lakh, CGTMSE coverage, timely rehabilitation framework.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: For stressed but viable MSMEs, RBI's framework requires banks to first attempt:
o: a Corrective Action Plan for revival/rehabilitation
questions.e: The revival framework requires a Corrective Action Plan — rectification, restructuring or recovery — decided by a committee within defined timelines before NPA classification.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following is an early warning signal in an MSME account?
o: frequent overdrawing beyond drawing power and delayed financials
questions.e: Warning signals: fund diversion, frequent excess drawings, delayed stock statements/financials, cheque bounces, and promoter distraction to group companies.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Break-even point in project appraisal means:
o: the sales level at which the unit covers all its costs
questions.e: Break-even analysis finds the sales level where the unit covers all costs — essential for judging whether projected cash flows can service debt.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Promoter's contribution in an MSME project is important because it is:
o: a margin demonstrating promoter commitment and cushion
questions.e: Promoter contribution (margin) demonstrates commitment and provides a cushion; banks typically require 10–25% depending on the scheme.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: CIBIL commercial reports and CRILC help banks assess:
o: existing credit exposures and repayment conduct
questions.e: CRILC (Central Repository of Information on Large Credits) and CIBIL commercial reports let lenders check the borrower's existing exposures and conduct.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The difference between a term loan and working-capital finance is:
o: term loans fund fixed assets; working capital funds the operating cycle
questions.e: Term loans fund fixed assets (plant, machinery) and are repaid from project cash flows over 5–7+ years; working capital funds the operating cycle.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Stock audit in MSME lending refers to:
o: verification of hypothecated stock by empanelled auditors
questions.e: Stock audits by empanelled auditors verify that the hypothecated inventory exists and matches drawing power — a key control against diversion.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under hypothecation of stocks:
o: the borrower retains possession while the bank holds a charge
questions.e: Hypothecation: the borrower retains possession of the asset (stock, machinery) while the bank holds a charge — the standard MSME working-capital security.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: 'Evergreening' of MSME loans refers to:
o: extending fresh loans to hide stress in existing loans
questions.e: Evergreening — fresh loans to service old dues, hiding stress — is prohibited; banks must recognise stress early and use the revival framework.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The principal financial institution for MSME development is:
questions.e: SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India, 1990) is the principal financial institution for MSME promotion, refinancing and development.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Cluster-based financing of MSMEs means:
o: financing units in an industrial cluster leveraging common facilities
questions.e: Cluster financing leverages common facilities, shared credit history and peer monitoring in industrial clusters — improving appraisal and recovery.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Micro loans under PMMY are covered by the guarantee fund known as:
questions.e: The Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) under MUDRA covers micro loans up to ₹10 lakh (Shishu/Kishore/Tarun) extended by member institutions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Udyam registration for MSMEs:
o: is free, paperless and self-declaration based
questions.e: Udyam registration is free, paperless and based on self-declaration, with verification through GST and income-tax data — no documents need uploading.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Delayed-payment disputes of MSMEs are adjudicated by:
questions.e: MSE Facilitation Councils (state-level) conciliate and arbitrate delayed-payment disputes; awards are executable like court decrees.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Interest subvention for MSME/export credit means:
o: government bearing part of the interest cost to reduce the borrower's effective rate
questions.e: Interest subvention schemes periodically reduce the effective rate on MSME/export credit — the bank claims the subvention from the government.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which institutions can avail CGTMSE cover?
o: scheduled commercial banks, RRBs, select NBFCs and eligible MFIs as members
questions.e: CGTMSE cover is available to scheduled commercial banks, select NBFCs, regional rural banks and eligible MFIs that are member lending institutions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The investment limit for MSME classification is computed on:
o: original cost of plant & machinery/equipment (excluding land and building)
questions.e: Investment is computed on the original (purchase) cost of plant & machinery/equipment; land and building are excluded from the computation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A unit has investment of ₹20 crore and turnover of ₹150 crore. Its MSME classification is:
questions.e: Investment ₹20 cr fits Small (≤25 cr) but turnover ₹150 cr exceeds Small's ₹100 cr cap — the composite test pushes it to Medium (≤125 cr investment, ≤500 cr turnover).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The 'graduation' benefit for growing MSMEs (retaining non-tax benefits for 3 years after moving up a category) was announced in:
questions.e: Budget 2025-26 provided that MSMEs graduating to a higher category retain non-tax benefits for three years, encouraging growth without fear of losing support.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following is a fund-based working-capital facility for MSMEs?
questions.e: Cash credit (against hypothecation of stock/book debts) is fund-based — money is actually lent. Bank guarantees and LCs are non-fund-based (contingent).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Margin money under the PMEGP scheme for general-category beneficiaries in rural areas is:
questions.e: Under PMEGP, margin-money subsidy is 25% for general category in rural areas (35% for special categories); the beneficiary contributes 10% (5% for special categories).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The IIBF digital banking certificate syllabus is organised into how many modules?
questions.e: The digital banking certificate syllabus has 12 modules — from digital products and cards to MIS and data analytics.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in India is owned and operated by:
questions.e: UPI, launched on 11 April 2016, is NPCI's instant payment system using Virtual Payment Addresses for push and pull transactions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Immediate Payment Service (IMPS) is best described as:
o: A 24x7 instant interbank electronic fund-transfer service
questions.e: IMPS (NPCI, 2010) offers round-the-clock instant credit confirmation for interbank transfers via mobile, internet and ATM channels.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: NEFT became operational 24x7 on:
questions.e: NEFT moved to 24x7 operation on 16 December 2019, settling in half-hourly batches with no minimum or maximum amount.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The RTGS system in India is owned and operated by:
questions.e: RTGS is the RBI's real-time gross settlement system for large-value transfers (minimum Rs.2 lakh, no upper limit).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: *99# in digital banking refers to:
o: USSD-based mobile banking for feature phones
questions.e: *99# is the USSD-based mobile banking service for feature phones, working without internet data.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: AEPS stands for:
questions.e: AEPS enables banking transactions through Aadhaar authentication at business correspondents and micro-ATMs — interoperable across banks.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The central unit that sets business standards for the Bharat Bill Payment System is:
questions.e: NBBL, an NPCI subsidiary, is the authorised Bharat Bill Payment Central Unit; banks and fintechs join as operating units.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The National Automated Clearing House (NACH) is operated by:
questions.e: NACH, NPCI's web-based bulk electronic clearing system, handles recurring debits/credits like salaries, EMIs and dividends.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The e-RUPI prepaid digital voucher system was developed by:
questions.e: e-RUPI, a person-and-purpose-specific cashless voucher delivered by SMS/QR, was developed by NPCI with government departments.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI's regulatory sandbox is:
o: a supervised testing environment for fintech innovations
questions.e: RBI's regulatory sandbox (announced August 2019) lets fintechs test innovative products with real customers under regulatory supervision.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The e-Rupee (CBDC) is:
o: RBI's central bank digital currency with legal-tender status
questions.e: The e-Rupee (CBDC) is RBI's digital currency with legal-tender status like physical cash, being piloted in wholesale and retail forms.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI permitted video-KYC for customer onboarding in:
questions.e: Video-based customer identification (V-CIP) has been permitted by RBI since January 2020, with liveness checks and geo-tagging.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The maximum balance in a full-KYC prepaid payment instrument is:
questions.e: Full-KYC PPIs can hold up to ₹2 lakh; minimum-KYC PPIs are capped lower (₹10,000, reloadable in some cases).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which PPI type allows cash withdrawal at ATMs?
questions.e: Open-system PPIs (bank-issued) allow cash withdrawal at ATMs; semi-closed PPIs work only at contracted merchants; closed PPIs work only with the issuer.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Payment systems in India are regulated under the:
questions.e: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 requires RBI authorisation for operating any payment system in India.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Electronic contracts and digital signatures derive legal validity from the IT Act of:
questions.e: The IT Act, 2000 gives legal validity to electronic contracts and digital signatures — the legal basis of digital banking.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: 'Vishing' in the context of banking fraud refers to:
o: Fraudulent voice calls impersonating banks to steal OTPs and credentials
questions.e: Vishing = voice phishing: fraudsters call posing as bank/RBI staff and extract OTPs, PINs and card details.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: SIM-swap fraud involves:
o: fraudulently reissuing the victim's SIM to intercept OTPs
questions.e: SIM-swap fraud gets the victim's mobile number reissued to the fraudster's SIM, intercepting OTPs — banks counter with cooling periods and alerts.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under RBI's zero-liability framework, if a customer reports an unauthorised electronic transaction after 4-7 working days, the customer's liability is capped at:
questions.e: Reported within 3 working days: zero liability; 4-7 days: capped (Rs.5,000-25,000 by account type); beyond 7 days: as per bank policy.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The 'golden hour' in cyber-fraud response refers to:
o: the first 1–2 hours after a fraud when recovery is most possible
questions.e: The golden hour — the first 1–2 hours after a fraud — is when banks can freeze mule accounts via CFCFRMS before money is layered out.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The national helpline for reporting financial cyber fraud is:
questions.e: The 1930 helpline and the CFCFRMS portal (cybercrime.gov.in) are the national rails for reporting financial cyber fraud and freezing funds.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: CFCFRMS is:
o: the system for reporting financial cyber fraud and freezing funds
questions.e: CFCFRMS (Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System) routes complaints to banks and police for rapid lien-marking of suspect accounts.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Money mules are:
o: accounts used to launder fraud proceeds
questions.e: Money mules are accounts used to receive and pass on fraud proceeds; banks monitor for mule patterns and RBI has proposed debit-freeze rules for suspect mule accounts.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Multi-factor authentication means:
o: combining two or more authentication factors
questions.e: Multi-factor authentication combines two or more factors — something you know (password/OTP), have (device/token) or are (biometric) — for transaction security.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Device fingerprinting in fraud control is:
o: identifying the device used for a transaction to detect fraud
questions.e: Device fingerprinting identifies the device used for a transaction, flagging logins from unknown devices as risky.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Velocity checks in transaction monitoring:
o: flagging unusually frequent or large transactions
questions.e: Velocity checks flag transactions that are too frequent or too large versus the customer's profile — a classic real-time fraud control.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, penalties for data breaches are adjudicated by the:
questions.e: The Act constitutes the Data Protection Board of India to inquire into breaches and impose graded penalties.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under the account-aggregator framework, customer financial data can be shared:
questions.e: Account aggregators move financial data only on explicit, granular, revocable customer consent — the consent architecture of open finance.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Straight-through processing in digital lending means:
o: straight-through processing with e-KYC and e-signatures
questions.e: Digital lending uses straight-through processing — e-KYC, e-signatures, e-mandates and automated underwriting — for instant loan journeys.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Bharat QR is:
o: the interoperable QR standard for merchant payments
questions.e: Bharat QR is the interoperable QR standard (Visa/Mastercard/RuPay) for merchant payments, unlike proprietary closed-loop QRs.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Effectiveness of a bank's digital marketing is measured by:
o: customer acquisition cost and conversion rates
questions.e: Digital marketing metrics: customer acquisition cost, conversion rates, app-store ratings and campaign ROI measure digital marketing effectiveness.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Management Information Systems (MIS) in banks provide:
o: real-time business and risk information for management decisions
questions.e: MIS dashboards give management real-time views of business, risk and operations — the data backbone of digital banking decisions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Data analytics in banking is used for:
questions.e: Analytics powers cross-selling (next-best-product), early-warning signals for stress, and personalised offers — the data-driven banking edge.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The maker-checker principle in digital banking means:
o: one user initiates and another authorises a transaction
questions.e: Maker-checker requires one user to initiate (maker) and another to authorise (checker) — the fundamental control in internet banking and payments.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Customer-protection policies for digital transactions are:
questions.e: Banks must publish board-approved customer-protection policies covering unauthorised transactions, failed-transaction reversals and grievance redressal.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Failed digital transactions must be reversed within:
o: defined turnaround times with compensation for delay
questions.e: A failed UPI/IMPS transaction must be reversed within defined turnaround times with compensation for delay — a testable service standard.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI's data-localisation requirement means:
o: data must be stored only abroad
payment data must be stored in India
questions.e: RBI requires banks to localise payment data — storing payment-system data in India — for supervisory access and security.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Frauds involving screen-sharing apps work by:
o: a common fraud where victims are tricked into sharing their screen
questions.e: Screen-sharing-app frauds (AnyDesk/TeamViewer) let fraudsters see OTPs and operate the victim's phone — banks warn customers never to share screens with strangers.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Digital fixed deposits are:
questions.e: Digital fixed deposits are opened and managed entirely online — instant, paperless term deposits, often at slightly better rates.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: QR-code fraud typically involves:
o: replacing a merchant's QR code with the fraudster's
questions.e: QR-code swap fraud replaces a merchant's QR with the fraudster's — customers should verify the payee name before paying.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: UPI, IMPS, RuPay and NACH are all operated by:
questions.e: NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India, 2008) operates UPI, IMPS, NACH, RuPay, AEPS and BBPS — India's retail payment rails.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: UPI 123Pay was specifically launched to enable digital payments for:
questions.e: UPI 123Pay (2022) brings UPI to 40+ crore feature-phone users via IVR, missed-call, app and proximity sound-based options.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Card tokenisation enhances security by:
o: replacing card numbers with unique tokens for secure transactions
questions.e: Tokenisation replaces card details with a unique token for each merchant/device — stolen tokens are useless elsewhere, cutting card fraud.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: For digital-banking vendors and fintech partners, RBI's outsourcing norms require:
o: banks remain responsible for outsourced digital activities' compliance
questions.e: RBI's outsourcing and cyber-security directions make banks responsible for vendor risk — vendor due diligence, audits and incident reporting apply to digital partners.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Embedded finance refers to:
o: integrating banking services into non-bank platforms
questions.e: Embedded finance integrates banking services (payments, lending) into non-bank apps and journeys — banking as a feature, not a destination.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Open banking is:
o: API-based sharing of banking services with third parties
questions.e: Open banking uses APIs to let third parties build on bank data and services (with consent) — the architecture behind account aggregators and fintech apps.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The final module of the digital banking certificate syllabus covers:
questions.e: The 12th module covers data analysis for business — using data for decisions, the capstone of the digital banking syllabus.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The JAM trinity refers to:
questions.e: The Digital India programme's JAM trinity (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile) is the inclusion stack on which digital banking scales.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: UPI 123Pay is designed for:
questions.e: UPI 123Pay enables UPI payments on feature phones (IVR, missed call, app-based) — extending digital payments beyond smartphones.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Banking Codes and Standards Board of India (BCSBI) published codes covering:
questions.e: BCSBI's Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers (and to MSEs) set minimum service standards; it was wound up with functions moving to the RBI's CEPD.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: BCSBI was dissolved with effect from:
questions.e: RBI dissolved BCSBI on 28 September 2021, folding its consumer-protection role into the central bank's Consumer Education and Protection framework.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which committee recommended the creation of BCSBI?
questions.e: BCSBI was set up on the recommendation of the S.S. Tarapore Committee on Procedures and Performance Audit of Public Services.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following was a BCSBI code?
o: Code of Bank's Commitment to Shareholders
Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers
questions.e: BCSBI published two voluntary codes: the Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers and the Code of Bank's Commitment to Micro and Small Enterprises.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A common misconception about BCSBI is corrected by noting that:
o: it was a standards watchdog, not a complaint forum
questions.e: BCSBI was an autonomous standards watchdog publishing voluntary codes — it was never an individual complaint-redressal forum.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, a customer can escalate a complaint to the Ombudsman after first approaching the bank and waiting:
questions.e: RB-IOS (in force 12 Nov 2021): complain to the regulated entity first; escalate to the Ombudsman if unresolved after 30 days.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Integrated Ombudsman Scheme subsumed how many earlier schemes?
questions.e: RB-IOS subsumed the Banking Ombudsman, the NBFC Ombudsman and the Digital Transactions Ombudsman schemes into one.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Who can file a complaint under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme?
o: any customer of a regulated entity
questions.e: Any customer of a regulated entity — banks, NBFCs, system participants — can complain under RB-IOS after first approaching the entity.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Before approaching the RBI Ombudsman, a complainant must:
o: complain to the bank first and wait 30 days
questions.e: The customer must first complain to the bank and wait 30 days (or receive an unsatisfactory response) before approaching the Ombudsman.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The fee for filing a complaint under the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme is:
questions.e: Filing under RB-IOS is free — no fee is charged at any stage, and complainants need no legal representation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under RB-IOS, compensation for consequential loss is capped at:
questions.e: Under RB-IOS 2026 (effective 1 July 2026), the Ombudsman can award up to ₹30 lakh for consequential loss suffered by the complainant — enhanced from ₹20 lakh under the 2021 scheme.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Compensation for mental agony/harassment under the scheme is capped at:
questions.e: Compensation for mental agony and harassment under RB-IOS 2026 is capped at ₹3 lakh — enhanced from ₹1 lakh under the 2021 scheme.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: An appeal against the Ombudsman's decision lies to:
questions.e: The complainant may appeal to the RBI Executive Director (Appellate Authority) within 30 days of the award or rejection.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Internal Ombudsman of a bank is:
o: an RBI officer posted in branches
a bank-level reviewer of the bank's own complaint rejections
questions.e: The Internal Ombudsman (mandatory for banks with more than 10 branches since 2015, extended to all SCBs except RRBs in 2018) reviews the bank's own rejections before RBI Ombudsman escalation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The RBI Charter of Customer Rights lists how many rights?
questions.e: The Charter of Customer Rights (2015) enumerates five rights: fair treatment; transparency, fair and honest dealing; suitability; privacy; and grievance redress and compensation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following is a right under the Charter of Customer Rights?
o: right to a job in the bank
questions.e: The five Charter rights are fair treatment, transparency and honest dealing, suitability, privacy, and grievance redress and compensation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: DICGC deposit insurance cover per depositor per bank is:
questions.e: DICGC insures each depositor up to ₹5 lakh per bank (principal + interest) since the enhancement effective 4 February 2020.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: For zero liability on unauthorised electronic transactions, the customer must report within:
questions.e: RBI's 6 July 2017 circular: report within 3 working days → zero liability; 4–7 days → capped liability; beyond → bank's policy.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Compensation for delayed reversal of failed ATM transactions is:
questions.e: Banks must reverse failed ATM transactions within 5 days (T+5); delay beyond that attracts ₹100 per day compensation to the customer.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Nomination in bank deposits is governed by:
o: Sections 45ZA–45ZF of the Banking Regulation Act
questions.e: Nomination facilities under Sections 45ZA–45ZF of the Banking Regulation Act let depositors nominate beneficiaries for deposits, lockers and safe custody.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Doorstep banking facilities are mandated for:
questions.e: RBI's customer-service guidelines require doorstep banking facilities for senior citizens (above 70) and differently-abled customers.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Complaints under the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme are filed:
o: through RBI's Complaint Management System portal
questions.e: Complaints are filed through RBI's Complaint Management System (CMS) portal — the single digital doorway to the Ombudsman.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The correct grievance-redressal ladder in a bank is:
o: branch → regional office → principal nodal officer → Internal Ombudsman → RBI Ombudsman
questions.e: The standard ladder: branch → regional/zonal office → principal nodal officer → Internal Ombudsman → RBI Ombudsman → Appellate Authority.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Complaint trends in a bank are reviewed quarterly by:
o: the Customer Service Committee of the Board
questions.e: The Customer Service Committee of the Board reviews complaint trends and service quality quarterly — a Board-level oversight requirement.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The original Banking Ombudsman Scheme was introduced in:
questions.e: The Banking Ombudsman scheme originated in 1995 (revised several times) before being subsumed into the Integrated Scheme in 2021.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Banking Ombudsman scheme was originally launched under:
o: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act
questions.e: The first Banking Ombudsman scheme (1995) was launched under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: When many customers complain about the same product feature, the bank should treat it as:
o: treated as a service-design failure needing process correction
questions.e: Persistent complaint clusters indicate a product or process design failure — the syllabus stresses treating them as service-design issues, not isolated grievances.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Display of the grievance-redressal policy and nodal officer details in branches is:
questions.e: Banks must display their grievance-redressal policy and the nodal officer's details prominently — a basic customer-service disclosure.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: After complaining to the bank, the customer can approach the Ombudsman if there is no response within:
questions.e: The 30-day clock: if the bank does not respond within 30 days of the complaint, the customer can approach the RBI Ombudsman.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which statement about the Ombudsman's powers is correct?
o: it can reject frivolous, sub judice or already-decided complaints
it can only accept corporate complaints
questions.e: The Ombudsman can reject complaints that are frivolous, already decided, sub judice, or beyond the scheme's pecuniary/territorial scope.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: An Ombudsman award must normally be implemented by the bank within:
questions.e: The award must generally be implemented by the bank within 30 days — the scheme prescribes timelines for both sides.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Ombudsman scheme performance data is:
o: published in RBI's annual report on the schemes
questions.e: RBI's annual report on the Ombudsman schemes discloses complaint volumes, disposal and awards — the system's public scorecard.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Mis-selling in banking means:
o: selling unsuitable products like insurance misrepresented as deposits
questions.e: Mis-selling — selling unsuitable products like pushing insurance as deposits — is a core conduct-risk and customer-service violation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The 'suitability' right in the Charter of Customer Rights requires banks to offer:
o: products appropriate to the customer's needs and risk profile
questions.e: The suitability right requires banks to offer products appropriate to the customer's needs and risk profile — the Charter's anti-mis-selling pillar.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Failed ATM transactions must be reversed within:
questions.e: RBI's 2019 customer-service guidelines cap the turnaround time for failed ATM transactions at T+5 days with ₹100/day compensation thereafter.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Customers can reach the Integrated Ombudsman through:
o: the CMS portal and the contact centre
questions.e: The contact centre (toll-free) and the CMS portal are the two access channels for the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Can banks compensate customers for deficient service on their own?
questions.e: Banks may proactively compensate for deficient service — delayed cheque collection, failed transactions, unauthorised debits — per their board-approved policies.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: BCSBI's Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers covered:
o: deposit accounts, remittances, loans and complaint handling
questions.e: The Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers covered deposit accounts, remittances, loans and complaint handling — the service standards banks signed up to.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: BCSBI's second code was the Code of Bank's Commitment to:
questions.e: The MSE code set standards for lending to micro and small enterprises — transparency in loan terms, timely decisions, and non-discriminatory treatment.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The first chairperson of the Banking Codes and Standards Board of India (BCSBI) was:
questions.e: Ms. K.J. Udeshi, former RBI Deputy Governor, chaired the first Governing Council of BCSBI, set up on 18 February 2006 on the Tarapore Committee's recommendation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: After BCSBI's dissolution, its consumer-protection role moved to:
o: RBI's Consumer Education and Protection framework
questions.e: With BCSBI gone, RBI's Consumer Education and Protection Department (now part of the central consumer-protection architecture) carries the mandate.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which scheme covered digital-transaction complaints before the 2021 integration?
questions.e: The Ombudsman for Digital Transactions (2019) was one of the three schemes subsumed — it covered prepaid instruments, mobile banking and other digital complaints.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The NBFC Ombudsman scheme was introduced in:
questions.e: The NBFC Ombudsman (2018) covered complaints against non-deposit-taking NBFCs before subsumption into the Integrated Scheme.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The key control against mis-selling is:
o: needs analysis and documented customer consent
questions.e: Suitability, needs analysis and documented consent are the controls against mis-selling — the compliance answer to conduct risk.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Banks must provide account statements and passbook updates:
o: promptly as part of basic customer service
only on payment of high fees
questions.e: RBI's guidelines on customer service require banks to provide statements, passbooks and balance information promptly and free of prescribed charges.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Integrated Ombudsman Scheme covers:
o: banks, NBFCs and system participants as notified by RBI
questions.e: The Banking Ombudsman historically excluded RRBs from some versions; under RB-IOS the coverage extends to banks, NBFCs and system participants as notified.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The correct approach to an unresolved bank complaint is to:
o: follow the sequential ladder: bank → Internal Ombudsman → RBI Ombudsman → appeal
questions.e: Grievance redressal is a defined sequential process — jumping stages or approaching multiple forums simultaneously can get the complaint rejected.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Customer-service quality in banks is measured using:
o: complaint volumes, turnaround times and satisfaction scores
questions.e: Service quality is measured through complaint volumes, turnaround times, customer satisfaction surveys and Ombudsman awards — the standard metrics.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI's Charter of Customer Rights was issued in:
questions.e: The 2015 Charter was RBI's five-rights framework — the foundation of modern customer-service regulation in Indian banking.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Disclosure of all charges and terms before selling a product flows from the Charter right to:
questions.e: Transparency — clear, honest disclosure of terms, charges and risks — is the Charter right that underpins fair dealing.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: FEMA replaced FERA with a key philosophical shift. What was it?
o: From criminal prosecution to civil monetary penalties
From central control to state control
From civil penalties to criminal prosecution
questions.e: FEMA (1999) replaced FERA (1973), shifting from a criminal 'control' regime with imprisonment to a civil 'management' regime with monetary penalties — the philosophical core of the reform.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: FEMA replaced which earlier legislation?
questions.e: FEMA replaced FERA 1973 — the shift from a criminal 'control' regime to a civil 'management' regime for foreign exchange.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Authorised Dealer Category II banks are permitted to handle:
o: Specified non-trade current-account transactions such as forex for travel and business
questions.e: AD Category II (including FFMCs upgraded) handle specified non-trade current-account transactions; only AD Category I handles all current and capital account transactions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under FEMA, current-account vs capital-account transactions:
o: capital account is free; current account is restricted
current account is generally free; capital account faces restrictions
questions.e: Current-account transactions (trade, remittances, travel) are generally free; capital-account transactions face Schedules I and II restrictions.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Export proceeds must normally be realised within how many months of shipment?
questions.e: Export proceeds must be realised and repatriated within 9 months of shipment (6 months for SEZ units).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Advance remittance for imports beyond which amount requires a guarantee?
questions.e: Advance remittance for imports above USD 200,000 requires a bank guarantee or standby LC — the control against advance-payment fraud.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Liberalised Remittance Scheme remittances beyond the annual per-person cap require:
o: Prior approval of the Reserve Bank of India
questions.e: LRS caps remittances at USD 250,000 per resident individual per financial year; amounts above need RBI's prior approval.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: In a direct quotation of exchange rates:
o: the first currency is fixed, the second varies
questions.e: In a direct quote (e.g., USD/INR 83.00), the first currency is fixed and the second varies — the convention for most pairs involving the rupee.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A forex dealer quotes bid and offer. The dealing principle is:
o: buy and sell at the same rate
questions.e: Every market-maker quotes two prices: the lower bid (buy) and the higher offer/ask (sell) — the spread is the dealer's margin.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A cross rate is computed by:
o: chain-multiplying pairs sharing a common currency
questions.e: Cross rates combine two pairs sharing a common currency (e.g., USD/INR and USD/JPY → INR/JPY) by chain-multiplying on the same side.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The interest-rate parity principle for forward rates states:
o: higher domestic rates push the currency to a forward discount
the forward rate equals the spot rate
questions.e: Forward rate = Spot × (1 + id×n/360)/(1 + if×n/360). Higher domestic interest rates → forward discount on the domestic currency.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A foreign-exchange swap consists of:
o: a spot deal combined with a forward deal in opposite directions
questions.e: A swap = spot purchase (or sale) + forward sale (or purchase) — used to roll over positions or manage short-term liquidity.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Cancellation of a forward contract is effected at:
o: the opposite rate prevailing at cancellation
questions.e: Cancellation of a forward contract is done at the opposite (current market) rate; the difference is profit or loss to the customer.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Extension of a forward contract is done at:
o: the current forward rate for the extended period
questions.e: Extension (rollover) uses the current forward rate for the new period — the customer bears the swap cost or gain.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: 'Cash/tom' and 'tom/spot' refer to:
questions.e: Cash/tom rolls today's position to tomorrow; tom/spot rolls tomorrow's to spot — the standard short-date rollovers using swap points.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Merchant exchange rates are computed as:
o: interbank rate plus the bank's margin
questions.e: Merchant rates = interbank rate ± the bank's margin (TT buying/selling, bills buying/selling) per FEDAI rules.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Rules for forex dealing and merchant rates in India are set by:
questions.e: FEDAI (Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India) sets dealing rules, publishes benchmarks and standardises market practice for forex.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The benchmark rate for merchant forex transactions is:
questions.e: The RBI reference rate (published around noon) is the benchmark for merchant transactions and revaluation.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Nostro and Vostro accounts differ in that:
o: Nostro is our foreign-currency account with the correspondent; Vostro is their rupee account with us
questions.e: Nostro = 'our account with you' (in foreign currency with the overseas correspondent); Vostro = 'your account with us' (in rupees).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which SWIFT message is used for issuing a letter of credit?
questions.e: MT103 = customer transfer; MT202 = bank-to-bank cover; MT700 = LC issuance; MT760 = guarantee issuance — the core SWIFT family.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Bank-to-bank cover payments use SWIFT message:
questions.e: MT202 is the general financial-institution transfer — the cover payment message between banks.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A customer remittance abroad is transmitted via SWIFT:
questions.e: MT103 is the single customer credit transfer — the standard cross-border remittance message.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A bank guarantee is issued over SWIFT via message:
questions.e: MT760 issues the guarantee; MT767 amends it. (MT700 is for LCs.)

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which settlement method is safest for the exporter?
questions.e: Risk ranking: advance payment (exporter-safe) → documentary credit → documentary collection → open account (importer-safe).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which settlement method carries the highest risk for the exporter?
questions.e: Open account — shipping first and billing later — leaves the exporter fully exposed to buyer default; safest for the importer.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Country risk in international banking refers to:
o: sovereign actions blocking payment despite a willing buyer
questions.e: Country risk = sovereign actions (transfer blocks, moratoria, expropriation, war) preventing payment even when the buyer is willing.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Banks manage country risk by:
o: grade countries, set limits and price the risk
questions.e: Banks grade countries, set country limits and price country risk into trade transactions — the standard country-risk toolkit.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: ECGC was established in:
questions.e: ECGC (1957) insures exporters and banks against commercial and political non-payment risks.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Lines of credit to foreign governments for Indian exports are extended by:
questions.e: EXIM Bank (1982) funds project exports, extends lines of credit to foreign governments and supports overseas investment.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: International project finance is typically supported by:
o: multilateral institutions like World Bank, IMF and ADB
questions.e: The World Bank (IBRD/IDA), IMF and ADB are the multilateral institutions financing development and balance-of-payments support.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Penalties for FEMA contraventions are:
o: monetary penalties up to three times the sum involved
questions.e: FEMA penalties are civil and monetary — up to three times the sum involved — adjudicated by the Directorate of Enforcement.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Appeals under FEMA lie to:
questions.e: Appeals against Enforcement Directorate adjudication go to the Appellate Tribunal (and then the High Court).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Exchange-control compliance by AD banks requires:
o: verifying bona-fide purpose and matching trade documentation
questions.e: AD banks must verify bona-fide purpose for outward remittances, match import payments with bills of entry, and follow up overdue export bills.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Offshore Banking Units (OBUs) in India handle:
o: foreign-currency business with special regulatory treatment
questions.e: Offshore Banking Units in SEZs conduct foreign-currency business with special regulatory treatment — India's offshore banking window.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: AML obligations in international banking cover:
questions.e: KYC, transaction monitoring and reporting to FIU-IND apply to cross-border transactions — AML discipline is integral to forex business.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The forward-cover decision depends on:
o: comparing the cost of cover with the risk appetite
questions.e: Whether to hedge depends on the cost of cover versus risk appetite; options cap downside while retaining upside — at the premium's cost.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A currency option provides the holder:
o: the right without obligation, for a premium
questions.e: A currency option gives the right (not obligation) to buy/sell at a strike price for a premium — capping downside while keeping upside.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Market conventions for forex dealing (margins, rounding) are prescribed by:
questions.e: FEDAI's rulebook covers dealing hours, merchant-rate computation, rounding, and market conventions for forex business.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Cross-border payments are settled through:
questions.e: Correspondent banking — Nostro/Vostro accounts and SWIFT messaging — is the plumbing that makes cross-border payments possible.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under documentary collections, D/P differs from D/A in that:
o: D/P releases against payment; D/A against acceptance
questions.e: In D/P, documents are released against payment; in D/A, against the buyer's acceptance of a time draft — the URC 522 collection terms.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which ICC publication supplements UCP 600 for electronic presentation of documents?
questions.e: The eUCP (eUCP Version 2.0) is the ICC supplement to UCP 600 governing electronic records and electronic presentation; ISBP 745 covers paper-document examination practice.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Under UCP 600, document examination follows:
o: 2 banking days; data must be identical
1 banking day; data must match exactly
5 banking days; data must not conflict
10 banking days; any data is fine
questions.e: Banks have up to 5 banking days to examine documents; data need not be identical but must not conflict (Article 14).

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: International loan syndication means:
questions.e: International syndication shares large exposures among banks — standard for big-ticket cross-border finance.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: An Indian bank's foreign branch is governed by:
questions.e: A foreign branch operates under host-country regulation plus RBI's overseas-investment norms — dual compliance.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Transfer risk in export finance means:
o: inability to convert and transfer currency out of the buyer's country
questions.e: Transfer risk (inability to convert/transfer currency out) is the classic country-risk component in trade finance.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: ECGC's standard export-credit insurance covers:
o: commercial and political risks of non-payment
questions.e: ECGC's standard policy covers commercial risks (buyer insolvency/default) and political risks (war, transfer blocks) for exporters.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Export credit is typically structured as:
questions.e: Buyer finance and supplier finance are the two export-credit structures — funded or insured with ECGC/EXIM support.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: For overdue export bills, the AD bank must:
o: pursuing realisation within 9 months and reporting overdue bills
questions.e: The 9-month realisation rule (6 for SEZ) with reporting of overdue bills is the core export-regulatory discipline for AD banks.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Diploma in International Banking & Finance is structured as:
o: two papers combining theory with exchange arithmetic
questions.e: The Diploma in International Banking & Finance is IIBF's two-paper deep credential pairing forex theory with exchange-arithmetic — the dealing-room qualification.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A 'clean' bill of lading indicates that:
o: the goods were received in apparent good order without damage remarks
questions.e: A clean bill of lading bears no remarks about damage or defective condition — LCs normally require clean bills; a 'claused' (foul) bill notes damage.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI permitted banks to engage Business Correspondents in:
questions.e: RBI's January 2006 circular permitted banks to engage business correspondents and facilitators for branchless banking, following the Khan Committee's recommendations.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The BC/BF model was recommended by the:
questions.e: The Khan Committee (Committee on Financial Inclusion, 2006) recommended the BC/BF model for extending banking to the unbanked.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The certifying agency for the BC/BF examination is:
questions.e: IIBF is the sole certifying agency — its board approves the course content, examination and certificate for BCs/BFs.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A BC candidate must pass the examination within:
questions.e: Candidates must pass within 270 days or three attempts from completion of training, whichever is earlier — otherwise training must be repeated.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The key difference between a Business Facilitator and a Business Correspondent is:
o: BFs cannot handle cash; BCs can transact
questions.e: Business Facilitators only refer and mobilise — they cannot handle cash or transact. Business Correspondents transact as the bank's retail outlet.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A Business Correspondent is authorised to:
o: accept and disburse cash and operate as the bank's retail outlet
questions.e: BCs transact: accept/disburse cash, open accounts, process remittances, and operate customer service points (kiosks) as the bank's outlet.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Which of the following is a Business Facilitator's role?
o: identifying borrowers and collecting loan applications
questions.e: BF activities: identifying borrowers, collecting loan applications, creating savings awareness, follow-up for recovery — no cash handling.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The permitted scope of BC activities includes:
o: deposits, loans, remittances, micro-insurance and pension products
questions.e: BC scope includes deposit mobilisation, loan disbursal and recovery, remittances, and sale of micro-insurance, mutual funds and pension products.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Business Correspondents are remunerated through:
o: commissions and fees from the sponsor bank
questions.e: Banks pay BCs commissions and fees (often activity/transaction-based); the viability debate centres on whether volumes cover the agent's costs.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Cash management by a BC requires:
o: cash-holding limits with timely settlement to the link branch
questions.e: Agents work under cash-holding limits set by the sponsor bank and must settle with the link branch within prescribed timelines — the cash-management control.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: BC transactions are typically conducted using:
questions.e: Micro-ATMs and handheld POS devices, with biometric authentication, are the BC's transaction hardware.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: AEPS in the BC channel stands for:
questions.e: AEPS enables interoperable banking through Aadhaar authentication and biometrics at any BC of any bank.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Account opening by BCs for first-time customers uses:
questions.e: Simplified KYC (small accounts with relaxed documentation and balance caps) lets BCs open accounts for the unbanked.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Issuing receipts for cash transactions by a BC is:
questions.e: Every cash transaction must be receipted — the audit trail that protects both the customer and the agent.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana provides:
o: zero-balance accounts with RuPay cards for the unbanked
questions.e: PMJDY (2014) provides zero-balance Basic Savings Bank Deposit Accounts with RuPay debit cards — the flagship product BCs sell.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The annual premium for PMJJBY is:
questions.e: PMJJBY: life insurance (₹2 lakh cover) at ₹436 annual premium, auto-debited — sold through banks and BCs.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The annual premium for PMSBY is:
questions.e: PMSBY: accident insurance (₹2 lakh) at ₹20 annual premium — the cheapest social-security product in the BC kit.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Atal Pension Yojana is:
o: a guaranteed pension scheme for the unorganised sector
questions.e: Atal Pension Yojana provides a guaranteed pension (₹1,000–₹5,000/month from age 60) with contributions based on entry age.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Financial-literacy duties of a BC are:
o: a core duty — explaining products in the local language
questions.e: BCs must display charges, explain products in the local language, and build financial literacy — interest, insurance, pension concepts.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Sub-contracting of a BC outlet is:
questions.e: BCs cannot sub-contract their outlet without the bank's approval — the outlet is the bank's responsibility.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Police verification of BC agents is:
questions.e: Police verification of agents is required in many states — the integrity control on who handles public money.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Grievance redressal for BC customers flows through:
o: the bank's channels and ultimately the RBI Ombudsman
questions.e: Customers escalate through the bank's complaint channels and ultimately the RBI Integrated Ombudsman — BC customers have full grievance rights.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The Khan Committee's 40:60 principle for the BC model referred to:
o: banks bearing ~40% of cost economics through fees
questions.e: The original 40:60 principle — banks bearing ~40% of cost economics through fees — shaped the BC viability debate.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Training cost support for BCs comes from:
o: NABARD reimburses training costs for eligible functionaries
questions.e: NABARD reimburses training costs for eligible rural functionaries — the funding that lets the BC model scale.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: BC operations are subject to audit by:
questions.e: Concurrent auditors examine the BC's transactions, cash handling and audit trail — the oversight control on agents.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A BC outlet with no transactions for months is:
o: a supervisory red flag — activity levels matter
questions.e: Dormant BCs are a supervisory red flag — banks are graded on active BC transactions, not just outlet counts.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Smart cards in the BC model are:
o: cards storing account data for offline transactions
questions.e: Smart cards store account data offline, enabling transactions in connectivity-poor areas — the original BC technology.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Customer authentication at BC outlets primarily uses:
questions.e: Biometric (Aadhaar) authentication at micro-ATMs/POS is the standard customer-authentication method in the BC channel.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The evolving role of BCs emphasises:
o: assisted digital journeys — mobile banking, UPI, government apps
questions.e: The assisted-digital shift: BCs help customers use mobile banking, UPI and government apps — beyond cash dispensing.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RBI's financial-inclusion plans expect banks to ensure:
questions.e: RBI's financial-inclusion plans set outlet-coverage expectations for unbanked rural centres — the inclusion mandate BCs serve.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Customer Service Points (CSPs) in the BC model are:
questions.e: Customer Service Points (kiosks) are the BC's retail outlet — the physical last-mile presence.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: For the sponsor bank, the BC network is:
o: a low-cost distribution arm for deposits, loans, insurance and pension
questions.e: BCs source deposits, loans, insurance and pension business — a low-cost distribution arm, not just a cash point.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The 'link branch' for a BC is:
o: the BC's base branch for settlement and supervision
questions.e: The link branch is the BC's base branch for cash settlement, supervision and support.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Deposit mobilisation by BCs is:
questions.e: Deposit mobilisation through savings accounts is a core BC function — bringing the unbanked into the banking fold.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Recovery-related work by BCs/BFs covers:
o: follow-up for recovery within the code of conduct
questions.e: Loan recovery follow-up is a permitted BF/BC activity — but coercive practices are prohibited; the recovery code of conduct applies.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Customer due diligence by a BC requires:
o: verifying identity per simplified KYC norms
questions.e: The BC must verify identity documents per simplified KYC norms before opening accounts — the first-line AML control.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Domestic remittances through the BC channel are:
o: a flagship BC service for migrant workers
questions.e: Remittances (domestic money transfer) through BCs serve migrant workers — a flagship BC service.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Sale of micro-insurance by BCs is:
o: part of the BC product suite
questions.e: Micro-insurance (PMJJBY/PMSBY) sold through BCs extends risk cover to the unbanked — part of the inclusion product suite.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: When BC devices fail due to connectivity issues, the agent should:
o: manual fallbacks with receipts and later syncing
questions.e: Technology failures need manual fallbacks — registers, receipts and next-day syncing — so customers are never turned away.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The BC/BF certificate's value to an agent is:
o: employability as a trained, certified agent
questions.e: The certificate signals trained, examined competence — banks and corporate BCs prefer certified agents.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: BC training is delivered through:
questions.e: Training is delivered through accredited institutions including NABARD's network — standardised before the IIBF examination.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A high-performing BC is measured by:
o: PMJDY usage, digital transactions and social-security enrolments
questions.e: BCs driving PMJDY usage, digital transactions and social-security enrolments deliver the inclusion mandate — the model's success metric.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The BC/BF certification examination covers:
o: the full syllabus — roles, technology, products and compliance
questions.e: The BC/BF examination tests the full syllabus: model origins, BF/BC roles, technology, products, compliance and the 270-day rule.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Fraud involving a BC agent must be:
o: reported through the bank's fraud-reporting machinery
questions.e: Fraud by BC agents must be reported through the bank's fraud-reporting machinery — agents are within the bank's fraud-risk perimeter.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: RuPay cards issued through BCs work:
o: at ATMs, POS terminals and e-commerce
questions.e: RuPay debit cards issued with PMJDY accounts work at ATMs, POS and e-commerce — the card rail of inclusion.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: A BC charging customers above the bank's prescribed charges is:
questions.e: Overcharging or hidden charges violate the BC's duty to display and explain charges — a service and compliance breach.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Quality control on BC competence is enforced through:
questions.e: The 270-day/3-attempt rule with training repetition is the compliance gate that keeps the BC workforce current.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: Corporate Business Correspondents are:
o: companies managing BC agent networks under bank agreements
questions.e: Corporate BCs (companies managing agent networks) operate under the bank's BC agreement — scale with supervision.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: AEPS interoperability means:
o: customers of any bank at any BC outlet
questions.e: Interoperable AEPS means a customer of any bank can transact at any BC — the network effect of inclusion.

questions.subject: Other Banking Certifications
questions.q: The BC model has anchored rural banking since:
questions.e: The BC model (2006) is the backbone of rural service delivery — two decades of branchless banking.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: NSO's provisional data (released 12 Oct 2026) put September 2026 CPI inflation at:
questions.e: The highest of 2026 under the new 2024-base series; food inflation 7.74% and onion inflation 108.09% drove the 71 bps rise from August's 4.83%.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: Which instrument did the RBI deploy on 13 October 2026 to absorb surplus liquidity?
o: Open market operation (OMO) sale of government securities worth Rs 25,000 crore
A hike in the statutory liquidity ratio
questions.e: The OMO sale was announced alongside the 99% daily CRR maintenance floor, to align the overnight call rate with the 5.50% repo rate.

questions.subject: JAIIB
questions.q: The Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) announced by the RBI in October 2026 requires authorised dealers to hold:
o: 20% of the rupee notional of specified FX derivative contracts above $2 million
A flat Rs 500-crore reserve per dealer
questions.e: Part of the October 2026 rupee-defence package: FX exposure threshold cut to $5 million, rebooking of cancelled rupee derivative contracts barred.

questions.subject: RBI Policy
questions.q: In the RBI’s LAF corridor (rates as of 7 October 2026), which instruments form the floor and the ceiling?
questions.e: Under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility, the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) is the floor of the LAF corridor and the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) the ceiling, with the policy repo rate in between. Post-7-Oct-2026: SDF 5.25%, repo 5.50%, MSF 5.75%.

questions.subject: RBI Policy
questions.q: Under the RBI’s ‘calibrated tightening’ stance (October 2026), future policy action could be:
questions.e: ‘Calibrated tightening’, adopted 4–2 on 7 October 2026, signals that the RBI’s next move will be either a hike or a pause — an easing bias is withdrawn. It differs from outright ‘tightening’, which would pre-commit to further hikes.

questions.subject: RBI Policy
questions.q: Before the October 2026 hike, how much had the RBI cumulatively cut the repo rate during the 2025 easing cycle?
questions.e: The October 2026 hike reversed part of the 2025 easing cycle, in which the MPC cut the repo by 125 bps in phases from 6.50% to 5.25% (Dec 2025 cut of 25 bps took it to 5.25%). The new rate of 5.50% is the first increase since February 2023.

questions.subject: RBI Policy
questions.q: Which statement about the Bank Rate (5.75% from 7 October 2026) is correct?
o: It is the repo rate for 91-day T-bills
It equals the reverse repo rate
It is the rate on Ways and Means Advances only
It is the RBI’s rediscount rate for bills of exchange
questions.e: The Bank Rate (5.75% from 7 October 2026) is the rate at which the RBI buys or rediscounts bills of exchange and commercial paper of eligible maturity. Penal interest on shortfalls in CRR/SLR maintenance is linked to the Bank Rate.

questions.subject: Regulatory framework
questions.q: The RBI's 12 October 2026 restriction of INR NDDCs to hedging-only for non-residents amends which framework?
o: Master Direction on Risk Management and Inter-Bank Dealings
Master Direction on External Commercial Borrowings
questions.e: The amendments form part of the Master Direction on Risk Management and Inter-Bank Dealings, originally issued on 5 July 2016, and apply prospectively to contracts undertaken after the circular.

questions.subject: RBI
questions.q: The minimum daily CRR maintenance requirement was raised to 99% with effect from:
