oneliners.text: Input controls: accuracy/completeness/authorisation at entry; processing: complete/accurate/once.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: General controls = IT environment-wide; application controls = inside specific modules.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Three lines of defence: operations, risk/compliance, independent internal audit.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: KRI = metric signalling rising risk (e.g. failed-login rate, unpatched-critical count).

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Outsourcing: bank retains responsibility; contracts need right-to-audit for bank and RBI.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: CISA (ISACA) = benchmark IS-audit certification.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: CITAP = CISB + IT Security + Prevention of Cyber Crimes & Fraud Management + mandatory training.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Audit evidence must be sufficient, relevant and reliable; working papers document it.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: CTS-2010 = image-based cheque clearing with standardised cheque security features.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: NACH = bulk credits/debits (salaries, EMIs) with mandate management; NPCI-operated.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: NEFT = half-hourly net batches, 24x7 since 16 Dec 2019, no min/max.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: RTGS = real-time gross settlement, min Rs. 2 lakh, 24x7 since 14 Dec 2020.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Gross settlement = immediate finality per instruction; net settlement saves liquidity but leaves intraday settlement exposure.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: IMPS (2010) = 24x7 instant retail transfers, UPI's ancestor.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: UPI (2016) = VPA-based push/pull settling on IMPS infrastructure; two factors = device binding + UPI PIN.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: UPI Lite = on-device wallet for small offline-capable payments; 123Pay = UPI on feature phones.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: *99# = USSD mobile banking on any GSM phone.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: AePS = Aadhaar biometric authentication at BC micro-ATMs.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: RuPay = NPCI's domestic card scheme; NFS = NPCI's ATM switching network.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: NETC FASTag = RFID toll collection; e-RUPI = purpose-specific prepaid voucher.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: BBPS standardises recurring bill payments; NACH handles bulk direct debits/credits.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: RBI tokenisation: PAN replaced by merchant-specific tokens.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: EMV chip = unique cryptogram per transaction; kills stripe cloning.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: PPI: full-KYC = higher limits and transfers; minimum-KYC = capped, restricted.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Nostro = our account with a foreign bank; Vostro = their account with us; SWIFT = messaging only.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Cooling period restricts newly added payees to blunt account-takeover fraud.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: UPI Tap & Pay (Sep 2026) = PIN-free NFC up to Rs. 5,000; FiMI = NPCI's Finance Model for India small language model.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: RBI 2018 circular: payment system data must be stored only in India.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Account Aggregators (2021) = consent-based financial data sharing via licensed NBFC-AAs.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: CBDC e-rupee retail pilot began 1 Dec 2022.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: ML fraud detection scores transactions against learned behaviour in real time.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: NPCI = Section 8 not-for-profit, incorporated Dec 2008, operational 2009.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Cloud risks for banks: data residency, concentration risk, exit strategy.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: BCP keeps the business alive; DRP restores IT — DRP is the IT subset of BCP.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: BIA identifies critical processes; outputs RTO, RPO, MTD.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: RTO = max acceptable downtime; RPO = max tolerable data loss (in time); MTD = survival deadline.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Incremental = changes since last backup (any); differential = changes since last full.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: 3-2-1 rule: 3 copies, 2 media types, 1 offsite.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Hot site = live and synchronised; warm = hardware ready; cold = space only.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: DR drills prove recovery works within RTO/RPO — untested plans fail.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: ISO 22301 = Business Continuity Management Systems standard.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: IT Act 2000: assent 9 Jun 2000; in force 17 Oct 2000; 2008 amendment effective 27 Oct 2009.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Sec 10A = e-contracts valid; Sec 43 = civil liability for unauthorised access/damage.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Sec 43A = compensation for negligent handling of sensitive personal data.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Sec 66 = hacking with dishonest intent (criminal, up to 3 yrs); Sec 66C = identity theft.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Sec 66D = cheating by personation online (fake bank sites); Sec 66F = cyber terrorism (up to life).

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Sec 66A struck down in Shreya Singhal (2015) — still invoked by police sometimes (exam trap).

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Sec 69 = interception/monitoring; 69A = blocking; 69B = traffic-data monitoring.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Sec 70 = protected systems; Sec 70B = CERT-In as national nodal agency.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: CERT-In operational Jan 2004; 2022 directions: report incidents within 6 hours.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: CERT-In: 180-day log retention in India; NTP sync (NIC/NPL servers).

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: Sec 72/72A = confidentiality breaches; Sec 79 = intermediary safe harbour.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: CCA licenses Certifying Authorities; only Class 3 DSCs are issued now (Classes 1-2 discontinued Jan 2021); e-Sign via Aadhaar.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: TDSAT hears IT Act appeals (after CAT merger); then High Court.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: DPDP Act 2023: assent 11 Aug 2023 (Act 22 of 2023); phased commencement via rules.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: DPDP: Data Principal = individual; Data Fiduciary = decides purpose/means of processing.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: DPDP rights: access, correction, erasure, grievance redressal, nomination.

oneliners.subject: Certified Information System Banker
oneliners.text: DPDP penalties up to Rs. 250 crore per contravention; breaches notified to Board + principals.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: CBCP is offered jointly by IIBF and the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: CBCP pass marks: 50/100 in the online exam and 25/50 in the 3-day classroom training.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: Compliance risk = risk of legal/regulatory sanctions, material financial loss or reputation loss from rule breaches.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: RBI mandates the compliance function be permanent, independent and adequately resourced.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: The Chief Compliance Officer reports to the Board or the Audit Committee of the Board, not business heads.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: The RBI's risk-based supervision framework for banks is called SPARC.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: Ultimate responsibility for compliance rests with the Board and senior management.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: Basel Committee paper 'Compliance and the compliance function in banks' is dated April 2005.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: BCSBI was registered on 18 February 2006 on the S.S. Tarapore Committee's recommendation.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: BCSBI was dissolved on 28 September 2021; its role moved to RBI's consumer-protection framework.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: BCSBI published the Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers and the Code for Micro and Small Enterprises.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: RBI can impose monetary penalties on banks under Section 46(4) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act was enacted in 2002.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: Suspicious transaction reports are filed with FIU-IND (Financial Intelligence Unit – India).

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: Under PMLA, banks must preserve transaction records for 5 years.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: FEMA was enacted in 1999 and came into force on 1 June 2000, replacing FERA 1973.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: FEMA violations attract civil monetary penalties; FERA's criminal regime was abolished.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: The compliance-risk assessment must be refreshed at least annually and on new products/regulations.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: The compliance function typically owns the independence of the whistle-blower mechanism.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: A near miss is a control failure caught before any breach — a leading compliance-risk indicator.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: Compliance risk turns on the possibility of sanction, not on actual financial loss.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: RBI mandated Chief Compliance Officers for banks in September 2020.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: The regulatory calendar tracks due dates of RBI returns, disclosures and inspection responses.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: Outsourcing does not diminish the bank's responsibility for the outsourced activity's compliance.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: CTP is offered jointly by IIBF and FIMMDA; training must follow within 15 months of the online exam.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: CTP Module I: financial markets & role of treasury; Module II: money-market operations; Module III: investments.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Front office trades, mid office measures risk and monitors limits, back office confirms and settles.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Segregation of front, mid and back offices is the core dealing-room control.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: CCIL (2001) guarantees settlement of money-market and forex trades.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Call money = overnight; notice money = 2–14 days; term money = beyond 14 days.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Treasury Bills are issued in 91-day, 182-day and 364-day tenors.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Commercial Paper is issued in minimum denominations of ₹5 lakh.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Repo = selling securities with an agreement to repurchase; reverse repo is the mirror image.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: MSF lets banks borrow overnight from RBI against SLR securities in emergencies.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: CBLO has been replaced by tri-party repo (TREPS) on the CCIL platform.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Certificates of Deposit are issued by scheduled commercial banks and financial institutions.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Bond prices and yields move inversely.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Duration measures a bond's price sensitivity to interest-rate changes.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Modified duration ≈ percentage price change for a 1% yield move.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: PV01 = change in portfolio value for a one-basis-point (0.01%) yield move.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Convexity captures the curvature of the price-yield relationship.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Dirty price = clean price + accrued interest; settlement happens at the dirty price.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Forwards are customised OTC contracts; futures are standardised and exchange-traded.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: An option buyer pays a premium for the right, not the obligation, to buy or sell.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: An interest-rate swap exchanges fixed and floating cash flows on a notional principal.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: VaR = maximum expected loss at a given confidence level over a given horizon.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: Back-testing compares VaR predictions with actual outcomes to validate the risk model.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: NDS-OM is RBI's electronic trading platform for government securities.

oneliners.subject: Certified Banking Compliance Professional
oneliners.text: Conduct risk — mis-selling and unfair practices — is squarely within compliance's remit.

oneliners.subject: Treasury Professional / Dealer
oneliners.text: One basis point = 0.01%; the bid is the dealer's buying price, the offer the selling price.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: UCP 600 (ICC Publication 600) came into force on 1 July 2007 and has 39 articles.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Under UCP 600, all letters of credit are irrevocable by default.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Banks deal with documents, not goods — the independence principle (UCP 600 Articles 4–5).

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Banks have a maximum of 5 banking days to examine documents (UCP 600 Article 14).

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Documents must be presented within 21 calendar days of shipment and before expiry.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Document data need not be identical but must not conflict (Article 14(d)).

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: LC amendments need agreement of issuing bank, confirming bank (if any) and beneficiary (Article 10).

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Transferable credits are governed by UCP 600 Article 38.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: ISBP 745 is the ICC's standard practice for examining documents.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: eUCP governs electronic records and presentation under UCP 600.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Documentary collections follow URC 522 (1995, 21 articles); banks act as agents with no payment undertaking.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: D/P releases documents against payment; D/A releases against acceptance of a time draft.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Demand guarantees follow URDG 758 (2010); standby LCs follow ISP98.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Bank-to-bank reimbursements follow URR 725; claims honoured within 3 banking days.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Refusal of documents needs a single notice by the 5th banking day stating all discrepancies (Article 16).

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Missing the Article 16 refusal discipline precludes the bank from claiming discrepancies.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Pre-shipment (packing) credit funds manufacture/shipment; post-shipment credit bridges the post-shipment wait.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: PCFC = pre/post-shipment export credit denominated in foreign currency.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: ECGC (1957) insures exporters and banks against commercial and political non-payment risks.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: EXIM Bank (1982) funds project exports and extends lines of credit to foreign governments.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Forfaiting discounts medium-term export receivables on a non-recourse basis.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: INCOTERMS 2020 has 11 delivery terms; they define delivery obligations, not payment.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: FEMA came into force on 1 June 2000, replacing FERA 1973 with civil penalties.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: LRS cap: USD 250,000 per resident individual per financial year.

oneliners.subject: Trade Finance
oneliners.text: Export proceeds must be realised within 9 months of shipment (6 months for SEZ units).

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: MSME definition from 1 April 2025: micro ₹2.5 cr/₹10 cr, small ₹25 cr/₹100 cr, medium ₹125 cr/₹500 cr (investment/turnover).

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: MSME classification uses a composite test — both investment and turnover limits must be met.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: Export turnover is excluded from MSME turnover computation.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: The 2025 MSME limits apply uniformly to manufacturing and services.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: MSME registration runs on the Udyam portal, linked to GST and income-tax data.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: The MSMED Act was enacted in 2006.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: CGTMSE was set up by the Government of India and SIDBI.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: CGTMSE guarantee ceiling rose from ₹5 crore to ₹10 crore per borrower from 1 April 2025.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: CGTMSE cover ranges from 75% to 90% by borrower category.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: CGTMSE Annual Guarantee Fee ranges from 0.37% to 1.20%.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: Banks may not take collateral for MSE loans up to ₹20 lakh (RBI Master Direction, Feb 2026).

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: PMMY categories: Shishu (≤₹50,000), Kishore (≤₹5 lakh), Tarun (≤₹10 lakh), Tarun Plus (≤₹20 lakh).

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: Tarun Plus (Oct 2024) is for borrowers who successfully repaid a Tarun loan.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: PMMY was launched on 8 April 2015; MUDRA is a SIDBI subsidiary.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: Stand-Up India (2016): each branch finances one SC/ST and one woman entrepreneur (₹10 lakh–₹1 crore).

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: MSMED Act 45-day rule: buyers must pay MSME suppliers within 45 days.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: Delayed MSME payments attract interest at three times the RBI bank rate.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: Section 43B(h) disallows the buyer's tax deduction until the MSME is actually paid.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: MSME delayed-payment complaints are filed on the MSME Samadhaan portal.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: TReDS is RBI's platform for auctioning MSME receivables to financiers.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: Nayak Committee norm: working capital at 20% of projected annual turnover (up to ₹5 cr turnover).

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: DSCR = Debt Service Coverage Ratio; lenders look for comfort above 1.25–1.5.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: Priority-sector target is 40% of ANBC for domestic banks; micro enterprises carry an 8% sub-target.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: SIDBI (1990) is the principal financial institution for MSME development.

oneliners.subject: MSME / SME Finance
oneliners.text: Stressed but viable MSMEs get a Corrective Action Plan under RBI's revival framework before NPA classification.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: The digital banking certificate syllabus has 12 modules, ending with data analysis for business.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: UPI was launched by NPCI on 11 April 2016.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: IMPS was launched on 22 November 2010 — 24x7x365 instant transfers.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: NEFT went 24x7 on 16 December 2019; RTGS went 24x7 on 14 December 2020 (minimum ₹2 lakh).

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: *99# is USSD-based mobile banking for feature phones.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: AEPS = Aadhaar Enabled Payment System — interoperable banking via Aadhaar biometrics.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: BBPS standardises bill payments; NACH handles bulk recurring debits like EMIs.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: e-RUPI (2 August 2021) is a person-and-purpose-specific digital voucher.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: RBI's regulatory sandbox (Aug 2019) lets fintechs test innovations under supervision.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: The e-Rupee (CBDC) is RBI's digital currency with legal-tender status.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Video-KYC (V-CIP) has been permitted by RBI since January 2020.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Full-KYC PPIs can hold up to ₹2 lakh; open-system PPIs allow ATM cash withdrawal.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Payment systems are authorised under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: The IT Act, 2000 gives legal validity to electronic contracts and digital signatures.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Phishing (email), vishing (voice), smishing (SMS) — the social-engineering trio.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: SIM-swap fraud reissues the victim's SIM to intercept OTPs.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Zero liability if an unauthorised transaction is reported within 3 working days (RBI, 6 July 2017).

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: The golden hour = the first 1–2 hours after a fraud, when mule accounts can be frozen.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: 1930 is the national helpline for financial cyber fraud; CFCFRMS routes complaints for fund-freezing.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Money mules are accounts used to receive and pass on fraud proceeds.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Multi-factor authentication combines two or more of: know, have, are.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Velocity checks flag unusually frequent or large transactions versus the customer profile.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act was enacted in 2023.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Account aggregators share financial data only on explicit customer consent.

oneliners.subject: Digital Banking
oneliners.text: Maker-checker: one user initiates, another authorises — the fundamental digital-banking control.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: BCSBI was registered on 18 February 2006 and dissolved on 28 September 2021.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: BCSBI was set up on the S.S. Tarapore Committee's recommendation; Y.V. Reddy was its first chair.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: BCSBI was a standards watchdog, not an individual complaint forum.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: The Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme launched 12 Nov 2021; replaced by RB-IOS 2026 effective 1 July 2026.

oneliners.text: RB-IOS subsumed the Banking, NBFC and Digital Transactions Ombudsman schemes.

oneliners.text: Any customer of a regulated entity can complain under RB-IOS — filing is free.

oneliners.text: Complain to the bank first; approach the Ombudsman after 30 days or an unsatisfactory response.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: RB-IOS 2026 (effective 1 July 2026) compensation caps: ₹30 lakh for consequential loss, ₹3 lakh for mental agony.

oneliners.text: Appeals against Ombudsman decisions go to the RBI Executive Director (Appellate Authority) within 30 days.

oneliners.text: The Internal Ombudsman reviews the bank's own complaint rejections before RBI escalation.

oneliners.text: The Charter of Customer Rights (2015) lists five rights: fair treatment, transparency, suitability, privacy, grievance redress.

oneliners.text: DICGC insures deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (since 4 February 2020).

oneliners.text: Failed ATM transactions must be reversed within T+5 days; ₹100/day compensation for delay.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: Nomination in deposits is governed by Sections 45ZA–45ZF of the Banking Regulation Act.

oneliners.text: Complaints are filed through RBI's Complaint Management System (CMS) portal.

oneliners.text: Grievance ladder: branch → regional office → principal nodal officer → Internal Ombudsman → RBI Ombudsman → appeal.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: The original Banking Ombudsman Scheme dates to 1995, launched under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: The Ombudsman can reject frivolous, sub judice or already-decided complaints.

oneliners.text: Ombudsman awards must normally be implemented by the bank within 30 days.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: Mis-selling = selling unsuitable products, e.g., insurance misrepresented as deposits.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: The suitability right requires products appropriate to the customer's needs and risk profile.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: The Customer Service Committee of the Board reviews complaint trends quarterly.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: After BCSBI's dissolution, its role moved to RBI's Consumer Education and Protection framework.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: The NBFC Ombudsman scheme (2018) was subsumed into the Integrated Scheme in 2021.

oneliners.subject: Customer Service & Banking Codes
oneliners.text: Persistent complaint clusters signal a service-design failure, not isolated grievances.

oneliners.text: FEMA violations are civil offences investigated by the Directorate of Enforcement.

oneliners.text: AD Category I banks handle all current and capital account transactions.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Current-account transactions are generally free; capital-account transactions face restrictions.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: An EEFC account can hold up to 100% of a resident's foreign-exchange earnings.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Advance import remittance beyond USD 200,000 needs a bank guarantee or standby LC.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: FEMA replaced FERA with effect from 1 June 2000.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: In a direct quote, the first currency is fixed and the second varies.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Cross rates chain-multiply two pairs sharing a common currency.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Higher domestic interest rates push the currency to a forward discount (interest-rate parity).

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: A forex swap = spot deal + forward deal in opposite directions.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Forward-contract cancellation is at the opposite rate; extension at the current forward rate.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Merchant rates = interbank rate ± the bank's margin, per FEDAI rules.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: FEDAI sets forex market conventions; FIMMDA covers fixed income.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Nostro = our foreign-currency account with the correspondent; Vostro = their rupee account with us.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: SWIFT: MT103 customer transfer, MT202 bank cover, MT700 LC issuance, MT760 guarantee.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Settlement safety ranking: advance payment > documentary credit > collection > open account.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Country risk = sovereign actions blocking payment despite a willing buyer.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: ECGC (1957) insures export credit; EXIM Bank (1982) funds project exports and foreign lines of credit.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: FEMA penalties are civil, up to three times the sum involved; appeals go to the Appellate Tribunal.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: AD banks must verify bona-fide purpose of outward remittances and pursue overdue export bills.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Currency options give the right without obligation, for a premium — capping downside, keeping upside.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Offshore Banking Units conduct foreign-currency business with special regulatory treatment.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: The Diploma in International Banking & Finance pairs forex theory with exchange-rate arithmetic.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: A clean bill of lading bears no damage remarks; LCs normally require clean bills.

oneliners.subject: International Banking & Finance
oneliners.text: Transfer risk = inability to convert and transfer currency out of the buyer's country.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: RBI permitted the BC/BF model in January 2006 on the Khan Committee's recommendations.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: IIBF is the sole certifying agency for the BC/BF examination.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BC candidates must pass within 270 days or three attempts from training, whichever is earlier.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: Business Facilitators cannot handle cash; Business Correspondents transact as the bank's outlet.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BCs accept/disburse cash, open accounts, process remittances and run customer service points.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BFs identify borrowers, collect loan applications and follow up recovery — referral only.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BC scope: deposits, loans, remittances, micro-insurance, mutual funds and pension products.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BCs are paid commissions and fees by the sponsor bank, often activity-based.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BCs work under bank-set cash-holding limits and settle with the link branch on time.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: Micro-ATMs and handheld POS devices with biometric authentication are the BC's hardware.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: AEPS enables interoperable Aadhaar-biometric transactions at any BC of any bank.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BCs open accounts under simplified KYC for small accounts.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: Receipts are mandatory for every BC cash transaction.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: PMJDY (2014): zero-balance accounts with RuPay debit cards.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: PMJJBY premium ₹436/year; PMSBY premium ₹20/year; APY gives guaranteed pension from age 60.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BCs cannot sub-contract their outlet without the bank's approval.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: Police verification of BC agents is required in many states.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BC customers can escalate grievances to the bank and ultimately the RBI Ombudsman.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: NABARD reimburses BC training costs for eligible rural functionaries.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: BC operations are audited by the bank's concurrent auditors.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: Dormant BC outlets are a supervisory red flag — activity levels matter, not just outlet counts.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: Smart cards store account data for offline transactions in low-connectivity areas.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: High-performing BCs drive PMJDY usage, digital transactions and social-security enrolments.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: Fraud by BC agents is reported through the bank's fraud-reporting machinery.

oneliners.subject: Business Correspondent / Facilitator
oneliners.text: Corporate BCs manage agent networks under agreements with banks.

oneliners.subject: RBI
oneliners.text: FM Nirmala Sitharaman said on 13 Oct 2026 that the RBI will sustain measures against excessive rupee volatility without targeting any specific exchange rate.

oneliners.subject: RBI
oneliners.text: The rupee closed at 95.78 per dollar on 12 Oct 2026 and appreciated 77 paise to 95.05 in early trade on 13 Oct.

oneliners.subject: RBI
oneliners.text: The RBI reduced the threshold for certain forex derivative deals without underlying exposure from $100 million to $5 million (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: RBI Policy
oneliners.text: October 2026 was the first RBI repo rate hike since February 2023 (5.25% to 5.50%).

oneliners.subject: RBI Policy
oneliners.text: The RBI’s next MPC meeting is scheduled for 2–4 December 2026.

oneliners.subject: CAIIB
oneliners.text: CAIIB qualifying marks: 50 out of 100 in each subject; IIBF publishes paper-wise marks and qualifying status in the candidate login (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: New IIBF Digital Candidate Portal: first-time users must use 'Forgot Password' to set a password before signing in; results appear under the candidate profile (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: RBI Policy
oneliners.text: Revised WPI series (base 2022-23) inflation: 11.39% in September 2026 vs 9.92% in August; WPI food index up to 8.66% from 7.05%.

oneliners.subject: Banking Certifications
oneliners.text: Cabinet cleared the Rs. 52,878 crore Fairfax deal for 60.72% of IDBI Bank — India's biggest financial-sector FDI approval (15 October 2026).

oneliners.subject: Banking awareness
oneliners.text: The 63rd MPC meeting (5-7 October 2026) under Governor Sanjay Malhotra raised the repo rate unanimously; the stance change to 'calibrated tightening' was supported 4-2.

oneliners.subject: Banking awareness
oneliners.text: In the Yes Bank AT-1 case (2026 INSC 1132), the Court held that the objective of restoring a bank's financial stability does not permit acting beyond powers available under the governing legal framework.

oneliners.subject: Banking Awareness
oneliners.text: Largest FDI in Indian banking: Emirates NBD's Rs 26,000 crore capital infusion for a 60% stake in RBL Bank (deal completed June 2026) — Verified: 17 Oct 2026

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: JAIIB November 2026: IE&IFS on 1 Nov, PPB on 22 Nov, AFM on 28 Nov, RBWM on 29 Nov — 100 MCQs, 2 hours, no negative marking, pass at 50/100.

oneliners.subject: CAIIB
oneliners.text: CAIIB December 2026: ABM on 6 Dec, BFM on 12 Dec, ABFM on 13 Dec, BRBL on 20 Dec, electives on 27 Dec.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: RBI's October 2026 policy: repo 5.50%, stance 'calibrated tightening' — key current-affairs input for IE&IFS.

oneliners.subject: Banking
oneliners.text: RBI October 2026: repo 5.50% (+25 bps), SDF 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%; stance 'calibrated tightening' (4-2 vote). Note: 25 basis points = 0.25 percentage point.

oneliners.subject: Bank Exams
oneliners.text: IBPS Clerk (CSA-XVI) Mains on 27 December 2026; IBPS SO Mains on 1 November 2026; IBPS PO Mains was held on 4 October 2026.

oneliners.subject: Banking Certifications
oneliners.text: At the 3rd World AI Summit (Bengaluru, 14-15 Oct 2026), Dr. Hemant Garg (ESIC) won 'Excellence in AI for Public Policy' for IFSCA Karmayogi (2023), the first AI agent at IFSCA, GIFT City, plus research on AI in anti-money laundering. (21 Oct 2026)

oneliners.subject: RBI & Monetary Policy
oneliners.text: 21 Oct 2026: RBI MPC minutes — the 4–2 stance vote for “calibrated tightening” had dissenters Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh preferring neutral.

oneliners.subject: Financial Markets
oneliners.text: 21 Oct 2026: Goldman Sachs — private equity funding for Indian AI startups has tripled since 2024; AI is now ~one-fifth of all private capital invested in India.

oneliners.subject: Banking
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% in October 2026 (first hike in ~2.5 years); daily CRR maintenance up to 99% from 16 October 2026.

oneliners.subject: Banking
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: OMO sale of ₹25,000 crore G-Secs on 13 October 2026; system liquidity surplus ₹3.88 lakh crore on 8 October.

oneliners.subject: Banking Awareness
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: SBI Research's Ecowrap (23 Oct) questioned the RBI's Rs 2.5 lakh crore liquidity injection alongside its 25 bps hike to 5.50% as potentially 'mixed signals'.

oneliners.subject: Banking Awareness
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: Next RBI MPC meeting: 2-4 December 2026.

oneliners.subject: Banking Awareness
oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: GST process reforms from 1 November 2026 — automatic refunds, simpler e-commerce seller registration, 90% provisional sanction for zero-rated/inverted-duty claims.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: CRR unchanged at 3% in the RBI's October 2026 policy.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: MPC minutes of the 5-7 Oct meeting were released on 21 Oct 2026; rate cuts are off the table with Q3 inflation seen near 6%.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: Next RBI MPC meeting: 2-4 December 2026.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: DICGC: Rs 5 lakh cover per depositor per bank; premium 12 paise per Rs 100 of deposits.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: RBI tightened forex derivative rules and opened a special dollar window on 13 Oct 2026 amid rupee pressure.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: CCEA approved the 60.72% IDBI Bank stake sale to Fairfax for Rs 52,878.08 crore on 14 October 2026.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: RBI FY27 projections after the October 2026 MPC: real GDP growth 7.1% and CPI inflation 5.2%.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: October 2026: the RBI's open market sale of Rs 25,000 crore of government securities was scheduled for 13 October 2026 to absorb surplus liquidity.

oneliners.subject: CAIIB
oneliners.text: October 2026: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the October foreign-exchange measures were aimed at genuine hedging needs, not speculation, and were not capital controls.

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: CA Intermediate September 2026: AIR 2 went to Shruti V of Chennai (492 marks, 82%) and AIR 3 to Prem Agarwal of Surat (490 marks, 81.67%).

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: CA Intermediate September 2026: of 38,339 candidates appearing for both groups, 5,066 passed (13.21%).

oneliners.subject: Regulation
oneliners.text: FSDC members: Finance Minister (chair), RBI Governor, Finance Ministry secretaries, and heads of SEBI, IRDAI, IFSCA, PFRDA and IBBI.

oneliners.subject: Markets
oneliners.text: T-Bill auction 28 October 2026: ₹23,000 crore total; retail non-competitive bids via RBI Retail Direct, capped at 5%.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: Daily CRR maintenance: banks must now maintain at least 99% of prescribed CRR every day of the fortnight, up from 90% (RBI, October 2026).

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: MPC minutes, 21 October 2026: the repo hike to 5.50% was unanimous, but the shift to 'calibrated tightening' was carried 4-2.

oneliners.subject: Banking Awareness
oneliners.text: 27 October 2026: PIB Fact Check debunked claims of a new Rs 1,000 note; the RBI had announced no such note.

oneliners.subject: Risk Management
oneliners.text: October 2026: India's forthcoming AI consultation paper will address AI agents, deepfakes and education, with human control and audit trails urged for banking.

oneliners.subject: Banking Awareness
oneliners.text: May 2023: the RBI announced the withdrawal of Rs 2,000 banknotes from circulation, although they continued to remain legal tender.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: 28 Oct 2026: dearness allowance and dearness relief raised 3 points to 63% of basic pay/pension from 1 July 2026; combined exchequer impact Rs 10,016.10 crore a year, under the 7th Central Pay Commission formula.

oneliners.subject: CAIIB
oneliners.text: BEL Probationary Engineer Recruitment 2026 (Advt 17556/HR/All-India/2026): 350 posts, E-II Grade, pay scale Rs 40,000-1,40,000, approximate CTC Rs 13 lakh; apply at bel-india.in by 18 November 2026.

oneliners.subject: JAIIB
oneliners.text: Governor Sanjay Malhotra said excess liquidity would not last beyond end-FY27 and that raising the CRR itself would be the least preferred option for absorbing it, according to October 2026 reports.

oneliners.subject: CAIIB
oneliners.text: FCNR(B) mobilisation of USD 133 billion between 8 June and 31 August 2026 under the RBI swap window was a key driver of surplus rupee liquidity in October 2026.

oneliners.subject: Banking Regulation
oneliners.text: 29 Oct 2026: The RBI extended restrictive directions on Sonpeth Nagari Sahakari Bank (Parbhani, Maharashtra) and Lokapavani Mahila Sahakari Bank (Mandya, Karnataka) to 30 January 2027; the directions date from 29 July 2025.

oneliners.subject: Banking Awareness
oneliners.text: 29 Oct 2026: Banking-system surplus liquidity had fallen to about Rs 462 billion as of 26 October 2026 from Rs 11 lakh crore in early September, with the RBI capping liquidity support at Rs 1.5 lakh crore.

alerts.title: CAIIB December cycle dates
alerts.body: CAIIB papers are scheduled for 6, 12, 13, 20 and 27 December. Finish your JAIIB revision first, then switch to CAIIB electives in November.
